
Open **http://localhost:8080/books**:
+ The five sample books and Dawn, added in step 2, are listed by title, each with its author: `Page 1 of 1, 6 books`.
+ Click an author: `/books?author_id=2` lists only the books of Octavia E. Butler.
+ Submit the form with an empty title and year: the page comes back with `Some of the inputs are invalid` under the button, `The Title field is required` and `The Published Year field is required` under their fields, and the author you chose still selected.
+ Add *The Dispossessed*, Ursula K. Le Guin, 1974: you land on `/books/7`, which shows the title, `by Ursula K. Le Guin, 1974` and `Book added`.
+ `http://localhost:8080/books/99` shows *Not found* and `There is no book #99`, with status `404`.

### <a name="rest"></a>4. A REST API

The Quickstart's `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` already serves every capability to programs: `POST /capabilities/<name>` with the inputs as JSON, and `GET /capabilities` lists what the caller may use.
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"title": "Wild Seed", "published_year": 1980, "author_id": 2}' \
     http://localhost:8080/capabilities/create_book
```
```json
{"data":{"id":8,"title":"Wild Seed","published_year":1980,"summary":null,"author_id":2,"created_at":"2026-11-08 00:14:45","modified_at":"2026-11-08 00:14:45","author":{"id":2,"name":"Octavia E. Butler","bio":"American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.","created_at":"2026-11-08 00:13:35","modified_at":"2026-11-08 00:13:35"}}}
```
For addresses of your own, add one `Route::capability` per address under the `BOOKSHELF PAGES` lines of `web.php`:
```php
    // BOOKSHELF API: the same capabilities, for other applications (JSON)
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');
    Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/authors', 'list_authors');
```
The query string and the `{id}` of the address become inputs:
```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" "http://localhost:8080/api/books?author_id=3"
curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/books/3
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"title": "Mind of My Mind", "published_year": 1977, "author_id": 2}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
```
The first answers `{"data":{"data":[{"id":5,"title":"Invisible Cities",...,"author":{"id":3,"name":"Italo Calvino",...}}],"total":1,"page":1,"per_page":20,"pages":1}}`, the second `{"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred",...,"author":{"id":2,"name":"Octavia E. Butler",...}}}`, the third `201` with the new book.

| Request | Status | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a read, or a write of an existing record | `200` | `{"data": ...}` |
| a new record (`POST` on a capability that is not read-only) | `201` | `{"data": ...}` |
| refused input (`{"title": "No author", "published_year": 1990}`) | `422` | `{"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"author_id":"The Author Id field is required"}}}` |
| unknown id | `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"There is no book #99"}}` |
| no sign-in or token for a capability that is not public | `401` | `{"error":{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"Sign in or send a personal access token"}}` |
| a token without the scope | `403` | `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"This needs the scope books:write"}}` |

### <a name="agent"></a>5. Tools for AI agents

The Quickstart's `Route::mcp('/mcp')` makes every capability a tool. Give an agent a token with only the books scopes:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "books agent" --scopes books:read,books:write
```
```text
 Token #2 "books agent" created with books:read books:write

 cq_2_...

 It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
```
Connect Claude Code with it:
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http bookshelf http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cq_2_..."
```
Ask "add The Lathe of Heaven by Ursula K. Le Guin, 1971, to my shelf": the agent calls `list_authors` to find her id, then `create_book`. The same call with `curl`:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_2_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"create_book","arguments":{"title":"The Lathe of Heaven","published_year":1971,"author_id":1}}}' \
     http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
The answer has `"isError":false` and the new book, with its author, in `structuredContent`. Without `author_id`, it has `"isError":true` and the same `fields` as REST. `tools/list` shows the books tools and the public ones; the user administration tools stay hidden from this token. Without a token, `/mcp` answers `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header and the JSON-RPC error `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Unauthorized: send Authorization: Bearer <personal access token>"}}` (2.19.1; before, a browser's session cookie got a `403` CSRF page instead).

### <a name="client"></a>6. The JavaScript client, for Vue apps and page scripts

Generate the client again after every change to a capability:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client
```
```text
 public/js/capabilities.js written: 22 capabilities, calls /capabilities (Route::capabilities('/capabilities') in web.php)
 import { createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'
```
Each capability is a function (`list_books` becomes `listBooks`). In a page of the application it sends the visitor's session; elsewhere, `configure({ baseUrl, token })`:
```js
import { listBooks, createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'

const shelf = await listBooks({ author_id: 2, page: 1 })
console.log(shelf.total, shelf.data[0].title, shelf.data[0].author.name)
try {
  await createBook({ title: 'No author', published_year: 1990 })
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof CapabilityError) console.log(e.status, e.fields.author_id)   // 422 The Author Id field is required
}
```
Vue apps: see [Vue apps: the JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#client).

### <a name="secure"></a>7. Before you go online: sign-in

`public: true` on `create_book` lets anyone add books. Close it: readers keep the catalog, and only people who signed in, or a program with a token, add books.

1. Create the `users` table of the authentication module:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Auth/create_db.sql
    ```
2. In `application/config/routing/web.php`, remove the `// ` in front of `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');` near the top, and add `Route::auth` as the first line of the `BOOKSHELF PAGES` lines:
    ```php
        Auth::authentication('User', 'users');
    ```
    ```php
        // BOOKSHELF PAGES: rendered on the server with the data of the capabilities; the form calls create_book
        Route::auth(['home' => '/books']);
    ```
    `Route::auth` declares `/login`, `/logout`, `/register` and `/notAuthorized`, with the sign-in pages of the [authentication module](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication). After signing in, people land on `/books`.
3. In `application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php`, remove `public: true` and its comment (and the comma before it):
    ```php
    #[Capability(
        name: 'create_book',
        description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.',
        scope: 'books:write'
    )]
    ```

Now:
+ A visitor who submits the form on `/books` is sent to `/login`.
+ `POST /api/books` without a token gets `401` and `Sign in or send a personal access token`.
+ The `books agent` token still adds books (`201`): it has `books:write`.
+ Create an account at `/register` (usernames are letters and digits, for example `sam42`; to sign in with an email instead, see [Signing in with an email](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#emailsignin)); you are sent to `/login`. Sign in: you land on `/books`, and the form adds the book.

`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit` lists every change and every refusal: when, through which channel, who, which capability:
```text
 2026-11-08 00:15:31  web   user   1            create_book                  ok
 2026-11-08 00:15:30  web   guest  -            register_user                ok
 2026-11-08 00:15:18  rest  token  2            create_book                  ok
 2026-11-08 00:15:18  rest  guest  -            create_book                  unauthenticated  Sign in or send a personal access token
 2026-11-08 00:15:18  web   guest  -            create_book                  unauthenticated  Sign in or send a personal access token
```
To keep a capability for administrators (`permissions` of 1 or more in `users`), add `level: 1` to its `#[Capability]`. The Tasks example is still public: remove its `public: true` the same way, or remove the example.

### <a name="test"></a>8. A test

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test make Bookshelf
```
```text
 tests/BookshelfTest.php written: php caligrafer.php test Bookshelf
```
Replace the content of **`tests/BookshelfTest.php`**:
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase;

/**
 * php caligrafer.php test Bookshelf
 */
final class BookshelfTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testASignedInPersonAddsABook(): void
    {
        $book = $this->call('create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => 1], $this->user(1));
        $this->assertSame('Tehanu', $book['title']);
        $this->assertSame('Ursula K. Le Guin', $this->call('get_book', ['id' => $book['id']])['author']['name']);
    }

    public function testAVisitorCannotAddABook(): void
    {
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('unauthenticated', 'create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => 1], 'guest');
    }

    public function testABookNeedsAnAuthorThatExists(): void
    {
        $error = $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990], $this->user(1));
        $this->assertArrayHasKey('author_id', $error->fields);
        $error = $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => 999], $this->user(1));
        $this->assertSame('There is no such author', $error->fields['author_id']);
    }
}
```
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test
```
```text
PHPUnit 12.5.45 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.

Runtime:       PHP 8.5.12

...                                                                 3 / 3 (100%)

Time: 00:00.077, Memory: 20.00 MB

OK (3 tests, 7 assertions)
```
Each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back: the books it adds do not stay. More in [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App).

### <a name="migration"></a>9. Later: change the table with a migration

Once `books` holds data (on your computer or online), never edit its `create_db.sql` to change it: write a migration, a numbered SQL file that runs once. Give books an optional ISBN that two books never share:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate make add_books_isbn
```
```text
 application/migrations/20261108001545_add_books_isbn.sql written: add its SQL, then php caligrafer.php migrate
```
Add the SQL at the end of the file it wrote (one statement: the column and its unique index are added together, or not at all):
```sql
-- add_books_isbn
-- Runs once (php caligrafer.php migrate, and at every deploy). Never edit it after it ran: write a new one.

ALTER TABLE books
    ADD COLUMN isbn VARCHAR(20) NULL AFTER summary,
    ADD UNIQUE KEY uq_books_isbn (isbn);
```
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate
```
```text
 OK   20261108001545_add_books_isbn.sql

 1 migration(s) run on caligrafy
```
Then give the code the new column:
1. In `application/models/Bookshelf/Book.php`, add `public $isbn;` after `public $summary;`.
2. Make `application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php` read (the `isbn` input, its filter and its description, and an empty ISBN saved as `NULL`, which the unique index allows on many books):
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    // create_book: adds a book, with the same rules whoever calls it
    #[Capability(
        name: 'create_book',
        description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id. The ISBN is optional and unique.',
        scope: 'books:write'
    )]
    class CreateBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array(
            'title' => 'required|max_len,200',
            'published_year' => 'required|integer|min_numeric,1450|max_numeric,current_year',
            'summary' => 'max_len,2000',
            'isbn' => 'alpha_numeric_dash|max_len,20|unique,books.isbn',
            'author_id' => 'required|integer|exists,authors.id'
        );
        public $filters = array('title' => 'trim', 'summary' => 'trim', 'isbn' => 'trim');
        public $descriptions = array(
            'title' => 'The title of the book',
            'published_year' => 'The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)',
            'summary' => 'Optional: one or two sentences about the book',
            'isbn' => 'Optional: its ISBN, digits and dashes, for example 978-0-441-47812-5; two books never share one',
            'author_id' => 'The id of its author (list_authors)'
        );

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            // an empty ISBN is no ISBN: NULL, which the unique index allows on many books
            $input['isbn'] = ($input['isbn'] ?? '') === '' ? null : $input['isbn'];
            $id = Book::insert($input);   // one INSERT, every value bound; returns the id of the new book
            return Book::with('author')->find($id);
        }
    }
    ```
3. In `application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug`, add the field after the year's `.cq-field`, at the same depth:
    ```pug
                        .cq-field
                            label(for='isbn') ISBN
                            input#isbn.form-control(type='text', name='isbn', value=old('isbn'), placeholder='Optional', maxlength='20')
                            if errors('isbn')
                                p.cq-field-error= errors('isbn')
    ```

A second book with the same ISBN is now refused on every channel with `"isbn": "This isbn is already used"`. Online, the deploy runs the migrations that never ran. More in [Migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations).

### Check

+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists `list_books`, `get_book` and `list_authors` as `public` and `read`, and `create_book` as `books:write` and `writes`.
+ `/books` lists the books with their authors; an empty form shows a message under each required field; a new book opens its own page with `Book added`.
+ `curl http://localhost:8080/api/books` answers `200`; a `POST` without a token answers `401`; with the `books agent` token, `201`.
+ `php caligrafer.php test` ends with `OK`.
+ `php caligrafer.php migrate status` shows `add_books_isbn` as run.
## Common mistakes

+ **A capability without `--scope`.** `service` then writes `scope: ''`: the capability needs no scope, so any token can call it. Give every capability a scope.
+ **A foreign key without `exists`.** Without `exists,authors.id` in `$rules`, a book with an unknown author reaches the database, which refuses it with a foreign key error instead of a message under the field.
+ **`paginate()` without a page in a capability.** It then reads `$_GET`, which REST, MCP and the command line do not have: pass `$input['page'] ?? 1`, with `'page' => 'integer'` in `$rules`.
+ **A page fed by a capability that writes.** `Route::page` data accepts only `readOnly` capabilities: it stops with an error otherwise.
+ **`flash()`, `errors()` and `old()` last one request.** Point `success` (and `back`) at the page that shows them.
+ **A `POST` with `curl` without `Accept: application/json`.** It is treated as a form without a CSRF token: `[ERROR 3000]` (403).
+ **Editing a `create_db.sql` that already ran online** to change a table: the change is a migration (step 9).
+ **Model code outside a capability.** Pages, forms, custom requests (`Route::action`) and scripts call capabilities; only capabilities read and write models.

One feature, written once in four small classes, used from a web page, by other programs and by AI agents, with the same rules everywhere. Next:

+ [Build Once: Services, Capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP): every option of a capability, tokens, MCP over stdio, the audit log.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once%3A-Services%2C-Capabilities-and-MCP -->

**Build once, experience everywhere** is what Caligrafy is for. A feature is written once, as a **capability**: a small
PHP class (a **service**) that declares its inputs, checks who is asking, does the work and returns data. Every way of
reaching your application is a **channel** that calls the same capability: your Pug pages (`Route::page`,
`Route::form`), a REST API, the JavaScript client of your Vue apps, and AI agents over MCP. A rule written once
behaves the same for a person, a phone, a program and an agent.

**Since 2.26.0**: a write capability declared without a `scope` needs, from a token, the scope named after it (or `*`); a public read-only capability may declare `cache: <seconds>` to be served from the production image's memory ([performance](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Performance-and-Deployment)); and the experimental async server answers the capabilities channel from processes that keep the app in memory (`ASYNC=on`).
## <a name="overview"></a>How it fits together

| Channel | How it calls a capability | Who is calling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pug pages | `Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']])`; forms with `Route::form('/books', 'create_book', [...])` | the person who opens the page (signed in, or a visitor) |
| REST | `Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book')`, or every capability under `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` | a personal access token, or the signed-in user |
| Vue apps, the Vite SPA, Node | the generated JS client (`php caligrafer.php client`), on `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` | the signed-in user (session and CSRF token), or a token |
| AI agents | MCP: `Route::mcp('/mcp')` over HTTP, or `php caligrafer.php mcp` over stdio | a personal access token (stdio: also your own full access) |
| The command line, scripts, jobs | `php caligrafer.php call create_book ...`, `Capabilities::call()`, the queue and the scheduler | full access, or a token |

A capability declared `webOnly: true` has one channel instead of all of them: [`Route::action`](#webonly), for what only a
browser can do.

Every call goes through the same steps, in this order:

1. **Find** the capability (`not_found`, 404).
2. **Check who calls**: public, or signed in or a token (`unauthenticated`, 401), with the right scope and level
   (`forbidden`, 403).
3. **Keep, filter and validate** the declared inputs (`invalid`, 422, with a message per field).
4. **Run** `handle()`.
5. **Audit**: every refusal, and every success of a capability that changes data, is written to the audit log.

**Only capabilities touch models**: pages, forms, REST, agents and the controllers of older code all go through them, so
the rules exist once.
## With Claude

Ask for the feature with the `new-capability` skill of the Claude Code plugin: its name, its scope, and what it does.

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write: add a book (title, published year, summary, author) and return it
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability delete_book books:write destructive: only administrators (level 1)
```

Claude:
+ runs `php caligrafer.php service <Folder>/<Name> --scope <scope>` and fills
  `application/services/<Folder>/<Name>.php`: a `description` written for an AI agent, `$rules` for every input,
  `handle()` with the query builder, `ServiceError` refusals, `readOnly` / `destructive` / `level` / `public`;
+ adds the channels you need to `application/config/routing/web.php` (`Route::page`, `Route::form`,
  `Route::capability`, `Route::capabilities`, `Route::mcp`) and runs `php caligrafer.php client` for a Vue app;
+ creates a token only when an agent or a program needs one, shows it once, and never writes it in a file;
+ checks every channel (`capabilities`, `call`, REST with `curl`, MCP `tools/list` and `tools/call`, `audit`), and
  writes a test in `tests/` (`php caligrafer.php test`).

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists it with the scope and the flag you expect (`read`, `writes`, `destroys`);
+ the description says what it does and what it returns;
+ an invalid input gives a message per field, on the command line, over REST and over MCP alike;
+ a token without the scope gets `403` over REST, and does not see the tool in MCP `tools/list`;
+ `php caligrafer.php audit --capability <name>` shows the calls.
## By hand

This builds the Bookshelf capabilities and serves them on every channel. It starts from the tables and models of
[Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models), `get_book` of
[Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships) and `list_books` of
[Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries#capability). The server is the Docker server of the
[Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart), at `http://localhost:8080`; run each
`php caligrafer.php` command in its container, as written (without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box` and use
your own address).

### <a name="setup"></a>1. The framework tables

Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install
```
```text
 Framework tables ready: caligrafy_tokens, caligrafy_audit, caligrafy_job_runs, the notifications tables, caligrafy_jobs, caligrafy_cache and caligrafy_migrations
```
It is safe to run again. `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only database` then shows
`OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache and migrations installed`.

### <a name="service"></a>2. Write the capabilities

1. Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/CreateBook --scope books:write
    ```
    ```text
     Created application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php: capability 'create_book' (scope books:write)
    ```
2. Make `application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'create_book',
        description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.',
        scope: 'books:write'
    )]
    class CreateBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array(
            'title' => 'required|max_len,200',
            'published_year' => 'required|integer|min_numeric,1450|max_numeric,current_year',
            'summary' => 'max_len,2000',
            'author_id' => 'required|integer|exists,authors.id'
        );

        public $filters = array(
            'title' => 'trim',
            'summary' => 'trim'
        );

        public $descriptions = array(
            'title' => 'The title of the book',
            'published_year' => 'The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)',
            'summary' => 'Optional: one or two sentences about the book',
            'author_id' => 'The id of its author (list_authors)'
        );

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $id = Book::insert($input);   // one INSERT, every value bound; returns the id of the new book
            return Book::with('author')->find($id);
        }
    }
    ```
3. Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/DeleteBook --scope books:write`, then make
   `application/services/Bookshelf/DeleteBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;
    use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'delete_book',
        description: 'Deletes a book of the catalog for good, with its loans and its tags. Returns the id of the deleted book.',
        scope: 'books:write',
        level: 1,
        destructive: true
    )]
    class DeleteBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');

        public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book to delete');

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            if (Book::where('id', $input['id'])->delete() === 0) {
                throw ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #' . $input['id']);
            }
            return array('deleted' => (int) $input['id']);
        }
    }
    ```
    `level: 1`: a signed-in person needs `permissions` 1 or more in the `users` table (an administrator).
    `destructive: true`: agents ask the user before they call it.
4. Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities`. Among the framework's own capabilities
   (users, notifications, the queue), it lists:
    ```text
     create_book                  books:write    writes    Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.
     delete_book                  books:write    destroys  Deletes a book of the catalog for good, with its loans and its tags. Returns the id of the deleted book.
     get_book                     public         read      Returns one book by its id, with its author, its tags and its loans.
     list_books                   public         read      Lists the books of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page, ... (cut here)
    ```
5. Call it from the command line (full access, with the checks and the audit):
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call create_book '{"title": "The Dispossessed", "published_year": 1974, "author_id": 1}'
    ```
    ```json
    {
        "data": {
            "id": 6,
            "title": "The Dispossessed",
            "published_year": 1974,
            "summary": null,
            "author_id": 1,
            "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:17:13",
            "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:17:13",
            "author": {
                "id": 1,
                "name": "Ursula K. Le Guin",
                "bio": "American author of science fiction and fantasy, known for the Earthsea books.",
                "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:16:40",
                "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:16:40"
            }
        }
    }
    ```
    `call create_book title=Dune` answers the field messages:
    ```json
    {
        "error": {
            "code": "invalid",
            "message": "Some of the inputs are invalid",
            "fields": {
                "published_year": "The Published Year field is required",
                "author_id": "The Author Id field is required"
            }
        }
    }
    ```
    `call create_book title=Dune --guest` (as a visitor) answers `"code": "unauthenticated"`.

### <a name="web"></a>3. Pages

In `application/config/routing/web.php`, inside the `try` block and before `Route::run();`, add:
```php
    // BOOKSHELF: the pages
    Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
    Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book'], 'notFound' => 'Bookshelf/notfound']);
```
Write the three views. `application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug`:
```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block title
  | Books · Bookshelf

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display Books
    p.cq-lead= $books['total'] . ' books in the catalog'

  section.cq-band
    .cq-inner
      if flash('success')
        .cq-alert.cq-alert--success= flash('success')
      if $books['data']
        ul.cq-rows
          each $book in $books['data']
            li.cq-row
              a(href=$home . 'books/' . $book['id'])= $book['title']
              span.cq-muted= ' by ' . $book['author']['name']
      else
        .cq-empty-state No books yet.
```
`application/views/Bookshelf/book.pug`:
```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block title
  | #{$book['title']} · Bookshelf

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display= $book['title']
    p.cq-lead= $book['author']['name'] . ', ' . $book['published_year']

  section.cq-band
    .cq-inner
      if flash('success')
        .cq-alert.cq-alert--success= flash('success')
      p= $book['summary']
      p= 'Tags: ' . implode(', ', array_column($book['tags'], 'name'))
```
`application/views/Bookshelf/notfound.pug`, the page of a book that does not exist (`$message` is the refusal of
`get_book`):
```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block title
  | Not found · Bookshelf

block content
  section.cq-hero
    h1.cq-display Not found
    p.cq-lead= $message
    .cq-cta
      a.btn.btn-primary(href=$home . 'books') All books
```
Open `http://localhost:8080/books`: the books, each with its author. `http://localhost:8080/books/3` shows *Kindred*,
*Octavia E. Butler, 1979*; `/books/99` shows *Not found*, *There is no book #99*, with status 404.

+ A page's `data` capabilities must be read-only. They run as the person who opens the page, with the route
  variables (`{id}`) and the query string as inputs, the route variables winning. The view gets plain arrays
  (`$book['title']`), plus `$authorized` and `$user`, and of the query string only the names you list in `query`.
+ A capability that refuses a visitor sends them to sign in (with the authentication module), or answers 403 or 404.
+ A form posts to a capability:
  `Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Added {title}'])`. It calls the
  capability as the signed-in person; on invalid input it goes back, and the view shows `errors('title')`,
  `old('title')` and `flash('error')`. Sign-in pages come from `Route::auth()`. Both are on
  [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form) and
  [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#routeauth).

### <a name="tokens"></a>4. A personal access token

A program or an agent proves who it is with a **personal access token**: it has a name, **scopes** (what it may do)
and, optionally, an owner and an expiry, and it can be revoked on its own. Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "Bookshelf agent" --scopes books:read,books:write
```
```text
 Token #1 "Bookshelf agent" created with books:read books:write

 cq_1_<40 hexadecimal characters>

 It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
```
Keep it in your terminal for the next steps: `TOKEN=cq_1_...` (the whole token). Make a second one that can only read,
to see the refusals: `token create "Reader" --scopes books:read --expires 90` (it prints `..., expires <date in 90 days>`).

`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token list` shows them, never their secret:
```text
 #2    active   Reader                         books:read  never used
 #1    active   Bookshelf agent                books:read books:write  never used
```

### <a name="rest"></a>5. REST

In `web.php`, before `Route::run();`, add:
```php
    // BOOKSHELF: REST
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');
    Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
    Route::capability('DELETE', '/api/books/{id}', 'delete_book');
```
The route variables (`{id}`) become inputs. Then run (a `POST` with neither a token nor `Accept: application/json`
is taken for a form and answers `403` `[ERROR 3000]`):
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/books/3
# {"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred","published_year":1979,...}}            200: get_book is public

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" -d '{"title": "Dune"}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
# {"error":{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"Sign in or send a personal access token"}}   401

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"title": "The Lathe of Heaven", "published_year": 1971, "author_id": 1}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
# {"data":{"id":7,"title":"The Lathe of Heaven","published_year":1971,"summary":null,"author_id":1,...,"author":{"id":1,"name":"Ursula K. Le Guin",...}}}   201

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"title": "X", "published_year": 1971, "author_id": 42}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
# {"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"author_id":"There is no such author"}}}   422
```
With the Reader token, the same `POST` answers
`{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"This needs the scope books:write"}}` (403).

+ **Requests**: a JSON body, form fields, or the query string for `GET`. Then the route variables, which win.
+ **Responses**: `200` with `{"data": ...}`, `201` when a `POST` changes data, or `{"error": {"code", "message",
  "fields"}}` with 401 (and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), 403, 404, 409 or 422.
+ **Who calls**: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the session of a signed-in person. A call made with the session
  that changes data needs the session's CSRF token in an `X-CSRF-Token` header (403 `Missing or invalid CSRF token:
  send the X-CSRF-Token header` otherwise); the JS client sends it.

### <a name="mcp"></a>6. AI agents: MCP

[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (the Model Context Protocol) is how AI agents such as Claude use tools. With
`Route::mcp('/mcp')` every capability is a tool: its name, its description, its input schema, and hints that say
whether it only reads (`readOnlyHint`) or destroys data (`destructiveHint`). An agent sees only the tools its token
allows, and its calls go through the same checks, validation and audit as everyone else's.

In `web.php`, before `Route::run();`, add:
```php
    Route::mcp('/mcp');   // AI agents: personal access tokens only
```
Without a token it answers `401` and a JSON-RPC error (2.19.1):
```bash
curl -s -i -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Send a personal access token: php caligrafer.php token create"
Content-Type: application/json

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Unauthorized: send Authorization: Bearer <personal access token>"}}
```
Talk to it as an agent does, with `curl` and the token. Each request is one JSON-RPC message:
```bash
curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1"}}}' \
     http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"serverInfo":{"name":"caligrafy-app","title":"caligrafy-app","version":"2.25.0"},"instructions":"Tools are the capabilities of this application that your token allows. Tools marked destructive delete or overwrite data: confirm with the user first."}}
```
(`serverInfo.name` is your `APP_NAME`.) Then the tools:
```bash
curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
The list has `create_book`, `delete_book` (`"destructiveHint": true`), `get_book` and `list_books`
(`"readOnlyHint": true`), and the framework's public `register_user` (which refuses every channel but web pages and
the command line). Each tool looks like this one:
```json
{"name": "create_book", "title": "Create book", "description": "Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.",
 "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 200, "description": "The title of the book"},
    "published_year": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1450, "maximum": 2026, "description": "The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)"},
    "summary": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 2000, "description": "Optional: one or two sentences about the book"},
    "author_id": {"type": "integer", "description": "The id of its author (list_authors)"}},
  "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["title", "published_year", "author_id"]},
 "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": false, "destructiveHint": false, "openWorldHint": false}}
```
With the Reader token, `create_book` and `delete_book` are not in the list. Call a tool:
```bash
curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"create_book","arguments":{"title":"Dune"}}}' \
     http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid\",\"message\":\"Some of the inputs are invalid\",\"fields\":{\"published_year\":\"The Published Year field is required\",\"author_id\":\"The Author Id field is required\"}}}"}],"isError":true}}
```
A refused call is a tool result with `"isError": true` and the same fields as REST, so the agent can correct itself.
A successful one has `"isError": false`, the data as JSON in `content[0].text`, and the object in `structuredContent`.

**Connect Claude Code** to the server:
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http bookshelf http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cq_..."
```
**Over stdio**, a local agent starts the server itself, in the project folder:
```bash
claude mcp add bookshelf -- docker compose exec -T dev-box php caligrafer.php mcp
```
Without a token, stdio has full access, like any command you run yourself (it says so on stderr:
`caligrafer mcp: no token, full local access (set CALIGRAFY_TOKEN to limit it)`). With `CALIGRAFY_TOKEN=cq_...` (or
`--token cq_...`) it has the rights of that token.

### <a name="client"></a>7. Vue apps and the Vite SPA: the JS client

In `web.php`, before `Route::run();`, add:
```php
    Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // GET lists, POST /capabilities/{name} calls: the JS client uses it
```
Generate the client: one JavaScript function per capability. Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js
```
```text
 public/js/capabilities.js written: 17 capabilities, calls /capabilities (Route::capabilities('/capabilities') in web.php)
 import { createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'
```
(For a Vite SPA, write it in `public/<app>/src/capabilities.js`.) Use it in your app:
```js
import { createBook, listBooks, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'

try {
  const book = await createBook({ title: this.title, published_year: this.year, author_id: this.authorId })
  this.books = (await listBooks({ author_id: book.author_id })).data
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof CapabilityError && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields   // { published_year: '...' }
  else throw e
}
```
+ In a page of the application it uses the **session**: the cookie, and the CSRF token it reads once from
  `GET /capabilities`. No key is ever in the bundle.
+ From Node or another site, give it a token: `configure({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', token: process.env.CALIGRAFY_TOKEN })`.
+ Run `client` again after you add or change a capability.

`GET /capabilities` answers what the caller may call: `{"data": [{"name", "description", "scope", "level", "readOnly",
"destructive", "public", "input"}, ...], "csrf": "<the session's CSRF token>"}`. `POST /capabilities/get_book` with
`{"id": 3}` calls `get_book`.

### <a name="audit"></a>8. The audit log

Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit --capability create_book --limit 5
```
```text
 2026-11-07 23:18:39  mcp   token  1            create_book                  invalid  Some of the inputs are invalid
 2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  1            create_book                  invalid  Some of the inputs are invalid
 2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  1            create_book                  ok
 2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  2            create_book                  forbidden  This needs the scope books:write
 2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  guest  -            create_book                  unauthenticated  Sign in or send a personal access token
```
Each row: when, the channel (`web`, `rest`, `mcp`, `cli`), who (`user`, `token`, `key`, `cli`, `guest`, or `schedule`
and `queue` for jobs) and its id, the capability, the outcome and a short note. Inputs are never stored. A read-only
capability is written only when it is refused.

**Check** the whole chapter:
+ `capabilities` lists your four capabilities with the right flags;
+ the same invalid `create_book` gives the same `fields` from `call`, REST and MCP;
+ the Reader token gets 403 from REST and does not see `create_book` in `tools/list`;
+ `audit` shows the calls of every channel.
## <a name="experiences"></a>One look on every device

`public/css/tokens.css` defines the Caligrafy look as CSS custom properties (`--cq-color-ink`, `--cq-space-3`,
`--cq-touch-target`...), from `public/css/tokens.json`, so Pug pages, Vue apps and the SPA share it. The default
layout, the Vue app template and the SPA template include it. It gives larger touch targets on touch screens
(`pointer: coarse`), safe-area padding when the app is installed to the home screen, and `.cq-split` (one column on
phones, a list and its detail side by side from tablets up). Build each screen from the
[page components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#pagecomponents), and combine it with
[install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install) for a mobile app on the
same capabilities.
## <a name="test"></a>Testing a capability

Your tests call capabilities the way the channels do, with the checks, the validation and the audit, in a
transaction that is rolled back:
```php
$book = $this->call('create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => $authorId], $this->user(7));
$this->assertCapabilityFails('unauthenticated', 'create_book', ['title' => 'Tehanu'], 'guest');
$answer = $this->action('open_author_books', ['author_id' => 3])->describe();   // a web-only capability: what it answers
```
Run them with `php caligrafer.php test`: [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App).
A capability asks for what it uses in its constructor ([Dependency injection](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection)),
and can run later as a [background job](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) or on a
[schedule](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs).
## Reference

### `#[Capability(...)]`

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | (required) | snake_case, letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most 64 characters; unique in the application. How every channel calls it |
| `description` | `''` | one or two sentences: what it does and what it returns. Agents read it to choose the tool |
| `scope` | `''` | the scope a token needs, `resource:action` (`books:write`). `''`: any token |
| `level` | `0` | the minimum `permissions` of the user (signed in, or the owner of the token). `0`: anyone signed in |
| `readOnly` | `false` | it changes nothing: not audited when it succeeds; can be page data and a download; `readOnlyHint` for agents |
| `destructive` | `false` | it deletes or overwrites data: `destructiveHint`, agents ask the user first |
| `public` | `false` | anyone may call it, without signing in or a token |
| `mcp` | `true` | `false` keeps it out of MCP (a capability only a browser can use). REST still reaches it |
| `webOnly` | `false` | `true` (2.21.0): [`Route::action`](#webonly) reaches it, nothing else |
| `async` | `false` | `true` (2.23.0): a slow capability; [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#tasks) runs it in the background as a Track card: Task. Other channels call it as before |

`php caligrafer.php service <Folder>/<Name> [--scope <scope>] [--read-only]` writes the class in
`application/services/<Folder>/<Name>.php`, the name in snake_case (`CreateBook` -> `create_book`). Without
`--scope` it writes `scope: ''` (G76). There is no `--destructive`: write `destructive: true` yourself.

### The class

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `public $rules` | input => [validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation). **Only these inputs reach `handle()`**: an input with no rule is listed with `''` |
| `public $filters` | input => filters applied before validation (`trim`) |
| `public $descriptions` | input => what it is, for the schema agents and clients see |
| `handle(array $input, Context $context)` | does the work and returns data: an array, a model, a list of models, a value (models become arrays of their columns) |
| `__construct(...)` | what it uses, given by the [container](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection) |

A service does not render a view, redirect, print, or read the request or the session: the channel does that. A
web-only capability is the one exception, [below](#webonly).

`$this->capability($name, $input, $context)` (2.21.0) calls another capability as the same person, with its checks, its
validation and its audit, and throws its `ServiceError`.

### <a name="webonly"></a>Web-only capabilities

```php
#[Capability(name: 'open_author_books', description: 'Opens the books of an author.', readOnly: true, public: true, webOnly: true)]
```

For a request that belongs to the browser: a sign-in between two sites, a page that chooses where to go, a gate, a payment
page. A capability declared `webOnly: true` keeps its `public`, `scope` and `level` checks, its validation and its audit,
and may also return a `Caligrafy\Web` (`Web::view`, `Web::redirect`, `Web::json`, `Web::text`), read `session()` and
`request()`, sign people in, and change data on a `GET`. A JSON call to it needs the page's `X-CSRF-Token` or a token that grants `*`, signed in or not (2.21.1), and its route variables win over the query string (2.21.2). In exchange, **`Route::action` is the only way to it**: REST, MCP, the
JS client, `php caligrafer.php call`, `Route::page`, `Route::form` and a controller's `$this->call()` answer `not_found`, and it
is not listed in `GET /capabilities`, MCP or `php caligrafer.php capabilities`. A `service` command has no flag for it: add
`webOnly: true` to the attribute. Everything: [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webonly).

**From the rules to the input schema** (what MCP and `GET /capabilities` show):

| Rule | Schema |
| --- | --- |
| `required` | listed in `required` |
| `integer` / `numeric`, `float` / `boolean` | `"type": "integer"` / `"number"` / `"boolean"` (otherwise `"string"`) |
| `valid_email`, `valid_url`, `uuid`, `date` | `"format": "email"`, `"uri"`, `"uuid"`, `"date"` |
| `max_len,N`, `min_len,N`, `exact_len,N` | `maxLength`, `minLength` |
| `min_numeric,N`, `max_numeric,N` | `minimum`, `maximum` (`current_year` is this year) |
| `contains_list,a;b` | `"enum": ["a", "b"]` |
| `file` | `"description": "The URL or the path of a file"` (web pages and REST upload the file: [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#files)) |

### Refusals: `ServiceError`

| Throw | Code | Status | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ServiceError::invalid(['field' => 'message'])` | `invalid` | 422 | an input is wrong |
| `ServiceError::unauthenticated()` | `unauthenticated` | 401 | nobody is signed in |
| `ServiceError::forbidden()` | `forbidden` | 403 | this caller may not do it (beyond the scope and level checks) |
| `ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #12')` | `not_found` | 404 | the thing does not exist |
| `ServiceError::conflict('This book is already lent to Ana')` | `conflict` | 409 | it clashes with the current state |

`$e->kind`, `$e->fields`, `$e->status()`, `$e->toArray()` (`{"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}`).

### `Context`: who calls

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `$context->user` | the signed-in user, or the owner of the token (`null` otherwise) |
| `$context->token` | the token row (`id`, `name`, `scopes`, `user_id`...), or `null` |
| `$context->channel` | `web`, `rest`, `mcp` or `cli` |
| `$context->allows('books:write', 1)` | whether this caller has that scope and level |
| `$context->userId()`, `$context->level()` | the user's id, and `permissions` (0 without a user) |
| `$context->authenticated()` | anyone but a guest |
| `$context->actorType()`, `$context->actorId()` | who acts: `user`, `token`, `key`, `cli`, `guest`, or the system of a job or an event (`schedule`, `queue`, `webhook`), and its id. A capability only a webhook, the scheduler or the queue may run refuses every other `actorType()` |

**Scopes and levels** (`allows()`): the command line and the legacy key pass everything. A signed-in person needs
`permissions >= level` (no scopes). A token needs the scope (exact, `books:*` or `*`); when it has an owner
(`--user <id>`), the owner needs the level too. A token **without an owner** is limited by its scopes only: the level
does not apply to it, so give it destructive scopes with care (G53).

### Tokens

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `php caligrafer.php token create "<name>" --scopes a:read,b:write [--user <id>] [--expires <days>]` | creates it and prints it once (`cq_<id>_<40 hex>`); only its SHA-256 hash is kept, in `caligrafy_tokens` |
| `php caligrafer.php token list` | `#<id> active/revoked/expired <name> <scopes> [user <id>] last used <when>/never used` |
| `php caligrafer.php token revoke <id>` | `Token #2 revoked`; the number alone (`revoke #2` revokes nothing, G77) |

A revoked, expired or unknown token is a visitor: `401`. From PHP: `Caligrafy\Tokens::create($name, $scopes, $userId,
time() + 86400 * 90)` returns `['id', 'token']`. An application online has no shell: give signed-in people a page
that creates their token (G79).

### MCP over HTTP

+ `POST` only, one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request (no batches), answered in JSON: `initialize`, `ping`,
  `tools/list`, `tools/call`. A notification (no `id`) gets `202` and no body. `GET` and `DELETE` answer `405`.
+ Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05` (another request gets the first).
+ Personal access tokens only: without one, `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` and the
  JSON-RPC body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Unauthorized: send Authorization: Bearer
  <personal access token>"}}`, whatever the headers (2.19.1: before, a post with no token and no
  `Accept: application/json` was taken for a form and answered `403` `[ERROR 3000]`). The session is never used there.
+ A browser request from another site (`Origin` header) is refused with `403 Origin not allowed`. To allow a
  browser-based client, list its origin in `.env`: `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://inspector.example`.
+ A tool the token cannot see, or one that does not exist, answers `{"error": {"code": -32602, "message": "Unknown tool: create_book"}}`.

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `php caligrafer.php platform install` | the framework tables (tokens, audit, jobs, cache, migrations, notifications) |
| `php caligrafer.php capabilities [--json \| --markdown]` | the capabilities: a table, with the input schemas, or Markdown for your documentation |
| `php caligrafer.php call <name> ['{"key": "value"}' \| key=value ...] [--token <token>] [--guest]` | calls one, prints `{"data"}` or `{"error"}` (exit 1) |
| `php caligrafer.php client [<file>] [--prefix /capabilities]` | the JS client (default `public/js/capabilities.js`) |
| `php caligrafer.php mcp [--token <token>]` | MCP over stdio |
| `php caligrafer.php audit [--capability <name>] [--limit <n>]` | the latest calls, 50 by default |

All of them are on [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#service).
## Other ways

+ **A controller** [`Route::form`, `Route::page`, `Route::action`]: a controller you keep calls the capability as the
  signed-in person with `$this->call('create_book')`, the inputs being the posted fields and the route variables. New code
  does not need one: [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers) shows how to move it.
+ **A script** [`php caligrafer.php call`]: `Caligrafy\Capabilities::call('get_book', ['id' => 3], Caligrafy\Context::cli())`
  (with the checks and the audit), or `Caligrafy\Container::make(GetBook::class)->run(['id' => 3])` (validation only:
  no checks, no audit; it returns the model).
+ **The legacy API key** [tokens]: keys made with `generatekeys` and `generateapikey` all encrypt the same `APP_KEY`:
  each one gives full access, and none can be revoked without changing `APP_KEY`. They keep working for old programs
  (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` on REST, never on MCP). Once your programs use tokens, set `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` in
  `.env`; `doctor` reminds you while they are allowed. `Route::action` and controller routes accept JSON calls with a
  token that has the scope `*`. Never put a token or a key in a page or a Vue bundle: browser code uses the session.
## Common mistakes

+ **An input with no rule** (G52): it never reaches `handle()`. List it in `$rules`, with `''` when it has no rule.
+ **`service` without `--scope`** (G76): `scope: ''` lets any token call it.
+ **A write over the session without `X-CSRF-Token`** (G54): 403. Use the JS client, or send the `csrf` of `GET /capabilities`.
+ **A capability that is not read-only as page data** (G83): refused. Pages show read-only capabilities; forms use `Route::form`.
+ **`webOnly: true` on a feature agents or programs need** (G143): they get "There is no capability". Keep the work in a plain
  capability and let the web-only one call it with `$this->capability()`.
+ **Sending the legacy key to MCP** (G56): 401. MCP takes tokens only.
+ **Trusting the level with an application token** (G53): a token without `--user` passes any level. Create agent
  tokens with `--user <id>` when the level matters.
+ **Using `register_user` over REST or MCP** (G81): refused; sign-up is the sign-up page.
+ **Forgetting `php caligrafer.php client` after a change**: the Vue app calls the old functions.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute -->

A **capability** is a class of `application/services/` that extends `Caligrafy\Service` and carries the attribute
`#[Capability(...)]`. The attribute says what the capability is called, what it does, who may call it and how the
channels treat it. This page lists every option; each one has a page of its own. Since 2.1.0 (`webOnly` 2.21.0,
`async` 2.23.0).

**Since 2.26.0**: `cache: <seconds>` (with `readOnly: true` and `public: true`: a visitor's answer may be kept by shared caches, see [performance](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Performance-and-Deployment)); and an empty `scope` on a write capability means a token needs the scope named after the capability, or `*`.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability delete_book books:write destructive: only administrators (level 1)
```

Claude runs `php caligrafer.php service <Folder>/<Name> --scope <scope>` and writes the attribute: a `description`
written for an AI agent, the scope, and `readOnly`, `destructive`, `level` or `public` from what you asked.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists it with the scope (or `public`) and the flag you
expect (`read`, `writes`, `destroys`).
## By hand

`php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/DeleteBook --scope books:write` writes the class with its name in snake_case
(`DeleteBook` becomes `delete_book`). Complete the attribute:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'delete_book',
    description: 'Deletes a book of the catalog for good, with its loans and its tags. Returns the id of the deleted book.',
    scope: 'books:write',
    level: 1,
    destructive: true
)]
class DeleteBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');

    public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book to delete');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if (Book::where('id', $input['id'])->delete() === 0) {
            throw ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #' . $input['id']);
        }
        return array('deleted' => (int) $input['id']);
    }
}
```
## <a name="options"></a>Every option

The arguments of the attribute's constructor, in their order (`framework/core/Capability.php`):

| Option | Type, default | What it does | Learn more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string`, required | snake_case: a letter, then letters, digits and `_`, 64 characters at most; unique in the application. How REST, MCP, the JS client, the command line and the routes name it. Any other name throws `InvalidArgumentException` | [Calling a capability from code](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Call-a-Capability-from-Code) |
| `description` | `string`, `''` | one or two sentences: what it does and what it returns. Agents read it as the tool description | [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents) |
| `scope` | `string`, `''` | the token scope it needs, `resource:action` (`books:write`). `''`: any token | [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access) |
| `level` | `int`, `0` | the minimum value of the users' `permissions` column. `0`: anyone signed in | [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access#level) |
| `readOnly` | `bool`, `false` | it changes nothing: not audited when it succeeds, can be page data and a download, `readOnlyHint` for agents | [Read-only and destructive](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Read-Only-and-Destructive-Capabilities) |
| `destructive` | `bool`, `false` | it deletes or overwrites data: `destructiveHint`, agents ask the user first | [Read-only and destructive](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Read-Only-and-Destructive-Capabilities#destructive) |
| `public` | `bool`, `false` | anyone may call it, without signing in or a token | [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access#public) |
| `mcp` | `bool`, `true` | `false` keeps it out of the MCP tools (one only a browser can use, such as a push subscription). REST still reaches it | [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents#mcpfalse) |
| `webOnly` | `bool`, `false` | `true` (2.21.0): only `Route::action()` reaches it; it may read the session and sign people in | [Web-only capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities) |
| `async` | `bool`, `false` | `true` (2.23.0): a slow capability; Snap runs it in the background as a Track card: Task. Other channels call it as before | [Async capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Async-Capabilities) |

The class itself declares the inputs (`$rules`, `$filters`, `$descriptions`) and `handle()`:
[Capability inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Inputs). Its constructor gets what it
uses from the [container](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection).

`php caligrafer.php service <Folder>/<Name> [--scope <scope>] [--read-only]` writes `scope` and `readOnly`. There is no
flag for `destructive`, `level`, `public`, `mcp`, `webOnly` or `async`: write them in the attribute.
## <a name="registry"></a>How the attribute is found

`Caligrafy\Capabilities::all()` builds the registry once per request: it loads the files of `application/services/`
that mention `#[Capability]` (with the class map, 2.18.0) and the framework's own capabilities of `framework/services/`,
then keeps every class that extends `Service`, is not abstract and carries the attribute. Two classes that declare the
same name stop the registry with a `LogicException` naming both. A class outside `application/services/` (a package, a
test) is added with `Capabilities::register(MyService::class)`.

Since 2.26.1, with the class map, the registry is also kept in a file next to the class map (in the system's
temporary folder): a call by name (REST, MCP, the JS client, `Capabilities::call()`) reads it and loads only the file
of the capability it calls, instead of finding and reading every service on every request. It is out of date as soon
as the class map is (a file of `application/` added, removed or edited, found at once while you develop, within a
minute with `APP_ENV=production`) or a file of `framework/services/` changes. A name it does not have (a class
declared elsewhere, registered by hand) builds the registry as before; `CLASS_MAP=false` keeps no file.

Reference: [`Capability`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capability),
[`Capabilities::all()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-all),
[`Capabilities::register()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-register).
## Common mistakes

+ **`service` without `--scope`** (G76): it writes `scope: ''`, which any token may call. Give a scope, or write it in the
  attribute right away.
+ **`webOnly: true` on a feature agents or programs need** (G143): they get "There is no capability". Keep the work in a
  plain capability and let the web-only one call it with `$this->capability()`.
## Related pages

+ [Services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP): the whole chapter
+ [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability): the short tour
+ [Capability inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Inputs) · [Refusing a call](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Refusing-a-Call-ServiceError) · [The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context)
+ [API reference: services and capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Inputs -->

A capability declares its inputs with three arrays of its class: `$rules` (what is accepted), `$filters` (how it is
cleaned) and `$descriptions` (what each input is). The same three arrays validate every call, whatever the channel,
and become the **JSON Schema** that AI agents, the JS client and `GET /capabilities` see. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write: add a book (title up to 200 characters, published year from 1450 to this year, optional summary, an existing author)
```

Claude writes a rule for every input, a `trim` filter for the text ones and a description for each, written for an
agent ("The id of its author (list_authors)").

**Check** before you say OK:
+ every input `handle()` reads is in `$rules` (with `''` when it has no rule);
+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities --json` shows the schema you expect;
+ `php caligrafer.php call <name>` with a wrong value answers a message for that field.
## By hand

```php
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author.', scope: 'books:write')]
class CreateBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'title' => 'required|max_len,200',
        'published_year' => 'required|integer|min_numeric,1450|max_numeric,current_year',
        'summary' => 'max_len,2000',
        'author_id' => 'required|integer|exists,authors.id'
    );

    public $filters = array(
        'title' => 'trim',
        'summary' => 'trim'
    );

    public $descriptions = array(
        'title' => 'The title of the book',
        'published_year' => 'The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)',
        'summary' => 'Optional: one or two sentences about the book',
        'author_id' => 'The id of its author (list_authors)'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $id = Book::insert($input);
        return Book::with('author')->find($id);
    }
}
```

`php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dune` answers a message per field:
```json
{
    "error": {
        "code": "invalid",
        "message": "Some of the inputs are invalid",
        "fields": {
            "published_year": "The Published Year field is required",
            "author_id": "The Author Id field is required"
        }
    }
}
```
REST answers the same body with `422`, MCP as a tool result with `"isError": true`, a form goes back with
`errors('published_year')`.
## <a name="validate"></a>What happens to the inputs

`Service::validate()` runs before `handle()`, on every channel:

1. **Keep** only the inputs named in `$rules`. Any other key the caller sends is dropped: an input without a rule is
   listed with `''`.
2. **Files** (the `file` rule, 2.19.0): web pages and REST save the uploaded file and give the capability its public
   URL; MCP and the command line send a URL or a path, whose extension is checked. `required_file` (or
   `required|file`) with nothing sent is refused: "The Cover field needs a file".
3. **Numbers** (2.21.8): an input whose rule has `integer`, `numeric`, `float`, `min_numeric` or `max_numeric` never takes a
   list or `true`/`false`: "The Year field must be a number".
4. **Filter**, then **validate** with the [validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)
   (GUMP). `$filters` apply only to declared inputs.
5. Anything wrong throws `ServiceError::invalid([field => message])`. Otherwise `handle()` gets the clean inputs.

`$rules` with `unique` and `exists` read the database (`exists,authors.id`); `current_year` in `min_numeric` and
`max_numeric` is the year of today.
## <a name="schema"></a>From the rules to the JSON Schema

`Capabilities::schema('create_book')` (and `schemaFromRules($rules, $descriptions)`) gives an object schema with
`"additionalProperties": false`:

| Rule | Schema |
| --- | --- |
| `required` | listed in `required` |
| `integer` / `numeric`, `float` / `boolean` | `"type": "integer"` / `"number"` / `"boolean"` (otherwise `"string"`) |
| `valid_email`, `valid_url`, `uuid`, `date` | `"format": "email"`, `"uri"`, `"uuid"`, `"date"` |
| `max_len,N`, `min_len,N`, `exact_len,N` | `maxLength`, `minLength` (both for `exact_len`) |
| `min_numeric,N`, `max_numeric,N` | `minimum`, `maximum` (`current_year` is this year) |
| `contains_list,a;b` | `"enum": ["a", "b"]` |
| `file`, `required_file` | `"description": "The URL or the path of a file"` (`required_file` also in `required`) |
| `$descriptions[input]` | `"description"`, over the one above |

A string keeps only its `format` and lengths, a number only its `minimum` and `maximum`. A rule argument that is not a
number (`max_len` with nothing after it) is left out of the schema. The `create_book` above becomes:

```json
{"type": "object", "properties": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 200, "description": "The title of the book"},
    "published_year": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1450, "maximum": 2026, "description": "The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)"},
    "summary": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 2000, "description": "Optional: one or two sentences about the book"},
    "author_id": {"type": "integer", "description": "The id of its author (list_authors)"}},
 "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["title", "published_year", "author_id"]}
```

Reference: [`Service::validate()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#service-validate),
[`Capabilities::schema()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-schema),
[`Capabilities::schemaFromRules()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-schemafromrules),
[`Uploads`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#uploads).
## Common mistakes

+ **An input with no rule** (G52): it never reaches `handle()`. List it in `$rules`, with `''` when it has no rule.
+ **Forgetting `php caligrafer.php client` after changing the rules**: the Vue app's functions keep the old input types.

+ [Validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation): every rule and filter
+ [Declarative routes: file inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#files)
+ [The capability attribute](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute) · [Refusing a call](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Refusing-a-Call-ServiceError)
+ [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents): where agents read the schema

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/File-Uploads -->

# File uploads: the `file` rule

A capability declares a file input with the rule `file`, an optional allow-list of extensions and an optional maximum
size. Each channel then brings the file its own way, and `handle()` always gets a string: the file's public URL (web
pages, REST) or a URL or path (AI agents, the command line). Since 2.19.0; `required` with a file on every channel since
2.19.1.

```php
public $rules = array('cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg;webp|max_size,2mb');
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability set_cover books:write: sets the cover image of a book (PNG, JPG or WebP, 2 MB at most), from a form on the book's page
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the rule has `file`, an `extension` list and a `max_size`;
+ the form has `enctype='multipart/form-data'`;
+ a GIF, a 3 MB file and no file each come back with a message under the field.
## By hand

1. **A column for the file.** The table holds data: add it with a
   [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations):
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate make add_books_cover`, then in the file it names:

   ```sql
   -- add_books_cover
   ALTER TABLE books ADD COLUMN cover VARCHAR(255) NULL AFTER summary;
   ```

   Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate`.

2. **The capability.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/SetCover --scope books:write`,
   then make `application/services/Bookshelf/SetCover.php` read:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Database;
   use Caligrafy\Service;

   #[Capability(
       name: 'set_cover',
       description: 'Sets the cover image of a book, by its id. Returns the id and the URL of the cover.',
       scope: 'books:write'
   )]
   class SetCover extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array(
           'id' => 'required|integer|exists,books.id',
           'cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg;webp|max_size,2mb',
       );

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           Database::table('books')->where('id', $input['id'])->update(array('cover' => $input['cover']));
           return array('id' => (int) $input['id'], 'cover' => $input['cover']);
       }
   }
   ```

3. **The route and the form.** In `web.php`:

   ```php
       Route::form('/books/{id}/cover', 'set_cover', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Cover saved']);
   ```

   On the book's page:

   ```pug
   form(method='POST', action=$home . 'books/' . $book['id'] . '/cover', enctype='multipart/form-data')
     =csrf()
     .cq-field
       label(for='cover') Cover (PNG, JPG or WebP, 2 MB at most)
       input#cover(type='file', name='cover', accept='.png,.jpg,.webp')
       if errors('cover')
         p.cq-field-error= errors('cover')
     button.btn.btn-secondary(type='submit') Save the cover
   ```

4. **Try it.** Choose a PNG and click **Save the cover**: "Cover saved", and the `cover` column holds
   `http://localhost:8080/public/uploads/<24 random characters>.png`. A GIF answers "This type of file is not accepted:
   png, jpg, webp"; a 3 MB PNG "The file is too large (at most 2 MB)"; no file "The Cover field needs a file".
## <a name="rules"></a>The rules

| Rule | What it does |
|---|---|
| `file` | the input is a file |
| `extension,png;jpg` | the types allowed; without it, the default list of `uploadFile()` applies (images, documents, audio, video, `zip`, `json`). Scripts and markup (`php`, `phtml`, `phar`, `html`, `js`, `svg`...) are always refused |
| `max_size,2mb` | a number of bytes, or `kb`, `mb`, `gb` (`500kb`, `1.5mb`). PHP's own limits (`upload_max_filesize`, `post_max_size`) apply first |
| `required` with `file`, or `required_file` | the file is required on every channel: no file, URL or path answers "The &lt;Field&gt; field needs a file", and the input schema of MCP and `GET /capabilities` lists the field in `required` (2.19.1) |

The file rules are never given to the validation library: `Service::validate()` takes them out and
`Caligrafy\Uploads` applies them.
## <a name="channels"></a>What each channel sends

| Channel | What `handle()` gets |
|---|---|
| Web pages (`Route::form`, `Route::action`) and REST (`Route::capability`, `Route::capabilities`) | the file is taken from the request once the caller is allowed to call the capability, checked (one file, the allow-list, the size), saved in `public/uploads/` under a new random name (the name the browser sent is never used), and `handle()` gets its public **URL**. A text sent in that field is dropped. When the capability fails, the saved file is deleted |
| AI agents (MCP) and the command line | they cannot send a file: they send a URL or a path, whose extension is checked against the allow-list. Never open it without checking where it points |
## Reference

+ [`Caligrafy\Uploads`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#uploads)
+ The helpers [`uploadFile()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-uploadfile),
  [`isAllowedUpload()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-isallowedupload) and
  [`deleteFile()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-deletefile)
## Common mistakes

+ **A file form without `enctype='multipart/form-data'`**: no file arrives, and the form comes back with "The Cover
  field needs a file".
+ **`required_file` alone on 2.19.0** was ignored; since 2.19.1 it makes the file required on every channel.
+ **Opening the path an agent sent** without checking where it points: the command line and MCP send a string, not an
  uploaded file.

## Related pages

+ [Forms: `Route::form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Form)
+ [Validation](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)
+ [Migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations)
+ [Declarative routes, step 7](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#files)
