<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access -->

Three options of `#[Capability(...)]` say who may call a capability: `public`, `scope` and `level`. They are checked
once, in `Capabilities::call()`, for every channel: a page, a form, REST, the JS client, an agent over MCP, the command
line and the jobs all get the same answer. Since 2.1.0.

**Since 2.26.0** an empty `scope` on a write capability (not `readOnly`, not `public`) means a token needs the scope named after the capability (`create_book`) or `*`; `resource:*` does not cover it. Signed-in people and the command line are unchanged. `php caligrafer.php doctor` lists such capabilities; `TOKEN_DEFAULT_SCOPES=false` (deprecated) restores the old rule.
## With Claude

Say the scope and who may call it:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only public: the catalog, 20 per page
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability delete_book books:write destructive: only administrators (level 1)
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities` shows `public`, the scope, or `signed in` (no scope) in the second column;
+ `php caligrafer.php call <name> --guest` answers `unauthenticated` for a capability that is not public;
+ a token without the scope gets `403` over REST and does not see the tool in MCP `tools/list`.
## By hand

```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_books', description: 'Lists the books of the catalog, 20 per page.', readOnly: true, public: true)]
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book to the catalog and returns it.', scope: 'books:write')]
#[Capability(name: 'delete_book', description: 'Deletes a book for good. Returns its id.', scope: 'books:write', level: 1, destructive: true)]
```

(one attribute per class). Then try each caller:

```bash
php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dawn published_year=1987 author_id=2 --guest          # unauthenticated
php caligrafer.php token create "Reader" --scopes books:read
php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dawn published_year=1987 author_id=2 --token cq_...   # forbidden
```

The second call answers `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"This needs the scope books:write"}}`; with a `level`
the message ends with `and permission level 1`.
## <a name="order"></a>The checks, in order

`Capabilities::call()`:

1. **Find** it: no such name, or a `webOnly` capability reached by anything but `Route::action`, is `not_found`.
2. **`public: true`**: no check at all; anyone may call it, visitors included.
3. **Someone must act**: a guest (nobody signed in, no token) is `unauthenticated` (401).
4. **`$context->allows($scope, $level)`**, else `forbidden` (403).
5. Then the inputs are validated and `handle()` runs. A capability can still refuse more itself, with
   `ServiceError::forbidden()` ([Refusing a call](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Refusing-a-Call-ServiceError)).
## <a name="scope"></a>`scope`: what a token may do

A scope is `<resource>:<action>`: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` on each side (`books:read`,
`books:write`). The scopes a token was given cover a required scope when one of them is:

+ the same scope (`books:write`);
+ `<resource>:*` (`books:*` covers `books:read` and `books:write`);
+ `*` (everything).

`scope: ''` is met by **any** token. Scopes apply to tokens only: a signed-in person has every scope, and is checked by
the level.
## <a name="level"></a>`level`: how much a person may do

`level` is the minimum value of the users' `permissions` column (`Context::$levelAttribute`, `permissions` by default).
`0`, the default, means anyone signed in. `$context->level()` is the user's value, `0` without a user.

| Caller | What `allows($scope, $level)` checks |
| --- | --- |
| the command line, scripts and jobs (`Context::cli()`, `Context::system()`), the legacy API key | nothing: always allowed |
| a signed-in person | `permissions >= level` |
| a token with an owner (`token create ... --user 7`) | the scope, and the owner's `permissions >= level` |
| a token without an owner | the scope only: the level does not apply |
| a token whose owner was deleted (with authentication on) | refused |
| a guest | refused (only public capabilities) |
## <a name="public"></a>`public`: anyone

`public: true` skips the checks: a visitor's page, a REST call without a token and any MCP token reach it. Use it for
what anyone may read (the catalog), or for what a visitor must do before having an account. A public capability may still
look at `$context` and refuse: the framework's `register_user` is public but refuses every channel but web pages and the
command line (G81).
## <a name="lists"></a>What each caller sees

`Capabilities::available($context)` keeps the capabilities this caller may call (public, or allowed), web-only ones left
out. MCP `tools/list` and `GET /capabilities` show only those, so a token never sees a tool it may not call.

Reference: [`Context::allows()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#context-allows),
[`Tokens::allows()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#tokens-allows),
[`Capabilities::available()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-available).
## Common mistakes

+ **`service` without `--scope`** (G76): `scope: ''` lets any token call it.
+ **Trusting the level with an application token** (G53): a token without `--user` passes any level. Create agent tokens
  with `--user <id>` when the level matters.
+ **The legacy API key and tokens without an owner never manage users** (G85): the user capabilities need a real
  administrator, so give an agent that manages users a token of an administrator.
## Related pages

+ [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens) · [The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context)
+ [Authentication: users and levels](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication)
+ [The capability attribute](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Read-Only-and-Destructive-Capabilities -->

Two options of `#[Capability(...)]` say what a capability does to the data: `readOnly: true` (it changes nothing) and
`destructive: true` (it deletes or overwrites). They are promises the channels act on: where a capability may be used,
what is audited, and whether an agent or the assistant asks the person first. A capability with neither **writes**.
Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only public: the catalog, 20 per page
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability delete_book books:write destructive: only administrators (level 1)
```

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php capabilities` shows `read`, `writes` or `destroys` in the third column,
as you expect.
## By hand

`php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListBooks --scope books:read --read-only` writes `readOnly: true`. There is no flag
for `destructive`: add it to the attribute.

```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_books', description: 'Lists the books of the catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page.', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true)]
#[Capability(name: 'delete_book', description: 'Deletes a book of the catalog for good, with its loans and its tags. Returns the id of the deleted book.', scope: 'books:write', level: 1, destructive: true)]
```

(one attribute per class). Declare only what is true: `readOnly` on a capability that writes would let a page or a link
change data without a trace in the audit log.
## <a name="readonly"></a>What `readOnly: true` changes

| Where | A read-only capability | Any other |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The audit log | written only when it is refused | every call: success and refusal |
| `Route::page(..., ['data' => [...]])` | can be page data | refused: `LogicException` "changes data, and opening a page must not" |
| `Route::download` | can be downloaded | refused: `LogicException` "changes data, and opening a link must not" |
| REST with the session cookie | no CSRF token needed | needs `X-CSRF-Token` (403 without it) |
| REST `POST` | `200` | `201` |
| MCP | `"readOnlyHint": true` | `"readOnlyHint": false` |
| Snap | a card with nothing to ask runs at once; the assistant may call it to look things up | comes back as an Ask: Confirm card first |
## <a name="destructive"></a>What `destructive: true` changes

+ **MCP**: `"destructiveHint": true` on the tool (only when it is not also read-only), and the server's `initialize`
  instructions tell the agent: "Tools marked destructive delete or overwrite data: confirm with the user first."
+ **`php caligrafer.php capabilities`**: `destroys` instead of `writes`; `GET /capabilities` and `--json` give
  `"destructive": true`.
+ **The JS client**: the function's comment says `destructive`.
+ **Snap**: the card is a `destroy` risk (a `write` one without it); like every change, it runs only once the person has
  confirmed its Ask: Confirm card.

Nothing else differs: the checks, the validation and the audit are those of every capability that writes.
## <a name="snap"></a>Snap and the assistant

In [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant), nothing that changes data runs
from a card until the person confirms it: a capability that is not read-only answers an **Ask: Confirm** card with a
one-time token bound to that person, that capability and those inputs, for 10 minutes. The confirmed change is written to
the audit log as `snap_confirm`. The assistant (Claude) may call only the read-only capabilities the person may call, to
look things up; a change it proposes comes back as its Confirm card. A slow read-only capability declared
[`async: true`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Async-Capabilities) is proposed as a task instead of
being run in the turn.

Reference: [`Capabilities::call()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-call),
[`Mcp\Server::tools()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-server-tools),
[`Snap\Consent`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-consent).
## Common mistakes

+ **A capability that is not read-only as page data** (G83): refused. Pages show read-only capabilities; forms use
  `Route::form`.
## Related pages

+ [The capability attribute](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute) · [The audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Audit-Log)
+ [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents) · [REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/REST-API)
+ [Declarative routes: downloads](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#download)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities -->

A **web-only capability** is a capability declared `webOnly: true`. It is for a request that belongs to the browser: a
sign-in between two sites, a page that chooses between a view and a redirect, a gate, a page that creates a payment.
It keeps everything a capability has (its checks, its validation, its audit) and may do what a plain capability never
does: answer with a view or a redirect, read the session, sign people in. The price: `Route::action` is the only way to
it. Since 2.21.0.

This page is about the capability. The route that serves it, its options and how it answers are on
[`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability open_author_books web-only public: open the books of an author, the book itself when there is only one
```

Claude writes the capability with `webOnly: true`, keeps the shared work in plain capabilities that it calls with
`$this->capability()`, and adds the `Route::action` line to `web.php`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities` does not list it (web-only capabilities are left out);
+ the plain capabilities it calls are listed, so agents and programs can still do the work;
+ a test calls it with `$this->action()`.
## By hand

`php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks` writes the class; the command has no flag for web-only, so add
`webOnly: true` to the attribute:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\Web;

#[Capability(
    name: 'open_author_books',
    description: 'Opens the books of an author: the book itself when there is one, otherwise the list.',
    readOnly: true,
    public: true,
    webOnly: true
)]
class OpenAuthorBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'required|integer');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
        if ($books['total'] == 1) {
            return Web::redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
        }
        return Web::view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
    }
}
```

and serve it in `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

```php
Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books', ['back' => '/books']);
```
## <a name="may"></a>What it may do

The rule of the framework still holds: **only capabilities touch models**. A web-only capability is a capability; what
sets it apart is what it may do besides:

| A plain capability | A web-only capability |
|---|---|
| returns data, or refuses | may also return a view, a redirect, JSON or text (`Caligrafy\Web`) |
| never reads the session or the request: `$context` says who calls | may read `session()`, `request()`, `$_SERVER`, `$_COOKIE` |
| never signs anyone in | may sign people in and out |
| on a page, only `readOnly` | a `GET` may change data |
| reached by REST, MCP, the JS client, the command line, `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `$this->call()` | reached by **`Route::action` only** |

What it answers:

| It returns | The browser gets |
|---|---|
| `Web::view('Bookshelf/book', $data, $status = 200)` | a Pug view, with `$authorized` and `$user` as on `Route::page` |
| `Web::redirect('/books', $status = 302)` | a redirect: a path of this site or a full `http(s)` address |
| `Web::json($data, $status = 200)` | JSON, the data as it is |
| `Web::text($body, $status = 200)` | the text as it is |
| any of them `->header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` | one more response header |
| plain data | JSON |
## <a name="elsewhere"></a>Everywhere else: "There is no capability"

`Capabilities::call()` answers `not_found` `There is no capability '<name>'` to any context that does not come from
`Route::action` (`$context->viaAction`). So REST, MCP, the JS client, `php caligrafer.php call`, `Route::page`,
`Route::form`, `Route::download` and a controller's `$this->call()` cannot reach it, and it is left out of
`GET /capabilities`, MCP `tools/list`, `php caligrafer.php capabilities` and the generated JS client.

Keep the work several channels share in plain capabilities, and call them from the web-only one, as the same person:

```php
$books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => 2), $context);   // its checks, validation and audit
```
## <a name="signin"></a>Signing someone in

+ For a page that leaves or reloads: `Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::signIn($user, null, 'partner')`: a new session id, a new CSRF
  token and how it signed in (the third argument, 2.21.3, read by `AuthRoutes::signedInBy()`).
+ For a page that stays open and keeps sending JSON: `session_regenerate_id(true); Auth::authorize($user);
  AuthRoutes::rememberSignIn('face');`: the page keeps its token.
+ `$context` was built before the sign-in and does not change: to call a capability as the person just signed in, build a
  new one with `Context::fromRequest(request(), 'web')`.

A whole example, a sign-in through another site, is on
[Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#betweensites).
## <a name="test"></a>Testing

`$this->action('open_author_books', ['author_id' => 3], $user)` calls it as `Route::action` does and returns what it
answered; `->describe()` gives `type`, `target`, `data`, `status` and `headers`. `$this->call()` answers `not_found`, as
every other channel does ([Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App#helpers)).

Reference: [`Caligrafy\Web`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#web),
[`Caligrafy\Action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#action),
[`AuthRoutes::signIn()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-signin).
## Common mistakes

+ **`webOnly: true` on a feature agents or programs need** (G143): they get "There is no capability". Keep the work in a
  plain capability and let the web-only one call it with `$this->capability()`.
+ **Reading the session in a plain capability** (G52): only a web-only capability may; the others read `$context`.
+ **Snap's own `snap_ask` and `snap_run` in a test** (G158): they are web-only, so call them with `$this->action()`.
## Related pages

+ [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action): the route, its options, CSRF and JSON
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webonly)
+ [The capability attribute](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute) · [The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Async-Capabilities -->

A capability declared `async: true` is **slow**: a report, a long count, an AI call. In
[Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) it never runs in the request:
the person gets a **Track card: Task** at once, a job of the [queue](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
runs it as that person, and they are notified when it ends. Every other channel (pages, REST, MCP, the command line)
still calls it directly, as before. Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability reading_report books:read read-only async: the books read this year by every reader, by month
```

Claude writes the capability with `async: true` and makes sure a worker runs the queue (a job on `queue_work` in
`application/config/schedule.php`).

**Check** before you say OK:
+ in Snap, asking for it shows a Task card that goes from *Waiting to start* to *Working on it*, then its result;
+ `php caligrafer.php queue work --once` runs the waiting `snap_task_run` job.
## By hand

1. **The tables.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install` creates the queue's `caligrafy_jobs`
   and Snap's tables (the deploy step does too).
2. **Declare it.**
    ```php
    #[Capability(name: 'reading_report', description: '...', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true, async: true)]
    ```
    Or leave the attribute as it is and make it async for Snap only, with the hint `async` in `application/config/snap.php`;
    `working` gives the lines the card shows, in turn, while it runs:
    ```php
    return [
        'cards' => [
            'reading_report' => ['async' => true, 'working' => ['Counting the books…']],
        ],
    ];
    ```
3. **A worker.** Something must run the queue: a job on `queue_work` in `application/config/schedule.php`
   (`array('name' => 'queue', 'capability' => 'queue_work', 'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 55)`, which Caligrafy Cloud and
   `server start` run), or `php caligrafer.php queue work` on your own server. See
   [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs).
## <a name="run"></a>How a task runs

1. A read starts as a task at once; a change starts after the person confirms its Ask: Confirm card. Only a signed-in
   person can start one (a visitor gets `unauthenticated`).
2. `Snap\Tasks::start()` writes a row of `caligrafy_snap_tasks` (the person, the capability, the inputs, `queued`) and
   pushes the job `snap_task_run` to the queue, with 3 attempts and a 120 second timeout.
3. The worker runs the capability with `Capabilities::call()` **as the person who asked**: their user on the `web`
   channel, so their permissions, not the queue's full access. Its checks, validation and audit are those of any call.
4. It ends in one of three states, keeps the card it ended with, and notifies the person on every channel they turned on
   ([Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)):

| Status | Label | When | The card it ends with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | Waiting to start | pushed, or put back for the queue's next attempt after an error | |
| `running` | Working on it | the worker started it | |
| `done` | Done | it answered | the Show card of the result |
| `needs_input` | Needs your answer | it refused an input (`invalid`) | the Ask card of what it refused; answering it starts a new task |
| `failed` | Could not finish | it refused (`forbidden`, `unauthenticated`, `not_found`, `conflict`), the person no longer exists, or the queue's retries ran out | a notice |

The Track card shows where it is, live, with its steps (Asked, Started, then how it ended); Home shows it in progress,
then just done. A person sees only their own tasks.

Reference: [`Snap\Tasks`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-tasks),
[`Snap\Tasks::async()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-tasks-async),
[`Queue::push()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#queue-push).
## <a name="channels"></a>On the other channels

`async` changes nothing outside Snap: REST, MCP, the JS client, `Route::page`, `Route::form` and
`php caligrafer.php call` run it in the request, as any capability. To run any capability later from your own code,
push it to the queue yourself: `Queue::push('build_report', ['month' => '2026-11'])`
([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)).
## Related pages

+ [Snap Cards and the assistant: work in the background](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#tasks)
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) · [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)
+ [The capability attribute](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Refusing-a-Call-ServiceError -->

A capability refuses a call by throwing a `Caligrafy\ServiceError`. It never prints an error, redirects or picks an
HTTP status itself: each channel turns the same refusal into its own form, a status and a JSON error for REST, a tool
error for an agent, the errors of a form for a page. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

Say when the capability must refuse:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability lend_book loans:write: lend a book to a reader; refuse when the book is already out
```

Claude throws `ServiceError::notFound()` for a book that does not exist and `ServiceError::conflict()` when it is lent.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php call <name> ...` with the case that must be refused prints
`{"error": {"code": ...}}` with the code you expect, and exits with 1.
## By hand

```php
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
{
    $book = Book::find($input['book_id']);
    if (!$book) {
        throw ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #' . $input['book_id']);
    }
    if (Loan::where('book_id', $input['book_id'])->whereNull('returned_at')->exists()) {
        throw ServiceError::conflict('This book is already lent');
    }
    // ...
}
```

The invalid inputs of `$rules` are refused before `handle()` runs, with a message per field: you throw `invalid` only
for what the rules cannot say.

```php
throw ServiceError::invalid(['due_at' => 'The due date must be after today']);
```
## <a name="kinds"></a>The five kinds

| Throw | Code | Status | Default message | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ServiceError::invalid(['field' => 'message'], $message)` | `invalid` | 422 | Some of the inputs are invalid | an input is wrong |
| `ServiceError::unauthenticated($message)` | `unauthenticated` | 401 | Sign in or send a personal access token | nobody is signed in |
| `ServiceError::forbidden($message)` | `forbidden` | 403 | You are not allowed to do this | this caller may not do it |
| `ServiceError::notFound($message)` | `not_found` | 404 | Not found | the thing does not exist |
| `ServiceError::conflict($message)` | `conflict` | 409 | (a message is required) | it clashes with the current state |

`new ServiceError($kind, $message = '', $fields = [])` does the same; any other kind throws `InvalidArgumentException`.
On the error: `$e->kind`, `$e->fields`, `$e->getMessage()`, `$e->status()` and `$e->toArray()`, which is
`{"error": {"code": "invalid", "message": "...", "fields": {...}}}` (`fields` only when there are some).

The framework throws the same errors itself: `not_found` for an unknown capability, `unauthenticated` and `forbidden`
("This needs the scope books:write") from the [access checks](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access),
`invalid` from the [input rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Inputs).
## <a name="channels"></a>What each channel makes of it

| Channel | What the caller gets |
| --- | --- |
| REST (`Route::capability`, `Route::capabilities`) | the status of the kind and `$e->toArray()` as JSON; `401` also sends `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` |
| MCP | a tool result with `"isError": true` and `$e->toArray()` as its text, so the agent can read the reason and correct itself |
| `php caligrafer.php call` | `$e->toArray()` as JSON, exit code `1` |
| The JS client | a `CapabilityError` with `status`, `code`, `message` and `fields` |
| `Route::form`, `Route::action` (a browser) | `invalid` or `conflict`: back, with `errors()`, `old()`, `flash('error')`; `unauthenticated`: the sign-in page; `forbidden`: `403` `[ERROR 1006]`; `not_found` or anything else: `404` `[ERROR 1005]` |
| `Route::form`, `Route::action` (a JSON request) | the status of the kind and the REST error |
| `Route::page` data | a visitor goes to sign in (with the authentication module), otherwise `403` or `404`; with `'notFound' => 'Folder/view'` that view, its `$message` the refusal |
| Snap | an Ask card for `invalid` (the fields to fix), a notice for the others |

Every refusal is written to the [audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Audit-Log), its outcome
the code and its detail the message. Any other exception is written with the outcome `error` and the exception's class,
then thrown on: it is a bug, not a refusal.

Reference: [`ServiceError`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#serviceerror),
[`Capabilities::call()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-call).
## Related pages

+ [Declarative routes: forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form): `errors()`, `old()` and `flash()` in the view
+ [REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/REST-API) · [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents) · [The JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-JS-Client)
+ [The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context): who calls, to decide what to refuse


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context -->

Every capability gets a `Caligrafy\Context` as the second argument of `handle()`. It says **who calls, through which
channel, with which rights**: a signed-in person, a token, the command line, a job or a visitor. The channels build it
(a page, REST, MCP, the command line); a capability reads it instead of the request, the session or the headers, so the
same code works for every caller. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

Say what depends on the caller:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability my_loans loans:read read-only: the loans of the person who asks, newest first
```

Claude reads `$context->userId()` in `handle()`, and refuses with `ServiceError::unauthenticated()` when there is none.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php call my_loans --guest` is refused, and two people each see only their own
rows.
## By hand

```php
#[Capability(name: 'my_loans', description: 'Lists the loans of the person who asks, newest first.', scope: 'loans:read', readOnly: true)]
class MyLoans extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if (!$context->userId()) {
            throw ServiceError::unauthenticated();
        }
        return Loan::where('user_id', $context->userId())->latest()->get();
    }
}
```

A capability only a job may run (it works with full access) refuses everyone else by the actor type:

```php
if (!in_array($context->actorType(), array('queue', 'cli'), true)) {
    throw ServiceError::forbidden();
}
```
## <a name="members"></a>What it holds

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `$context->channel` | `web`, `rest`, `mcp` or `cli` |
| `$context->user` | the user model: signed in, or the owner of the token (`null` otherwise) |
| `$context->token` | the token row (`id`, `name`, `scopes`, `user_id`...), or `null` |
| `$context->viaAction` | `true` when the call comes from `Route::action` (2.21.0): the only way to a [web-only capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities) |
| `$context->authenticated()` | anyone but a guest |
| `$context->allows('books:write', 1)` | whether this caller has that scope and level ([Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access)) |
| `$context->userId()` | the user's id, signed in or owner of the token |
| `$context->level()` | the user's `permissions` column (`Context::$levelAttribute`), `0` without a user |
| `$context->actorType()` | `user`, `token`, `key`, `cli`, `guest`, or the system of a job or an event (`schedule`, `queue`, `webhook`), as written to the audit log |
| `$context->actorId()` | the token id or the user id as a string, or the job's name; `null` for the command line, the legacy key and guests |
## <a name="who"></a>Who the channels say calls

| Caller | How the context is made | Rights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a request with `Authorization: Bearer cq_...` | `Context::fromRequest($request, $channel)`: the token, and its owner when it has one and authentication is on | the token's scopes (an unknown, revoked or expired token is a guest) |
| a request with the legacy API key | `fromRequest`: a full-access context | everything (actor `key`) |
| a signed-in person (the session) | `fromRequest`: the user | their level |
| nobody | `Context::guest($channel)` | public capabilities only |
| the command line and scripts | `Context::cli()` | everything (actor `cli`) |
| `php caligrafer.php mcp` without a token | `Context::local('mcp')` | everything (actor `cli`) |
| a scheduled job or another system task | `Context::system('schedule', $jobName)` | everything; the audit log records the type and the name |
| a personal access token in code | `Context::forToken($tokenRow, $channel)` | the token's scopes |

`fromRequest()` looks in that order: a token, then the legacy key, then the session, else a guest. The context is made
once, before the capability runs: when a [web-only capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities#signin)
signs someone in, it builds a new one with `Context::fromRequest(request(), 'web')` to call as that person.

Reference: [`Caligrafy\Context`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#context).
## Common mistakes

+ **Reading the session or the request in a capability** (G52): the channel does that, and `$context` says who calls. Only a
  web-only capability may.
+ **A job capability that anyone may call**: it runs with full access, so check `actorType()`
  ([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)).
+ **Trusting the level with an application token** (G53): a token without an owner passes any level.
## Related pages

+ [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access) · [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens)
+ [Calling a capability from code](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Call-a-Capability-from-Code)
+ [The audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Audit-Log)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens -->

A program or an AI agent proves who it is with a **personal access token**: `cq_<id>_<40 hexadecimal characters>`,
sent as `Authorization: Bearer cq_...`. A token has a name, **scopes** (what it may do), and optionally an owner (the
user it acts for) and an expiry. It is shown once, only its SHA-256 hash is kept, and it can be revoked on its own.
REST, MCP, the JS client outside the browser and `php caligrafer.php call --token` all take it. Since 2.1.0.

**Since 2.26.0** a capability's name is a valid scope (`php caligrafer.php token create ci --scopes create_book`): a write capability declared without a `scope` needs it, or `*`.
## With Claude

```text
Create a token for my Claude Code on this laptop that can read and write books, for 90 days
```

Claude runs `php caligrafer.php token create` with the scopes, shows the token once, and never writes it in a file.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php token list` shows it `active` with the scopes you asked for.
## By hand

1. **The framework tables.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install` creates
   `caligrafy_tokens` (and the other framework tables; safe to run again).
2. **Create it.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "Bookshelf agent" --scopes books:read,books:write
    ```
    ```text
     Token #1 "Bookshelf agent" created with books:read books:write

     cq_1_<40 hexadecimal characters>

     It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
    ```
3. **Use it.**
    ```bash
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_1_..." http://localhost:8080/api/books
    ```
4. **List and revoke.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token list
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token revoke 1
    ```
    ```text
     #1    active   Bookshelf agent                books:read books:write  never used
    ```
## <a name="command"></a>The `token` command

```text
 php caligrafer.php token create <name> --scopes <a:read,b:write | *> [--user <id>] [--expires <days>]
 php caligrafer.php token list
 php caligrafer.php token revoke <id>
```

+ `--scopes` (required): `resource:action` values separated by commas; `books:*` for every action on books; `*` for everything.
+ `--user <id>`: the token acts for that user, so a capability's `level` applies to them.
+ `--expires <days>`: the token stops working after that many days.
+ `token list` shows `#<id>`, `active`, `revoked` or `expired`, the name, the scopes, the owner and the last use, never the
  secret. `token revoke` takes the number alone and stops the token at once.
## <a name="scopes"></a>Scopes

A scope is `<resource>:<action>` in lowercase (`books:read`, `loans:write`). A capability declares the one it needs with
`scope: 'books:write'`; a token reaches it when it has that scope, `books:*`, or `*`. A capability with `scope: ''` is
reached by any token. A token with an owner also needs the owner's level; a token **without** an owner is limited by its
scopes only. All the rules: [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access).

A revoked, expired or unknown token is a visitor: `401` on REST and MCP. A token whose owner was deleted is refused.
## <a name="php"></a>From PHP

```php
use Caligrafy\Tokens;

$created = Tokens::create('Sam\'s agent', ['books:read', 'books:write'], $userId, time() + 86400 * 90);
// ['id' => 3, 'token' => 'cq_3_...']: the token is never shown again

Tokens::revoke(3);       // true when a token was revoked
Tokens::all();           // the rows, newest first, without their secret
```

`Tokens::verify('cq_...')` returns the token row (its scopes as a list) and records its use, or `null`. The expiry is a
Unix time (or a local `'Y-m-d H:i:s'`, stored as given); a Unix time is stored so that the token never stops early when
the clocks fall back.
## <a name="online"></a>Tokens for an application online

An application on Caligrafy Cloud or your own server has no shell for `token create`. Give signed-in people a page that
creates their own token: a capability that calls `Tokens::create($name, $scopes, $context->user->id, $expiresAt)`, refuses
when `$context->token !== null` (a token must not create tokens), and a page that shows the token once with the
`claude mcp add` line.

Reference: [`Caligrafy\Tokens`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#tokens),
[`Tokens::create()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#tokens-create).
## Common mistakes

+ **`token revoke #2`** (G77): it reads `#2` as 0 and revokes nothing. Use `token revoke 2`.
+ **No page to create tokens online** (G79): agents cannot connect to a deployed application without one.
+ **An expiry as a date string near a clock change** (G91): give it as a Unix time (`time() + 86400 * 90`).
+ **Trusting the level with an application token** (G53): create agent tokens with `--user <id>` when the level matters.
+ **A token or a key in a page or a Vue bundle**: browser code uses the session; tokens are for programs and agents.
## Related pages

+ [MCP for AI agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents) · [REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/REST-API)
+ [Authentication: users, tokens and agents](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#agents)
+ [Caligrafer: `token`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#token)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Audit-Log -->

The **audit log** keeps one row per capability call that changes data, and per refused call: when, through which
channel, who (a person, a token, the command line, a job), which capability and the outcome. Inputs are never stored.
It is written by `Capabilities::call()`, so every channel is in it: pages, forms, REST, the JS client, MCP, the command
line, the queue and the scheduler. Since 2.1.0.
## By hand

1. **The table.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install` creates `caligrafy_audit`. Without it
   nothing is written and nothing fails.
2. **Read it.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit --capability create_book --limit 5
    ```
    ```text
     2026-11-07 23:18:39  mcp   token  1            create_book                  invalid  Some of the inputs are invalid
     2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  1            create_book                  invalid  Some of the inputs are invalid
     2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  1            create_book                  ok
     2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  token  2            create_book                  forbidden  This needs the scope books:write
     2026-11-07 23:18:25  rest  guest  -            create_book                  unauthenticated  Sign in or send a personal access token
    ```
    `audit` alone shows the latest 50 calls of every capability.
## <a name="what"></a>What is written

| A call | Written |
| --- | --- |
| succeeds, and the capability is not `readOnly` | yes, outcome `ok` |
| succeeds, and the capability is `readOnly` | no |
| is refused with a `ServiceError` | yes, outcome its code (`invalid`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`) and its message |
| throws any other exception | yes, outcome `error`, detail the exception's class |

The columns of `caligrafy_audit`:

| Column | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `occurred_at` | when (PHP's clock, `SERVER_TIMEZONE`) |
| `actor_type` | `user`, `token`, `key` (the legacy API key), `cli`, `guest`, or the system of a job or an event (`schedule`, `queue`, `webhook`) |
| `actor_id` | the token id or the user id, or the job's name; empty for the command line, the legacy key and guests |
| `channel` | `web`, `rest`, `mcp` or `cli` |
| `capability` | its name |
| `outcome` | `ok` or the refusal's code, or `error` |
| `detail` | a short note (the refusal's message), 500 characters at most |

A change confirmed in [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) is also
written as `snap_confirm`, its detail what was confirmed.
## <a name="php"></a>From PHP

```php
use Caligrafy\Audit;

$rows = Audit::latest(200, 'delete_book');   // newest first, 1 to 1000 rows; the capability is optional
```

`Audit::record($context, $capability, $outcome, $detail)` writes a row yourself (it returns `false` instead of failing
when the table is missing). Show the log to administrators with a read-only capability of `level: 1` that returns
`Audit::latest()`.

Reference: [`Caligrafy\Audit`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#audit),
[`Audit::latest()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#audit-latest).
## Common mistakes

+ **Looking for the successful reads**: a read-only capability is written only when it is refused.
+ **The audit time and the `created_at` of rows differ by hours** (G65): before 2.3.0 the audit used PHP's clock and the
  `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` columns MySQL's. Since 2.3.0 `Database::connect()` sets MySQL's session time zone to PHP's
  (`DB_TIMEZONE=server` keeps MySQL's); rows written before the upgrade keep their old times.
## Related pages

+ [Read-only and destructive capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Read-Only-and-Destructive-Capabilities)
+ [The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context): the actor types
+ [Caligrafer: `audit`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#audit)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Call-a-Capability-from-Code -->

The channels call capabilities for you: a page, a form, REST, MCP. Sometimes your own code calls one: a script, a
capability that builds on another, a controller you kept, a job, a test. This page shows each way, and what each one
checks. Since 2.1.0 (`$this->capability()` 2.21.0).
## <a name="ways"></a>The ways, side by side

| From | Call | Who it runs as | Checks, validation, audit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a terminal | `php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3` | full access (`--token`: a token, `--guest`: a visitor) | all three |
| any PHP code | `Capabilities::call('get_book', ['id' => 3], $context)` | the context you give | all three |
| a capability | `$this->capability('list_books', $input, $context)` | the same person | all three |
| a controller | `$this->call('create_book')` | the signed-in person (`Context::fromRequest($request, 'web')`) | all three |
| later, in the background | `Queue::push('send_loan_receipt', ['loan_id' => $id])` | the queue's system context | all three, when the worker runs it |
| a test | `$this->call('create_book', $input, $this->user(7))` | the user you give, or `'guest'` | all three, rolled back after the test |
| PHP, without the checks | `Container::make(GetBook::class)->run(['id' => 3])` | the command line, unless you pass a context | validation only: no access check, no audit |
## <a name="cli"></a>From the command line

```bash
php caligrafer.php call list_books
php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3
php caligrafer.php call create_book '{"title": "Dawn", "published_year": 1987, "author_id": 2}'
php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dawn published_year=1987 author_id=2 --guest          # as a visitor who is not signed in
php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dawn published_year=1987 author_id=2 --token cq_...   # as a token (or CALIGRAFY_TOKEN=cq_...)
```

It prints the same JSON as REST: `{"data": ...}` with exit code `0`, or `{"error": {...}}` with exit code `1`. Without
`--token` or `--guest` it has full access, like any script you run (channel `cli` in the audit log).
`php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists what there is to call.
## <a name="php"></a>From PHP: `Capabilities::call()`

```php
use Caligrafy\Capabilities;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

try {
    $book = Capabilities::call('get_book', ['id' => 3], Context::cli());
} catch (ServiceError $e) {
    echo json_encode($e->toArray());
}
```

`Capabilities::call($name, $input, $context, $uploads = null)` does what every channel does, in order: finds the
capability, checks the context, keeps, filters and validates the inputs, runs `handle()`, writes the audit log, and
returns plain data (models become arrays of their columns). Extra input keys are ignored. Choose the context for who
acts ([The context](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Context)): `Context::cli()` for full access,
`Context::system('schedule', 'nightly-report')` for work the system does on its own, `Context::forToken($row)` or
`Context::guest()` to act as a token or a visitor.
## <a name="capability"></a>From another capability: `$this->capability()`

```php
public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
{
    $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
    // ...
}
```

It runs the other capability **as the same person**, with its checks, its validation and its audit, and throws its
`ServiceError`. This is how a [web-only capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities)
reuses the work of plain ones.
## <a name="controller"></a>From a controller you kept: `$this->call()`

```php
try { $book = $this->call('create_book'); redirect('/books/' . $book['id']); }
catch (ServiceError $e) { return view('Books/form', ['errors' => $e->fields]); }
```

Without inputs it sends the route variables and the request's parameters (the parameters win on the same name). It runs
as the signed-in person, on the `web` channel. New code does not need a controller:
[Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers) shows how to move one to a declared route.
## <a name="run"></a>Without the checks: `Service::run()`

```php
use Caligrafy\Container;

$book = Container::make(GetBook::class)->run(['id' => 3]);
```

`run($input, $context = null)` validates the inputs and calls `handle()`, with `Context::cli()` when you give none. It
checks no access and writes no audit, and it returns what `handle()` returns (a model stays a model). `Container::make()`
builds the class with what its constructor asks for
([Dependency injection](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection)).

Reference: [`Capabilities::call()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities-call),
[`Service::run()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#service-run),
[`Controller::call()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Controller#controller-call),
[`Container::make()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#container-make).
## Common mistakes

+ **A web-only capability from code** (G143): `Capabilities::call()`, `$this->call()` and `call` answer `not_found`; only
  `Route::action` reaches it.
+ **A job capability anyone may call**: the queue runs it with full access, so it checks `$context->actorType()`
  ([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)).
## Related pages

+ [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App): `$this->call()`, `$this->action()`, `assertCapabilityFails()`
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) · [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)
+ [Caligrafer: `call`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#call)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs -->

A **scheduled job** runs one of your capabilities on a timer, with no page open: send a reminder every morning, clean
old rows every night, check prices every minute. You declare the jobs in one file, `application/config/schedule.php`;
Caligrafy runs them on your computer while you develop and on Caligrafy Cloud in production. Since 2.14.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability Every night at 3:00 New York time, delete the loans returned more than a year ago
```

Claude writes the capability in `application/services/`, adds the job to `application/config/schedule.php`, then runs
`php caligrafer.php schedule list` and `php caligrafer.php schedule run <job>`.

**Check**

+ The capability finds its rows itself: a job has nobody signed in, so it never reads `$context->userId()`.
+ `php caligrafer.php schedule list` shows the job with the rhythm you asked for.
+ `php caligrafer.php schedule history <job>` shows a run with `ok`.
## <a name="example"></a>By hand: clear the old loans every night

**Bookshelf** keeps every loan forever. This job deletes the loans returned more than a year ago, every night at 3:00
in New York. Start from the sign-in pages of [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication)
(the `users` table and the Bookshelf catalog). The commands run in the Docker server of the Quickstart; without Docker,
drop `docker compose exec dev-box`.

**1. The loans table.** It is the one of the course's
[lesson 13](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/13-Capstone-Loans). If you do not have it, write
`application/models/Loans/create_db.sql`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS loans (
    id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    book_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    borrower VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    due_on DATE NOT NULL,
    returned_at DATETIME NULL,
    created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    KEY idx_loans_book_id (book_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_loans_book_id FOREIGN KEY (book_id) REFERENCES books (id)
        ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;
```

and run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Loans/create_db.sql`.

**2. The capability.** Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Loans/ClearReturnedLoans --scope loans:write`, then replace
`application/services/Loans/ClearReturnedLoans.php` with:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;

#[Capability(
    name: 'clear_returned_loans',
    description: 'Deletes the loans returned more than a number of days ago (365 by default). Returns how many were deleted.',
    scope: 'loans:write',
    level: 1,
    destructive: true
)]
class ClearReturnedLoans extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('days' => 'integer|min_numeric,1|max_numeric,3650');
    public $descriptions = array('days' => 'Loans returned more than this many days ago are deleted (365 by default)');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $before = date('Y-m-d H:i:s', time() - (int) ($input['days'] ?? 365) * 86400);
        // delete() returns how many rows it deleted
        $deleted = Loan::whereNotNull('returned_at')->where('returned_at', '<', $before)->delete();
        return array('deleted' => $deleted);
    }
}
```

It is an ordinary capability: an administrator (`level: 1`) can also call it from a page, the REST API or an agent.

**3. The schedule.** Write `application/config/schedule.php`:

```php
<?php
return array(
    array('name' => 'clear-returned-loans', 'capability' => 'clear_returned_loans', 'input' => array('days' => 365),
        'cron' => '0 3 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
);
```

**4. Check it and run it once.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule list
```
```text
 clear-returned-loans     0 3 * * *      clear_returned_loans     America/New_York, timeout 55s
```
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule run clear-returned-loans
```
```text
 clear-returned-loans: ok
```
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule history
```
```text
 2026-11-07 23:19:29  clear-returned-loans     ok
```

`schedule run` prints the outcome, not the result: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call clear_returned_loans days=365` prints
`{"data": {"deleted": 0}}`. `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit` shows the run as `cli schedule clear-returned-loans
clear_returned_loans ok`.

**5. Let it run.** On your computer, the Docker server (`.bin/caligrafer server start`) has a `scheduler` container: the job runs at 3:00 every night while it is up. Without Docker, keep `php caligrafer.php schedule work` open in
a terminal. Online on Caligrafy Cloud, deploy, then check:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud jobs bookshelf          # clear-returned-loans, its last run and its next one
```

**Check**

+ `schedule list` prints the job (an invalid file prints every problem and exits with `2`).
+ `schedule run clear-returned-loans` prints `ok`.
+ `schedule history` has the run.

To tell people something from a job, call [`Caligrafy\Notify::user()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications#example)
from its capability.
## <a name="declare"></a>Reference: the schedule file

`application/config/schedule.php` returns a list of jobs. No file means no jobs.

| Field | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | A slug (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`), at most 40 characters, unique in the file |
| `capability` | yes | A capability of the app (`php caligrafer.php capabilities`) |
| `input` | no | Its inputs: an array that encodes to JSON, checked by the capability's rules when it runs |
| `every` | `every` or `cron` | `1m`, `5m`, `10m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `6h`, `12h` or `1d` (in UTC; `1d` is midnight UTC) |
| `cron` | `every` or `cron` | Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week (`*/15 * * * *`, `0 9-17 * * mon-fri`) |
| `timezone` | no | An IANA name such as `Europe/Paris`, for `cron` only; `UTC` by default |
| `timeout` | no | Seconds, 55 by default, from 1 to 300 |
| `enabled` | no | `true` by default; `false` keeps the job declared but never run |

Any other field is an error. Background jobs ([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs))
run through one more job of this file, on the framework's capability `queue_work`:
`array('name' => 'queue', 'capability' => 'queue_work', 'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 55)`.

### <a name="run"></a>How a job runs

+ **With full access**, like the command line. The audit log records it with the actor type `schedule` and the job's
  name. Nobody is signed in: `$context->userId()` is `null`, so a job that works for each user finds them itself.
+ **In its own process, one run at a time.** A run that starts while the previous one is still going is skipped and
  recorded as `skipped`.
+ **Stopped at its timeout**, and recorded as `timeout`.
+ **Recorded** in `caligrafy_job_runs` (made by `php caligrafer.php platform install` and the deploy step): the job, its
  start and end, the outcome (`ok`, `error`, `timeout`, `skipped`) and a short detail. Runs older than 30 days are
  deleted.
+ **Needs the database** (`DB_ACTIVATE=true`).

### <a name="commands"></a>Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `php caligrafer.php schedule list` | Checks the file and lists the jobs; `--json` prints what Caligrafy Cloud reads |
| `php caligrafer.php schedule run <job>` | Runs one job now; with `--if-due`, only when it is due this minute in its timezone |
| `php caligrafer.php schedule due` | Runs every enabled job due this minute, side by side, then stops |
| `php caligrafer.php schedule work` | Runs `schedule due` at the start of every minute until you stop it |
| `php caligrafer.php schedule history [<job>] [--limit 50]` | The latest runs, newest first |

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` the capability failed or timed out, `2` the file is invalid, `3` skipped. `php caligrafer.php
doctor` reports an invalid file too.

### <a name="develop"></a>While you develop

`.bin/caligrafer server start` starts the **scheduler** container: it runs `schedule work`, so your jobs run as they
will online. Without Docker, run `php caligrafer.php schedule work` in a terminal. Projects made before 2.14.0 get the
`scheduler` service in `docker-compose.yaml` with `php caligrafer.php update` (or `docker-compose.yaml.caligrafy-new`
when you changed the file: copy its `scheduler` service into yours).

### <a name="online"></a>Online

**Caligrafy Cloud** runs the jobs while the app is online. At each start the deploy step prints the jobs on one line of
the log (`caligrafy-schedule {...}`, the listing of `schedule list --json`), and Cloud runs each one inside the app's
container on its rhythm, with the app's code, settings and database.

| | |
|---|---|
| **See them** | `php caligrafer.php cloud jobs <app>` (each job, its last run and its next one), or **Jobs** on the app's page |
| **Run one now** | `php caligrafer.php cloud jobs <app> run <job>` (within the minute), or **Run now** |
| **Their runs** | `php caligrafer.php cloud jobs <app> history <job>` (7 days, with their output), `cloud logs <app> --jobs`. A run that has not ended shows `running`, with no duration |
| **Limits** | 20 jobs per app, once a minute at most, 300 seconds per run; included in the app's time, no extra credits |
| **Paused** | A paused app runs no jobs, and missed runs are not caught up |
| **Failing** | After 10 failed runs in a row of one job, Cloud emails you once; it never turns a job off |
| **Invalid file** | The app stays online but its jobs do not run: the app's page and an email say why. Fix the file and deploy again |

**Your own server** (Coolify, Docker): run a second container from the same image and `.env` with
`php caligrafer.php schedule work`, or `php caligrafer.php schedule due` from the system's cron every minute. One of
the two, never both.
## Common mistakes

+ **The job does nothing for "the current user".** A job has nobody signed in: find the users or rows in the capability.
+ **`'timezone' is for 'cron' only`.** `every` is always in UTC: use `cron` with a `timezone` for a time of day.
+ **A job stopped at 55 seconds.** Raise its `timeout` (300 at most), or move the work to a
  [background job](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) (900 seconds).
+ **Jobs run twice online.** Your own server runs both `schedule work` and a cron line: keep one.
+ **Nothing runs on your computer.** The `scheduler` container is not up (`server start`), or `schedule work` is not open.
## Related pages

+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
+ [Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)
+ [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications -->

**Notifications** reach your users when none of your pages are open: a book due tomorrow, a reservation ready, an
order shipped. One call, `Caligrafy\Notify::user()`, sends the message on every channel the user turned on: **web push**
(a notification on their phone or computer, browser closed) and **email** (an address they confirmed). Since 2.15.0.
Since 2.27.0 it also reaches the person's iPhones, iPads and Android phones when the project has its own app: see
[Phone and tablet apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.7-Phone-and-Tablet-Apps#notifications).

**Since 2.26.0** web push needs `php caligrafer.php add push` once (web-push and an HTTP client); without it, emails still go out and push is skipped with a message in the log. `php caligrafer.php doctor` says when the VAPID keys are set but the SDK is missing.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability Every morning at 8, tell the administrators how many books are due today or late, and add a "Turn on alerts" button to the loans page
```

Claude writes the capability that calls `Notify::user()`, the job in `application/config/schedule.php`, the button
with `public/js/notify.js`, and adds `Route::capabilities()` and `Route::notifications()` to `web.php`. It runs
`php caligrafer.php platform install` and `php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject mailto:<you>` on your computer
(Caligrafy Cloud makes its own keys).

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php notify status <your user id>` shows `push` `configured: true`.
+ After *Turn on alerts* in your browser, `php caligrafer.php notify test <your user id>` answers `"push": 1` and a
  notification appears.
+ `php caligrafer.php schedule run <job>` prints `ok`.
## <a name="example"></a>By hand: tell the administrators what is late, every morning

Every morning at 8 in New York, each administrator of **Bookshelf** hears how many loans are due today or late. Start
from [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs#example) (the `loans` table) and
an administrator (`permissions` 1, [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication)).
The commands run in the Docker server of the Quickstart; without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`.
The whole lesson, with a page and Caligrafy Cloud, is
[course lesson 15](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/15-Reminders).

**1. Turn notifications on, once.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject mailto:you@example.com
```

`notify keys` prints ` Web push keys written to .env (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT=mailto:you@example.com).
Keep them: new keys cut off every subscribed browser`. Run again, it keeps them.

**2. The routes.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, below `Route::auth(...)`:

```php
    Route::capabilities();      // what notify.js calls (/capabilities)
    Route::notifications();     // the pages the emails link to: /notify/confirm/{token}, /notify/unsubscribe
```

**3. The capability.** Write `application/services/Loans/RemindLoans.php` (the course's, lesson 15):

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Database;
use Caligrafy\Notify;
use Caligrafy\Service;

// remind_loans: tells the administrators which books are due today or late; a scheduled job runs it every morning
#[Capability(
    name: 'remind_loans',
    description: 'Notifies every administrator of the loans due today or late, by push and email. Returns how many loans are due today, how many are late, and how many administrators got the message.',
    scope: 'loans:write',
    level: 1
)]
class RemindLoans extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $today = date('Y-m-d');
        $due = Loan::whereNull('returned_at')->where('due_on', $today)->count();         // SELECT COUNT(*)
        $late = Loan::whereNull('returned_at')->where('due_on', '<', $today)->count();
        if ($due + $late === 0) {
            return array('due' => 0, 'late' => 0, 'notified' => 0);
        }
        $books = $due + $late;
        $message = array(
            'title' => $books === 1 ? '1 book to bring back' : "$books books to bring back",
            'body' => "$due due today, $late late. Open the loans to see who has them.",
            'url' => '/loans',
            'tag' => 'loans-due'
        );
        $notified = 0;
        foreach (Database::table('users')->where('permissions', '>=', 1)->pluck('id') as $admin) {
            $sent = Notify::user($admin, $message);
            if ($sent['push'] > 0 || $sent['email']) {
                $notified++;
            }
        }
        return array('due' => $due, 'late' => $late, 'notified' => $notified);
    }
}
```

A job has nobody signed in, so the capability finds the people it notifies itself.

**4. The schedule.** Add the job to `application/config/schedule.php`:

```php
<?php
return array(
    array('name' => 'clear-returned-loans', 'capability' => 'clear_returned_loans', 'input' => array('days' => 365),
        'cron' => '0 3 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
    array('name' => 'remind-loans', 'capability' => 'remind_loans', 'cron' => '0 8 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
);
```

**5. <a name="page"></a>The button.** Push needs the user's permission, asked from a click. Add to the loans page of
the course, `application/views/Loans/index.pug`, at the end of `block content`:

```pug
    button.btn.btn-primary#alerts(type='button') Turn on alerts
    script(src=$home . 'public/js/notify.js')
    script.
      document.getElementById('alerts').addEventListener('click', async () => {
        const status = await Notify.enable()
        if (status === 'install-needed') alert('On iPhone and iPad, add the app to your Home Screen first')
      })
```

**6. Try it.** Sign in as the administrator, open `http://localhost:8080/loans`, press *Turn on alerts* and allow notifications. Then:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify test 1          # 1: the administrator's user id
```
```json
{
    "push": 1,
    "email": false,
    "skipped": null
}
```

A *Notifications work* message appears. With a loan due today or late:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule run remind-loans     # remind-loans: ok
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call remind_loans             # {"data": {"due": 0, "late": 1, "notified": 1}}
```

Before any browser turned push on, the same calls answer `"push": 0` and `"notified": 0`: nothing is sent, nothing
fails.

**Check**

+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify status 1` lists `"browsers": 1` under `push`.
+ The *1 book to bring back* notification opens `/loans` on a tap.
+ The table `caligrafy_notifications` has one line per message (never its body).
## <a name="send"></a>Reference: `Notify::user`

```php
$result = Caligrafy\Notify::user($userId, array(
    'title'   => 'Kindred is due tomorrow', // required, at most 80 characters
    'body'    => 'Bring it back by Friday.', // required, at most 300 characters
    'url'     => '/books/3',               // opened on a tap: a path of the app, or an https:// address
    'tag'     => 'loan-17',                // optional: a new message with the same tag replaces the old one
    'urgency' => 'high',                   // optional: low, normal (default) or high
));
// array('push' => 1, 'email' => true, 'skipped' => null)
```

+ `$userId` is the id `$context->userId()` gives (in a job, the id of each user it works for).
+ `push` is how many browsers got it; `email` whether an email was sent.
+ A delivery failure never throws. A bad message throws `ServiceError::invalid` with the fields.
+ At most `NOTIFY_RATE_PER_HOUR` messages per user and hour (30): above it nothing is sent (`'skipped' => 'rate'`).
+ Every call is logged in `caligrafy_notifications` (who, the title, the tag, what each channel did; never the body),
  kept 30 days.
+ Without the tables (`platform install`) nothing is sent and nothing fails.
+ When you delete a user, call `Caligrafy\Notify::forget($userId)`: their browsers, address, choices and log go.

### <a name="setup"></a>Settings

| `.env` | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `NOTIFY_CHANNELS` | `push,email` | The channels the app offers |
| `NOTIFY_RATE_PER_HOUR` | `30` | Messages per user and hour |
| `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, `VAPID_SUBJECT` | empty | Written by `notify keys`; never replaced (new keys cut off every subscribed browser) |
| `APP_URL` | empty | The app's address, for the links of emails sent by jobs and the command line (Caligrafy Cloud sets it) |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_USERNAME`, `MAIL_PASSWORD`, `MAIL_FROM` | | The emails' server and sender; without them email reports `not-configured` and push still works |

On **Caligrafy Cloud** each app gets its web push keys at its first deploy, kept across deploys.

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `php caligrafer.php notify keys [--subject mailto:you@example.com]` | writes the web push keys to `.env`, once |
| `php caligrafer.php notify test <user id>` | sends that user a test message on every channel they turned on |
| `php caligrafer.php notify status <user id>` | the channels, the browsers, the email address and whether it is confirmed |

### `notify.js`

| | |
|---|---|
| `Notify.status()` | `unsupported`, `install-needed` (iPhone and iPad outside the Home Screen app), `denied`, `off` or `on` |
| `Notify.enable()` | asks permission, subscribes this browser, saves it; returns the new status. Call it from a click |
| `Notify.disable()` | unsubscribes this browser |
| `Notify.test()` | sends a test message to the signed-in user |
| `Notify.email(address)` | sets the address and emails a link to confirm it (24 hours) |
| `Notify.channel('email', false)` | turns a channel off (or on) |
| `Notify.info()` | what `notify_status` answers |

It registers `public/sw.js`, which shows the message with the browser closed and, on a tap, focuses a tab of its
address or opens one. Keep an in-page banner for when a page is open: notifications are for when it is not.

### <a name="email"></a>Email

+ **Only to a confirmed address.** `Notify.email()` (the `notify_email_set` capability) sends a link valid 24 hours,
  used once. Nothing else is sent there before.
+ **Unsubscribe in one click:** every email has a signed link and the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`
  headers that mail apps show as a button (`Route::notifications()` answers them).
+ **In your app's look:** the emails take the colors, font and corners of your
  [design style](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles) (`DESIGN_STYLE`), else Caligrafy's.

### <a name="capabilities"></a>Built-in capabilities

They ship with the framework, so pages, REST and the JS client use them with no code of yours. Each acts only on the
signed-in user's own data; none is an MCP tool (only a browser can subscribe or open a link).

| Capability | Input |
|---|---|
| `notify_status` | none: the channels and their state |
| `notify_subscribe` | the browser's `PushSubscription` JSON |
| `notify_unsubscribe` | `endpoint` |
| `notify_email_set` | `email` (sends the confirmation) |
| `notify_email_confirm` | `token` (public: the email's link) |
| `notify_preferences` | `channel`, `enabled` |
| `notify_test` | none |

### <a name="devices"></a>Where push works

Chrome, Edge and Firefox on computers and Android; Safari on Mac; Safari on iPhone and iPad once the app is added to
the Home Screen ([install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)). A
device that is off gets the message when it comes back, within 24 hours. Push needs HTTPS (or `localhost`).
## Common mistakes

+ **`Notify.enable()` does nothing.** It was called on page load: browsers ask permission only from a click.
+ **`"push": 0` for everyone.** No browser turned push on yet, or the VAPID keys changed (`notify keys` was run on a new
  `.env`): every browser must turn it on again.
+ **Emails from a job have no links.** `APP_URL` is empty: set it to the app's address.
+ **`"email": false`.** The user has no confirmed address, or `MAIL_*` is not set.
+ **Nothing on iPhone.** The app must be added to the Home Screen, and served over HTTPS.

+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
+ [Views: install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)
