# Forms: `Route::form`

`Route::form($route, $capability, $options)` answers a form's `POST` (or its `PUT` or `DELETE` through `_method`) by
calling a capability with the form's fields, its files and the route variables (the route variables win), as the
person who sent it, then redirects. The page that shows the form stays a
[`Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Page). Since 2.19.0; `visitorsOnly`, `same`,
`accepted`, `inputs` and `signsIn` since 2.20.0, `signsInWith` since 2.21.7.

```php
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Book added']);
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write
"Add a 'New book' form at /books/new for signed-in people. After saving, go to the book's page and say 'Book added'.
If a field is wrong, come back to the form with the message under the field and what was typed."
```

Claude writes the capability, the `Route::page` of the form and its `Route::form`, and the Pug view with `=csrf()`,
`old()`, `errors()` and `flash()`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the form has `method='POST'`, `=csrf()`, and `=methodField('PUT')` or `'DELETE'` for those routes;
+ `success` and `back` point at the pages that show `flash()` and `errors()`;
+ sending the form empty shows the messages under the fields, and the typed values stay.
## By hand

The `create_book` capability is the one of
[Declarative routes, step 1](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes).

1. **Declare the page and the form.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`:

   ```php
       Route::page('/books/new', 'Bookshelf/new', ['signedIn' => true, 'comeBack' => true, 'data' => ['authors' => 'list_authors']]);
       Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Book added']);
       Route::form('/books/{id}', 'update_book', ['method' => 'PUT', 'success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Saved']);
       Route::form('/books/{id}', 'delete_book', ['method' => 'DELETE', 'success' => '/books', 'flash' => 'Book deleted']);
   ```

2. **Write the form.** `application/views/Bookshelf/new.pug`:

   ```pug
   extends ../default/master/site

   block content
     section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
       h1.cq-display New book

     section.cq-band.cq-band--tight
       .cq-inner.cq-inner--narrow
         if flash('error')
           .cq-alert.cq-alert--error(role='alert')= flash('error')
         form(method='POST', action=$home . 'books')
           =csrf()
           .cq-field
             label(for='title') Title
             input#title.form-control(type='text', name='title', value=old('title'))
             if errors('title')
               p.cq-field-error= errors('title')
           .cq-field
             label(for='author_id') Author
             select#author_id.form-select(name='author_id')
               each $a in $authors
                 option(value=$a['id'], selected=$a['id'] == old('author_id'))= $a['name']
             if errors('author_id')
               p.cq-field-error= errors('author_id')
           button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Add book
   ```

   A `PUT` or `DELETE` form adds `=methodField('PUT')` (or `'DELETE'`) after `=csrf()`.

3. **Try it.** On `/books/new`, send the form empty: the page comes back with "Some of the inputs are invalid" at the
   top and "The Title field is required" under the title. Fill it in: you land on `/books/<id>` with "Book added".
## <a name="outcomes"></a>What happens after the post

| The capability | The person goes to | The next page has |
|---|---|---|
| succeeds | `success`, its `{name}` filled from the result, then from the route variables; without `success`, back to the form | `flash('success')` with the `flash` message |
| refuses the input (`invalid`) or finds a duplicate (`conflict`) | back: the `back` option, else the page it came from (the `Referer`, when it is a page of this site), else `/` | `errors('title')`, `old('title')`, `flash('error')` |
| needs someone signed in, nobody is | the sign-in page (`signIn`, default `/login`); without the authentication module, `403` | |
| refuses the person (`forbidden`) | `403` `[ERROR 1006] Forbidden` | |
| finds nothing, or anything else | `404` `[ERROR 1005] Page Not Found` | |
## <a name="options"></a>Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `'POST'` | `'PUT'`, `'DELETE'`, or a list (`['POST', 'PUT']`); `GET` is refused (pages are `Route::page`) |
| `success` | back to the form | a path with `{placeholders}`, a full `https://` address, or `function ($result) { return '/books/' . $result['id']; }` |
| `flash` | none | the message for `flash('success')`, with `{placeholders}` as in `success`; or `['key' => 'message']` |
| `back` | the `Referer` of this site, else `/` | where invalid input goes, with the route's `{placeholders}`: `'back' => '/books/{id}'` |
| `error` | the capability's message | your message for `flash('error')`, or `['key' => 'message']` |
| `signIn` | `'/login'` | where a visitor goes when the capability needs someone |
| `visitorsOnly` | none | a path: people already signed in are sent there and the capability does not run; a JSON request gets `403` |
| `same` | none | fields that must match: `['password_again' => ['password', 'The two passwords are not the same']]`; without a message, "The two values are not the same" |
| `accepted` | none | boxes that must be ticked: `['terms' => 'Accept the terms of use']` |
| `inputs` | none | values only the server sets: an array, or `function ($input) { return [...]; }`. They replace what the form sent; the route variables still win |
| `signsIn` | none | the field of the capability's answer that holds the id of the person to sign in: `'signsIn' => 'id'`. A new session id and a new CSRF token, as for `Route::auth` |
| `signsInWith` | `'password'` | how `signsIn` signed the person in: what `AuthRoutes::signedInBy()` answers for that session (2.21.7) |

**The order of the checks.** `visitorsOnly`, then (JSON with the session) the CSRF header, then `same` and `accepted`,
then the capability. A form that breaks `same` or `accepted` never reaches the capability, and their messages arrive in
`errors('password_again')`, like the capability's. Both are read from what the person sent: declare `password_again` in
`$rules` only if the capability needs it.

**Values the form must not choose.** A form can send any field. `inputs` writes the ones only the server knows, over
anything the form sent: the address a payment page comes back to, the visitor's address, today's price.

**A form that leaves the site** for a payment page:

```php
Route::form('/orders/{order}/pay', 'start_checkout', [
    'inputs' => fn () => ['site' => session('home')],
    'success' => fn ($result) => $result['url'],
    'back' => '/orders',
]);
```

**A sign-up form that signs the person in**, for visitors only (`register_user` is the capability the authentication
module ships):

```php
Route::page('/join', 'Bookshelf/join', ['visitorsOnly' => '/books']);
Route::form('/join', 'register_user', [
    'visitorsOnly' => '/books',
    'same' => ['confirmpasscode' => ['passcode', 'The two passwords are not the same']],
    'accepted' => ['terms' => 'Accept the terms of use to create an account'],
    'signsIn' => 'id',
    'success' => '/books',
    'back' => '/join',
    'flash' => 'Welcome to the Bookshelf',
]);
```

`signsIn` is for a capability that creates or finds the person and answers their id: sign-up, an invitation link, a
confirmation code. A sign-in that decides how to sign in, or that has a state to check, is a
[`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action).
## <a name="helpers"></a>The view helpers

| Helper | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `=csrf()` | the hidden `_token` field every form post needs (`403` `[ERROR 3000]` without it) |
| `=methodField('PUT')` | the hidden `_method` field of a `PUT` or `DELETE` form |
| `errors()`, `errors('title')` | all the messages, or one field's (`null` when it has none) |
| `old('title', $default)` | what the person typed, else `$default` |
| `flash('success')`, `flash('error')` | the message of the last post; `flash('saved', 'Your changes are saved')` in your own code keeps one for the next request |

+ **One request only.** The errors, the old values and the messages are read by the next page, then gone.
+ Passwords, card numbers, tokens (any field whose name contains `pass`, `secret`, `token`, `card`, `cvc`, `cvv` or
  `iban`), files and `_` fields are never kept for `old()`.
+ **JSON**: a request with `Accept: application/json` gets the REST answer instead of redirects: `{"data": ...}` with
  `201` (a `POST` that changes data) or `200`, or `{"error": ...}` with `401`, `403`, `404`, `409` or `422`. With the
  session cookie it needs the `X-CSRF-Token` header.
## Reference

+ [`Route::form()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-form)
+ [`Caligrafy\Form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#form): how the post is answered
+ [`Caligrafy\Flash`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#flash) and the helpers
  [`csrf()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-csrf),
  [`methodField()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-methodfield),
  [`errors()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-errors),
  [`old()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-old),
  [`flash()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Helpers#fn-flash)
## Common mistakes

+ **`success` redirects to a page that redirects again**: the message is read by the page in between and lost. Point
  `success` and `back` at the page that shows it.
+ **A JSON post with the session and no `X-CSRF-Token`** answers `403`: send the header (`apiHeaders()` in the Vue
  apps).
+ **A placeholder with no value** (`'success' => '/authors/{author}'` when neither the result nor the route has
  `author`) stops with an error that names it.
+ **A file form without `enctype='multipart/form-data'`**: no file arrives
  ([File uploads](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/File-Uploads)).
+ **`Route::form` on a `webOnly` capability**: it answers "There is no capability". Use `Route::action`.

## Related pages

+ [Pages: `Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Page)
+ [File uploads: the `file` rule](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/File-Uploads)
+ [Validation](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation): the rules of `$rules`

# Sign-in pages: `Route::auth`

`Route::auth($options)` declares the sign-in, sign-out and sign-up pages in one line, with the views of the
authentication module, and no controller. It goes after `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');` in `web.php`. Since
2.19.0; `level` since 2.19.5, `attemptsPerUser` since 2.19.6, coming back after signing in since 2.20.0.

```php
Auth::authentication('User', 'users');
Route::auth(['home' => '/books']);
```

This page is about the declaration. Users, levels, tokens, password reset and the views are in
[Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication).
## With Claude

```text
"Add sign-in pages: after signing in, people land on /books."
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');` is above `Route::auth(...)` and the `users` table exists;
+ a page only signed-in people open says `'signedIn' => true` (and `'comeBack' => true` to land back on it);
+ no controller and no closure was written for the sign-in.
## By hand

1. **The `users` table.** Run:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Auth/create_db.sql
   ```

2. **Turn on sign-in.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, remove the `//` in front of
   `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');`, and add below it:

   ```php
       // sign-in pages: /login, /logout, /register, /notAuthorized
       Route::auth(['home' => '/books']);
   ```

3. **Try it.** Open `http://localhost:8080/register`, create an account (a username, a password typed twice), then
   sign in on `/login`: you land on `/books`.
## <a name="routes"></a>What it declares

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /login` | the sign-in page (`Auth/login`); a signed-in person goes to `home`, or to `?return=` |
| `POST /login` | checks the identifier field and `passcode`; on success a new session id and a new CSRF token, then `home`, or the page of `/login?return=` |
| `GET /logout`, `POST /logout` | signs out (a new session id and CSRF token), then `logout` |
| `GET /notAuthorized` | the page of people below the level a page needs (403) |
| `GET /register`, `POST /register` | the sign-up page (`Auth/register`) and the `register_user` capability, then `/login` |
| `POST /passkey/register/options`, `/passkey/register`, `/passkey/login/options`, `/passkey/login` | with `'passkeys' => true` only |
## <a name="options"></a>Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `home` | `'/'` | where people go after signing in (a signed-in person who opens `/login` goes there too) |
| `logout` | `'/'` | where people go after signing out |
| `register` | `true` | `true`: `/register` with the `register_user` capability; `false`: no sign-up; a capability name: yours |
| `identifier` | `'username'` | the `users` column people sign in with, and the name of the sign-in field (`'email'`) |
| `signInAfterRegister` | `false` | `true`: a new account is signed in and goes to `home` instead of the sign-in page |
| `attempts`, `lock` | `5`, `900` | failed sign-ins per username and address before a `429`, and the window in seconds |
| `attemptsPerUser` | `0` (off) | failed sign-ins of one username from any address before it is locked (2.19.6). Someone could lock a known username out on purpose: keep it high (20) |
| `level` | `0` | the lowest permission level that may sign in (2.19.5): below it, a sign-in is refused like a wrong password |
| `messages` | human words | what sign-in and sign-up say: `invalid`, `locked` (2.19.3, `{minutes}` is the wait), `mismatch`, `register_invalid`, `register_taken`, `registered` (2.19.4); the defaults are `AuthRoutes::MESSAGES` |
| `views` | `['login' => 'Auth/login', 'register' => 'Auth/register']` | your own views |
| `prefix` | `''` | `'/account'` gives `/account/login`... (the shipped views post to `/login`: write your own) |
| `passkeys` | `false` | `true` adds the passkey endpoints ([passkeys](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition#passkeys)) |

```php
// a users table with an email column: people sign in with it, and are signed in right after signing up
Route::auth(['home' => '/books', 'identifier' => 'email', 'signInAfterRegister' => true]);

// only administrators may sign in, in your own words
Route::auth(['home' => '/admin', 'level' => 1, 'messages' => ['invalid' => 'This account cannot sign in here.']]);
```
## <a name="behavior"></a>How it behaves

+ Signing in and signing out give the person a new session id and a new CSRF token.
+ The fifth failed sign-in for a username from one address within 15 minutes, and every one after it until the 15
  minutes end, answers `429` (2.19.3; `messages` sets your own words).
+ A JSON request with `X-CSRF-Token` gets `200` `{"data":{"user":{"id":1,"username":"ada","permissions":0}}}`, `401`
  or `429` in JSON: a Vue app signs in with the same routes.
+ Sign-up sends the register capability every input its `$rules` declare; nothing else of the form reaches it.
+ After signing in, a person goes to `home`, or to the page named by `/login?return=/books/3` (2.20.0). Only a path of
  this site is followed: another site, or `//evil.example`, is ignored. `Route::page` and `Route::action` with
  `'comeBack' => true` build that address for you.
+ `Route::auth` records how the session signed in, `password` or `passkey`, for `AuthRoutes::signedInBy()` (2.21.3).
+ **Not in `Route::auth`**: password reset and face sign-in. `'reset' => true` or `'face' => true` stops with an error.
  [Password reset](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#passwordreset) is `Route::page`
  and `Route::form`; [face sign-in](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition#face-login)
  is `Route::action`.
## Reference

+ [`Route::auth()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-auth)
+ [`Caligrafy\AuthRoutes`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes):
  [`signIn()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-signin),
  [`signedInBy()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-signedinby),
  [`signOut()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-signout)
+ [`Caligrafy\Auth`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#auth)
## Common mistakes

+ **`Route::auth` without `Auth::authentication('User', 'users')` above it**: there is no user model to sign in with.
+ **`'identifier' => 'email'` with the shipped `login.pug`**: the sign-in form posts a field named after the
  identifier, so the view needs an `email` field. For people who sign in with an email and no separate username, keep
  the address in `username` instead ([Signing in with an email](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#emailsignin)).
+ **A `prefix` with the shipped views**: they post to `/login`. Write your own views.
+ **`comeBack` with a `return=` you build by hand to another site**: it is ignored, the person goes to `home`.

## Related pages

+ [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication): users, levels, tokens, password reset
+ [Pages: `Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Page): `signedIn`, `level`, `comeBack`, `visitorsOnly`
+ [Forms: `Route::form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Form): a sign-up of your own with `signsIn`
+ [Face detection and face login](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition)

# Webhooks: `Route::webhook`

A payment provider, a library service or GitHub posts events to an address of yours. `Route::webhook($route,
$capability, $options)` checks that the event comes from them (its signature), then calls a capability with it. There
is no session and no CSRF token: the signature is the only proof. Since 2.19.0.

```php
Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_event', ['verify' => 'stripe']);   // STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... in .env
```
## With Claude

```text
"Receive Stripe's checkout events at /stripe/events and record each one once."
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the route has `verify`, and the secret is the endpoint's `whsec_...`, not the API key;
+ the capability starts by refusing every caller that is not the webhook (`$context->actorType() !== 'webhook'`);
+ the same event posted twice is recorded once.
## By hand

1. **A table that remembers the events.** Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate make create_webhook_events`, and write in the file it names:

   ```sql
   -- create_webhook_events
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_events (
       id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
       event_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
       type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
       created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       PRIMARY KEY (id),
       UNIQUE KEY uq_webhook_events_event_id (event_id)
   ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;
   ```

   Then `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate`.

2. **The capability.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/RecordEvent`, then make
   `application/services/Bookshelf/RecordEvent.php` read:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Database;
   use Caligrafy\Service;
   use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

   #[Capability(
       name: 'record_event',
       description: 'Records an event that the library service posts (its id and type), once per event id.'
   )]
   class RecordEvent extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('event' => 'required');

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           // only the webhook route may record events: REST, MCP and pages would let a signed-in user make one up
           if ($context->actorType() !== 'webhook') {
               throw ServiceError::forbidden('Only the library service sends events');
           }
           $event = $input['event'];
           if (!is_array($event) || empty($event['id']) || empty($event['type'])) {
               throw ServiceError::invalid(array('event' => 'The event needs an id and a type'));
           }
           // the sender posts an event again until it gets a 2xx: record each id once
           if (!Database::table('webhook_events')->where('event_id', $event['id'])->exists()) {
               Database::table('webhook_events')->insert(array('event_id' => $event['id'], 'type' => $event['type']));
           }
           return array('recorded' => $event['id']);
       }
   }
   ```

3. **The secret and the route.** Add the secret the sender gave you to `.env` (a placeholder here):
   `LIBRARY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_test_library`. In `web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

   ```php
       // the library service signs each event: X-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the secret>
       Route::webhook('/hooks/library', 'record_event', ['verify' => function ($rawBody, $headers) {
           $expected = 'sha256=' . hash_hmac('sha256', $rawBody, (string) getenv('LIBRARY_WEBHOOK_SECRET'));
           return hash_equals($expected, $headers['x-signature'] ?? '');
       }]);
   ```

4. **Post a signed event.** Run:

   ```bash
   BODY='{"id":"evt_1","type":"loan.returned"}'
   SIG="sha256=$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac whsec_test_library -r | cut -d' ' -f1)"
   curl -s -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Signature: $SIG" http://localhost:8080/hooks/library -d "$BODY"
   ```

   It answers `200` with `{"received":true}`, and `webhook_events` has one row. The same post again adds nothing. With
   `-H "X-Signature: sha256=bad"`: `400` and `{"error":{"code":"invalid_signature","message":"The signature is not valid"}}`.
   A `GET` answers `405`.
## <a name="options"></a>Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `verify` | required | `'stripe'`, or `function (string $rawBody, array $headers): bool` (header names in lower case; only `true` passes) |
| `secret_env` | `'STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET'` | with `'stripe'`: the `.env` variable that holds the endpoint's signing secret (`whsec_...`, not the API key) |
| `secret` | none | with `'stripe'`: the secret itself, instead of the variable (tests) |
| `tolerance` | `300` | with `'stripe'`: how many seconds old a signature may be |

`'stripe'` checks the `Stripe-Signature` header with the Stripe library. Anything else is a function of yours, as in
step 3.
## <a name="answers"></a>What the sender gets

| The event | The answer |
|---|---|
| signature checked, capability done | `200 {"received": true}` |
| bad or missing signature | `400 {"error":{"code":"invalid_signature",...}}` |
| a body that is not JSON | `400 {"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"The body is not JSON"}}` |
| the capability refuses (`ServiceError`) | its status and its error (`422` for `invalid`) |
| no secret set, no such capability, an error in the capability | `500`; the message goes to the PHP error log |

+ `verify` is required: a webhook without it stops with an error when `web.php` runs.
+ The body must be JSON; the capability gets `['event' => the decoded body]`, so declare `$rules = ['event' => 'required']`.
+ The capability runs as the system, with full access (`Context::system('webhook', $path)`; the audit log shows
  `webhook /hooks/library`): treat the event as data from outside. Before trusting an amount, ask the provider again
  ([Stripe](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.2-Stripe-&-Cryptocurrency-Payment#webhook)).
+ Webhook addresses skip the CSRF check that every other form post goes through.
## Reference

+ [`Route::webhook()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-webhook)
+ [`Caligrafy\Webhook`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#webhook):
  [`verify()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#webhook-verify),
  [`process()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#webhook-process) (a test posts an event
  without a server)
+ [`Context::actorType()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#context-actortype)
## Common mistakes

+ **`'verify' => 'stripe'` without `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`**: every event answers `500`. Use the endpoint's
  `whsec_...`, not the `sk_...` key.
+ **A webhook capability that is not idempotent**: services post an event again until they get a `2xx`, and a retried
  event is recorded twice.
+ **No `actorType()` check**: the capability is also served by REST, the JS client, MCP and `php caligrafer.php call`,
  to anyone its `scope` and `level` let in, with an event they made up.

## Related pages

+ [Stripe & cryptocurrency payment](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.2-Stripe-&-Cryptocurrency-Payment#webhook)
+ [Migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations)
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webhook)
+ [The audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#audit)

# Downloads: `Route::download`

`Route::download($route, $capability, $options)` answers a `GET` with the result of a **read-only** capability as a
file: a CSV, a JSON file, or the files it lists in one ZIP. The capability stays plain data, so the same list also
reaches REST, the JS client and agents. Since 2.19.0; `columns` since 2.19.5, ZIP since 2.22.0.

```php
Route::download('/authors.csv', 'list_authors', ['filename' => 'authors.csv']);
Route::download('/books.json', 'list_books', ['as' => 'json']);   // a page of list_books, ?page=2 for the next
Route::download('/photos.zip', 'list_photo_files', ['as' => 'zip', 'root' => 'public/uploads/photos']);
```
## With Claude

```text
"Let people export the authors as CSV from a link on the authors page."
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the route names a read-only capability;
+ the export returns arrays with the columns it means to show (not models: they carry every property);
+ a ZIP's `root` is the folder that holds the files, relative to the project.

A step-by-step CSV export: [How to export a list as CSV](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Export-a-List-as-CSV).
## <a name="options"></a>Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `as` | `'csv'` | `'csv'`, `'json'` (pretty-printed) or `'zip'` (the files the capability lists, 2.22.0); anything else stops with an error when `web.php` runs |
| `root` | `'public/uploads'` | for `zip`: the folder of the project the files are read from; a file outside it is never sent. A `root` with `..` stops with an error when `web.php` runs |
| `columns` | the first row's keys | the header row and its order, written even when there is no row: `['title', 'year']` (2.19.5) |
| `filename` | `<capability>.<as>` | a name, or `function ($result, $input) { return 'books-' . date('Y-m-d') . '.csv'; }` |
| `bom` | `false` | `true` starts the CSV with a UTF-8 BOM (Excel) |
| `formulas` | `false` | `true` keeps cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` as they are |
| `signIn` | `'/login'` | where a visitor goes when the capability needs someone |
## <a name="inputs"></a>Inputs and refusals

+ The capability must be read-only: opening a link must not change data.
+ It gets the query string and the route variables (`/books.csv?author_id=2`) as the person who opens the link; the
  route variables win.
+ Refusals are those of `Route::page`: a visitor goes to sign in, `forbidden` is `403`, nothing found is `404`. An input
  to fix (`?author_id=abc`) answers `422` with the capability's error as JSON, as REST does (2.19.5; before, `404`).
+ The answer carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
## <a name="csv"></a>CSV

+ The header row comes from `columns`, else from the first row's keys (then an empty result is an empty file).
+ Values are quoted where needed (RFC 4180, lines end with CRLF), UTF-8.
+ A text cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` or a tab gets a `'` first, so a spreadsheet does not run it as a
  formula (`formulas` turns that off).
+ Arrays in a cell are written as JSON, booleans as `true` / `false`. A related row (`with('author')`) is one cell, in
  JSON.
+ Each row of the list is a line. A `paginate()` page exports that page only: return `get()` to export every row; a
  single record gives one line.
+ **The columns are the keys of the first row.** A model carries every one of its properties:
  `Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->get()` exports `id`, `title` and every other column of `Book`, empty. Return
  arrays for a narrow export: `Database::table('books')->select('id', 'title')->get()` or
  `Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->arrays()->get()`.
## <a name="zip"></a>Many files as one ZIP (2.22.0)

The capability lists the files; `Route::download` puts them in one archive and sends it.

```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_photo_files', description: 'The files of the photos, oldest first', scope: 'photos:read', level: 1, readOnly: true)]
class ListPhotoFiles extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        return array_map(fn ($photo) => [
            'file' => $photo['image'],                                        // relative to 'root'
            'name' => 'pictures/' . date('Y-m-d_H-i-s', strtotime($photo['created_at'])) . '.jpg',   // in the archive
        ], Photo::query()->arrays()->select('image', 'created_at')->orderBy('created_at')->get());
    }
}
```

```php
Route::download('/photos.zip', 'list_photo_files', ['as' => 'zip', 'root' => 'public/uploads/photos',
    'filename' => fn ($files, $input) => 'photos-' . date('Y-m-d') . '.zip']);
```

+ **Each item** is a path (the file keeps its own name) or `['file' => path, 'name' => 'folder/name.jpg']`. Paths are
  relative to `root`; a `paginate()` page gives its rows.
+ **Only files under `root` go in.** A path that leaves it (`../../.env`), a folder, or a missing file is left out
  without an error. Names are cleaned (no `..`, no leading `/`), and a name used twice becomes `name (2).jpg`.
+ **No file at all answers `404`.** Hide the link when there is nothing to download, or throw
  `ServiceError::notFound('No photo yet')` in the capability.
+ Images, video, audio and archives are stored as they are; other files are compressed. The archive is written to a
  temporary file, sent with its `Content-Length`, then removed.
+ It needs PHP's **zip** extension: Caligrafy's Docker images and Caligrafy Cloud have it.
+ In a test, `Download::archive($files, ['root' => ...])` builds the same archive (`['path', 'count', 'names']`;
  remove `path` afterwards).
## Reference

+ [`Route::download()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-download)
+ [`Caligrafy\Download`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#download):
  [`archive()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#download-archive),
  [`csv()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#download-csv),
  [`rows()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#download-rows)
## Common mistakes

+ **A download of a capability that writes**: `Route::download` refuses it when the link is opened.
+ **A model query for a narrow export**: every column of the model is in the file. Return arrays.
+ **A ZIP whose files live outside `root`**: they are left out, and an empty list answers `404`. Give the folder that
  holds them, relative to the project (`public/uploads/photos`), and paths relative to it.
+ **A web-only capability that streams its own ZIP** (before 2.22.0): return the list and use `'as' => 'zip'`.

## Related pages

+ [How to export a list as CSV](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Export-a-List-as-CSV)
+ [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries): `select()`, `arrays()`, `paginate()`
+ [Pages: `Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Page): the same refusals
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#download)

# Redirects: `Route::redirect`

`Route::redirect($from, $to, $status = 302, $options = [])` answers a `GET` by sending the visitor elsewhere, without
a closure or a controller: an address that moved, a short address, the home page of a section. Since 2.19.0;
`keepQuery` since 2.20.0.

```php
Route::redirect('/catalog', '/books');                   // 302
Route::redirect('/old/books/{id}', '/books/{id}', 301);  // moved for good
```
## With Claude

```text
"Redirect /catalog to /books, and the old /old/books/{id} addresses to /books/{id} for good."
```
## By hand

1. In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

   ```php
       Route::redirect('/catalog', '/books');
   ```

2. Run `curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/catalog`: it answers `302 Found` with `Location: http://localhost:8080/books`.
## <a name="rules"></a>How it works

+ `{name}` in the target takes the route variable of the same name (url-encoded); the query string never fills it
  (`/old/books/2?x=1` goes to `/books/2`).
+ The target is a path of the site or a full `https://` address.
+ The status is `301`, `302` (default), `303`, `307` or `308`; anything else, or an empty target, stops with an error
  when `web.php` runs.
+ `['keepQuery' => true]` (2.20.0) takes the query string along: `/old?page=2` goes to `/new?page=2`. A `#fragment` of
  the target stays last.

```php
Route::redirect('/old', '/new', 301, ['keepQuery' => true]);
```
## Reference

+ [`Route::redirect()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-redirect),
  [`Route::withQuery()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-withquery),
  [`Route::redirectTarget()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-redirecttarget)
## Common mistakes

+ **A redirect that depends on who asks, or on the data**: that is a
  [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action) whose capability returns
  `Web::redirect(...)`.
+ **`redirect()` in a closure without `return`**: `redirect()` only sends a `Location` header; code after it still
  runs. `Route::redirect` has no such problem.
+ **Expecting the query string to fill `{name}`**: only the route variables of `$from` do.

## Related pages

+ [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing): how a request finds its route
+ [Everything else: `Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action)
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#redirect)

# Everything else: `Route::action` and web-only capabilities

`Route::page` shows a view and `Route::form` calls a capability and redirects. A few requests are neither: a sign-in
between two sites, a page that chooses between a view and a redirect, a gate, a page that creates a payment. Since
2.21.0 they are capabilities too, declared `webOnly: true` and served by one line, `Route::action($route, $capability,
$options)`. This is what replaces the controller of a new application.

```php
Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books', ['back' => '/books']);
```
## With Claude

```text
"Add GET /authors/{author_id}/books: when the author has exactly one book, go straight to that book's page;
otherwise show the list."
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `webOnly: true` is on a capability that needs the session, signs someone in, or chooses between a page and a
  redirect; everything else stays a plain capability, so REST and agents can reach it;
+ the web-only capability calls the plain ones with `$this->capability()`;
+ no controller and no closure was written.
## By hand

1. **The capability.** Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks` and make
   `application/services/Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks.php` read:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Service;
   use Caligrafy\Web;

   // open_author_books: one book goes straight to its page, otherwise the list
   #[Capability(
       name: 'open_author_books',
       description: 'Opens the books of an author: the book itself when there is one, otherwise the list.',
       readOnly: true,
       public: true,
       webOnly: true
   )]
   class OpenAuthorBooks extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('author_id' => 'required|integer');

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
           if ($books['total'] == 1) {
               return Web::redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
           }
           return Web::view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
       }
   }
   ```

2. **The route.** In `web.php`:

   ```php
       Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books', ['back' => '/books']);
   ```

3. **Try it.**

   ```bash
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/3/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/authors/2/books
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/abc/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
   ```

   They print `302` to `/books/5` (one book), `200` (a list of two), and `302` to `/books` (the `back` option), where
   `flash('error')` says "Some of the inputs are invalid".
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call open_author_books author_id=3` prints
   `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"There is no capability 'open_author_books'"}}`: only the route reaches it.
## <a name="options"></a>Options

```php
Route::action('/unlock/{name}', 'unlock_shelf', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/shelf/report', 'shelf_report', ['level' => 1, 'comeBack' => true]);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `'GET'` | `'POST'`, `'PUT'`, `'DELETE'`, or a list (`['GET', 'POST']`) |
| `signedIn`, `level` | none | as in `Route::page`: visitors go to `/login`, people below the level to `/notAuthorized` |
| `comeBack` | `false` | with `signedIn` or `level`, or when the capability needs someone: visitors go to `/login?return=<this page>` |
| `visitorsOnly` | none | a path: people already signed in are sent there |
| `back` | the `Referer` of this site, else `/` | where invalid input or a conflict goes, with the route's `{placeholders}` |
| `error` | the capability's message | your message for `flash('error')` |
| `signIn` | `'/login'` | where a visitor goes when the capability needs someone (`comeBack` replaces it) |
## <a name="answers"></a>What it answers: `Caligrafy\Web`

| The capability returns | The browser gets |
|---|---|
| `Web::view('Bookshelf/book', $data, $status = 200)` | a Pug view, with `$authorized` and `$user` as on `Route::page` (`$data` wins). A request that asks for JSON gets the data as JSON |
| `Web::redirect('/books', $status = 302)` | a redirect: a path of this site or a full `http(s)` address |
| `Web::json($data, $status = 200)` | JSON, the data as it is, with no `{"data": ...}` around it |
| `Web::text($body, $status = 200)` | the text as it is |
| any of them `->header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` | one more response header |
| plain data (an array, a model) | JSON, as with `Web::json` |

**When it refuses.** A capability that answers a refusal itself returns a `Web`. One that throws a `ServiceError` gets
the answers of `Route::form`:

| It throws | A browser | A JSON request |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid` or `conflict` | back (`back`, the `Referer`, or `/`) with `errors()`, `old()`, `flash('error')` | `422` or `409` and the REST error |
| `unauthenticated` | the sign-in page (`comeBack`: and back here) | `401` |
| `forbidden` | `403` `[ERROR 1006]` | `403` |
| `not_found` or anything else | `404` `[ERROR 1005]` | `404` |

**What it receives.** The inputs its `$rules` declare, from the form, the JSON body or the query string, and the route
variables, which win (`/books/3?id=9` gives `id = 3`, 2.21.2). Its files are saved and given as URLs, as for
`Route::form`. It runs as the person who sent the request, with its `public`, `scope` and `level` checks, its
validation and its audit log, like any capability.
## <a name="webonly"></a>What a web-only capability may do

**Only capabilities touch models**: a web-only capability is a capability. What sets it apart is what it may do besides:

| A plain capability | A web-only capability |
|---|---|
| returns data, or refuses | may also return a view, a redirect, JSON or text |
| never reads the session or the request: `$context` says who calls | may read `session()`, `request()`, `$_SERVER`, `$_COOKIE` |
| never signs anyone in | may sign people in and out |
| on a page, only `readOnly` | a `GET` may change data |
| reached by REST, MCP, the JS client, the command line, `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `$this->call()` | reached by **`Route::action` only** |

Everywhere else it answers `not_found` "There is no capability", and it is left out of `GET /capabilities`, MCP,
`php caligrafer.php capabilities` and `php caligrafer.php client`. So keep the work several channels share in plain
capabilities, and call them from the web-only one:

```php
$books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => 2), $context);   // as the same person, with its rules
```
## <a name="signin"></a>Signing someone in from an action

+ **A page that leaves or reloads**: `Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::signIn($user, null, 'partner')` gives a new session id, a
  new CSRF token, and records how the session signed in (the third argument, 2.21.3, read by
  `AuthRoutes::signedInBy()`).
+ **A page that stays open and keeps sending JSON**: `session_regenerate_id(true); Auth::authorize($user);
  AuthRoutes::rememberSignIn('face');`. The page keeps its token.
+ `$context` was built before the sign-in and does not change: to call a capability as the person just signed in,
  build a new one with `Context::fromRequest(request(), 'web')`.

A complete sign-in through another site is in
[Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#betweensites).
## <a name="csrf"></a>CSRF and JSON

+ A form's `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` needs its `_token` (`=csrf()`): `403` `[ERROR 3000]` without it.
+ A JSON call (`Accept: application/json`), `GET` included, needs the page's `X-CSRF-Token` header (`apiHeaders()` of
  the Vue apps) or, with `Auth::activateAPI();` in `web.php`, a token that grants everything (`--scopes "*"`), signed
  in or not: `401` `[ERROR 1004]` without it (2.21.1). A scoped token is refused: programs use the capability routes.
+ A plain `GET` opened by a link has no token, and can be triggered by a link on another site: keep a `GET` that
  changes data to what is harmless when that happens, and use `'method' => 'POST'` with a form for the rest.

**Tests.** `$this->action('open_author_books', ['author_id' => 3], $user)` calls it as `Route::action` does and returns
what it answered; `->describe()` gives `type`, `target`, `data`, `status` and `headers`. `$this->call()` answers
`not_found`, as every other channel does. See [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App#helpers).
## Reference

+ [`Route::action()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-action)
+ [`Caligrafy\Action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#action) and
  [`Caligrafy\Web`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#web)
+ [`AuthRoutes::signIn()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-signin),
  [`AuthRoutes::rememberSignIn()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-AuthRoutes#authroutes-remembersignin)
+ [`Context::fromRequest()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing#context-fromrequest)
## Common mistakes

+ **`Route::action` on a capability without `webOnly: true`**, or `webOnly: true` behind `Route::page`, `Route::form` or
  REST: the first stops with an error that names it, the others answer "There is no capability".
+ **A web-only capability for work other channels need**: agents and programs cannot reach it. Put the work in a plain
  capability and call it with `$this->capability()`.
+ **A JSON call without `X-CSRF-Token`**: `401` `[ERROR 1004]`, even for a `GET` and for a visitor. Send `apiHeaders()`.
+ **`AuthRoutes::signIn()` on a page that stays open**: it gives the session a new CSRF token, and the page's next JSON
  call answers `401`. Use `session_regenerate_id(true); Auth::authorize($user);` there.
+ **Calling a capability as the person just signed in with the old `$context`**: it still says who called before. Build
  a new one with `Context::fromRequest(request(), 'web')`.

# Snap Cards and the assistant: `Route::snap`

`Route::snap($options)` declares, in one line of `web.php`, every capability of the app as a card and an assistant that
answers with them. Since 2.23.0. This page is about the declaration; what people get, the card types, card views and
hints are in [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant).

```php
Auth::authentication('User', 'users');
Route::snap();
```
## With Claude

```text
"Add Snap Cards and the assistant to the app."
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `Route::snap();` is below `Auth::authentication(...)`;
+ `php caligrafer.php snap install` was run (the `caligrafy_snap_*` tables);
+ `/assistant` opens for a signed-in person and `/snap` lists the cards.
## By hand

1. **One line** in `application/config/routing/web.php`, after `Auth::authentication(...)`:

   ```php
   Route::snap();
   ```

2. **Its tables, and a starter hints file:**

   ```bash
   php caligrafer.php snap install
   ```

   It creates the `caligrafy_snap_*` tables (they also come with `php caligrafer.php platform install`, and with every
   deploy) and `application/config/snap.php`, then prints what is ready.

3. **Open `/assistant`.** The rest is optional: the `queue_work` job for background tasks, the `snap_routines_due` job
   for routines, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env` for the assistant's model (without it, the assistant answers from the
   cards' names).
## <a name="routes"></a>What it declares

| Address | What it is |
|---|---|
| `GET /assistant` | Home (what needs you, insights, things to browse, shortcuts) and the task space; signed-in people only (`comeBack`) |
| `POST /assistant/ask` | what the person typed, said, attached or clicked (`snap_ask`, a `Route::action`) |
| `GET /assistant/noticed` | what the assistant noticed, and the person's routines (a settings page); signed-in people only |
| `GET /snap` | every card the person may use (a gallery); visitors see the public capabilities |
| `GET /snap/c/{capability}` | one card at its own address |
| `POST /snap/run` | a card sent (`snap_run`, a `Route::action`) |
| `POST /snap/call/{name}` | the `snap_*` capabilities the pages call, and only them, as the signed-in person |

Changes only ever run from a Confirm the person clicks.
## <a name="options"></a>Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `assistant` | `'/assistant'` | the path of the assistant and its pages |
| `cards` | `'/snap'` | the path of the cards and their routes |

```php
Route::snap(['assistant' => '/help', 'cards' => '/cards']);
```
## Reference

+ [`Route::snap()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-snap)
+ [Snap in the API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap):
  [`Snap\Cards`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards),
  [`Snap\Consent`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-consent),
  [`Snap\Setup`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-setup)
## Common mistakes

+ **"Snap is almost ready" (503)** on every Snap page: its `caligrafy_snap_*` tables are missing. Run
  `php caligrafer.php snap install` or `platform install` (after an `update` to 2.23.0, run one of them locally).
+ **`Route::snap()` without `Auth::authentication(...)` above it**: `/assistant` and `/assistant/noticed` are signed-in
  pages, and opening them stops with "'signedIn', 'level' and 'visitorsOnly' need Auth::authentication(...) in web.php".
+ **Expecting `async: true` to change REST or MCP**: `#[Capability(..., async: true)]` only changes Snap, where the
  card runs in the background as a Track: Task card.

## Related pages

+ [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant)
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
+ [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)
+ [Release notes 2.23.0](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-2.23.0)

# Capability routes: REST, the JS client, MCP, notifications and bots

Five lines of `web.php` serve the capabilities to programs instead of browsers: one capability at one REST address
(`Route::capability`), all of them for the JS client (`Route::capabilities`), all of them as tools for AI agents
(`Route::mcp`), and two framework sets of routes, the pages of notification emails (`Route::notifications`) and the data
routes of the Watson bot apps (`Route::bots`).

```php
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');          // one route, one capability, JSON
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');       // {id} becomes the input "id"
Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');                          // GET lists, POST /capabilities/{name} calls
Route::mcp('/mcp');                                            // AI agents: the capabilities their token allows
Route::notifications();                                        // the confirm and unsubscribe pages of notification emails
Route::bots();                                                 // the data routes of the Watson bot apps
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write: also as POST /api/books, for the JS client, and for AI agents
```

**Check** before you say OK:
+ each REST route names a capability, never a closure;
+ `Route::mcp` is there when agents should use the app, and a token is created with only the scopes they need;
+ `php caligrafer.php client` was run again after adding or changing a capability.
## <a name="what"></a>What each one declares

| Line | Declares | Who calls |
|---|---|---|
| `Route::capability($method, $route, $name)` | `$method $route` (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE`; anything else stops with an error) | programs with a personal access token, or a page of the app with the session |
| `Route::capabilities($prefix = '/capabilities')` | `GET {prefix}` (what the caller may call, with the input schemas and the session's CSRF token) and `POST {prefix}/{name}` | the JS client of the Vue apps and the SPA |
| `Route::mcp($route = '/mcp')` | `POST {route}` (one JSON-RPC message per request); `GET` and `DELETE` answer `405` | AI agents, with a personal access token only |
| `Route::notifications()` | `GET /notify/confirm/{token}`, `GET` and `POST /notify/unsubscribe` | the links of notification emails (2.15.0) |
| `Route::bots()` | `POST /__bots__/{appName}/communicate`, `POST /__bots__/{appName}/{appId}`, `DELETE /__bots__/{appName}` | the Watson bot apps of `public/` (2.21.0) |
## <a name="rest"></a>REST: `Route::capability`

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/books/3
# {"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred","published_year":1979,...}}            200: get_book is public

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"title": "X", "published_year": 1971, "author_id": 42}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
# {"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"author_id":"There is no such author"}}}   422
```

+ **Requests**: a JSON body, form fields, or the query string for `GET`. Then the route variables, which win
  (`/books/3?id=9` gives `id = 3`, 2.21.2).
+ **Responses**: `200` with `{"data": ...}`, `201` when a `POST` changes data, or `{"error": {"code", "message",
  "fields"}}` with `401` (and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), `403`, `404`, `409` or `422`.
+ **Who calls**: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the session of a signed-in person. A session call that changes data
  needs the `X-CSRF-Token` header (`403` "Missing or invalid CSRF token" otherwise).
+ A `POST` with neither a token nor `Accept: application/json` is taken for a form and answers `403` `[ERROR 3000]`.
+ Files: a `file` rule takes the uploaded file ([File uploads](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/File-Uploads)).
## <a name="client"></a>The JS client: `Route::capabilities`

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js
```

writes one JavaScript function per capability, calling `/capabilities`. In a page of the app it uses the session (the
cookie, and the CSRF token it reads once from `GET /capabilities`); from Node or another site, a token:
`configure({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', token: process.env.CALIGRAFY_TOKEN })`.
`GET /capabilities` answers `{"data": [{"name", "description", "scope", "level", "readOnly", "destructive", "public",
"input"}, ...], "csrf": "<the session's CSRF token>"}`. More:
[The JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#client).
## <a name="mcp"></a>AI agents: `Route::mcp`

Every capability the token allows is a tool, with its description, its input schema and the hints `readOnlyHint` and
`destructiveHint`. A refused call is a tool result with `"isError": true`, so the agent can correct itself.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http bookshelf http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cq_..."
```

Without a token it answers `401` with `WWW-Authenticate` (2.19.1). MCP addresses skip the form CSRF check: the token is
the proof. More: [MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#mcp).
## Reference

+ [`Route::capability()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-capability),
  [`Route::capabilities()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-capabilities),
  [`Route::mcp()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-mcp),
  [`Route::notifications()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-notifications),
  [`Route::bots()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-bots)
+ [`Caligrafy\Rest`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#rest),
  [`Caligrafy\Client`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#client),
  [`Caligrafy\Mcp\Http`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-http),
  [`Caligrafy\Mcp\Server`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-server)
## Common mistakes

+ **A JSON write with the session and no `X-CSRF-Token`**: `403`. The JS client sends it; `fetch()` by hand must too.
+ **Data work in a closure route** (`Route::post('/x', function () {...})`): it has no permission rules and no CSRF
  check for JSON calls. Use `Route::capability`.
+ **MCP with the legacy API key**: refused (`401`); agents use personal access tokens.
+ **A `webOnly` capability behind these routes**: it answers "There is no capability"; only `Route::action` reaches it.
+ **A webhook's capability** is served by these routes too: guard it with `$context->actorType() !== 'webhook'`
  ([Webhooks](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Webhook)).

## Related pages

+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)
+ [Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)
+ [Creating bots with Watson](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.1-Creating-Bots-with-Watson)
+ [Vue: calling capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities)
+ [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#capabilityroutes)

# How to export a list as CSV

A link people click to download a list as a spreadsheet: one read-only capability that returns the rows, and one line
of `web.php`, `Route::download`. The same capability keeps serving the page, REST and agents. This guide exports the
authors of the Bookshelf, with a narrow set of columns and a dated file name.

Before you start: the Bookshelf tables of
[Routing, steps 1 to 3](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#definingroutes). The commands run in
the project folder (with Docker: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability export_authors books:read read-only public: the authors (id, name) sorted by name, downloadable as authors-<date>.csv from the authors page
```
## By hand

1. **The capability.** Run:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ExportAuthors --scope books:read --read-only
   ```

   Make `application/services/Bookshelf/ExportAuthors.php` read:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Database;
   use Caligrafy\Service;

   #[Capability(
       name: 'export_authors',
       description: 'Lists the authors of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by name: id and name.',
       scope: 'books:read',
       readOnly: true,
       public: true
   )]
   class ExportAuthors extends Service
   {
       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           // arrays, not models: the columns of the file are the keys of the first row
           return Database::table('authors')->select('id', 'name')->orderBy('name')->get();
       }
   }
   ```

   It returns `get()`, every row; a `paginate()` page would export one page only.

2. **The route.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

   ```php
       Route::download('/authors.csv', 'export_authors', [
           'columns' => ['id', 'name'],
           'filename' => fn ($rows, $input) => 'authors-' . date('Y-m-d') . '.csv',
           'bom' => true,
       ]);
   ```

   `columns` writes the header row even when there is no author yet; `bom` lets Excel read the accents.

3. **The link.** In the authors' page view:

   ```pug
   a.btn.btn-secondary(href=$home . 'authors.csv') Download as CSV
   ```

4. **Try it.** Run:

   ```bash
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors.csv
   ```

   It answers `200` with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment;
   filename="authors-<today>.csv"`, the header row `id,name` and one line per author, lines ending with CRLF.
## Variations

+ **Filtered**: the query string and the route variables are the capability's inputs. A capability that declares
  `public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer');` and filters on it is exported for one author with
  `/books.csv?author_id=2`; `?author_id=abc` answers `422` with the error as JSON.
+ **For signed-in people only**: drop `public: true`. A visitor who opens the link is sent to `/login` (`signIn` sets
  another page).
+ **JSON instead**: `'as' => 'json'`.
+ **The files themselves**: `'as' => 'zip'` ([Downloads, ZIP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Download#zip)).
## Common mistakes

+ **A model query** (`Author::query()->select('id', 'name')->get()`): models carry every property, so every column of
  `Author` is in the file, empty. Return arrays (`Database::table(...)` or `->arrays()`).
+ **A capability that is not read-only**: `Route::download` refuses it.

## Related pages

+ [Downloads: `Route::download`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Download): every option
+ [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries)
+ [`Route::download()` in the API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-download)
