# Controllers

A controller is a PHP class whose actions answer routes. It is how Caligrafy applications answered custom requests
before 2.21.0, and **a new application does not need one**: every request can be declared in one line of `web.php`
([Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes)), the rules of a feature live in a capability
(`application/services/`), and what a page or a form cannot say is a web-only capability served by `Route::action`.

Existing controllers keep working, with nothing to change. This page says what replaces each use of a controller, shows
how to move one, and documents the controllers you may still have.

## <a name="when"></a>What replaces a controller

| You need | Write | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A page, with or without data | `Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']]);` | [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#pageroutes) |
| A page only signed-in people or administrators open | `Route::page(..., ['signedIn' => true])` or `['level' => 1]` | the same |
| A page that sends people back after signing in | `Route::page(..., ['signedIn' => true, 'comeBack' => true])` | the same |
| A page for visitors only | `Route::page('/join', 'Bookshelf/join', ['visitorsOnly' => '/books']);` | the same |
| A page that reads the query string | `Route::page(..., ['query' => ['sort' => 'title']])` | the same |
| A Vue, bot or machine learning app | `Route::page('/apps/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']]);` | [Routes for client apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.2-Routes) |
| A form that creates, changes or deletes | `Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}']);` | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form) |
| A sign-up with a confirmation field, a box to tick, that signs in | `Route::form` with `same`, `accepted`, `signsIn` | the same |
| A form that leaves for a payment page | `Route::form` with `'success' => fn ($r) => $r['url']` | [Payments](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.2-Stripe-&-Cryptocurrency-Payment) |
| Password reset | `Route::page` and `Route::form` on two capabilities | [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#passwordreset) |
| Sign-in, sign-out, sign-up | `Route::auth(['home' => '/books']);` | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#auth) |
| Events Stripe or another service posts | `Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_event', ['verify' => 'stripe']);` | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webhook) |
| A CSV or JSON file to download | `Route::download('/books.csv', 'list_books');` | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#download) |
| An address that moved | `Route::redirect('/old/books/{id}', '/books/{id}', 301);` | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#redirect) |
| A JSON API | `Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');` | [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#capabilityroutes) |
| Several capabilities with conditions, a choice between a redirect and a view | `Route::action` and a web-only capability | [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action) |
| The session, a sign-in of your own (face, another site), a gate, a payment page, custom headers | the same | [the same](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webonly) |

`AdminController`, `AuthController`, `AIController`, `ClientController` and `WatsonController` ship in
`application/controllers/core/`, and the routes of a new project's `web.php` still name them. They are examples that work:
leave them, or replace their lines with the routes above.

## With Claude

```text
"Move application/controllers/BookController.php to declared routes."
"Add GET /authors/{author_id}/books: when the author has exactly one book, go straight to that book's page;
otherwise show the list."
```

For a new request, the `caligrafy` skill never writes a controller: Claude writes a capability in
`application/services/<Folder>/`, `webOnly: true` only when the request needs it, and one line of
`application/config/routing/web.php`. To move an existing controller, it writes one capability per action, swaps the
routes, removes the controller, and runs `php caligrafer.php test`. Ask the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent to review it: it
flags new controllers where a declared route fits.

**Check**

- [ ] `application/controllers/` got no new file.
- [ ] A capability with `webOnly: true` is one that returns a view or a redirect, reads the session, or signs someone
      in. The rest stays a plain capability, which REST and agents can reach.
- [ ] The web-only capability calls other capabilities with `$this->capability()`.
- [ ] `/authors/3/books` redirects and `/authors/2/books` shows the list.

## <a name="controllerstartup"></a>By hand: move a controller to a declared route

Before you start: the Bookshelf tables, the `Book` model, `list_books`, `get_book` and the views of
[Routing, steps 1 to 5](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#definingroutes). You have this controller, and want it gone:

```php
<?php
// application/controllers/BookController.php

use Caligrafy\Controller;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

class BookController extends Controller
{
    // GET /authors/{author_id}/books: one book goes straight to its page, otherwise the list
    public function byAuthor()
    {
        try {
            $books = $this->call('list_books', array('author_id' => $this->request->fetch('author_id')));
        } catch (ServiceError $e) {
            http_response_code($e->status());
            return view('Bookshelf/notfound', array('message' => $e->getMessage()));
        }
        if ($books['total'] == 1) {
            redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
            return null;
        }
        return view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
    }
}
```

```php
Route::get('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'BookController@byAuthor');
```

1. <a name="createcontroller"></a>**Write the capability.** Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks`, and replace the content of
   `application/services/Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks.php` with:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Service;
   use Caligrafy\Web;

   // open_author_books: one book goes straight to its page, otherwise the list
   #[Capability(
       name: 'open_author_books',
       description: 'Opens the books of an author: the book itself when there is one, otherwise the list.',
       readOnly: true,
       public: true,
       webOnly: true
   )]
   class OpenAuthorBooks extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('author_id' => 'required|integer');

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
           if ($books['total'] == 1) {
               return Web::redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
           }
           return Web::view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
       }
   }
   ```

   Each action becomes one capability. `$this->call()` becomes `$this->capability($name, $input, $context)`, `view()`
   `Web::view()`, `redirect()` `Web::redirect()`, `api()` `Web::json()`, and `$this->request->fetch('author_id')` an input
   declared in `$rules`.

2. <a name="controllerrouting"></a>**Swap the route.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, replace the
   `Route::get` line with:

   ```php
       Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books', ['back' => '/books']);
   ```

3. **Remove the controller.** Delete `application/controllers/BookController.php`.

4. **Try it.** Run:

   ```bash
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/3/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/authors/2/books
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/authors/9/books
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/abc/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
   ```

   They print `HTTP/1.1 302 Found` with `Location: http://localhost:8080/books/5` (Italo Calvino has one book, *Invisible
   Cities*), `200` (Octavia E. Butler's two books), `200` (the list with "No books yet.": nobody has the id 9) and
   `302` with `Location: http://localhost:8080/books` (`author_id` must be an integer: the `back` option, with the message
   in `flash('error')`).

   A JSON call needs the page's `X-CSRF-Token` header or a token that grants `*`, as on a controller route:

   ```bash
   curl -s -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/authors/3/books
   ```

   prints `{"error":{"code":1004,"message":"Access Denied: send the page's CSRF token in an X-CSRF-Token header (pages,
   with the session cookie) or Authorization: Bearer <personal access token> (programs and agents)"}}` with `401`.

**Check**

- [ ] `/authors/3/books` redirects to `/books/5`, and `/authors/abc/books` to `/books`, not `500`.
- [ ] `php caligrafer.php call open_author_books author_id=3` answers `not_found`: only the route reaches it.
- [ ] `application/controllers/` no longer has the class, and `grep -n BookController application/config/routing/web.php`
      prints nothing.

**What moves, and what does not**

| In the controller | In the web-only capability |
| --- | --- |
| `$this->call('x', $input)` | `$this->capability('x', $input, $context)` |
| `$this->request->fetch('id')`, `$this->request->parameters()` | an input declared in `$rules` |
| `view('X', $data)`, with `'authorized' => authorized()` by hand | `Web::view('X', $data)`: `$authorized` and `$user` are given |
| `redirect('/x'); return;` | `return Web::redirect('/x');` |
| `http_response_code(422); return api($data);` | `return Web::json($data, 422);` |
| `header('X: y');` | `Web::text('...')->header('X', 'y')`, on any `Web` |
| `guard('permissions', 1);` | `'level' => 1` on the route, or `level: 1` on the capability |
| `try { ... } catch (ServiceError $e)` | nothing, unless you answer it yourself: `Route::action` sends it back like a form |
| `$_SESSION`, `authorized()`, `user()` | the same, a web-only capability may read them |
| a form and `=csrf()` | the same: a form's `POST` needs its token |
| a file: `uploadFile($this->request->files('x'))` | a `file` rule in `$rules`: `handle()` gets the URL |

## <a name="callcapability"></a>In a controller you keep: `$this->call()`

```php
$book = $this->call('create_book');                                  // inputs: the route variables and the request's fields
$books = $this->call('list_books', array('author_id' => 2));         // inputs you give
```

`$this->call($name, $input = null)` runs the capability as the person who sent the request (the signed-in user, a
token, or a visitor), with its validation, its permissions and its audit, exactly as REST and AI agents call it. It
returns plain data (arrays: `$book['id']`) or throws `Caligrafy\ServiceError`. It answers `not_found` for a capability
declared `webOnly: true`.

| `$e->kind` | `$e->status()` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid` | `422` | an input breaks a rule; `$e->fields` is `['title' => 'The Title field is required', ...]` |
| `unauthenticated` | `401` | the capability needs someone and nobody is signed in |
| `forbidden` | `403` | the person lacks the level, or the token the scope |
| `not_found` | `404` | the capability found nothing |
| `conflict` | `409` | a duplicate |

Without `$input`, the inputs are the route variables and the request's parameters (the form fields, the JSON body or,
for a `GET`, the query string); only the inputs the capability declares in `$rules` reach it. `$this->call()` does not
take uploaded files: a form with a file input posts to `Route::form`, `Route::action` or a capability route. The
framework's own user administration works this way: `AdminController` calls `list_users`, `get_user`, `update_user` and `delete_user`
([Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#usercapabilities)).

## <a name="namespacedcontrollers"></a>Namespaced controllers

A controller can live in a namespace. Declare it at the top of the file and use the full name in the route:

```php
<?php
// application/controllers/Shop/ReportController.php
namespace Shop;

use Caligrafy\Controller;

class ReportController extends Controller
{
    public function show()
    {
        header('Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8');
        echo 'Report ' . $this->request->fetch('id');
    }
}
```

```php
Route::get('/reports/{id}', 'Shop\ReportController@show');
```

`curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/reports/7` answers `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and
`Report 7`.

How the router finds the class of `'Name@action'`:

1. a declared class named `Name` (global or fully qualified, with or without a leading `\`) is used: your own
   `AIController` wins over the example one;
2. otherwise, a short name (no backslash) falls back to the example controllers of `Caligrafy\Controllers`
   (`application/controllers/core/`: `AIController`, `AdminController`, `AuthController`, `ClientController`,
   `WatsonController`), so routes such as `'ClientController'` keep working;
3. otherwise the request answers `404` `[ERROR 1001] Invalid Controller or Action`, as for a missing action.

In a PHP single-quoted string `'Shop\ReportController'` and `'Shop\\ReportController'` are the same. The routes of a
new project use the full names (`'Caligrafy\\Controllers\\ClientController'`). Two classes with the same fully
qualified name in `application/` are an error.

## <a name="controllermethods"></a>Reference

A controller extends `Caligrafy\Controller`. Without an action in the route (`'BookController'`), `index()` runs; the
base `index()` does nothing. Do not give your own methods the names below.

| Property | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `$this->request` | the [Request](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/3.-Request) |
| `$this->validator` | a `Caligrafy\Validator` (GUMP with the framework's rules) |
| `$this->model` | the model set by `associate()` (an empty `Model` otherwise) |
| `$this->connection` | the database connection (PDO), or `null` |
| `$this->payment` | the Stripe module after `activatePayment()`, else `null` |
| `$this->loader` | `Caligrafy\Loader`: `library($name)`, `helper($name)` include a file of `framework/librairies` or `framework/helpers` |

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `call($name, $input = null)` | runs a capability as the person who sent the request ([above](#callcapability)) |
| `view($viewName, $viewData = [])` | renders a Pug view; a request that asks for JSON gets `$viewData` as JSON |
| `api($viewData = [])` | answers `$viewData` as JSON |
| `check($data, $rules = [], $filters = [])`, `validate($data, $rules)`, `filter($data, $filters)` | GUMP validation and filtering ([Validation](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation#validationandfiltering)) |
| `activatePayment()` | sets `$this->payment` to a new `Caligrafy\Payment` |
| `associate($modelName, $table)`, `all()`, `find()`, `save()`, `delete()`, `search()`, `table()` | the classic model methods ([Other ways](#controllercontext)) |

`redirect('/path')` only sends a `Location` header: `return` right after it. Set a status with
`http_response_code($code)` before `view()` or `api()`.

## <a name="controllercontext"></a>Other ways: controllers that read and write models

Before capabilities, a controller read and wrote its model itself. These methods still work, for existing projects; a
new feature is a capability with `Route::form` or `Route::capability` instead, so the web, REST and agents follow the
same rules.

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Controller;

class LegacyBookController extends Controller
{
    public function show()
    {
        $this->associate('Book', 'books');   // the model class (or a Model object) and its table
        return api($this->find());           // the id comes from the {id} route variable
    }
}
```

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `associate($modelName, $table)` | sets `$this->model`; call it again to work on another model in the same controller |
| `all($args = [])` | every row; `$args` adds `condition`, `order`, `limit` (raw SQL) and `bindings` |
| `find($id = null)` | one row; without `$id`, the `{id}` route variable |
| `save($inputs, $id = null)` | updates the row `$id` (or the `{id}` route variable), else creates one |
| `delete($id = null)` | deletes the row `$id` (or the `{id}` route variable) |
| `search($scope = null, $keywords = null)` | rows whose columns `$scope` (comma separated) match `$keywords` (bound; `%` and `_` are wildcards) |
| `table()` | the table of `$this->model` |

+ **`{id}` routes**: `find()`, `save()` and `delete()` take the `{id}` route variable when no id is given. On
  `POST /books/{id}/reviews`, `$this->save($review)` **updates** the review whose id is the book's id. Name the
  variable `{book_id}` or pass the id.
+ **`all($args)` clauses are SQL**: never put input in them; use `?` and `bindings`.
+ The replacement: a capability that uses the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries),
  served with `Route::page`, `Route::form` and `Route::capability`.

## Common mistakes

+ **A new controller**: every request can be declared. A form post is `Route::form`, in one line, with `errors()`,
  `old()` and `flash()`; the rest is `Route::action`.
+ **Code after `redirect()`** keeps running: `return` after it.
+ **A JSON call from a page without `X-CSRF-Token`** answers `401` `[ERROR 1004]`: send `apiHeaders()` (Vue apps)
  or the token in the header.
+ **A scoped token on a controller route** is refused: controller routes, like `Route::action`, need a token that grants
  `*`. Give programs capability routes with scoped tokens instead.
+ **A short controller name that collides with an example controller** (`AuthController`): yours wins when it is
  declared; otherwise the example one answers.
+ **Overriding a base method** (`find`, `save`, `view`, `call`...) breaks the controller.

## Related pages

+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes): what replaces controllers
+ [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#controllerroute): controller and closure routes
+ [Request](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/3.-Request): `$this->request`
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service)
+ [Validation](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-To-Move-a-Controller-Route-to-a-Declared-Route -->

# How to move a controller route to a declared route

Since 2.21.0 every request can be declared in one line of `web.php`, and a new application needs no controller.
Existing controllers keep working; this guide moves one action, `BookController@byAuthor`, to a web-only capability
served by `Route::action`, then removes the controller. The same steps move any action.

Before you start: the Bookshelf tables, the `Book` model, `list_books`, `get_book` and the views of
[Routing, steps 1 to 5](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#definingroutes).
## With Claude

```text
"Move application/controllers/BookController.php to declared routes."
```

Claude writes one capability per action, swaps the routes, removes the controller, and runs `php caligrafer.php test`.
Ask the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent to review it: it flags controllers where a declared route fits.
## 1. Pick the route type

Most actions are not web-only. Choose the narrowest line that says what the action does:

| The action | Declare it with |
|---|---|
| shows a view, with data | [`Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Page) and read-only capabilities |
| saves a form, then redirects | [`Route::form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Form) |
| sign-in, sign-out, sign-up | [`Route::auth`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Auth) |
| receives another service's events | [`Route::webhook`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Webhook) |
| sends a file | [`Route::download`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Download) |
| always sends to the same address | [`Route::redirect`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Redirect) |
| answers JSON to programs | [`Route::capability`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Capability-and-REST) |
| chooses between a view and a redirect, reads the session, signs someone in | [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action) |

The action below chooses between a redirect and a view: a `Route::action`.
## 2. The controller you have

```php
<?php
// application/controllers/BookController.php

use Caligrafy\Controller;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

class BookController extends Controller
{
    // GET /authors/{author_id}/books: one book goes straight to its page, otherwise the list
    public function byAuthor()
    {
        try {
            $books = $this->call('list_books', array('author_id' => $this->request->fetch('author_id')));
        } catch (ServiceError $e) {
            http_response_code($e->status());
            return view('Bookshelf/notfound', array('message' => $e->getMessage()));
        }
        if ($books['total'] == 1) {
            redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
            return null;
        }
        return view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
    }
}
```

```php
Route::get('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'BookController@byAuthor');
```
## 3. Write the capability

Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks`, and make
`application/services/Bookshelf/OpenAuthorBooks.php` read:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\Web;

// open_author_books: one book goes straight to its page, otherwise the list
#[Capability(
    name: 'open_author_books',
    description: 'Opens the books of an author: the book itself when there is one, otherwise the list.',
    readOnly: true,
    public: true,
    webOnly: true
)]
class OpenAuthorBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'required|integer');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
        if ($books['total'] == 1) {
            return Web::redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']);
        }
        return Web::view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
    }
}
```

**What moves, and how:**

| In the controller | In the web-only capability |
| --- | --- |
| `$this->call('x', $input)` | `$this->capability('x', $input, $context)` |
| `$this->request->fetch('id')`, `$this->request->parameters()` | an input declared in `$rules` |
| `view('X', $data)`, with `'authorized' => authorized()` by hand | `Web::view('X', $data)`: `$authorized` and `$user` are given |
| `redirect('/x'); return;` | `return Web::redirect('/x');` |
| `http_response_code(422); return api($data);` | `return Web::json($data, 422);` |
| `header('X: y');` | `Web::text('...')->header('X', 'y')`, on any `Web` |
| `guard('permissions', 1);` | `'level' => 1` on the route, or `level: 1` on the capability |
| `try { ... } catch (ServiceError $e)` | nothing, unless you answer it yourself: `Route::action` sends it back like a form |
| `$_SESSION`, `authorized()`, `user()` | the same, a web-only capability may read them |
| a form and `=csrf()` | the same: a form's `POST` needs its token |
| a file: `uploadFile($this->request->files('x'))` | a `file` rule in `$rules`: `handle()` gets the URL |
## 4. Swap the route

In `application/config/routing/web.php`, replace the `Route::get` line with:

```php
    Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books', ['back' => '/books']);
```
## 5. Remove the controller and try it

Delete `application/controllers/BookController.php`, then run:

```bash
curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/3/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/authors/2/books
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/authors/9/books
curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/authors/abc/books | grep -iE "^HTTP|^Location"
```

They print `302` with `Location: http://localhost:8080/books/5` (one book), `200` (two books), `200` (the list with
"No books yet.": nobody has the id 9) and `302` to `/books` (`author_id` must be an integer: the `back` option, with
the message in `flash('error')`).

**Check**

- [ ] `/authors/3/books` redirects to `/books/5`, and `/authors/abc/books` to `/books`, not `500`.
- [ ] `php caligrafer.php call open_author_books author_id=3` answers `not_found`: only the route reaches it.
- [ ] `grep -n BookController application/config/routing/web.php` prints nothing.
- [ ] `php caligrafer.php test` passes; a test of the action uses `$this->action(...)`, not `$this->call(...)`.
## Common mistakes

+ **Everything made web-only**: a web-only capability is reached by `Route::action` only. Work that REST, the JS client
  or agents also need stays a plain capability, called with `$this->capability()`.
+ **A JSON call without `X-CSRF-Token`**: `401` `[ERROR 1004]`, as on the controller route it replaces.
+ **Moving the examples that ship in `application/controllers/core/`** (`AdminController`, `AuthController`,
  `AIController`, `ClientController`, `WatsonController`): they work; leave them, or replace their lines with
  `Route::auth`, `Route::page('/apps/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']])` and `Route::bots()`.

## Related pages

+ [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers): the controllers you may still have
+ [Everything else: `Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Route-Action)
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#controller)
+ [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App#helpers)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.-Helpers-%2C-Forms-%26-REST-API -->

# Helpers, forms and REST API

Three things that every Caligrafy app uses: the **global helpers** (functions such as `view()`, `redirect()`,
`csrf()`, `old()`), **forms** (a form posts to a capability with `Route::form`, protected by a CSRF token), and the
**REST API** (each capability as a JSON endpoint with `Route::capability`, called with a personal access token). The
same capability answers the form, the API, the Vue apps and AI agents.

## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write
"Give create_book a REST endpoint at POST /api/books, and a token for my import script."
```

Claude writes the capability, the `Route::capability` line in `application/config/routing/web.php`, and creates the
token with `php caligrafer.php token create "<what it is for>" --scopes books:write`. The token is shown once: store it
as a secret yourself; Claude never writes it into a file of the project. For a form, the same skill writes
`Route::form` and the view ([Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form)).

**Check**

- [ ] `curl` with the token answers `201` and `{"data": ...}`; without it, `401`.
- [ ] A token without the scope answers `403` "This needs the scope books:write".
- [ ] A missing input answers `422` with `fields`.
- [ ] No token, key or secret was written to a file of the project or printed in a commit.

## By hand: a REST API

Before you start: the Bookshelf tables, `list_books` and `get_book` of
[Routing, steps 1 to 3](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing#definingroutes), and `create_book`
of [Declarative routes, step 1](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form). The
framework tables must be installed (`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install`, done by the
Quickstart).

1. **Declare the endpoints.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

   ```php
       // the Bookshelf REST API: one route, one capability
       Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');
       Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');
       Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
   ```

2. **Create a token for the program that calls it.** Run:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "Bookshelf script" --scopes "books:read,books:write"
   ```

   It prints ` Token #<n> "Bookshelf script" created with books:read books:write`, the token (`cq_<id>_<40 hex
   characters>`) and ` It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).`

3. **Call the API.** Run:

   ```bash
   curl -s -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/books/3
   ```

   It prints `{"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred","published_year":1979,"summary":"A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.","author_id":2,"created_at":"...","modified_at":"...","author":{"id":2,"name":"Octavia E. Butler",...}}}`
   (`get_book` is public: no token needed). Create a book with the token:

   ```bash
   curl -s -i -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_..." \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/books \
        -d '{"title":"The Dispossessed","published_year":1974,"author_id":1}'
   ```

   It answers `201` with `{"data":{"id":<new id>,"title":"The Dispossessed","published_year":1974,...,"author":{"id":1,"name":"Ursula K. Le Guin",...}}}`.
   The same call without the `Authorization` header answers `401` with
   `{"error":{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"Sign in or send a personal access token"}}`; with
   `-d '{"title":"","published_year":1969,"author_id":9}'` it answers `422` with
   `{"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"title":"The Title field is required","author_id":"There is no such author"}}}`.

**Check**

- [ ] `GET /api/books` answers `{"data":{"data":[...],"total":6,"page":1,"per_page":20,"pages":1}}` (a page of
      `list_books`).
- [ ] `POST /api/books` with the token answers `201`; without it `401`; with a `books:read` token `403`.
- [ ] `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit --capability create_book` lists the call.

## <a name="restapi"></a>REST API

A capability becomes a JSON endpoint in one line. The route variables become inputs (`{id}` is the input `id`).

```php
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');
Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
Route::capability('PUT', '/api/books/{id}', 'update_book');
Route::capability('DELETE', '/api/books/{id}', 'delete_book');
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // GET /capabilities lists what the caller may call; POST /capabilities/{name} calls one
```

**Who may call.** A personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer cq_...`) that grants the capability's scope
(`books:write`, `books:*` or `*`), or the signed-in person (a page of the app, with the session cookie). A session call
that changes data also sends the CSRF token in an `X-CSRF-Token` header (`GET /capabilities` returns it in `csrf`; the
Vue apps send it with `apiHeaders()`). A `public: true` capability answers anyone. Tokens:
`php caligrafer.php token create <name> --scopes <scopes> [--user <id>] [--expires <days>]`, `token list`,
`token revoke <id>` ([Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#tokens)).

**Inputs.** The JSON body (or the form fields, or the query string for a `GET`), and the route variables, which win
(2.21.2: `/api/books/3?id=9` is the book 3).
Only the inputs the capability declares in `$rules` reach it. A `file` input takes a multipart upload
(`curl -F "cover=@cover.png"`) ([File inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#files)).

**Answers.**

| Status | Body | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | `{"data": ...}` | the capability answered |
| `201` | `{"data": ...}` | a `POST` to a capability that changes data |
| `401` | `{"error":{"code":"unauthenticated",...}}` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`) | nobody signed in and no valid token |
| `403` | `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"This needs the scope books:write"}}` | the token lacks the scope, the person the level, or a session write lacks `X-CSRF-Token` |
| `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found",...}}` | the capability found nothing |
| `409` | `{"error":{"code":"conflict",...}}` | a duplicate |
| `422` | `{"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"...","fields":{"title":"..."}}}` | an input breaks a rule |

**Errors of the framework** (not of a capability) answer with a real status too, and JSON to a JSON request:

| Status | Error | When |
| - | - | - |
| `401` | `1004` Access Denied | a JSON call to `Route::action` or a controller route, `GET` included, without `X-CSRF-Token` (pages) or a token that grants `*`. The message ends with the reason |
| `403` | `3000` Cross Site Forgery | a form post without a valid `_token` |
| `403` | `1006` Forbidden | a `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::action` or `Route::download` whose capability refuses the person |
| `404` | `1001` Invalid Controller or Action | a route names a controller or an action that does not exist |
| `404` | `1005` Page Not Found | no route matches, or a page's capability finds nothing |
| `405` | `1000` Invalid Http Request Method | the address exists with other methods (`Allow` header) |
| `500` | any other error | the message is shown only with `APP_DEBUG=true` for PHP fatal errors |

```json
{"error":{"code":1005,"message":"Page Not Found"}}
```

Test with `curl` or an API client (Postman, Bruno): set `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`
for a JSON body, and the `Authorization: Bearer cq_...` header.

### Other ways: controller APIs and the legacy API key

Before capabilities, an API was a controller whose actions returned `api($data)`:

```php
Route::get('/legacy/books/{id}', 'LegacyBookController@show');   // the controller of 8.-Controllers, Other ways
```

+ A JSON call to a controller route needs, with `Auth::activateAPI();` in `web.php` (the template has it), a token
  that grants **everything** (`--scopes "*"`), or the page's `X-CSRF-Token` header. Scoped tokens are refused there:
  give programs capability routes instead.
+ **The legacy API key** (`php caligrafer.php generatekeys`, `generateapikey`) is the `APP_KEY` encrypted with itself:
  every key of one `APP_KEY` is valid, and they cannot be revoked one by one. It still works while `LEGACY_API_KEY` is
  not `false` (Caligrafy Cloud sets `false`). Give each program a personal access token instead.
+ `api($data)` and `view(null, $data)` print `$data` as JSON; set a status first with `http_response_code()`. The
  replacement is a capability with `Route::capability`: the same rules for the web, REST and agents.

## <a name="forms"></a>Forms

A form posts to `Route::form`, which calls a capability and redirects
([Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form) has the complete
example):

```php
Route::page('/books/new', 'Bookshelf/new', ['signedIn' => true, 'data' => ['authors' => 'list_authors']]);
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Book added']);
Route::form('/books/{id}', 'update_book', ['method' => 'PUT', 'success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Saved']);
```

```pug
form(method='POST', action=$home . 'books')
  =csrf()
  .cq-field
    label(for='title') Title
    input#title.form-control(type='text', name='title', value=old('title'))
    if errors('title')
      p.cq-field-error= errors('title')
  button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Add book
```

| In the view | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `=csrf()` | `<input type='hidden' name='_token' value='<the session's CSRF token>'>`: every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` form needs it |
| `=methodField('PUT')` | `<input type='hidden' name='_method' value='PUT'>`: the form reaches a `PUT` (or `DELETE`) route |
| `errors('title')` | the message of the field after a refused post, or `null`; `errors()` gives them all |
| `old('title', $default)` | what the field held after a refused post, else `$default` (never passwords or other secrets) |
| `flash('success')`, `flash('error')` | the message of the previous post; `flash('key', 'text')` keeps one for the next request |

**CSRF** (cross-site request forgery: another site making your visitor's browser post to your app). The framework
checks every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` that is not JSON: its `_token` must be the session's token, else `403`
`[ERROR 3000] Security Error - Cross Site Forgery`. A script that sends JSON sends the token in an `X-CSRF-Token`
header instead. Read the token with `session('token')`, never `$_SESSION['token']`: since 2.19.0 a session starts
only when it is needed.

A form that does more than call one capability and redirect posts to a
[`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action) (`'method' => 'POST'`): same `=csrf()`, same `errors()`, `old()` and `flash()` after a
refusal, and the capability chooses what comes next. In plain HTML the field is
`<input type="hidden" name="_token" value="<?= session('token') ?>">`.

### Other ways: a hand-written form to a controller

A form in older code posts to a controller route (`Route::post('/books', 'BookController@store')`) whose action calls
`$this->call('create_book')` and renders the errors itself. It keeps working
([Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers#callcapability)), and it needs `=csrf()` too.

## <a name="helpers"></a>Helpers

Global functions of `framework/helpers/corehelpers.php`, available everywhere in `application/` and in the views.

**Views, requests and routing**

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `view($viewName, $viewData = [])` | renders `application/views/<viewName>.pug` with the data; a request that asks for JSON gets the data as JSON |
| `api($viewData = [])` | answers the data as JSON |
| `redirect($url)` | sends a `Location` header: a path of the site, or a full `http(s)://` address as it is. It does not stop the script: `return` after it |
| `request()` | a new `Caligrafy\Request` |
| `currentRoute()`, `currentBind()` | the matched route pattern and its variables |
| `csrf()`, `methodField($method)` | print the hidden `_token` and `_method` inputs (`=csrf()` in Pug) |
| `errors($field = null)`, `old($field, $default = '')`, `flash($key, $value = null)` | the form helpers ([above](#forms)) |
| `connect()` | the database connection (PDO) |
| `import($filename)` | includes `framework/librairies/<name>.php` or `framework/helpers/<name>.php` |

**Session and page settings**

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `session($key, $value = null)` | reads a session value, or saves one (any value but `null`, including `0`, `''` and `false`) |
| `saveInSession($data, $name)`, `clearFromSession($name)` | save or remove a session value |
| `scripts($key, $value = null)` | the URL of a front-end library (`bootstrap_css`, `bootstrap_script`, `vue`, `axios`, `jquery`, `wysiwyg_css`, `wysiwyg_js`...), pinned in `framework/settings/coresettings.php`; override one in `application/config/config.php` with `scripts('vue', '<url>')` |
| `metadata($pairs = [])` | merges `title`, `description`, `image`... into the page's metadata and returns it ([Metadata](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.3-Metadata-&-Social-Rich-Cards)) |
| `keywords($value = null)`, `copyright($value = null)` | the page keywords and the copyright line |
| `design_stylesheet()` | the URL of the `DESIGN_STYLE` stylesheet, or `''` |
| `terminateSession($url)` | empties the session and redirects |
| `getGlobalInformation($superGlobal = 'session')` | `$_SESSION`, or `'post'`, `'get'`, `'files'` (those are then unset) |
| `isSessionExpired($time)` | whether the session was idle more than `$time` seconds |

**Files**

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `uploadFile($file, $allowedExtensions = null)` | moves a `$_FILES` entry to `public/uploads/<random>.<ext>` and returns its public URL, or `''` when refused. In a capability, the `file` rule does this for you |
| `isAllowedUpload($filename, $allowedExtensions = null)` | whether `uploadFile()` would accept the name. Default list `DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXTENSIONS`: jpg jpeg png gif webp bmp ico heic pdf txt csv md rtf doc docx xls xlsx ppt pptx odt ods odp mp3 wav ogg m4a mp4 mov webm avi zip json. Scripts and markup (php, phtml, phar, cgi, pl, py, sh, asp, jsp, htaccess, ini, svg, html, js, exe, bat) are always refused |
| `deleteFile($url)` | deletes a file of `public/uploads/` by its URL (never a hidden file) |
| `imageCanva()` | a new `claviska\SimpleImage` for image changes ([SimpleImage](https://github.com/claviska/SimpleImage)) |
| `rearrange($files)` | turns a multiple file input's `$_FILES` entry into one array per file |

**HTTP and mail**

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `httpRequest($url, $method, $data, $headers, $username = null, $password = null)` | a cURL request; `$data` is sent as JSON for every method but `GET`; returns the decoded JSON |
| `httpFile($url, $filepath, $headers, $username = null, $password = null, $purpose = 'assistants')` | posts a file (multipart) |
| `sendMail($recipients, $emailContent, $from)` | sends an email through `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_USERNAME`, `MAIL_PASSWORD`: `['email' => ..., 'name' => ...]`, `['subject' => ..., 'body' => '<p>html</p>']`, `['email' => ..., 'name' => ...]`; returns `true` or `false` |

**Authentication** (need `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');` in `web.php`)

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `authorize($user)`, `unauthorize()` | signs a user in or out of the session (`Route::auth` does this for you) |
| `authorized()` | whether someone signed in is still valid |
| `user()` | the signed-in user |
| `guard($attribute, $level, $loginUrl = '/login', $notAuthorized = '/notAuthorized')` | sends visitors to `$loginUrl` and people below `$level` to `$notAuthorized`, then stops |
| `logout($redirectUrl = '/')` | signs out, ends the session and redirects |

**Strings, arrays, time and keys**

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `generateToken($size = 12)` | `2 × $size` random hexadecimal characters |
| `generateKey($size = 32)` | random bytes in base64 (the `APP_KEY` format) |
| `encryptDecrypt($action, $data, $key = APP_KEY)` | `'encrypt'` or `'decrypt'` with AES-256-CBC |
| `sanitize($string)` | `htmlentities()` in UTF-8 |
| `isJson($string)` | whether the string is valid JSON |
| `findKey($array, $key)`, `recursive_filter(&$array, $allowed)` | find a key at any depth; keep only allowed keys |
| `arraySort($array, $attribute, $sort = SORT_DESC)` | sorts rows by a column |
| `loadConstantFromArray($array)` | defines a constant for each key |
| `parsePath($path)`, `sanitizePath($path)`, `startWith($s, $p)`, `endWith($s, $p)` | path and string checks |
| `bindRouteToVar($route, $uri)`, `parseRoute($path)` | the variables of a route pattern |
| `singularize($word)` | drops the last letter (`books` -> `book`, but `categories` -> `categorie`) |
| `now()` | the current time as `Y-m-d H:i:s` |
| `getRelativeTime($datetime, $depth = 1)` | `3 days ago`, `2 hours left` |

## Common mistakes

+ **A form without `=csrf()`** answers `403` `[ERROR 3000]`.
+ **`fetch()` from the browser without `Accept: application/json`**: it is treated as a form post and needs `_token`.
+ **A JSON session call that writes, without `X-CSRF-Token`**: `403` "Missing or invalid CSRF token".
+ **A scoped token on a controller route**: `401` `[ERROR 1004]`; controller routes need `*`.
+ **Code after `redirect()`** keeps running.
+ **`$_SESSION['token']` read before the session started** is empty: use `session('token')`.
+ **Checking the status of a client call as `200` only**: errors answer with their real status (since the security
  release; earlier versions answered `200`).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library -->

**Vue as a library** is the shortest way to add a Vue screen to a Caligrafy application: no Node.js, no build step. Vue 3 loads from a pinned CDN address, your markup is a `.php` file in `public/<app>/`, your script is `public/<app>/scripts/main.js`, and Caligrafy serves the page through a page route. The app reads and writes data by calling your capabilities through the generated JS client. For a larger app with its own routes and a build, see the [Vite single page app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app app bookshelf
```
Then describe the screen: "a list of the books with an add form, through the books capabilities". Claude checks the name, runs `php caligrafer.php app bookshelf`, generates `public/js/capabilities.js`, adds the page route to `application/config/routing/web.php`, and writes `public/bookshelf/index.php` and `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` with the page components.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The address Claude gives opens the screen, and the browser console has no error.
+ `main.js` loads `public/js/capabilities.js` and calls the capabilities by name; no `apiKey`, no `Authorization` header.
+ Adding a book without a year shows `The Published Year field is required` under the year.
## By hand

You build the Bookshelf screen at `/bookshelf`: the books, 20 a page, and a form to add one. You need the Bookshelf tables and capabilities (`list_books`, `create_book`, `list_authors`) of [Views, steps 1 to 3](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#viewsstartup), and `Route::capabilities('/capabilities');` in `application/config/routing/web.php` (the Quickstart adds it). Commands run in the project folder with the Docker server; addresses start with `http://localhost:8080/`.

**1. Scaffold the app.** Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php app bookshelf
```
Expected: `Project created in the public folder.` It copies `framework/plugins/app` to `public/bookshelf/`: `index.php` and `scripts/main.js`. The name must not be a folder Caligrafy already uses in `public/` (`app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`, `ml`, `resources`, `uploads`) and `public/bookshelf/` must not exist yet.

**2. Generate the JS client.** Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js
```
Expected: `public/js/capabilities.js written: <n> capabilities, calls /capabilities (Route::capabilities('/capabilities') in web.php)`. Run it again after every change to a capability.

**3. The page route.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, above `Route::run();`, write:
```php
    // BOOKSHELF: the Vue app (public/bookshelf/index.php)
    Route::page('/bookshelf', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index']]);
```
Open `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`: the template's screen, *My Vue app*, lists the capabilities a visitor may call (`create_book`, `get_book`, `list_books`...).

**4. The markup.** Replace `public/bookshelf/index.php` with:
```php
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
        <title>Bookshelf</title>
        <link rel="shortcut icon" href="<?php echo scripts('favicon'); ?>" type="image/x-icon" />
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo scripts('bootstrap_css'); ?>" />
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/theme.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/tokens.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/layout.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/look.css';?>">
        <?php if (design_stylesheet()): ?><link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo design_stylesheet(); ?>"><?php endif; ?>
    </head>

    <body class="cq-site">
        <div id="app" v-cloak>
            <nav class="cq-nav" aria-label="Main">
                <a class="cq-nav-brand" :href="env.home"><img class="cq-nav-mark" :src="env.home + 'public/images/resources/caligrafy-mark.svg'" alt="" width="28" height="28"><span class="semibold">Book</span>shelf</a>
            </nav>
            <section class="cq-hero cq-hero--page">
                <h1 class="cq-display">Books</h1>
                <p class="cq-lead">{{ total }} books on the shelf.</p>
            </section>
            <section class="cq-band cq-band--tight">
                <div class="cq-inner cq-inner--narrow">
                    <p class="cq-alert cq-alert--error" role="alert" v-if="error">{{ error }}</p>
                    <form method="POST" novalidate @submit.prevent="addBook">
                        <div class="cq-form-grid cq-form-grid--2">
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="title">Title</label>
                                <input id="title" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="200" v-model="book.title">
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.title">{{ errors.title }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="author_id">Author</label>
                                <select id="author_id" class="form-select" v-model.number="book.author_id">
                                    <option v-for="author in authors" :key="author.id" :value="author.id">{{ author.name }}</option>
                                </select>
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.author_id">{{ errors.author_id }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="published_year">Year</label>
                                <input id="published_year" class="form-control" type="number" v-model.number="book.published_year">
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.published_year">{{ errors.published_year }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="summary">Summary</label>
                                <input id="summary" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="2000" v-model="book.summary">
                            </div>
                        </div>
                        <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Add book</button>
                    </form>
                    <ul class="cq-rows" v-if="books.length">
                        <li class="cq-row" v-for="item in books" :key="item.id">
                            <div class="cq-row-main">
                                <p class="cq-row-title">{{ item.title }}</p>
                                <p class="cq-row-meta">{{ item.author.name }}, {{ item.published_year }}</p>
                            </div>
                        </li>
                    </ul>
                    <p class="cq-empty-state" v-else>No books yet: add the first one above.</p>
                    <p v-if="pages > 1">
                        <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" :disabled="page === 1" @click="load(page - 1)">Previous</button>
                        <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" :disabled="page === pages" @click="load(page + 1)">Next</button>
                    </p>
                </div>
            </section>
        </div>

        <script src="<?php echo scripts('vue'); ?>"></script>
        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
        <script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
        <script>loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] });</script>
    </body>
</html>
```

**5. The script.** Replace `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` with:
```js
// Bookshelf: the books of the catalog, through the generated JS client (public/js/capabilities.js)
const app = Vue.createApp({
    data () {
        return {
            env: env,
            books: [], total: 0, page: 1, pages: 1,
            authors: [],
            book: { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' },
            errors: {},
            error: ''
        }
    },
    async mounted () {
        this.api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')
        this.api.configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })   // the application root, whatever APP_ROOT is
        this.authors = await this.api.listAuthors()
        await this.load(1)
    },
    methods: {
        async load (page) {
            const result = await this.api.listBooks({ page: page })   // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
            this.books = result.data
            this.total = result.total
            this.page = result.page
            this.pages = result.pages
        },
        async addBook () {
            this.errors = {}
            this.error = ''
            try {
                await this.api.createBook(this.book)
                this.book = { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' }
                await this.load(1)
            } catch (e) {
                if (e.name === 'CapabilityError' && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields
                else this.error = e.message
            }
        }
    }
})

app.mount('#app')
```

**6. Try it.** Reload `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`:
+ The title band says `5 books on the shelf.`, the list shows them sorted by title (`Ursula K. Le Guin, 1968` under *A Wizard of Earthsea*), and the Author list holds the three authors.
+ Type `Dawn`, choose Octavia E. Butler, leave the year empty, press **Add book**: `The Published Year field is required` appears under the year, and the title stays.
+ Type `1987` and press **Add book**: the count says `6 books on the shelf.`, *Dawn* is in the list, and the fields are empty.

**Check**
+ The browser console shows no error other than the `422` of the refused book, and the network panel shows `POST /capabilities/list_authors`, `list_books` and `create_book`, each with an `X-CSRF-Token` header.
+ The page source contains no API key in `main.js` and no `Authorization` header is sent.
+ At phone width the two fields stack and the rows stay readable.
## Reference

| What | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Command | `php caligrafer.php app <name>` (or `.bin/caligrafer app <name>`): copies `framework/plugins/app` to `public/<name>/` |
| Files | `public/<name>/index.php` (the markup: a `.php` file, so it can use Caligrafy's helpers), `public/<name>/scripts/main.js` (loaded by `loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] })`) |
| Script versions | `app.js?v=<file time>` in the markup (2.21.6), and `loadVue()` adds `?v=<env.scripts_version>` to `scripts/<name>.js` (2.21.5): each deploy reaches every browser |
| Vue | `scripts('vue')`: Vue 3.5.45, the global production build from jsDelivr, pinned in `framework/settings/coresettings.php` |
| Page route | `Route::page('<path>', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => '<name>', 'app' => 'index']])`, or the ready-made `/apps/<name>` ([Routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.2-Routes)) |
| JS client | `php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js`; loaded with `await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')` because `main.js` is a classic script ([Requests](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities)) |
| Stylesheets | `theme.css`, `tokens.css`, `layout.css`, `look.css` and the design style, as in the template; `body.cq-site` and the page components |

`configure({ baseUrl })` matters when the application is not at the root of its address (`APP_ROOT` not empty, for example `http://localhost:8888/myapp/` with MAMP): without it the client calls `/capabilities` at the root of the server.
## Other ways

+ **The template's own screen.** Before step 4, the template lists the capabilities the visitor may call (`await this.api.capabilities()`): use it to see what a visitor or a signed-in user may do.
+ **Copying the template yourself.** Without PHP on the computer, `cp -r framework/plugins/app public/bookshelf` is what the command does.
## Common mistakes

+ **Running `app <name>` for a folder that exists**: the template is copied inside it, as `public/<name>/app/`. Pick a new name.
+ **`import` at the top of `main.js`**: it is a classic script; load the client with `await import(...)` inside `mounted()`.
+ **The client file is missing**: the template's screen says `The JS client is missing`, and your own script stops with a failed import in the console. Run step 2.
+ **A capability added later is not in the client**: run step 2 again.
+ **`Bearer ' + apiKey` in old scripts**: the legacy key is public and turned off on Caligrafy Cloud (`LEGACY_API_KEY=false`): call the capabilities through the client.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests -->

A Vue app asks the server for data, and sends it what people type, through **requests**. In Caligrafy the app does not build these requests: `php caligrafer.php client` writes a JavaScript module with one function per capability (`listBooks()`, `createBook()`), and each function sends the request with the visitor's session and CSRF token, then returns the answer or throws a `CapabilityError`. This page is the reference of that client.
## With Claude

Ask for the screen and the data it needs: "the bookshelf app lists the books 20 at a time with Previous and Next". Claude uses the generated client (`/caligrafy-quill:new-app`, `/caligrafy-quill:new-capability`) and runs `php caligrafer.php client` again when a capability changes.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ Every call goes through a function of `capabilities.js`; no `axios`, `fetch` or `Authorization` header written by hand for capabilities.
+ A refused call is caught: `invalid` shows the field messages, any other error shows its message.
+ `public/js/capabilities.js` was generated again after the last capability change (its functions match `php caligrafer.php capabilities`).
## <a name="capabilities"></a>By hand: calling capabilities

You call the Bookshelf capabilities from the Bookshelf app of [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library), then from a Node script.

**1. Generate the client.** `web.php` needs `Route::capabilities('/capabilities');`. Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js
```
Expected: `public/js/capabilities.js written: <n> capabilities, calls /capabilities (Route::capabilities('/capabilities') in web.php)` and an example line `import { createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'`.

**2. Load it in the app.** In `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js`, `mounted()` loads it and points it at the application:
```js
this.api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')
this.api.configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })
```

**3. Call it.** Open `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`, then type in the browser console:
```js
const api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')
await api.listBooks({ page: 1 })
```
Expected: `{data: Array(n), total: n, page: 1, per_page: 20, pages: 1}`, the paged answer of `list_books`. Then:
```js
await api.getBook({ id: 3 })
```
Expected: `{id: 3, title: 'Kindred', published_year: 1979, ..., author: {id: 2, name: 'Octavia E. Butler', ...}}`.

**4. A refusal.** Type:
```js
try { await api.createBook({ title: 'Lilith' }) } catch (e) { console.log(e.name, e.status, e.code, e.fields) }
```
Expected: `CapabilityError 422 invalid {published_year: 'The Published Year field is required', author_id: 'The Author Id field is required'}`.

**5. From a Node script.** Programs use a personal access token instead of a session. Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "bookshelf script" --scopes books:read,books:write
```
It prints the token once (`cq_...`). Copy `public/js/capabilities.js` next to your script as `capabilities.mjs`, and write `books.mjs`:
```js
import { configure, listBooks, createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.mjs'

configure({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', token: process.env.CALIGRAFY_TOKEN })
const page = await listBooks({ page: 1 })
console.log(page.total, page.pages)
try {
  await createBook({ title: 'Lilith' })
} catch (e) {
  console.log(e instanceof CapabilityError, e.status, e.code, JSON.stringify(e.fields))
}
```
Run `CALIGRAFY_TOKEN=cq_... node books.mjs` (Node.js 18 or later). Expected: the number of books and of pages (`5 1` with the sample data), then `true 422 invalid {"published_year":"The Published Year field is required","author_id":"The Author Id field is required"}`.

**Check**
+ In the browser's network panel, writes carry `X-CSRF-Token` and no `Authorization`; the first write is preceded by one `GET /capabilities`.
+ The Node script sends `Authorization: Bearer cq_...` and no cookie.
## Reference

### The generated module

`php caligrafer.php client [<file>] [--prefix /capabilities]` writes an ES module with no dependency (default file `public/js/capabilities.js`). Run it again after adding or changing a capability.

| Export | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `listBooks(input = {})`, `createBook(input)`... | one function per capability: `create_book` becomes `createBook`. A JSDoc comment gives its description, whether it reads, writes or destroys, who may call it, and its inputs |
| `call(name, input = {})` | calls a capability by name: `call('create_book', {...})` |
| `capabilities()` | the capabilities this caller may use, with their input schema |
| `configure(options)` | `baseUrl` (default `''`: this origin), `token` (a personal access token), `prefix` (default the `--prefix`, `/capabilities`), `credentials` (default `'same-origin'`) |
| `CapabilityError` | thrown on a refusal: `status` (HTTP), `code`, `message`, `fields` (`{}` unless `invalid`) |

Each function sends `POST <baseUrl><prefix>/<name>` with the input as JSON and `Accept: application/json`, and returns what is inside `data`. With a `token` it sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; without one, writes send `X-CSRF-Token`, read once from `GET <baseUrl><prefix>` (the answer's `csrf`), and the browser sends the session cookie.

### Answers

| Capability returns | The function returns |
| --- | --- |
| a row (`Book::find()`, `->first()`) | an object: `{id, title, published_year, ...}` |
| a list (`->get()`) | an array of objects |
| a page (`->paginate(20)`) | `{data, total, page, per_page, pages}`; with `with('author')` each book has its `author` object |

### Refusals

| `code` | `status` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid` | 422 | an input breaks a rule of `$rules`: `fields` has one message per field |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | the capability is not public and nobody is signed in (no token) |
| `forbidden` | 403 | the caller lacks the scope or level, or a write of a signed-in session came without `X-CSRF-Token` (a visitor's write to a `public` capability needs no token) |
| `not_found` | 404 | no capability with that name, or the capability answered `not_found` |
| `conflict` | 409 | the capability refused a duplicate or a state change |
| `error` | other | no JSON error in the answer (a server error) |

### Where the app runs

| App | Client | `baseUrl` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vue as a library | `public/js/capabilities.js`, loaded with `await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')` | `env.home` without its last `/` |
| Vite single page app | `public/<app>/src/capabilities.js`, `import { listBooks } from '@/capabilities.js'` | `''` (same origin; in development the Vite proxy forwards `/capabilities`) |
| A Node script or another site | a copy of the module | the application's address, with a `token` |
## Other ways: `Route::action` and controller routes with `fetch` or axios

The generated client reaches capabilities. A JSON route of your own, a [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action) or a controller route in older code, is called with `fetch` or axios. What other experiences need belongs in a capability: the same rules then serve pages, REST and agents.

+ **The headers.** A JSON call from a page to its own `Route::action` (`GET` included, signed in or not, 2.21.1) or controller route sends `Accept: application/json` and the session's token in `X-CSRF-Token` (since 2.7.0): `apiHeaders()` of `public/js/services/app.js` returns both. The controller then sees the signed-in person or a visitor, as for a form post. Without them the route answers `401` and `{"error":{"code":1004,"message":"Access Denied: send the page's CSRF token in an X-CSRF-Token header (pages, with the session cookie) or Authorization: Bearer <personal access token> (programs and agents)"}}`.
  ```js
  const response = await fetch(env.home + 'api/shelf', { headers: apiHeaders() })
  const books = await response.json()
  ```
  For a JSON body with `fetch`, add the type: `apiHeaders({ 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })`. axios is not in the template: add `<script src="<?php echo scripts('axios'); ?>"></script>` (axios 1.21.1) before `app.js`, then `axios.get(env.home + 'api/shelf', { headers: apiHeaders() })`; axios sets `Content-Type` itself (JSON for an object, multipart for a `FormData`) and rejects an error status (`error.response.status`, `error.response.data`).
+ **Form requests.** A request without `Accept: application/json` is a form request: its `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` carry the CSRF token as the form field `_token` (`formData.append('_token', env.token)`), otherwise `403` (`[ERROR 3000]`). PHP does not read form data sent with a real `PUT`: send `POST` with `_method` set to `PUT` ([Forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms)).
+ **The legacy API key** (`'Bearer ' + apiKey`): readable by anyone who opens the page, and turned off on Caligrafy Cloud (`LEGACY_API_KEY=false`, then `env.apiKey` is `null`). Do not use it.
## Common mistakes

+ **`/capabilities` not found under a sub-folder** (`APP_ROOT` not empty): call `configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })`.
+ **A new capability is missing from the client**: generate it again.
+ **`fetch` without `Accept: application/json`** to a `Route::action` or a controller route: it is a form request, and a write fails the CSRF check.
+ **An error shown as `[object Object]`**: show `e.message`, or `e.fields` for `invalid`.

+ [Request](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/3.-Request)
+ [Forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.1-Understanding-the-structure -->

A Vue app made with `php caligrafer.php app` has two files of its own, and Caligrafy does the rest: it renders the markup through a page route, hands the page an `env` object with what the server knows (the application's address, the CSRF token, who is signed in, your `with` values), and loads your script. This page shows where each part lives and what the "handshake" between the server and the app does.
## With Claude

Claude follows this structure when it scaffolds or changes a Vue app (`/caligrafy-quill:new-app app <name>`). To understand an existing app, ask: "explain the structure of public/bookshelf and how it gets its data".

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The markup is a `.php` file in `public/<app>/`, the scripts are in `public/<app>/scripts/`.
+ The markup loads `scripts('vue')`, then `app.js`, then `loadEnvironment(...)`, then `loadVue(...)`, in this order.
+ Nothing from `application/` is linked from the page.
## By hand

You look inside the Bookshelf app of [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library) and read its `env`.

**1. The files.** Run `ls -R public/bookshelf`. Expected:
```text
index.php
scripts

public/bookshelf/scripts:
main.js
```

**2. The handshake in the markup.** The end of `public/bookshelf/index.php` holds four lines, in this order:
```php
<script src="<?php echo scripts('vue'); ?>"></script>
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
<script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
<script>loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] });</script>
```
`scripts('vue')` is Vue 3; `app.js` (`public/js/services/app.js`, with a version in its address so a deploy reaches every browser) defines `loadEnvironment`, `loadVue` and `apiHeaders`; `$env` is the JSON the server prepared; `loadVue` adds `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` to the page.

**3. Read `env`.** Open `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`, open the browser console and type `Object.keys(env)`. Expected:
```js
['appName', 'app', 'authorized', 'user', '__pug_adapter', 'scripts_version', 'app_root', 'service_root', 'app_resources', 'request', 'apiKey', 'token', 'csrf', 'home', 'keywords', 'metadata', 'copyright']
```
`env.home` is the application's address (`http://localhost:8080/`), `env.authorized` is `false` for a visitor, `env.user` is `null` (`__pug_adapter` is the view engine's own: ignore it). `Object.keys(env.request)` gives `['method', 'host', 'uri', 'fullUri', 'uriComponents', 'uriParameters', 'parameters', 'parsedURI', 'currentRoute', 'fetch', 'acceptLanguage']`: no header, no cookie (2.19.1).

**4. Pass your own value.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, give the route a `with` value:
```php
    Route::page('/bookshelf', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index', 'shelf' => 'Science fiction']]);
```
Reload the page and type `env.shelf` in the console: `'Science fiction'`. In `main.js`, the script reads it as `env.shelf` (or `this.env.shelf`, since `data()` returns `env: env`).

**Check**
+ `env.home` ends with `/` and is the address of the application, also when `APP_ROOT` is not empty.
+ `env.csrf` is a 64-character token, the same as `env.token`.
+ `JSON.stringify(env.request)` contains no `Cookie`, no `Authorization` and no session id.
## Reference

### Folders

| Folder | What lives there |
| --- | --- |
| `application/` | the server: routes, capabilities, models, Pug views. Never served to browsers |
| `public/` | what browsers load: `css/`, `js/`, `images/`, and each client app in its own folder |
| `public/<app>/` | one Vue app: its markup (`index.php`, or other `.php` files), `scripts/` for its scripts; add `css/` or `images/` as needed |
| `public/js/capabilities.js` | the generated JS client, shared by every Vue app and the Pug pages |

### Why `.php` and not `.html`

The markup is included by the view `application/views/Client/app.pug`, so it runs as PHP: it can call `scripts()`, `session('public')`, `design_stylesheet()` and print `$env`. Write it as HTML with these few PHP lines; the rest is Vue.

### `env`

`application/views/Client/app.pug` builds `env` from every value the route gives the view, plus:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `appName`, `app` | the app folder and the markup file (without `.php`) |
| your `with` values, `data` answers and route variables | as the route gives them |
| `authorized`, `user` | who is signed in (with `Route::page`) |
| `home` | the application's address, ending with `/` |
| `token`, `csrf` | the session's CSRF token (the same value) |
| `app_root`, `service_root`, `app_resources` | `public/app/`, `public/js/services/`, `public/resources/` as full addresses |
| `scripts_version` | the modification time of `public/js/services/app.js`: it changes at each deploy, and `loadVue()` adds it to the app's scripts (2.21.5) |
| `request` | what the page may see of the request that opened it, `request()->forClient()` (2.19.1): `method`, `host`, `uri`, `fullUri`, `uriComponents`, `uriParameters` (the query string, without `_token`), `parameters` (the query string, or the route variables when there is none), `parsedURI`, `currentRoute`, `fetch` (the route variables), `acceptLanguage`. Never the headers: no `Cookie` (the session id), no `Authorization`, and no POST body. Before 2.19.1 it was the whole request, headers included |
| `apiKey` | the legacy API key, or `null` when `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` (Caligrafy Cloud). Never use it in a page |
| `keywords`, `metadata`, `copyright` | the values of `application/config/config.php` |

`env` is printed inside `` loadEnvironment(`...`) ``: Caligrafy escapes it so any value, including one from the address, reaches your script unchanged and never runs as code.

### Globals of `public/js/services/app.js`

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `env` | the object above |
| `csrfToken` | `env.csrf` |
| `apiHeaders(extra)` | `{ Accept: 'application/json', 'X-CSRF-Token': csrfToken }` merged with `extra`: the headers of a JSON call from the page to its own `Route::action` or controller routes |
| `apiKey` | `env.apiKey` (legacy) |
| `loadEnvironment(json)` | parses `env` |
| `loadVue({ scripts: [...] })` | adds `public/<appName>/scripts/<name>.js?v=<env.scripts_version>` for each name, in order (2.21.5: a browser never keeps the scripts of the deploy before) |

### The script

`main.js` creates the app with `Vue.createApp({...})`, registers its components with `app.component(...)`, then `app.mount('#app')`. Keep `env: env` in `data()` so the markup can use `env.home`.
## Other ways

`views/Client/app.pug` is the same for the bot, face detection and machine learning apps (`php caligrafer.php bot|facedetect|ml <name>`); their scaffolds differ in what they load.
## Common mistakes

+ **A script placed in `application/`**: the browser cannot load it. Scripts go in `public/<app>/scripts/`.
+ **`main.js` loaded before `loadEnvironment`**: `env` is `null`. Keep the order of step 2.
+ **A value expected in `env` that the route does not give**: add it to the route's `with`, or read it through a capability.
+ **Looking for a header or the cookie in `env.request`**: since 2.19.1 it has neither. Who is signed in is `env.user`; the CSRF token is `env.csrf`.
+ **A client app made before 2.21.6 with a bare `app.js` line**: a browser holding the old `app.js` never gets the script versions. Load it as in step 2, with `?v=`.
+ **Printing `env.apiKey` on screen**: it is the legacy key; never show or use it.

+ [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library)
+ [Routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.2-Routes)
+ [Requests](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests)
