<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms -->

A **form** in a Vue app collects what a person types and hands it to a capability. Vue keeps the fields in `data` (`v-model`), stops the browser from sending the form itself (`@submit.prevent`), and the generated client sends the values: no hidden `_token` field, no method spoofing, no request to build. The capability's rules answer, and the form shows each refusal under its field.
## With Claude

Ask for the form with the capability it calls: "in the bookshelf app, a form to add a book that shows each error under its field and a message when the book is added". Claude writes it in `public/<app>/index.php` and `scripts/main.js` with the page components (`.cq-form-grid`, `.cq-field`, `.cq-field-error`, `.cq-alert`).

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The `form` has `method="POST"` and `@submit.prevent`; the button is `type="submit"`.
+ Sending it empty shows one message under each required field; what was typed stays.
+ Sending it filled shows the success message once, and the fields are emptied.
+ The submit button cannot be pressed twice while the call runs.
## By hand

You finish the add form of the Bookshelf app of [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library): trimmed values, a length limit, a busy button and a success message.

**1. The form.** In `public/bookshelf/index.php`, replace the `cq-alert` line and the `form` with:
```html
                    <p class="cq-alert cq-alert--error" role="alert" v-if="error">{{ error }}</p>
                    <p class="cq-alert" role="status" v-if="message">{{ message }}</p>
                    <form method="POST" novalidate @submit.prevent="addBook">
                        <div class="cq-form-grid cq-form-grid--2">
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="title">Title</label>
                                <input id="title" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="200" v-model.trim="book.title">
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.title">{{ errors.title }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="author_id">Author</label>
                                <select id="author_id" class="form-select" v-model.number="book.author_id">
                                    <option v-for="author in authors" :key="author.id" :value="author.id">{{ author.name }}</option>
                                </select>
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.author_id">{{ errors.author_id }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="published_year">Year</label>
                                <input id="published_year" class="form-control" type="number" v-model.number="book.published_year">
                                <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.published_year">{{ errors.published_year }}</p>
                            </div>
                            <div class="cq-field">
                                <label for="summary">Summary</label>
                                <input id="summary" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="2000" v-model.trim="book.summary">
                            </div>
                        </div>
                        <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit" :disabled="sending">{{ sending ? 'Adding...' : 'Add book' }}</button>
                    </form>
```
+ `method="POST"`: if the script does not run, the browser never puts the fields in the address.
+ `novalidate`: the server's rules give the messages, the same as on the Pug page and over REST.
+ `@submit.prevent`: Vue calls `addBook` instead of the browser sending the form.
+ `v-model.trim`: the field's value, without spaces around it, in `book.title`; `v-model.number`: the year and the author's id as numbers, as the `integer` rules expect.
+ The Author list comes from `list_authors` (`this.authors`), each option's value an author's id.

**2. The script.** Replace `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` with:
```js
// Bookshelf: the books of the catalog, through the generated JS client (public/js/capabilities.js)
const app = Vue.createApp({
    data () {
        return {
            env: env,
            books: [], total: 0, page: 1, pages: 1,
            authors: [],
            book: { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' },
            errors: {},
            error: '',
            message: '',
            sending: false
        }
    },
    async mounted () {
        this.api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')
        this.api.configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })   // the application root, whatever APP_ROOT is
        this.authors = await this.api.listAuthors()
        await this.load(1)
    },
    methods: {
        async load (page) {
            const result = await this.api.listBooks({ page: page })   // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
            this.books = result.data
            this.total = result.total
            this.page = result.page
            this.pages = result.pages
        },
        async addBook () {
            this.errors = {}
            this.error = ''
            this.message = ''
            this.sending = true
            try {
                const created = await this.api.createBook(this.book)
                this.message = 'Book added: ' + created.title
                this.book = { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' }
                await this.load(1)
            } catch (e) {
                if (e.name === 'CapabilityError' && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields
                else this.error = e.message
            } finally {
                this.sending = false
            }
        }
    }
})

app.mount('#app')
```

**3. Try it.** Reload `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`:
+ Press **Add book** with every field empty: `The Title field is required`, `The Author Id field is required` and `The Published Year field is required`, each under its field.
+ Type `  Imago  ` as the title, choose Octavia E. Butler, type `1989`, press **Add book**: `Book added: Imago` (without the spaces) above the form, the book in the list, the fields empty.

**Check**
+ The address bar never gets a `?` after sending.
+ The network panel shows one `POST /capabilities/create_book` per press, with a JSON body.
## Reference

| Part | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `form(method="POST" novalidate @submit.prevent="method")` | Vue handles the submit; the browser never sends it as a `GET` |
| `v-model`, `v-model.trim`, `v-model.number` | the value in `data`, trimmed, or as a number (for an `integer` rule) |
| `:disabled="sending"` | one call at a time |
| `e.fields` of a `CapabilityError` with `code === 'invalid'` | one message per field, keyed by the input's name |
| `.cq-form-grid`, `.cq-form-grid--2`, `.cq-field`, `p.cq-field-error`, `.cq-alert`, `.cq-alert--error` | the page components of a form ([Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#pagecomponents)) |

**Files.** The generated client sends JSON, so it cannot send a file. A capability with a `file` rule (`'cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'`) receives its file from a web form or REST: post a `FormData` to its [`Route::form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form) address with `fetch(env.home + 'books', { method: 'POST', headers: apiHeaders(), body: formData })`. With `Accept: application/json` (in `apiHeaders()`), `Route::form` answers JSON instead of redirecting: `{"data": ...}` with `201`, or `{"error": {"code": "invalid", "fields": {...}}}` with `422`. See [file inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#files).

Vue's own guides: [form bindings](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/forms.html), [event handling](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/event-handling.html), [conditional rendering](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/conditional.html), [list rendering](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/list.html).
## Other ways: form posts with `_token` and `_method`

A form request (without `Accept: application/json`) to a `Route::form`, a `Route::action` or a controller route must carry the session's CSRF token as the form field `_token`, or Caligrafy answers `403` (`[ERROR 3000]`). HTML forms only send `GET` and `POST`: a `_method` field turns a `POST` into a `PUT` or a `DELETE`.
```js
const formData = new FormData()
formData.append('title', 'Survivor')
formData.append('author_id', '2')
formData.append('published_year', '1978')
formData.append('_token', env.token)
const response = await fetch(env.home + 'books', { method: 'POST', body: formData })
// the Route::form of Views: redirected to /books/<id> (response.url); without _token: 403
```
For a route declared with `PUT` or `DELETE` (`Route::form('/books/{id}', 'update_book', ['method' => 'PUT'])`), add `formData.append('_method', 'PUT')` and keep `method: 'POST'`.
A Pug page writes the same fields with `= csrf()` and `= methodField('PUT')` ([Views: forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#formhelpers)). The generated client replaces this for capabilities; the token is read from form data only, never from a JSON body.
## Common mistakes

+ **No `method` on the form**: when the script fails to load, the browser sends the fields in the address (`GET /bookshelf?title=...`).
+ **Clearing the fields before the call answers**: a refused book would be lost. Clear them after success.
+ **`e.fields` shown for every error**: only `invalid` has fields; show `e.message` otherwise.
+ **A file field sent through `createBook()`**: JSON carries no file. Post a `FormData` to the `Route::form` address.
## Related pages

+ [Requests](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities)
+ [Validations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.5-Validations)
+ [Declarative routes: `Route::form`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#form)

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.6-Components -->

A **component** is a piece of a Vue screen with its own markup and behaviour, used like a new HTML tag: `<book-row>`, `<book-form>`. A parent passes data down to it through **props** and hears from it through **events**. In a Vue app as a library, components are registered in `scripts/main.js` with `app.component()`, and their markup lives in the `.php` file inside `<script type="text/x-template">` blocks. For larger apps, each component gets its own `.vue` file in a [single page app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.3-Single-File-Components).
## With Claude

Ask for the split: "in the bookshelf app, make the book row and the add form two components; the page keeps the data and calls the capabilities". Claude registers them in `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` and puts their templates in `public/bookshelf/index.php`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ Each component is registered with `app.component()` **before** `app.mount('#app')`.
+ Each template is a `<script type="text/x-template" id="...">` outside `<div id="app">`, with one root element.
+ Data flows down through props, and up through events declared in `emits`: a component never changes its props.
+ Only the page (the root app) calls the capabilities.
## By hand

You split the Bookshelf app of [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library) into two components: `book-row` shows one book, `book-form` keeps what is typed, gets the authors and the errors from the page, and sends an `add` event.

**1. The markup.** Replace `public/bookshelf/index.php` with:
```php
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
        <title>Bookshelf</title>
        <link rel="shortcut icon" href="<?php echo scripts('favicon'); ?>" type="image/x-icon" />
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo scripts('bootstrap_css'); ?>" />
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/theme.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/tokens.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/layout.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/look.css';?>">
        <?php if (design_stylesheet()): ?><link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo design_stylesheet(); ?>"><?php endif; ?>
    </head>

    <body class="cq-site">
        <div id="app" v-cloak>
            <nav class="cq-nav" aria-label="Main">
                <a class="cq-nav-brand" :href="env.home"><img class="cq-nav-mark" :src="env.home + 'public/images/resources/caligrafy-mark.svg'" alt="" width="28" height="28"><span class="semibold">Book</span>shelf</a>
            </nav>
            <section class="cq-hero cq-hero--page">
                <h1 class="cq-display">Books</h1>
                <p class="cq-lead">{{ total }} books on the shelf.</p>
            </section>
            <section class="cq-band cq-band--tight">
                <div class="cq-inner cq-inner--narrow">
                    <p class="cq-alert cq-alert--error" role="alert" v-if="error">{{ error }}</p>
                    <book-form :authors="authors" :errors="errors" @add="addBook"></book-form>
                    <ul class="cq-rows" v-if="books.length">
                        <book-row v-for="item in books" :key="item.id" :book="item"></book-row>
                    </ul>
                    <p class="cq-empty-state" v-else>No books yet: add the first one above.</p>
                    <p v-if="pages > 1">
                        <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" :disabled="page === 1" @click="load(page - 1)">Previous</button>
                        <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" :disabled="page === pages" @click="load(page + 1)">Next</button>
                    </p>
                </div>
            </section>
        </div>

        <!-- TEMPLATES FOR VUE COMPONENTS -->
        <script type="text/x-template" id="book-row">
            <li class="cq-row">
                <div class="cq-row-main">
                    <p class="cq-row-title">{{ book.title }}</p>
                    <p class="cq-row-meta">{{ book.author.name }}, {{ book.published_year }}</p>
                </div>
            </li>
        </script>

        <script type="text/x-template" id="book-form">
            <form method="POST" novalidate @submit.prevent="submit">
                <div class="cq-form-grid cq-form-grid--2">
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="title">Title</label>
                        <input id="title" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="200" v-model="book.title">
                        <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.title">{{ errors.title }}</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="author_id">Author</label>
                        <select id="author_id" class="form-select" v-model.number="book.author_id">
                            <option v-for="author in authors" :key="author.id" :value="author.id">{{ author.name }}</option>
                        </select>
                        <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.author_id">{{ errors.author_id }}</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="published_year">Year</label>
                        <input id="published_year" class="form-control" type="number" v-model.number="book.published_year">
                        <p class="cq-field-error" v-if="errors.published_year">{{ errors.published_year }}</p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="summary">Summary</label>
                        <input id="summary" class="form-control" type="text" maxlength="2000" v-model="book.summary">
                    </div>
                </div>
                <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Add book</button>
            </form>
        </script>

        <script src="<?php echo scripts('vue'); ?>"></script>
        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
        <script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
        <script>loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] });</script>
    </body>
</html>
```

**2. The script.** Replace `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js` with:
```js
// Bookshelf: the books of the catalog, through the generated JS client (public/js/capabilities.js)
const app = Vue.createApp({
    data () {
        return {
            env: env,
            books: [], total: 0, page: 1, pages: 1,
            authors: [],
            errors: {},
            error: ''
        }
    },
    async mounted () {
        this.api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')
        this.api.configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })   // the application root, whatever APP_ROOT is
        this.authors = await this.api.listAuthors()
        await this.load(1)
    },
    methods: {
        async load (page) {
            const result = await this.api.listBooks({ page: page })   // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
            this.books = result.data
            this.total = result.total
            this.page = result.page
            this.pages = result.pages
        },
        async addBook (book, done) {
            this.errors = {}
            this.error = ''
            try {
                await this.api.createBook(book)
                done()
                await this.load(1)
            } catch (e) {
                if (e.name === 'CapabilityError' && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields
                else this.error = e.message
            }
        }
    }
})

// One book of the list: the parent passes it as a prop
app.component('book-row', {
    template: '#book-row',
    props: ['book']
})

// The form: it keeps what is typed, shows the errors the parent passes, and sends 'add' with the book
app.component('book-form', {
    template: '#book-form',
    props: ['authors', 'errors'],
    emits: ['add'],
    data () {
        return { book: { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' } }
    },
    methods: {
        submit () {
            this.$emit('add', { ...this.book }, () => { this.book = { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' } })
        }
    }
})

app.mount('#app')
```
The form sends a copy of the book and a `done` function; the page calls the capability and calls `done()` only when the book was added, so a refused book stays in the fields.

**3. Try it.** Reload `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`:
+ The list shows the books, each drawn by `book-row`.
+ `Lilith` with Octavia E. Butler and no year: `The Published Year field is required` under the year (the page passed `errors` down), and the title stays.
+ With the year `1989`: the count goes up, *Lilith* is in the list and the fields empty.

**Check**
+ In the browser's element inspector, each row is a `li.cq-row` directly inside `ul.cq-rows`, and no `<book-row>` tag is left in the page (an unknown component stays as its tag).
+ The browser console shows no error other than the `422` of a refused book. (`scripts('vue')` is Vue's production build, which prints no development warnings.)
## Reference

| Property | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `template` | `'#id'` of a `<script type="text/x-template" id="id">` in the markup, or the markup itself in a string |
| `props` | the values the parent passes: `props: ['book']`, used as `<book-row :book="item">` (`:` binds a value; without it the attribute is a fixed string) |
| `emits` | the events it sends: `emits: ['add']`, sent with `this.$emit('add', ...values)`, heard with `@add="addBook"` (the method gets the values) |
| `data()`, `methods`, `computed`, `watch`, `mounted()` | as for the app itself |
| slots | markup the parent places between the tags: `<slot></slot>` in the template, `<slot name="actions">` for a named one, filled with `<template v-slot:actions>` |

Register every component on the app returned by `Vue.createApp()`, before `app.mount('#app')`. A component name used in HTML markup is written in lowercase with dashes (`book-row`), because the browser reads `#app` as HTML before Vue does. A component's template has one root element.

Vue's guides: [components](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/component-basics.html), [props](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/props.html), [events](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/events.html), [slots](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/slots.html).
## Other ways

+ **The template in the script**: `template: '<li class="cq-row">...</li>'`. It works, and mixes markup into the script: keep templates in the markup file.
+ **`v-model` on a component** (`<book-title v-model="book.title">`): the component declares the prop `modelValue` and the event `update:modelValue`; see Vue's [component v-model](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/v-model.html).
## Common mistakes

+ **`app.component()` after `app.mount()`**: the tag stays unknown.
+ **A template inside `<div id="app">`**: Vue renders it as part of the page. Keep the `x-template` blocks after it.
+ **A component that changes its prop** (`this.errors = {}` in `book-form`): Vue warns and the parent's value does not change. Send an event; the parent changes its data.
+ **A component that calls the capabilities itself**: every row would call the server. Keep the calls in the page and pass the results down.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application -->

A **single page app** (SPA) is a Vue app with its own routes between screens, `.vue` component files and a shared store, built with [Vite](https://vite.dev) into plain files. Caligrafy's template (`php caligrafer.php create`) gives you Vite 8, Vue 3.5, Vue Router 5 and Pinia, with Caligrafy's look already imported. The app lives in `public/<app>/`, calls your capabilities through the generated JS client, runs on Vite's development server while you work, and is served from `public/<app>/dist/` once built.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app create shelfapp
```
Then describe the screens: "the list of the books with an add form, and a page for one book". Claude scaffolds the app, generates the client into `public/shelfapp/src/capabilities.js`, adds the `/capabilities` development proxy to `vite.config.js` and the books screens to the router, and writes the components with the page components. The template already has `base: './'`, hash addresses and no API key (2.19.1). It runs `npm install` on your computer, never in the Docker server (which has no Node.js).

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `npm run dev` opens the app and the books load; `npm run build` ends with `✓ built`.
+ `public/shelfapp/dist/index.html` opens from the Caligrafy server, and a reload of `#/books/1` shows the same book.
+ `src/main.js` has no `VITE_API_KEY` and no `Authorization` header: the built files contain no key.
## By hand

You create the Bookshelf single page app, `shelfapp`, run it in development, and build it. You need the Bookshelf tables and capabilities of [Views, steps 1 to 3](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#viewsstartup) and `Route::capabilities('/capabilities');` in `web.php`.

**1. Node.js.** On your computer, run `node --version`. It must be 20.19 or later in the 20 line, or 22.12 or later ([download](https://nodejs.org/en/download)). The Docker `dev-box` has no Node.js: run every `npm` command on your computer, in the project folder.

**2. Create the app.** Run, on your computer, from the project folder (this one command needs PHP 8.3+ on the computer, because `create` runs `npm install` where it runs):
```bash
php caligrafer.php create shelfapp
```
Expected, after npm's own lines:
```text
 VueJS project created and its packages installed.

 - To run the development server: cd public/shelfapp && npm run dev
 - To build it for production: npm run build (in the same folder)
```
With the Docker server instead (`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php create shelfapp`), it prints `VueJS project created, but its packages are NOT installed: npm is not available here (the Docker dev-box has no Node.js)`: then run `cd public/shelfapp && npm install` on your computer.

**3. The JS client.** Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/shelfapp/src/capabilities.js
```
Expected: `public/shelfapp/src/capabilities.js written: <n> capabilities, calls /capabilities ...`. Run it again after every change to a capability.

**4. The development proxy.** The template (2.19.1) already builds for any folder (`base: './'`), uses hash addresses (`createWebHashHistory()` in `src/router/index.js`), keeps no API key and commits `dist/`: nothing to change for those. What it does not have is a proxy for `npm run dev`: Vite's server runs on its own port (5173), so a call to `/capabilities` there answers `404` unless Vite forwards it to Caligrafy. Calling `http://localhost:8080` directly from port 5173 instead (`VITE_API_ROUTE`) is a call to another origin: the browser does not send the session cookie with the generated client's default (`credentials: 'same-origin'`). Replace `public/shelfapp/vite.config.js` with:
```js
import { fileURLToPath, URL } from 'node:url'

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'
import vueDevTools from 'vite-plugin-vue-devtools'

// https://vite.dev/config/
export default defineConfig({
  // the built app works from any folder: public/shelfapp/dist/
  base: './',
  plugins: [
    vue(),
    vueDevTools(),
  ],
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@': fileURLToPath(new URL('./src', import.meta.url))
    },
  },
  // npm run dev: the capability calls go to the Caligrafy server, with its session cookie
  server: {
    proxy: { '/capabilities': 'http://localhost:8080' }
  }
})
```
Use the address of your Caligrafy server in `proxy` (`http://localhost:8080` with Docker). The page and the proxied calls are then on one origin (`localhost:5173`), and the browser keeps one cookie per host whatever the port, so the session of `localhost:8080` goes with them.

<a name="router"></a>The router of the template, `public/shelfapp/src/router/index.js`, uses hash addresses (`#/books/3`) since 2.19.1: they work with `npm run dev` and in `dist/` from any folder, and survive a reload. Apps created before 2.19.1 use `createWebHistory()`: change it as [Routing for single page apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications) shows, which also adds the books screens.

**5. Run it in development.** Start the Caligrafy server, then run:
```bash
cd public/shelfapp
npm run dev
```
Expected: `VITE v8.x.x  ready in ... ms` and `➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/`. Open that address: the template's home, *Welcome to Caligrafy*, in Caligrafy's look. Every file you save shows at once. In the browser console, `(await import('/src/capabilities.js')).listBooks()` answers the books through the proxy.

**6. Build it.** Stop the development server (Ctrl+C) and run:
```bash
npm run build
```
Expected: three lines for `dist/index.html`, `dist/assets/index-<hash>.css` and `dist/assets/index-<hash>.js`, each with its size, then `✓ built in ...ms`. Open `http://localhost:8080/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html`: the same app, served by Caligrafy, calling `/capabilities` on the same server.

**Check**
+ `grep -rc VITE_API_KEY src` prints `0` for every file, and the files of `dist/assets/` contain no API key.
+ `http://localhost:8080/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html#/` reloads without an error.
+ `npm run lint` ends without errors (it fixes the formatting it can).
## <a name="capabilities"></a>Calling the capabilities of the application

A single page app is one more experience of your [capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service): import the functions you need from the generated client.
```js
import { listBooks, createBook, CapabilityError } from '@/capabilities.js'

const page = await listBooks({ page: 1 })      // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
try {
  await createBook({ title: 'Dawn', author_id: 2, published_year: 1987 })
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof CapabilityError && e.code === 'invalid') errors.value = e.fields
}
```
+ The client uses the visitor's session (cookie and CSRF token): nothing secret is built into the app.
+ In development the app runs on Vite's port and the proxy of step 4 forwards `/capabilities` to Caligrafy; the browser keeps one cookie for `localhost` whatever the port, so a person signed in on the Caligrafy server is signed in in the app.
+ Built, `dist/` is served by Caligrafy itself: the calls go to the same server. When the application is in a sub-folder (`APP_ROOT` not empty), call `configure({ baseUrl: '/<APP_ROOT>' })` once in `src/main.js`.
+ The [Requests reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities) lists every function, option and error.
## Reference

### The template (`framework/librairies/app`)

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | scripts `dev` and `serve` (Vite's server), `host` (the same, open to your network), `build`, `preview` (serves `dist/`), `lint` (ESLint 10 with `--fix`); dependencies Vue 3.5, Vue Router 5, Pinia, axios 1.21; Node `^20.19.0 \|\| >=22.12.0`; `overrides` keeps `minimatch` 11 |
| `vite.config.js` | Vite 8, `base: './'` (2.19.1: `dist/` works from any folder), the Vue plugin, Vue devtools, the alias `@` = `src/`; no proxy (step 4 adds it) |
| `index.html` | the page: Bootstrap 5.3.9 from jsDelivr, `<div id="app">`, `src/main.js` |
| `src/main.js` | the app, Pinia, the router, Caligrafy's stylesheets from `public/css/`; `this.http` (axios), `this.config`, `this.apiConfig` and `this.apiHeaders` from `src/common/app.js` for every component |
| `src/App.vue` | the frame: the top bar, `<router-view>`, the footer |
| `src/router/index.js` | the routes, with `createWebHashHistory()` (2.19.1) |
| `src/common/store.js` | an example Pinia store ([State management](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.4-State-Management)) |
| `src/common/app.js` | axios settings for calls the generated client does not make (controller routes), 2.19.1: `config` (`apiRoute` = `VITE_API_ROUTE` or `''`, `capabilities` = `VITE_CAPABILITIES_ROUTE` or `/capabilities`), `csrfToken()` (reads `csrf` from `GET /capabilities` once), `apiHeaders(extra)` (`Accept: application/json` and `X-CSRF-Token`), `apiConfig` (JSON, `withCredentials: true`). No API key |
| `src/components/pages/`, `src/components/global/` | page components (`HomePage.vue`) and shared ones (`ShowNavigation.vue`, `ShowMessage.vue`, `ShowGeneralCard.vue`) |
| `.env` | `VITE_API_ROUTE=` (empty: the same site), written by `php caligrafer.php initialize` into the template and copied by `create`. No key since 2.19.1: everything in it ends up in the public build. Never committed (the project's `.gitignore` has `.env`) |
| `.gitignore` | `node_modules`, `dist-ssr`, logs and editor files; `dist/` is not ignored (2.19.1): it is committed |

`create <name>` copies the template to `public/<name>/`, then runs `npm install` when `npm` is found. The name must not be a folder Caligrafy uses in `public/` (`app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`, `ml`, `resources`, `uploads`), and `public/<name>/` must not exist yet.

### <a name="online"></a>Online

The production image of Caligrafy does not run `npm`: commit the built app.
1. Run `npm run build` in `public/shelfapp/`.
2. Commit `public/shelfapp/dist/` with the rest of the project (`node_modules/` stays out). The template's `.gitignore` does not ignore `dist/` since 2.19.1; in an app created before, delete the line `dist` from `public/shelfapp/.gitignore` first.
3. The app is at `https://<your site>/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html`, with hash addresses.

Build again and commit `dist/` after every change. A design style is imported in `src/main.js` (`import '../../css/designs/<name>.css'`) and needs a new build too.
## Other ways

+ **An address of its own** (`https://books.example.com/`): point a virtual host at `public/shelfapp/dist/`, keep `base: './'`, and set `configure({ baseUrl: 'https://<the Caligrafy address>' })` with a token, since the session cookie does not go to another site. With `createWebHistory()` instead of hash addresses, the virtual host needs a fallback to `index.html` (`FallbackResource /index.html`), or a reload of `/books/3` answers `404`.
+ **axios for a controller route** (one that answers with `api()`, not a capability): `this.http.post(this.config.apiRoute.replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/books/import', body, { headers: await this.apiHeaders(), withCredentials: true })` (an absolute path: the built app lives in `public/shelfapp/dist/`, so a relative `'books/import'` would point inside it), and add `'/books'` to the `proxy` of step 4 for `npm run dev`. The template sends the session and `X-CSRF-Token`, never an API key (2.19.1). Apps created before 2.19.1 have `'Bearer ' + VITE_API_KEY` in `src/main.js` and `src/common/app.js`: the key is readable by anyone in the built files and Caligrafy Cloud turns it off (`LEGACY_API_KEY=false`); replace both files with the template's.
## Common mistakes

+ **`npm install` reports 10 moderate vulnerabilities** (apps created with 2.2.0 or older): they come from `minimatch` below 11.0.1, used by ESLint only. Never run `npm audit fix --force` (it installs ESLint 4). Add `"overrides": { "minimatch": "^11.0.1" }` to `package.json`, then `rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install`.
+ **A blank page from `dist/`** (apps created before 2.19.1): the router uses `createWebHistory()`, or `base` is not `'./'` in `vite.config.js`. Use `createWebHashHistory()` and `base: './'`, as the template does now, and build again.
+ **`/capabilities` answers 404 in development**: the proxy of step 4 is missing or points to the wrong port.
+ **Changes not online**: `dist/` was not built again, or not committed.

> [Next Section: Routing for Single Page Applications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications -->

A single page app has one HTML page, and shows a different screen for each address: `#/` the list of the books, `#/books/3` one book. **Vue Router** maps each address to a page component; the page then asks the server for its data through the generated client. Caligrafy's server still answers the data (`Route::capabilities`) and serves the built app; the routes between screens live in `src/router/index.js`.
## With Claude

Ask for the screens and their addresses: "in shelfapp, the list of the books at #/ and one book at #/books/:id, each title a link". Claude writes the routes in `public/shelfapp/src/router/index.js`, the page components in `src/components/pages/`, and keeps hash addresses and the `:key` on `<router-view>`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The router uses `createWebHashHistory()`.
+ `App.vue` has `<router-view :key="$route.fullPath">`.
+ From one book, opening another (`#/books/1` then `#/books/3`) shows the second book.
+ A reload of `#/books/3` in the built app shows the same book.
## <a name="mainjs"></a>By hand

You give the Bookshelf app of [Setting up the Vue application](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application) two screens. Files are in `public/shelfapp/`.

**1. The routes.** The template's router already uses hash addresses (`createWebHashHistory()`, 2.19.1); give it the two screens. Replace `src/router/index.js` with:
```js
import { createRouter, createWebHashHistory } from 'vue-router'
import BooksPage from '../components/pages/BooksPage.vue'
import BookPage from '../components/pages/BookPage.vue'

const router = createRouter({
  // #/books/3: works with npm run dev and in dist/, from any folder, and survives a reload
  history: createWebHashHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/', name: 'books', component: BooksPage },
    { path: '/books/:id', name: 'book', component: BookPage, props: true }
  ]
})

export default router
```
`:id` is a parameter of the address; `props: true` gives it to the page as the prop `id`.

**2. The list.** Write `src/components/pages/BooksPage.vue`:
```vue
<template>
	<main>
		<section class='cq-hero cq-hero--page'>
			<h1 class='cq-display'>Books</h1>
			<p class='cq-lead'>{{ total }} books on the shelf.</p>
		</section>
		<section class='cq-band cq-band--tight'>
			<div class='cq-inner cq-inner--narrow'>
				<p class='cq-alert cq-alert--error' role='alert' v-if='error'>{{ error }}</p>
				<ul class='cq-rows' v-if='books.length'>
					<li class='cq-row' v-for='book in books' :key='book.id'>
						<div class='cq-row-main'>
							<p class='cq-row-title'>
								<router-link :to='{ name: "book", params: { id: book.id } }'>{{ book.title }}</router-link>
							</p>
							<p class='cq-row-meta'>{{ book.author.name }}, {{ book.published_year }}</p>
						</div>
					</li>
				</ul>
				<p class='cq-empty-state' v-else>No books yet.</p>
			</div>
		</section>
	</main>
</template>

<script>
import { listBooks } from '@/capabilities.js'

export default {
	name: 'books-page',
	data() {
		return { books: [], total: 0, error: '' }
	},
	async mounted() {
		try {
			const page = await listBooks({ page: 1 })   // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
			this.books = page.data
			this.total = page.total
		} catch (e) {
			this.error = e.message
		}
	}
}
</script>
```

**3. One book.** Write `src/components/pages/BookPage.vue`:
```vue
<template>
	<main>
		<section class='cq-hero cq-hero--page'>
			<h1 class='cq-display'>{{ book ? book.title : 'Book' }}</h1>
			<p class='cq-lead' v-if='book'>by {{ book.author.name }}, {{ book.published_year }}</p>
		</section>
		<section class='cq-band cq-band--tight'>
			<div class='cq-inner cq-inner--narrow'>
				<p class='cq-alert cq-alert--error' role='alert' v-if='error'>{{ error }}</p>
				<p v-if='book'>{{ book.summary || 'No summary yet.' }}</p>
				<p><router-link class='btn btn-secondary' :to='{ name: "books" }'>All books</router-link></p>
			</div>
		</section>
	</main>
</template>

<script>
import { getBook } from '@/capabilities.js'

export default {
	name: 'book-page',
	props: ['id'],
	data() {
		return { book: null, error: '' }
	},
	async mounted() {
		try {
			this.book = await getBook({ id: this.id })   // the book, with its author in book.author
		} catch (e) {
			this.error = e.message
		}
	}
}
</script>
```

**4. The frame.** Replace `src/App.vue` with (the template's, plus the `:key`):
```vue
<template>
	<show-navigation></show-navigation>
	<router-view :key="$route.fullPath"></router-view>
	<footer class='cq-footer'>
		<p>Copyright &copy; {{ new Date().getFullYear() }}</p>
	</footer>
</template>

<script>
import ShowNavigation from './components/global/ShowNavigation.vue'

export default {
	name: 'App',
	components: {
		'show-navigation': ShowNavigation
	}
}
</script>
```
The `:key` gives every address a fresh page: without it, going from `#/books/1` to `#/books/3` reuses the same `BookPage`, `mounted()` does not run again, and book 1 stays on screen.

**5. The top bar link.** In `src/components/global/ShowNavigation.vue`, the brand links to the old home: replace `:to='{ name: "home" }'` with `:to='{ name: "books" }'`. Then delete `src/components/pages/HomePage.vue` (nothing imports it any more).

**6. Try it.** Run `npm run build`, then open `http://localhost:8080/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html`:
+ The list says `5 books on the shelf.` and shows them sorted by title, each with its author and year; *A Wizard of Earthsea* links to `#/books/1`.
+ Click *Kindred*: the address becomes `#/books/3` and the page shows `Kindred`, `by Octavia E. Butler, 1979` and its summary.
+ Change the address to `#/books/1`: the page shows *A Wizard of Earthsea*. Reload: still the same book.
+ `#/books/999` shows `There is no book #999`.

**Check**
+ `npm run dev` gives the same screens at `http://localhost:5173/#/`.
+ The address bar never leaves `index.html`: every screen is after the `#`.
## Reference

| Part | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `createRouter({ history, routes })` | the router, installed by `app.use(router)` in `src/main.js` |
| `createWebHashHistory()` | addresses after a `#`: they work in development and in `dist/` from any folder, and survive a reload |
| `{ path, name, component }` | one screen; `name` lets links say `{ name: 'book', params: { id: 3 } }` instead of building the address |
| `path: '/books/:id'` | a parameter, read with `this.$route.params.id`, or as the prop `id` with `props: true` |
| `component: () => import('../components/pages/BookPage.vue')` | loads the page only when it is opened (a separate file in `dist/assets/`) |
| `<router-link :to="{ name: 'book', params: { id } }">` | a link between screens, without reloading |
| `this.$router.push({ name: 'book', params: { id } })` | goes to a screen from code (after a form, for example) |
| `<router-view :key="$route.fullPath">` | where the screen of the address appears, rebuilt for every address |
| `useRoute()`, `useRouter()` | the same in `<script setup>` components: `import { useRoute } from 'vue-router'` |

The server's routes and the app's routes are separate: `web.php` answers `/capabilities` and serves the files of `dist/`; the router chooses the screen from the part after `#`. See [Vue Router](https://router.vuejs.org/).
## Other ways

+ **Addresses without `#`** (`createWebHistory()`, the template's default before 2.19.1): `/books/3` works with `npm run dev`, but a reload asks the server for `/books/3`. The built app then needs its own site (a virtual host on `dist/` with `FallbackResource /index.html`, and `base` set to its path), or a reload answers `404`. Under `public/<app>/dist/`, keep hash addresses.
+ **Watching the parameter** instead of the `:key`: `watch: { id() { this.load() } }` in the page, when rebuilding the whole page is too much.
## Common mistakes

+ **A blank screen in `dist/`**: `createWebHistory()` with the app in a sub-folder (apps created before 2.19.1). Use `createWebHashHistory()`, as the template does since 2.19.1.
+ **The previous book stays on screen**: `<router-view>` without `:key="$route.fullPath"`.
+ **A route to a component that is not imported**: Vite stops the build (`Could not resolve`). Import every page the routes name, or use `() => import(...)`.
+ **Expecting `web.php` to know `#/books/3`**: the browser never sends the part after `#` to the server.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.3-Single-File-Components -->

A **single file component** is one `.vue` file that holds a piece of the screen: its markup (`<template>`), its behaviour (`<script>`) and, when it needs one, its style (`<style>`). Vite turns these files into the built app. In a Caligrafy single page app, the screens of the router are **page** components (`src/components/pages/`), and pieces used on several screens are **global** components (`src/components/global/`). A parent passes data down through **props** and hears from a child through **events**.
## With Claude

Ask for the piece and who uses it: "in shelfapp, make the add form a component BookForm that shows the errors the page gives it and sends the book to the page; after adding, open the new book". Claude writes `src/components/global/BookForm.vue` and changes `src/components/pages/BooksPage.vue`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The child declares its `props` and `emits`; it never changes a prop.
+ Only page components (or the store) call the capabilities.
+ The markup uses the page components (`.cq-form-grid`, `.cq-field`, `.cq-field-error`), with no `<style>` for what they already do.
+ `npm run build` ends with `✓ built`.
## By hand

You add a form component to the Bookshelf app of [Routing for single page apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications). Files are in `public/shelfapp/`.

**1. The child.** Write `src/components/global/BookForm.vue`:
```vue
<template>
	<form method='POST' novalidate @submit.prevent='submit'>
		<div class='cq-form-grid cq-form-grid--2'>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='title'>Title</label>
				<input id='title' class='form-control' type='text' maxlength='200' v-model.trim='book.title'>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='errors.title'>{{ errors.title }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='author_id'>Author</label>
				<select id='author_id' class='form-select' v-model.number='book.author_id'>
					<option v-for='author in authors' :key='author.id' :value='author.id'>{{ author.name }}</option>
				</select>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='errors.author_id'>{{ errors.author_id }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='published_year'>Year</label>
				<input id='published_year' class='form-control' type='number' v-model.number='book.published_year'>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='errors.published_year'>{{ errors.published_year }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='summary'>Summary</label>
				<input id='summary' class='form-control' type='text' maxlength='2000' v-model.trim='book.summary'>
			</div>
		</div>
		<button class='btn btn-primary' type='submit'>Add book</button>
	</form>
</template>

<script>
export default {
	name: 'book-form',
	props: {
		authors: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
		errors: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) }
	},
	emits: ['add'],
	data() {
		return { book: { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' } }
	},
	methods: {
		submit() {
			this.$emit('add', { ...this.book })
		}
	}
}
</script>
```
It keeps what is typed, lists the `authors` and shows the `errors` its parent passes, and sends a copy of the book with the `add` event.

**2. The parent.** Replace `src/components/pages/BooksPage.vue` with:
```vue
<template>
	<main>
		<section class='cq-hero cq-hero--page'>
			<h1 class='cq-display'>Books</h1>
			<p class='cq-lead'>{{ total }} books on the shelf.</p>
		</section>
		<section class='cq-band cq-band--tight'>
			<div class='cq-inner cq-inner--narrow'>
				<p class='cq-alert cq-alert--error' role='alert' v-if='error'>{{ error }}</p>
				<book-form :authors='authors' :errors='errors' @add='addBook'></book-form>
				<ul class='cq-rows' v-if='books.length'>
					<li class='cq-row' v-for='book in books' :key='book.id'>
						<div class='cq-row-main'>
							<p class='cq-row-title'>
								<router-link :to='{ name: "book", params: { id: book.id } }'>{{ book.title }}</router-link>
							</p>
							<p class='cq-row-meta'>{{ book.author.name }}, {{ book.published_year }}</p>
						</div>
					</li>
				</ul>
				<p class='cq-empty-state' v-else>No books yet: add the first one above.</p>
			</div>
		</section>
	</main>
</template>

<script>
import { listBooks, listAuthors, createBook, CapabilityError } from '@/capabilities.js'
import BookForm from '../global/BookForm.vue'

export default {
	name: 'books-page',
	components: {
		'book-form': BookForm
	},
	data() {
		return { books: [], total: 0, authors: [], errors: {}, error: '' }
	},
	async mounted() {
		try {
			this.authors = await listAuthors()
			const page = await listBooks({ page: 1 })
			this.books = page.data
			this.total = page.total
		} catch (e) {
			this.error = e.message
		}
	},
	methods: {
		async addBook(book) {
			this.errors = {}
			this.error = ''
			try {
				const created = await createBook(book)
				this.$router.push({ name: 'book', params: { id: created.id } })
			} catch (e) {
				if (e instanceof CapabilityError && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields
				else this.error = e.message
			}
		}
	}
}
</script>
```

**3. Try it.** Run `npm run dev` and open `http://localhost:5173/#/` (or `npm run build` and `http://localhost:8080/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html`):
+ Type `Mind of My Mind`, choose Octavia E. Butler, no year, press **Add book**: `The Published Year field is required` under the year; the title stays.
+ Type `1977` and press **Add book**: the address becomes `#/books/6` and the page shows *Mind of My Mind*, `by Octavia E. Butler, 1977`.

**Check**
+ `BookForm.vue` imports nothing from `capabilities.js`.
+ `npm run build` ends with `✓ built`.
## Reference

### The parts of a `.vue` file

| Part | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `<template>` | the markup, with Vue's syntax (`{{ }}`, `v-if`, `v-for`, `v-model`, `:prop`, `@event`) |
| `<script>` | `export default { name, components, props, emits, data(), computed, watch, mounted(), methods }`, and the `import`s it needs |
| `<style>` | its own CSS when the page components do not cover it; `<style scoped>` keeps it to this component |

`@` is the `src/` folder (the alias of `vite.config.js`): `import BookForm from '@/components/global/BookForm.vue'`.

### Kinds of components

| Kind | Where | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frame | `src/App.vue` | the top bar, `<router-view>`, the footer |
| page | `src/components/pages/` | `BooksPage.vue`, `BookPage.vue`: named by the routes |
| global | `src/components/global/` | `ShowNavigation.vue`, `BookForm.vue`: used by several pages |

### Talking between components

| Direction | How |
| --- | --- |
| parent to child | props: `props: { errors: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) } }` in the child, `<book-form :errors="errors">` in the parent |
| child to parent | events: `emits: ['add']` and `this.$emit('add', book)` in the child, `<book-form @add="addBook">` in the parent (the method gets `book`) |
| markup from the parent | slots: `<slot></slot>` in the child's template |
| between any components | a store ([State management](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.4-State-Management)) |

Vue's guides: [single file components](https://vuejs.org/guide/scaling-up/sfc.html), [props](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/props.html), [events](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/events.html), [slots](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/slots.html).
## Other ways

+ **The Composition API** (`<script setup>`): the same component written with `defineProps`, `defineEmits` and `ref`:
  ```vue
  <script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'
  defineProps({
    authors: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
    errors: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) }
  })
  const emit = defineEmits(['add'])
  const book = ref({ title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' })
  function submit() { emit('add', { ...book.value }) }
  </script>
  ```
  The template is the same. Pick one style per app; this wiki uses the Options API of the template.
## Common mistakes

+ **A component that changes its prop** (`this.errors = {}` in `BookForm`): Vue warns in development and the parent's value does not change. Send an event.
+ **Forgetting `components: { 'book-form': BookForm }`** in the parent: the tag stays unknown (a warning in `npm run dev`).
+ **An event not in `emits`**: it still works, but Vue also passes the listener to the root element; declare every event.
+ **A `<style>` that copies the page components**: use their classes, so the app keeps Caligrafy's look and its design style.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.4-State-Management -->

**State management** keeps the data that several components share in one place, a **store**, so every component shows the same thing and changes it the same way. Caligrafy's single page app template uses [Pinia](https://pinia.vuejs.org/), the official store of Vue (it replaces Vuex): `src/main.js` installs it (`app.use(createPinia())`) and `src/common/store.js` holds an example. In a Caligrafy app, the store's actions call the capabilities, so the store also holds what the server answered: the books, their count, the field errors.
## With Claude

Ask for what is shared: "in shelfapp, keep the books, the authors and the form errors in a Pinia store; the top bar shows how many books there are". Claude writes the store in `public/shelfapp/src/common/store.js`, with actions that call the generated client, and changes the components to read it.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ Only the store's actions call the capabilities; the components call the actions.
+ After adding a book, the count in the top bar and in the list change together, without a reload.
+ `npm run build` ends with `✓ built`.
## By hand

You move the data of the Bookshelf app of [Single file components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.3-Single-File-Components) into a store, and show the count of books in the top bar. Files are in `public/shelfapp/`.

**1. The store.** Replace `src/common/store.js` with:
```js
import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
import { listBooks, listAuthors, createBook, CapabilityError } from '@/capabilities.js'

export const useBooksStore = defineStore('books', {
    // shared data
    state: () => ({
        books: [],
        total: 0,
        page: 1,
        pages: 1,
        authors: [],
        errors: {},
        error: ''
    }),

    // values computed from the state
    getters: {
        isEmpty: (state) => state.total === 0
    },

    // what changes the state: here, through the capabilities
    actions: {
        async load(page = 1) {
            try {
                if (!this.authors.length) this.authors = await listAuthors()
                const result = await listBooks({ page })   // { data, total, page, per_page, pages }
                this.books = result.data
                this.total = result.total
                this.page = result.page
                this.pages = result.pages
            } catch (e) {
                this.error = e.message
            }
        },
        async add(book) {
            this.errors = {}
            this.error = ''
            try {
                const created = await createBook(book)
                await this.load(1)
                return created
            } catch (e) {
                if (e instanceof CapabilityError && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields
                else this.error = e.message
                return null
            }
        }
    }
})
```

**2. The top bar loads it.** The top bar is on every screen, so it loads the books once for the whole app. Replace `src/components/global/ShowNavigation.vue` with:
```vue
<template>
	<nav class='cq-nav' aria-label='Main'>
		<router-link class='cq-nav-brand' :to='{ name: "books" }'>
			<img class='cq-nav-mark' :src='mark' alt='' width='28' height='28'>
			<span class='semibold'>Book</span><span>shelf</span>
		</router-link>
		<div class='cq-nav-links'>
			<router-link class='cq-nav-link' :to='{ name: "books" }'>{{ store.total }} books</router-link>
		</div>
	</nav>
</template>

<script>
import mark from '../../assets/caligrafy-mark.svg'
import { useBooksStore } from '@/common/store'

export default {
	name: 'show-navigation',
	data() {
		return { mark, store: useBooksStore() }
	},
	mounted() {
		// the top bar is on every screen: it loads the books once for the whole app
		this.store.load(1)
	}
}
</script>
```

**3. The form uses it.** Replace `src/components/global/BookForm.vue` with:
```vue
<template>
	<form method='POST' novalidate @submit.prevent='submit'>
		<div class='cq-form-grid cq-form-grid--2'>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='title'>Title</label>
				<input id='title' class='form-control' type='text' maxlength='200' v-model.trim='book.title'>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='store.errors.title'>{{ store.errors.title }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='author_id'>Author</label>
				<select id='author_id' class='form-select' v-model.number='book.author_id'>
					<option v-for='author in store.authors' :key='author.id' :value='author.id'>{{ author.name }}</option>
				</select>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='store.errors.author_id'>{{ store.errors.author_id }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='published_year'>Year</label>
				<input id='published_year' class='form-control' type='number' v-model.number='book.published_year'>
				<p class='cq-field-error' v-if='store.errors.published_year'>{{ store.errors.published_year }}</p>
			</div>
			<div class='cq-field'>
				<label for='summary'>Summary</label>
				<input id='summary' class='form-control' type='text' maxlength='2000' v-model.trim='book.summary'>
			</div>
		</div>
		<button class='btn btn-primary' type='submit'>Add book</button>
	</form>
</template>

<script>
import { useBooksStore } from '@/common/store'

export default {
	name: 'book-form',
	emits: ['added'],
	data() {
		return {
			store: useBooksStore(),
			book: { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' }
		}
	},
	methods: {
		async submit() {
			const created = await this.store.add(this.book)
			if (created) {
				this.book = { title: '', author_id: null, published_year: null, summary: '' }
				this.$emit('added', created)
			}
		}
	}
}
</script>
```
The form calls the store's `add` action, reads the errors from the store, and tells the page when a book was added.

**4. The list uses it.** Replace `src/components/pages/BooksPage.vue` with:
```vue
<template>
	<main>
		<section class='cq-hero cq-hero--page'>
			<h1 class='cq-display'>Books</h1>
			<p class='cq-lead'>{{ store.total }} books on the shelf.</p>
		</section>
		<section class='cq-band cq-band--tight'>
			<div class='cq-inner cq-inner--narrow'>
				<p class='cq-alert cq-alert--error' role='alert' v-if='store.error'>{{ store.error }}</p>
				<book-form @added='open'></book-form>
				<ul class='cq-rows' v-if='!store.isEmpty'>
					<li class='cq-row' v-for='book in store.books' :key='book.id'>
						<div class='cq-row-main'>
							<p class='cq-row-title'>
								<router-link :to='{ name: "book", params: { id: book.id } }'>{{ book.title }}</router-link>
							</p>
							<p class='cq-row-meta'>{{ book.author.name }}, {{ book.published_year }}</p>
						</div>
					</li>
				</ul>
				<p class='cq-empty-state' v-else>No books yet: add the first one above.</p>
			</div>
		</section>
	</main>
</template>

<script>
import { useBooksStore } from '@/common/store'
import BookForm from '../global/BookForm.vue'

export default {
	name: 'books-page',
	components: {
		'book-form': BookForm
	},
	data() {
		return {
			store: useBooksStore()
		}
	},
	methods: {
		open(book) {
			this.$router.push({ name: 'book', params: { id: book.id } })
		}
	}
}
</script>
```
The page no longer loads anything: the top bar did, and the list reads the store.

**5. Try it.** Run `npm run build`, then open `http://localhost:8080/public/shelfapp/dist/index.html#/books/3`:
+ The top bar says `5 books` on the page of *Kindred*: the store was loaded by the top bar.
+ Click `5 books`: the list shows the same books and the Author list its three authors, with no new call to `list_books` (the network panel shows none).
+ Type `Bloodchild`, choose Octavia E. Butler, no year, press **Add book**: `The Published Year field is required` under the year.
+ Type `1995` and press **Add book**: the address becomes `#/books/6`, and the top bar says `6 books`.

**Check**
+ `BooksPage.vue` and `BookForm.vue` import nothing from `capabilities.js`.
+ The count in the top bar and in the title band of the list are always the same.
## Reference

### A store

`defineStore(id, { state, getters, actions })` returns a function; call it in a component to get the store (`useBooksStore()`). Every component that calls it gets the same store.

| Part | What it is | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state: () => ({...})` | the shared data and its first values | `store.books`, `store.total`; change it in place (`store.total++`), several at once with `store.$patch({ page: 2 })`; `store.$reset()` restores the first values |
| `getters` | values computed from the state, kept until the state they read changes | `store.isEmpty`; a getter that takes an argument returns a function: `byAuthor: (state) => (id) => state.books.filter(b => b.author_id === id)` |
| `actions` | methods that change the state, synchronous or `async`; `this` is the store | `await store.load(2)`, `await store.add(book)` |

In an Options API component, keep the store in `data()` (`store: useBooksStore()`) and read it in the template (`store.total`). In a `<script setup>` component: `const store = useBooksStore()`. You can have as many stores as you need, one per subject (books, the signed-in person, a cart), each with its own id.

### Stores and capabilities

| In the store | Comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `books`, `total`, `page`, `pages` | `listBooks({ page })`: `{ data, total, page, per_page, pages }` |
| `authors` | `listAuthors()` |
| `errors` | `e.fields` of a `CapabilityError` with `code === 'invalid'` |
| `error` | `e.message` of any other refusal |

The store holds a copy of what the server answered. Load it again (`store.load(1)`) when the data may have changed elsewhere: another person, the REST API or an AI agent.

### Migrating from Vuex

| Vuex | Pinia |
| --- | --- |
| `createStore({ state, mutations, actions, getters })` | `defineStore('id', { state: () => ({...}), getters, actions })` |
| `app.use(store)` | `app.use(createPinia())` |
| `this.$store.state.count` | `store.count` (with `const store = useBooksStore()`) |
| `this.$store.commit('increment', 1)` (a mutation) | `store.increment(1)` (an action) or `store.count++`: there are no mutations |
| `this.$store.dispatch('load', 1)` | `store.load(1)` |
| `this.$store.getters.isEmpty` | `store.isEmpty` |
## Other ways

+ **No store**: for one or two screens, the page component keeps the data and passes it down with props, as in [Single file components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.3-Single-File-Components). Add a store when two components that are not parent and child need the same data.
+ **The template's example store** (`useAppStore`, a counter with `count`, `isEven` and `increment`) shows the three parts with no server: replace it with stores of your own.
## Common mistakes

+ **`useBooksStore()` outside a component, before `app.use(createPinia())`**: Pinia is not installed yet. Call it in `data()` or `setup`.
+ **Copying a store value into a component's own data** (`total: store.total`): the copy does not follow the store. Read `store.total` in the template.
+ **A component that calls a capability and also the store**: two copies of the same data. Let the store's actions call the capabilities.
+ **Expecting the store to survive a reload**: it lives in the page. A reload loads it again from the server.
## Related pages

+ [Pinia](https://pinia.vuejs.org/)
+ [Requests: the generated client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities)
+ [Setting up the Vue application](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/REST-API -->

The **REST API** of a Caligrafy application is its capabilities, answered in JSON. One line maps a route to a
capability (`Route::capability`), or one line serves them all by name (`Route::capabilities`). Programs send a personal
access token; pages of the application send the session and its CSRF token. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write: add a book and return it; serve it as POST /api/books
```

Claude adds the `Route::capability` line to `web.php` and checks it with `curl`: without a token, with a token that lacks
the scope, and with a good one.

**Check** before you say OK: the calls answer `401`, `403` and `201` as below.
## By hand

1. **The routes.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:
    ```php
    // BOOKSHELF: REST
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');
    Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
    Route::capability('DELETE', '/api/books/{id}', 'delete_book');
    ```
    The method is `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE`. The route variables (`{id}`) become inputs.
2. **A token** for the program: `php caligrafer.php token create "Bookshelf agent" --scopes books:read,books:write`
   ([Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens)).
3. **Call it.**
    ```bash
    curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/books/3
    # {"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred","published_year":1979,...}}            200: get_book is public

    curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" -d '{"title": "Dune"}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
    # {"error":{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"Sign in or send a personal access token"}}   401

    curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
         -d '{"title": "The Lathe of Heaven", "published_year": 1971, "author_id": 1}' http://localhost:8080/api/books
    # {"data":{"id":7,"title":"The Lathe of Heaven",...}}   201
    ```
    A `POST` with neither a token nor `Accept: application/json` is taken for a form and answers `403` `[ERROR 3000]`.
## <a name="all"></a>Every capability by name: `Route::capabilities`

```php
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // GET lists, POST /capabilities/{name} calls
```

+ `GET /capabilities` answers what the caller may call, with the input schemas, and the session's CSRF token:
  `{"data": [{"name", "description", "scope", "level", "readOnly", "destructive", "public", "input"}, ...], "csrf": "..."}`.
  Web-only capabilities are left out.
+ `POST /capabilities/get_book` with `{"id": 3}` calls `get_book`. The
  [JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-JS-Client) uses these two routes.
## <a name="reference"></a>Requests and responses

**Who calls** (`Context::fromRequest`): `Authorization: Bearer cq_...` (a token), else the legacy API key, else the
session of a signed-in person, else a visitor.

**Inputs**: the JSON body, or the form fields, or the query string for `GET`; then the route variables, which win
(`/api/books/3?id=9` is the book 3). `_token`, `_method` and `uri` are never inputs. Of the inputs, the capability keeps
only those of its `$rules`.

**Files**: a capability with a `file` input takes a multipart upload; the file is saved once the caller is allowed, and
deleted again when the call fails.

**CSRF**: a call made with the session cookie that is not read-only needs the session's CSRF token in an `X-CSRF-Token`
header (or `_token`), else `403` "Missing or invalid CSRF token: send the X-CSRF-Token header". A token or the legacy key
is not a cookie, so it needs none.

**Responses**:

| Status | Body | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | `{"data": ...}` | a success |
| `201` | `{"data": ...}` | a `POST` to a capability that is not read-only |
| `401` | `{"error": {"code": "unauthenticated", "message": ...}}`, and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` | nobody, or an unknown, revoked or expired token |
| `403` | `{"error": {"code": "forbidden", ...}}` | the scope or the level is missing, or the CSRF token |
| `404` | `{"error": {"code": "not_found", ...}}` | no such capability, or the thing does not exist |
| `409` | `{"error": {"code": "conflict", ...}}` | it clashes with the current state |
| `422` | `{"error": {"code": "invalid", "message": ..., "fields": {...}}}` | an input is wrong, a message per field |

The data is plain: models become arrays of their columns. All the refusals:
[Refusing a call](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Refusing-a-Call-ServiceError).

Reference: [`Route::capability()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-capability),
[`Route::capabilities()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-capabilities),
[`Rest`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#rest).
## Common mistakes

+ **A write over the session without `X-CSRF-Token`** (G54): 403. Use the JS client, or send the `csrf` of `GET /capabilities`.
+ **A JSON call from a page without `Accept: application/json`** (G1): it is taken for a form and fails CSRF, `[ERROR 3000]`.
+ **`register_user` over REST** (G81): refused; sign-up is the sign-up page.
+ **A closure route for JSON** (G51): `Route::post('/x', function () {...})` is not protected for JSON. Use a capability route.
## Related pages

+ [The JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-JS-Client) · [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens)
+ [Services, capabilities and MCP: REST](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#rest)
+ [Controller APIs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.-Helpers-,-Forms-&-REST-API#restapi): the older way

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-JS-Client -->

The **JS client** is one ES module, with no dependency, that `php caligrafer.php client` writes from your capabilities:
one async function per capability (`create_book` becomes `createBook`), plus `call()`, `capabilities()`, `configure()`
and `CapabilityError`. Vue apps, the Vite SPA and Node scripts call the capabilities through it, with the session in a
page of the application and a token anywhere else. It talks to `Route::capabilities()`. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write: add a book from the Bookshelf Vue app
```

Claude adds `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` to `web.php`, runs `php caligrafer.php client` and calls `createBook`
from the app.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ every call of the app goes through a function of `capabilities.js`: no `axios`, `fetch` or `Authorization` header
  written by hand for capabilities;
+ `capabilities.js` was generated again after the last capability change.
## By hand

1. **The route.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:
    ```php
    Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // GET lists, POST /capabilities/{name} calls: the JS client uses it
    ```
2. **Generate the client.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js
    ```
    ```text
     public/js/capabilities.js written: 17 capabilities, calls /capabilities (Route::capabilities('/capabilities') in web.php)
     import { createBook, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'
    ```
    For a Vite SPA, write it in `public/<app>/src/capabilities.js`. With another prefix:
    `php caligrafer.php client --prefix /api/capabilities` for `Route::capabilities('/api/capabilities')`.
3. **Use it in a Vue app.**
    ```js
    import { createBook, listBooks, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'

    try {
      const book = await createBook({ title: this.title, published_year: this.year, author_id: this.authorId })
      this.books = (await listBooks({ author_id: book.author_id })).data
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof CapabilityError && e.code === 'invalid') this.errors = e.fields   // { published_year: '...' }
      else throw e
    }
    ```
    A Vue app loaded as a library imports it from the page:
    `this.api = await import(env.home + 'public/js/capabilities.js')`, then
    `this.api.configure({ baseUrl: env.home.replace(/\/$/, '') })`.
4. **From Node**, with a personal access token:
    ```js
    import { configure, listBooks } from './capabilities.mjs'

    configure({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', token: process.env.CALIGRAFY_TOKEN })
    const page = await listBooks({ page: 1 })
    ```
5. Run `client` again after you add or change a capability.
## <a name="api"></a>What the module exports

| Export | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| one function per capability, `createBook(input = {})` | calls it and returns its result (the `data` of the answer) |
| `call(name, input = {})` | calls any capability by name: `POST <prefix>/<name>` |
| `capabilities()` | what the caller may call, with the input schemas: `GET <prefix>` |
| `configure({ baseUrl, token, prefix, credentials })` | the application root (default: this origin), a personal access token, the prefix, the `fetch` credentials (default `same-origin`) |
| `CapabilityError` | thrown by a refused call: `status`, `code` (`invalid`, `forbidden`...), `message`, `fields` |

Each function carries a comment from the capability: its description, its flag (`read-only`, `destructive` or `writes`),
who may call it (`public`, the scope, or `signed in`) and its inputs, typed from the schema (`number`, `boolean` or
`string`; optional ones with `?`).

**In a page of the application** it uses the session: the cookie, and the CSRF token it reads once from `GET <prefix>`
and sends as `X-CSRF-Token` on every call that is not a `GET`. No key is ever in the bundle. **Elsewhere** (Node, another
origin) `configure({ token })` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead.

Left out of the module: [web-only capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Web-Only-Capabilities)
and Snap's own capabilities (`snap_*`).

Reference: [`Client::generate()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#client-generate),
[`Route::capabilities()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-capabilities).
## Common mistakes

+ **Forgetting `php caligrafer.php client` after a change**: the Vue app calls the old functions.
+ **A write over the session without `X-CSRF-Token`** (G54): 403. The client sends it; hand-written calls must too.
+ **A token or a key in a page or a Vue bundle**: browser code uses the session; tokens are for programs.
+ **The legacy API key in a client page** (G27, G50): while `LEGACY_API_KEY` is on, client pages get the key. Call
  capabilities with the JS client and set `LEGACY_API_KEY=false`.
## Related pages

+ [Vue: requests and capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests#capabilities)
+ [REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/REST-API) · [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens)
+ [Caligrafer: `client`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#client)
