<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/MCP-for-AI-Agents -->

[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), the Model Context Protocol, is how AI agents such as Claude Code and Cursor use
tools. With `Route::mcp('/mcp')` every capability is a tool: its name, its description, its input schema, and hints that
say whether it only reads or destroys data. An agent sees only the tools its token allows, and its calls go through the
same checks, validation and audit as everyone else's. Since 2.1.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only public: the catalog, for agents too
```

Claude adds `Route::mcp('/mcp')` to `web.php` when agents need it, creates a token with the scopes they need (shown once),
and checks `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `tools/list` with the agent's token lists the tools you expect, and not the ones its scopes do not allow;
+ an invalid `tools/call` answers `"isError": true` with a message per field.
## By hand

1. **The route.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:
    ```php
    Route::mcp('/mcp');   // AI agents: personal access tokens only
    ```
2. **A token.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "Bookshelf agent" --scopes books:read,books:write`
   ([Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens)).
3. **Connect Claude Code** over HTTP:
    ```bash
    claude mcp add --transport http bookshelf http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cq_..."
    ```
   or over stdio, the agent starting the server itself in the project folder:
    ```bash
    claude mcp add bookshelf -- docker compose exec -T dev-box php caligrafer.php mcp
    ```
4. **Try it as an agent does**, one JSON-RPC message per request:
    ```bash
    curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
         -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' http://localhost:8080/mcp
    curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
         -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"create_book","arguments":{"title":"Dune"}}}' \
         http://localhost:8080/mcp
    ```
    ```json
    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid\",\"message\":\"Some of the inputs are invalid\",\"fields\":{\"published_year\":\"The Published Year field is required\",\"author_id\":\"The Author Id field is required\"}}}"}],"isError":true}}
    ```
## <a name="tools"></a>From capabilities to tools

`tools/list` gives one tool per capability the token may call (`Capabilities::available()`): public ones, and those whose
scope and level it passes. Web-only capabilities and those declared `mcp: false` are left out.

```json
{"name": "create_book", "title": "Create book", "description": "Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.",
 "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 200, "description": "The title of the book"},
    "published_year": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1450, "maximum": 2026, "description": "The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)"},
    "summary": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 2000, "description": "Optional: one or two sentences about the book"},
    "author_id": {"type": "integer", "description": "The id of its author (list_authors)"}},
  "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["title", "published_year", "author_id"]},
 "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": false, "destructiveHint": false, "openWorldHint": false}}
```

| Tool field | From |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | the capability's `name` |
| `title` | the name with spaces, capitalized (`create_book`: Create book) |
| `description` | the capability's `description`: write it for an agent, with what it returns and where to find the ids it needs |
| `inputSchema` | its `$rules` and `$descriptions` ([Capability inputs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Inputs#schema)) |
| `readOnlyHint` | `readOnly` |
| `destructiveHint` | `destructive`, when it is not also read-only |
| `openWorldHint` | always `false` |

`initialize` answers the server's name (`APP_NAME`), the framework version and these instructions for the agent: "Tools
are the capabilities of this application that your token allows. Tools marked destructive delete or overwrite data:
confirm with the user first."

**Calls.** `tools/call` runs `Capabilities::call()` with the arguments. A success is `"isError": false`, the data as JSON
in `content[0].text` and the object in `structuredContent` (a list is given as `{"result": [...]}`). A refusal is a tool
result with `"isError": true` and the same error as REST, so the agent can read the reason and correct itself. A tool the
token cannot see, or one that does not exist, answers the JSON-RPC error `-32602` `Unknown tool: <name>`.

<a name="mcpfalse"></a>**`mcp: false`** keeps a capability out of the tools: one only a browser can use, such as a push
subscription. REST still reaches it.
## <a name="http"></a>Over HTTP: `Route::mcp`

+ `POST` only, one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request (no batches), answered in JSON (no event stream): `initialize`,
  `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. A notification (no `id`) gets `202` and no body. `GET` and `DELETE` answer `405`.
+ Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`; any other request gets the first.
+ **Personal access tokens only**, never the session or the legacy key. Without a valid token: `401`,
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` and `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Unauthorized: send Authorization: Bearer <personal access token>"}}`.
+ A browser request from another site (an `Origin` header) is refused with `403 Origin not allowed`, against DNS
  rebinding. Allowed: no `Origin` (agents), the application's own host, and the origins of `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in `.env`
  (comma separated, such as `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://inspector.example`).
+ A message that is not JSON, or not one JSON-RPC request, answers `400`.
## <a name="stdio"></a>Over stdio: `php caligrafer.php mcp`

One JSON-RPC message per line on standard input, one answer per line on standard output. Without a token it has full
access, like any command you run yourself, and says so on standard error:
`caligrafer mcp: no token, full local access (set CALIGRAFY_TOKEN to limit it)`. With `CALIGRAFY_TOKEN=cq_...` (or
`--token cq_...`) it has the rights of that token. For agents that reach the application over the network, use
`Route::mcp` and a token.

Reference: [`Route::mcp()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Route#route-mcp),
[`Mcp\Server`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-server),
[`Mcp\Http`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-http).
## Common mistakes

+ **Sending the legacy key to MCP** (G56): 401. MCP takes tokens only.
+ **`webOnly: true` on a feature agents need** (G143): it is not a tool. Keep the work in a plain capability.
+ **`register_user` over MCP** (G81): refused; sign-up is the sign-up page.
+ **No page to create tokens online** (G79): agents cannot connect to a deployed application without one.
## Related pages

+ [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Personal-Access-Tokens) · [Scopes and access](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Scopes-and-Access)
+ [Read-only and destructive capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Read-Only-and-Destructive-Capabilities)
+ [Services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#mcp)
+ [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/10.-Claude-Code-Plugin)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant -->

**Snap Cards** turn every capability of your app into a card a person can use, and **the assistant** answers what
they type, say or attach with those cards. One line of `web.php`, `Route::snap();`, gives every signed-in person a Home
that shows what needs them, and a conversation that keeps its context. Nothing to design: each card is built from what
your capability already declares (its rules, descriptions, `readOnly`, `destructive`), and shown the way your app
shows it: its card view in your app's own look, or a card designed in your design system ([how a card looks](#looks)). Since 2.23.0.

**Since 2.26.0** the assistant's free-text understanding with Claude needs `php caligrafer.php add snap` once (the Anthropic SDK); without it, with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the assistant answers from the cards' names and logs which command to run.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude adds `Route::snap();` to `web.php`, runs `php caligrafer.php snap install`, writes the hints of
`application/config/snap.php` for your capabilities (titles, columns, the numbers of Home with their actions, what
Home invites to browse), writes a card view for each main list and record from your own pages (so every card looks
like your app), adds the two scheduled jobs, and asks you for an Anthropic API key if you want the assistant
to understand free text.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap` shows `[ok]` on every line you need.
+ Signed in, `/assistant` greets you; `/snap` shows one card per capability you may use.
+ `php caligrafer.php snap views` shows `[ok]` for each card view.
## <a name="start"></a>By hand, in three steps

**1. One line in `application/config/routing/web.php`** (after `Auth::authentication(...)`: the assistant is for
signed-in people):

```php
Route::snap();
```

**2. Its tables, and a starter hints file:**

```bash
php caligrafer.php snap install
```

It creates the `caligrafy_snap_*` tables (they also come with `php caligrafer.php platform install`, and with every
deploy) and `application/config/snap.php`, then prints what is ready:

```text
 Snap Cards and the assistant
  [ok] Tables            caligrafy_snap_*
  [ok] Route             Route::snap(); in application/config/routing/web.php
  [ok] Card hints        application/config/snap.php (optional: cards work without it)
  [--] Background tasks  the queue runs them: array('name' => 'queue', 'capability' => 'queue_work', ...)
  [--] Routines          array('name' => 'snap-routines', 'capability' => 'snap_routines_due', ...)
  [--] Assistant model   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env (without it the assistant answers from the cards' names)
```

**3. Open `/assistant`.** That is all you need. The three lines marked `[--]` are optional:

+ **Background tasks**: a capability declared `#[Capability(..., async: true)]` runs in the queue (see
  [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)): add the `queue_work` job to
  `application/config/schedule.php`.
+ **Routines** (things the assistant does for a person on a rhythm): add
  `array('name' => 'snap-routines', 'capability' => 'snap_routines_due', 'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 50)`.
+ **The assistant's model**: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` in `.env` (a key from console.anthropic.com, API keys). Without it,
  the assistant still answers the names of your cards ("the catalog", "lend a book"), your shortcuts and "What can I
  do?"; with it, Claude understands anything ("lend Kindred to Sam for a week", "who wrote it?").

`Route::snap(['assistant' => '/help', 'cards' => '/cards'])` puts them at other addresses.
## <a name="what"></a>What people get

| Address | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `/assistant` | **Home**: what needs them now, the numbers that call for an action, things to browse, their shortcuts; and the **task space**: one answer at a time, with what to do next |
| `/assistant/noticed` | What the assistant noticed (only if they turned noticing on), and their routines |
| `/snap` | Every card they may use (a gallery); `/snap/c/<capability>` one card at its own address |

**Home** is an orchestrator: it decides what the person should concentrate on and puts it first.
+ The assistant says it in at most two lines: what needs them on a line of its own, then one nudge
  ("Since you looked at Kindred, you might like Parable of the Sower.").
+ Sections, in the order of what to do: **Needs you** (alerts, tasks waiting for an answer, changes to confirm),
  insights, **For you** (offers), **In progress**, things to browse, **Just done**, **Your shortcuts**.
+ Each kind of card has its own shape (the card grammar below), and every row is full.

**The task space** is a conversation:
+ The assistant's line sits on the page; the cards are white, and read as the rest of the sentence.
+ Suggestions say what to do next, never a dead end (*Back to Home*, *What else can I do?*).
+ It keeps the context: "it", "this one", "him" mean what is on screen; "delete it" works at once.
+ Back and forth, history, a rating, a different answer; the keyboard (⌥K / Alt+K to type, ⌥M / Alt+M to talk);
  the + attaches pictures, PDFs and text files for the assistant to read.
## <a name="cards"></a>The cards: five families, nine types

Every card names its family with its type. People never see these names; they are how you talk about the cards.

| Family | Type | What it does | Built from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Ask** | Form | asks for the inputs still missing | the rules and descriptions of a capability |
| **Ask** | Choice | one pick (a book, an author) | a `*_id` input and the list it comes from |
| **Ask** | Confirm | what will change, before it changes | any capability that is not `readOnly` |
| **Show** | Answer | one record, a value, a message | the result of a read |
| **Show** | List | rows that open | a list result (with pages) |
| **Go** | Shortcut | a card a person saved, one click away | the person |
| **Track** | Task | work running in the background | `async: true` |
| **Offer** | Suggestion | the moment they usually do something; an alert | noticing; the hint `alert` |
| **Offer** | Routine | do it for them on a rhythm | noticing |

**A change only ever runs from its Confirm.** The Confirm carries a one-time token tied to the person, the capability
and these exact inputs; the assistant's model never sees it, and a card at an address never changes data. A change that
can be undone (an update, a creation, a hint `undo`) offers **Undo** right after.
## <a name="looks"></a>How a card looks: card views

A card that shows data (a list, a record) shows it the way your app does, at the size of a card (since 2.25.0):

1. **Its card view.** `application/views/snap/<capability>.pug` is a small Pug view made for the card, in your app's own
   markup and classes, rendered by the server inside the card. It keeps only what the card needs: a list's rows, a
   record's header and summary; the page around it (its title, tabs, filters, forms) stays on the page, and the card
   adds its own actions under it.

   ```pug
   //- snap card of list_books, from Bookshelf/books.pug 5fb9e0cf
   ul.cq-rows
       each $b in $rows
           li.cq-row
               .cq-row-main
                   p.cq-row-title
                       a(href="{$home}books/{$b['id']}", data-snap-open='get_book', data-snap-input=json_encode(array('id' => $b['id'])))= $b['title']
                   p.cq-row-meta= $b['author']['name'] . ', ' . $b['published_year']
   ```

   It gets `$rows` and `$page` (`page`, `pages`, `total`) for a list, `$record` for one record, `$result` (what the
   capability returned), `$input`, `$card`, `$home`, `$authorized` and `$user`. A link with `data-snap-open` and
   `data-snap-input` opens that card in the conversation. Its first line names the page it was made from and that
   page's fingerprint (`shasum application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug | cut -c1-8`): when the page changes,
   `php caligrafer.php snap views` and `doctor` say the card view is stale.

   **Claude writes them**: `/caligrafy-quill:assistant` reads each page and the scripts that draw it, keeps the part
   that matters and writes the card view with your classes only (a built stylesheet, such as Tailwind's, is checked
   class by class).
2. **The part of a page marked for it**, when there is no card view: `data-snap="<capability>"` on an element of the
   view whose first data it is shows that part alone, in a frame sized to it.
3. **A card designed for its data**, when there is neither, in your design system: the `--design-*` tokens of
   [`DESIGN_STYLE`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles), else Caligrafy's. A record becomes a
   hero (its name, a line under it, badges with a tone), a few numbers, its details, its text and its tags; a list
   becomes rows. With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Claude designs it from a sample of the data once per shape of data (kept 30
   days); without a key, rules do.

A card never shows a whole page. The hints decide otherwise:

```php
'search_books' => array('card' => 'snap/list_books'),   // the same rows as the catalog: its card view
'get_user' => array('card' => false),                     // no card view
'get_book' => array('view' => 'Bookshelf/book'),          // without a card view: this page, whole
'list_people' => array('design' => array('title' => 'name', 'subtitle' => 'role', 'meta' => array('email', 'active_cases'),
    'badge' => array('path' => 'status', 'tones' => array('away' => 'warning')))),   // a designed card, by hand
```

```text
php caligrafer.php snap views

 Card views (application/views/snap/<capability>.pug)
  [ok] get_book                   from Bookshelf/book.pug
  [ok] list_authors               made for the card (no page)
  [!!] list_books                 Bookshelf/books.pug changed since its card view was made: write it again
  [--] get_user                   no card view: a card designed from its data
```
## <a name="grammar"></a>Home's card grammar

Each section of Home uses one template, chosen by what the person does with it:

| Template | For | Width | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| banner | act now: alerts, waiting for an answer, failed, to confirm | full width, stacked | tinted by severity, a severity tag, its one action |
| offer | decide: suggestions, routines | halves | the question, why, Yes and Not now |
| progress | watch: tasks waiting or running | full-width rows | what it is doing now, its time, a live bar, a status |
| object | browse: the things your app is about | thirds (alone: a feature card) | why it is here, its name, two facts |
| update | revisit: just done | full-width rows | the result, how long ago, Done or Failed |
| shortcut | go | quarters | an icon and a name |
| insight | measure | a strip at the top | a number, and the action it calls for |

**The count rule**: a row has as many columns as cards (up to the template's most: offers 2, objects 3, shortcuts 4),
so no row has a hole; what does not fit is behind *See all*.
## <a name="hints"></a>Hints: `application/config/snap.php`

Cards work without hints. A hint makes one better: its name, the columns of a list, the words the assistant says,
the numbers of Home with their actions, what Home invites to browse, when an action applies.

```php
<?php
return array(
    'about' => 'a library app: the books of a catalog, their authors, and the books lent to people',
    'cards' => array(
        'list_books' => array(
            'title' => 'The catalog',
            'columns' => array('title', 'author.name', 'published_year'),
            'empty' => 'No book yet.',
            'insight' => array('label' => 'New this month', 'since' => array('field' => 'created_at', 'days' => 30),
                'action' => array('capability' => 'list_books', 'text' => 'Browse the catalog')),
            'discover' => array('open' => 'get_book', 'key' => 'id', 'title' => 'title', 'meta' => array('author.name', 'published_year'),
                'new' => 'created_at', 'related' => 'author.id', 'opened' => array('get_book' => 'id'),
                'unavailable' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'), 'available_label' => 'On the shelf',
                'title_section' => 'On the shelf for you'),
        ),
        'lend_book' => array('done' => 'Done! {heading} is lent. Enjoy the read.',
            'applies' => array('not_in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
        'return_book' => array('applies' => array('in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
        'reading_report' => array('working' => array('Counting the books of each author…', 'Putting the report together…')),
    ),
);
```

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `title`, `lead`, `submit`, `icon` | the card's name, its line, its button, its icon (Lucide names) |
| `columns`, `labels`, `hide`, `noun`, `variant` | a list's columns, the labels of fields, fields left out, what its rows are ("authors") |
| `values`, `choices` | the labels of fixed values; where a `*_id` field's choices come from |
| `open` | which capability a list's row opens (`array('capability' => 'get_book', 'input' => 'id', 'from' => 'book_id')`) |
| `full` | the page that shows the same thing in full (`'/books/{id}'`) |
| `empty`, `empty_next` | what an empty list says; what would fill it (`array('lend_book')`) |
| `done`, `consequence`, `confirm` | the assistant's line once done (`{heading}`), the line under a Confirm, its question |
| `undo` | what undoes it (`array('capability' => 'return_book', 'map' => array('book_id' => 'book_id'))`) |
| `next` | what it leads to (suggestions after it) |
| `applies` | when an action can be done to a record (`in` or `not_in` a list) |
| `alert` | an alert on Home when rows carry a flag (`'when' => 'overdue'`), with its action and tag |
| `insight` | a number on Home, only with the action it calls for |
| `discover` | the things Home invites to browse: more like what the person looked at, new, available by your rule |
| `working`, `async` | what a background task says while it runs; async without the attribute |
| `card` | its card view (`'snap/list_books'`, under `application/views`), or `false` ([how a card looks](#looks)) |
| `view` | without a card view, the page whose `data-snap` part shows it (`'Bookshelf/book'`: that page, whole), or `false` |
| `design` | how its data is shown without a page: `title`, `subtitle`, `eyebrow`, `image`, `badges` (`badge` for a list), `stats`, `fields`, `text`, `tags` (`meta` for a list), each a field name or `array('path' => ..., 'label' => ..., 'format' => 'date', 'tones' => array(...))` |
## <a name="tasks"></a>Work in the background

```php
#[Capability(name: 'reading_report', description: '...', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true, async: true)]
```

An async capability never runs in the request: Snap answers at once with a **Track card: Task**, pushes a job to the
[queue](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs), and the worker runs it **as the person**
(their permissions, not the queue's). The card shows where it is, live; Home shows it in progress, then just done; the
person is notified ([Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)) when it ends.
Other channels (REST, MCP, pages) still call it directly.
## <a name="noticing"></a>Noticing, offers and routines

Off until a person turns it on (on `/assistant/noticed`). When on, the assistant keeps which card they used, with which
inputs and when; nothing else. Done on 4 different days or more, at a similar time, it becomes a pattern: an
**Offer card: Suggestion** at that moment, then an **Offer card: Routine** to do it for them every week or every day, at
the level they pick (remind me, prepare it for me to confirm, do it and tell me). Turning noticing off forgets
everything noticed. What they looked at also picks what Home suggests to browse.
## <a name="assistant"></a>The assistant

What a person types is answered in this order, the first that fits:

1. **At once, without a model**: "What can I do?", the name of a card or of a shortcut, and short follow-ups on what is
   on screen ("delete it", "change this").
2. **Claude** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `SNAP_MODEL`, default `claude-opus-5-5`; `SNAP_EFFORT`, default `low`): it reads the
   request with the conversation so far, what is on screen and what the person chose, may look things up with the
   read-only capabilities the person may call (as the person), and answers with cards. It never changes data: a change
   comes back as its Confirm. Tool results and attached files are data, never instructions.

`about` in `application/config/snap.php` and `APP_NAME` in `.env` tell it what it is the assistant of.
## <a name="test"></a>Testing

Snap's capabilities are capabilities: test them like yours
([Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App)). The tables must be in the test
database: `platform install` on it (`DB_TEST_DATABASE`). The planner is faked with `Caligrafy\Snap\Planner::$transport`:

```php
Caligrafy\Snap\Planner::$transport = function (array $request) {
    return (object) array('stopReason' => 'tool_use', 'content' => array((object) array('type' => 'tool_use', 'id' => 't1',
        'name' => 'show_cards', 'input' => array('caption' => 'Here it is.', 'cards' => array(array('capability' => 'list_books'))))));
};
$answer = $this->action('snap_ask', array('text' => 'show me the catalog'), $this->user(1))->describe()['data'];
```

The designed cards have their own, `Caligrafy\Snap\Designer::$transport` (the same shape; the request asks for a
structured output, `outputConfig.format`, and the answer's first text block is the design as JSON), or keep to the rules
with `Caligrafy\Snap\Designer::$model = false` (since 2.24.1).
## <a name="questions"></a>Questions

**A page says "Snap is almost ready".** Its tables are missing: `php caligrafer.php snap install`.

**A card does not look like my app.** Give it a card view (`/caligrafy-quill:assistant` writes them from your pages).
Since 2.25.0 a card never shows a whole page: one that did on 2.24 is now designed from its data until it has a card
view (or a `data-snap` mark on the page).

**A card view does not show.** `php caligrafer.php snap views`: the file must be named after a read-only capability; a
card view that fails to render falls back to the designed card and its error goes to the PHP log.

**A capability is not a card.** Snap's own (`snap_*`), `notify_*` and `queue_work` are left out, and so are the
capabilities the person may not call: a card always respects permissions.

**Can agents use Snap?** Agents already use your capabilities over MCP; the `snap_*` capabilities serve a person's
shell: they are not MCP tools, nor functions of the generated JS client. `snap_card` and `snap_catalog` are capabilities, though: a program can ask for the card of
any capability.


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards -->

The **Ask** cards are the cards of [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant)
that ask a person for something before anything runs: **Ask: Form** asks for the inputs still missing, **Ask: Choice**
asks for one pick, and **Ask: Confirm** shows what a change will do and waits for the person's click. Nothing to design:
each is built from what the capability already declares (its `$rules`, `$descriptions`, `readOnly`, `destructive`).
Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude adds `Route::snap();`, runs `php caligrafer.php snap install` and writes the hints of
`application/config/snap.php` for your capabilities: the titles, the labels of fields, where a `*_id` field's choices
come from, the line under a Confirm.

**Check**

+ Signed in, `/snap/c/create_book` shows the form of `create_book`, with a pick list for `author_id`.
+ Sending it shows a Confirm first; nothing is added until you click it.
## By hand

Ask cards need nothing but `Route::snap();` in `web.php` (after `Auth::authentication(...)`) and the Snap tables
(`php caligrafer.php snap install`): every capability the person may call gets its card. Take the capability of
[Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service):

```php
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book', scope: 'books:write')]
class CreateBook extends Service {
    public $rules = ['title' => 'required|max_len,255', 'author_id' => 'required|integer'];
    public $filters = ['title' => 'trim|sanitize_string'];
    public $descriptions = ['title' => 'The title of the book'];
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        return (new Book('books'))->create($input);
    }
}
```

1. **Ask: Form.** Open `/snap/c/create_book`. The card has a field per input of `$rules` (the input `page` is left
   out); its limits come from the rules (`max_len,255` is a maximum length), its help line from
   `$descriptions`, its button from the capability's verb ("Add").
2. **Ask: Choice.** `author_id` is a `<thing>_id`, and `list_authors` is a read-only capability the person may call: the
   field becomes a pick among the authors. Open `/snap/c/create_book?in={"title":"Kindred"}`: with the title known, one
   pick is all that is missing, so the card is an **Ask: Choice** ("Which author?"), with what was already said shown
   read-only above it.
3. **Ask: Confirm.** Send the card. `create_book` is not `readOnly`, so it does not run: Snap answers with its Confirm
   (what will change, its question, its button "Yes, add"), and only the person's click runs it. A change that can be
   undone then offers **Undo**.
## <a name="form"></a>Reference: what builds an Ask card

`Caligrafy\Snap\Cards::ask()` builds the card ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards-ask)),
`Cards::fields()` its fields ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards-fields)):

| A field gets | From |
|---|---|
| its label | the hint `labels`, else the input's name in words, without `_id` (`published_year`: "Published year", `author_id`: "Author"); the `id` of `get_`, `update_` or `delete_<thing>` is named after the thing |
| its help line | `$descriptions` (a help line that starts with "The id of" is dropped when the field is a pick: a person picks by name) |
| required or not | the capability's schema (`required` in its rules) |
| its limits | the schema: `min`, `max`, `minlength`, `maxlength` |
| a select | the hint `values` (`array(1 => 'Monday', ...)`), or an `enum` in the schema |
| a pick (`choice`) | the first of: the hint `choices`, an `exists,<table>.<column>` rule (`list_<table>`), a `<thing>_id` input (`list_<things>`), the `id` of `get_`/`update_`/`delete_<thing>` (`list_<things>`); only a read-only capability the person may call, with 50 options at most (`Cards::MAX_OPTIONS`) |
| its icon | the hint `icons`, else a few known field names, else a dot |
| its current value | an `update_<thing>` form starts from the record of `get_<thing>` with the same `id` (the hint `current` names another reader) |

The options of a pick are the rows of its list: the value is `id` and the label the row's `title`, `name` or
`username`; `'choices' => array('author_id' => array('capability' => 'list_authors', 'value' => 'id', 'label' => 'name'))`
says otherwise.

A card is an **Ask: Choice** when exactly one required input is missing, it is a pick, and there are no errors to show;
anything else is an **Ask: Form**. `Cards::needsInput()` decides whether an Ask card still needs the person: a required
input is missing, or only the id of a thing to change was given (an `update_` starts as its form); a delete needs
nothing more than its id.
## <a name="confirm"></a>Reference: Ask: Confirm and consent

**A change only ever runs from its Confirm.** `Caligrafy\Snap\Flow::next()` decides the next card of any capability,
whoever asks (a card that is sent, the assistant's fast path, the model's choice):

```text
read:          inputs missing -> its Ask card; complete -> runs -> Show card
write/destroy: inputs missing -> its Ask card; refused by its rules -> Ask with errors; else -> Ask: Confirm
```

`Caligrafy\Snap\Consent` ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-consent)) makes the
Confirm:

+ what will change (before and after), and a one-time token bound to this person, this capability and these exact
  inputs, for 10 minutes (`Consent::TTL`), kept in the session, never in the card's address. Only the person's click on
  that card sends it back: a model, a page or a link cannot make one.
+ a confirmed change is recorded in the [audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#audit)
  (capability `snap_confirm`).
+ what undoes it: what was true before (an `update_`), what was created (`create_` is undone by `delete_`), or the hint
  `undo`. Undoing is a change too: it gets its own Confirm.

The Confirm's words: its question is the hint `confirm`, else "<title>: <subject>?"; the line under it is the hint
`consequence`, else *This cannot be undone.* for a `destructive` capability, *You can undo it right after.* when it can
be undone, *This cannot be undone from here.* otherwise. Its button is the hint `submit` (or the verb), as
"Yes, <verb>" (a delete names what it deletes).
## Common mistakes

+ **A pick shows as a text field.** Its list must be a read-only capability the person may call, named `list_<things>`
  (or given by the hint `choices`), with 50 rows at most.
+ **Hints on the capability.** Titles, labels, `choices`, `confirm` are keys of `application/config/snap.php`, keyed by
  capability name; a key the framework does not know is ignored silently (G157).
+ **A capability is not a card.** Snap's own (`snap_*`), `notify_*`, `queue_work` and web-only capabilities are left
  out, and so are the capabilities the person may not call.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards -->

The **Show** cards of [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) show
what a read returned: **Show: List** for rows (with their pages), that open one by one, and **Show: Answer** for one
record, a value or a message. A read-only capability whose inputs are complete runs at once and answers with its Show
card. Since 2.23.0; how they look (card views, designed cards) since 2.24.0 and 2.25.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude writes the hints of the lists (`title`, `columns`, `empty`, `open`) and a card view for each main list and
record from your own pages, so the cards look like your app.

**Check**

+ `/snap/c/list_books` shows the catalog as rows; a row opens its book.
+ `php caligrafer.php snap views` shows `[ok]` for each card view.
## By hand

With `Route::snap();` in `web.php` and the Snap tables, every read-only capability the person may call is a Show card
as soon as its inputs are complete:

1. **Show: List.** `list_books` returns a list (or a page of
   [`paginate()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Pagination)): `/snap/c/list_books` is a
   Show: List. Its rows open `get_book` because the name says so (`list_books` and `search_books` open
   `get_book` with the row's `id`, when the person may call it).
2. **Show: Answer.** `get_book` returns one record: `/snap/c/get_book?in={"id":3}` is a Show: Answer, a record named
   by its own name, with the actions of the same thing the person may call (`update_book` as *Change*, `delete_book` as
   *Delete*, and other `<verb>_book` capabilities such as `lend_book`), each an Ask card.
3. **Better words and columns.** In `application/config/snap.php`:
    ```php
    <?php
    return array(
        'cards' => array(
            'list_books' => array(
                'title' => 'The catalog',
                'columns' => array('title', 'author.name', 'published_year'),
                'empty' => 'No book yet.',
            ),
        ),
    );
    ```
## <a name="list"></a>Reference: Show: List

`Caligrafy\Snap\Cards::show()` builds both ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards-show)).
A result that is a list (or a page: `data`, `total`, `pages`) is a List:

| The card's | Comes from |
|---|---|
| title | the hint `title`, else the capability's name in words |
| columns | the hint `columns` (a related row's field is named after the relation: `author.name` is "Author"), else the first row's fields, without `id`, `*_id`, passwords, `created_at`, `updated_at` and long texts (over 140 characters), a related row by its `name` or `title`; 5 at most |
| what a row opens | the hint `open` (`array('capability' => 'get_book', 'input' => 'id', 'from' => 'book_id')`), else `get_<thing>` for `list_<things>` and `search_<things>` |
| its count line | the total and the hint `noun` ("authors"), else a noun from the name |
| an empty list | the hint `empty`, else *Nothing here yet.*; the hint `empty_next` names what would fill it |
| pages | `page`, `pages`, `total` of a `paginate()` page |
| its look | `variant` (`rows` by default), then its card view, else the part of its page marked for it, else rows designed for its data ([card views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Card-Views)) |
## <a name="answer"></a>Reference: Show: Answer

| The result | The card |
|---|---|
| one record (an array) | variant `record`: its heading is the record's own title or name, else the title or name of the record it is about (a loan is about its book), else its username, else `#id` (`Cards::name()`); its fields; its actions; its card view or designed blocks |
| a value | variant `fact`: the value; `true` and `false` read *Yes* and *No*; nothing reads *Done* |

**The actions of a record** are the capabilities of the same thing the person may call: `update_<thing>` (*Change*),
`delete_<thing>` (*Delete*), and any other `<verb>_<thing>` (it gets `<thing>_id`). The hint `applies` keeps only what
can be done now:

```php
'lend_book' => array('applies' => array('not_in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
'return_book' => array('applies' => array('in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
```

The list is read as the person, once per request; a list they may not read leaves the action out
([`Cards::applies()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards-applies)).

**A refusal that is not about the inputs** (not found, conflict, forbidden) is a notice instead of a result
([`Cards::notice()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards#snap-cards-notice)); a refusal about
the inputs comes back as the Ask card with its errors.
## Common mistakes

+ **A row does not open.** The getter must be named `get_<thing>` for `list_<things>`, and the person must be allowed
  to call it; or give the hint `open`.
+ **A card shows a whole page** on 2.24. Since 2.25.0 a card never does: it shows its card view, else the part of a page
  marked `data-snap`, else a card designed from its data (G163).
+ **`select()` with models** fills the other columns with `null`, and the card shows them: add `arrays()` (G138).
## Related pages

+ [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant)
+ [Snap: card views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Card-Views): how a Show card looks
+ [Snap: Ask cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards)
+ [Snap: hints](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Hints)
+ [API: Snap\Cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap-Cards)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Go-and-Track-Cards -->

Two families of [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) cards belong
to a person rather than to a capability: **Go: Shortcut**, a card they saved (a capability with its inputs) run with
one click, and **Track: Task**, work that runs in the background for them and shows where it is. Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude marks the slow capabilities `async: true`, writes their `working` lines in `application/config/snap.php` and
adds the `queue_work` job to `application/config/schedule.php`. Shortcuts need nothing: people save their own.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap` shows `[ok] Background tasks`.
+ On `/assistant`, *Save* on a card adds it under **Your shortcuts**; typing its title runs it.
+ An async card answers at once with a Task card that moves from *Waiting to start* to *Done*.
## <a name="shortcut"></a>Go: Shortcut

A person saves a card from its *Save* control (the capability `snap_shortcut_save`: a `title` of up to 80 characters,
the `capability` and its `inputs`). Their shortcuts are on Home, under **Your shortcuts**, and typing a shortcut's title
in the assistant runs it at once, without a model.

+ **Running one goes through `Snap\Flow` like any card**: a read shows its result, a change asks for its Confirm. A
  shortcut never skips consent.
+ **Only to a capability the person may use**: saving one to another is refused.
+ **12 per person** (`Shortcuts::MAX`): a 13th answers *You have 12 shortcuts already: delete one first.*
+ A Show card says whether it is one of the person's shortcuts already, so its control reads *Save* or *Remove*.
+ The menu ("What can I do?") is a Go: Shortcut too, in its `menu` variant: the ready-made starts the app offers, not the
  ones a person saved.

They are kept in `caligrafy_snap_shortcuts` ([API: Snap\Shortcuts](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-shortcuts)).
## <a name="task"></a>Track: Task

A capability declared `async: true` never runs in the request when a Snap card starts it:

```php
#[Capability(name: 'reading_report', description: '...', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true, async: true)]
```

The hint `'async' => true` in `application/config/snap.php` does the same without the attribute. Then:

1. **A read** starts as a task at once; **a change** after its Ask: Confirm.
2. The task is a row of `caligrafy_snap_tasks` and a job of the [queue](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
   (`snap_task_run`).
3. The worker runs the capability **as the person who asked** (their user, the web channel: their permissions, not the
   queue's full access), keeps the card it ends with, and notifies them
   ([Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)).

| Status | The card says | Then |
|---|---|---|
| `queued` | *Waiting to start* | |
| `running` | *Working on it* (and the hint `working` lines, in turn) | |
| `done` | *Done* | the Show card of the result |
| `needs_input` | *Needs your answer* | the Ask card of what the capability refused: the person answers it, a new task starts |
| `failed` | *Could not finish* | a notice, after the queue's retries |

Home shows tasks under **In progress**, then **Just done**; the ones that wait for an answer or failed are under
**Needs you**.

```php
'reading_report' => array('working' => array('Counting the books of each author…', 'Putting the report together…')),
```

**The queue must run.** Add the job to `application/config/schedule.php` (see
[Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)), or run
`php caligrafer.php queue work`; without it, tasks stay *Waiting to start*.
## Common mistakes

+ **`async: true` only changes Snap** (G155). REST, MCP, `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `$this->call()` and
  `php caligrafer.php call` still run the capability in the request.
+ **Tasks never start**: the queue does not run (G155).
+ **A shortcut to a change runs it at once**: it does not. It asks for its Confirm, every time.
## Related pages

+ [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#tasks)
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
+ [Snap: Offer cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Offer-Cards): routines run as tasks
+ [API: Snap\Tasks](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-tasks) · [Snap\Shortcuts](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-shortcuts)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Offer-Cards -->

The **Offer** cards of [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) are the
assistant's own suggestions. **Offer: Suggestion** comes at the moment a person usually does something, or when rows need
them (an alert). **Offer: Routine** offers to do it for them on that
rhythm. Both come from **noticing**, which is off until each person turns it on. Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude adds the routines' job to `application/config/schedule.php` and writes the `alert` hints of the lists whose rows
carry a flag (an overdue loan).

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap` shows `[ok] Routines`.
+ On `/assistant/noticed`, turning noticing on and off works, and off forgets what was noticed.
## By hand

1. **The routines' job**, in `application/config/schedule.php` (see
   [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)):
    ```php
    array('name' => 'snap-routines', 'capability' => 'snap_routines_due', 'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 50)
    ```
   Routines at the *auto* level run as [tasks](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Go-and-Track-Cards#task),
   so the queue must run too.
2. **An alert**, for rows that need someone now, in `application/config/snap.php`:
    ```php
    'list_loans' => array('alert' => array('when' => 'overdue', 'message' => '{count} loan{s} overdue', 'label' => 'borrower')),
    ```
   When rows of `list_loans` (a read-only capability) have a true `overdue`, Home shows an Offer: Suggestion in its
   `alert` variant under **Needs you**; `'action' => '<capability>'` adds the button that takes care of it.
3. **People turn noticing on** at `/assistant/noticed`. Nothing is noticed before.
## <a name="noticing"></a>Reference: noticing

`Caligrafy\Snap\Offers` ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-offers)):

+ **Opt-in per person**, off by default. When on, the assistant keeps which card they used, with which inputs and when
  (a read that ran, a change they confirmed, a task they started); nothing else. `/assistant/noticed` shows every
  pattern, each deletable; turning noticing off deletes everything noticed.
+ **A pattern** is the same request (capability and inputs) in the last 42 days (`WINDOW_DAYS`):
  + **weekly**: on 3 days or more (`MIN_DAYS`) of the same weekday, around the same hour ("You did this 3 Mondays in a
    row, around 9 am.");
  + **daily**: on 4 different days or more, around the same hour ("You did this on 4 different days, around 9 am.").

  Anything weaker says nothing.
+ **At most 2 offers at a time** (`MAX_OFFERS`): routines that are due, then suggestions of this moment, then routines
  to propose; never one dismissed. Each says why, and has *Not now* (today) and *Don't suggest this again* (never).
+ What a person opened also picks what Home suggests to browse (the hint `discover`).
## <a name="routine"></a>Reference: routines

Accepting an Offer: Routine is itself a change, with its Ask: Confirm (`snap_routine_save`), recorded in the audit log.
The person picks a level:

| Level | At the moment of the routine |
|---|---|
| `suggest` | an Offer: Suggestion |
| `confirm` | its Ask: Confirm, ready, under **Needs you** |
| `auto` | it runs as a task of its owner (the job `snap_routines_due`), and they are told |

A delete is never done on a rhythm: *A delete is never done on a rhythm.* A routine is stopped with
`snap_routine_delete`, from `/assistant/noticed`.
## <a name="alert"></a>Reference: alerts

The hint `alert` on a read-only capability whose rows carry a flag:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `when` | the field of a row that makes it count (true, not empty) |
| `message` | the line; `{count}` is how many rows, `{s}` an `s` when more than one |
| `title`, `reason` | the card's title and why (`{count}` works there too) |
| `label` | the field each row is named by (`title` by default); 5 are listed |
| `action`, `yes` | the capability that takes care of it and its button (*Take care of it*); without it, or when the person may not call it, the alert opens the list (*See them*) |
| `tag`, `severity` | *Needs you* and `danger` by default |
## Common mistakes

+ **No offer ever comes.** Noticing is off until the person turns it on; a pattern needs 3 weekdays or 4 days around one
  hour.
+ **Routines at the auto level never run.** The `snap-routines` job is missing from `schedule.php`, or the queue does
  not run.
+ **Hints on the capability.** `alert` is a key of `application/config/snap.php`, not of `#[Capability]` (G157).
## Related pages

+ [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#noticing)
+ [Snap: Go and Track cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Go-and-Track-Cards)
+ [Snap: hints](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Hints)
+ [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)
+ [API: Snap\Offers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-offers)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Card-Views -->

A **card view** makes a [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) card
that shows data (a list, a record) look like your app: `application/views/snap/<capability>.pug` is a small Pug view,
in your own markup and classes, that the server renders inside the card. Without one, the card shows the part of a page
marked for it, or a card designed for its data in your design system. A card never shows a whole page. Since 2.25.0
(the `data-snap` mark and designed cards since 2.24.0).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude reads each page and the scripts that draw it, keeps the part that matters (a list's rows, a record's header and
summary) and writes the card view with your classes only (a built stylesheet, such as Tailwind's, is checked class by
class).

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap views` shows `[ok]` for each card view.
+ `/snap/c/list_books` shows the rows as the catalog page does, without its title, tabs and filters.
## By hand

1. **Write the card view.** It is named after a read-only capability: `application/views/snap/list_books.pug`. Its
   first line names the page it was made from and that page's fingerprint
   (`shasum application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug | cut -c1-8`):
    ```pug
    //- snap card of list_books, from Bookshelf/books.pug 5fb9e0cf
    ul.cq-rows
        each $b in $rows
            li.cq-row
                .cq-row-main
                    p.cq-row-title
                        a(href="{$home}books/{$b['id']}", data-snap-open='get_book', data-snap-input=json_encode(array('id' => $b['id'])))= $b['title']
                    p.cq-row-meta= $b['author']['name'] . ', ' . $b['published_year']
    ```
   Pug in Caligrafy is PHP: strings join with `.`, never `+`.
2. **Check it.**
    ```bash
    php caligrafer.php snap views
    ```
    ```text
     Card views (application/views/snap/<capability>.pug)
      [ok] get_book                   from Bookshelf/book.pug
      [ok] list_authors               made for the card (no page)
      [!!] list_books                 Bookshelf/books.pug changed since its card view was made: write it again
      [--] get_user                   no card view: a card designed from its data
    ```
   `snap views` exits 1 when a card view is stale; `php caligrafer.php doctor` warns too (*Snap card views*).
## <a name="variables"></a>Reference: what a card view gets

| Variable | What it is |
|---|---|
| `$rows`, `$page` | for a list: its rows, and `page`, `pages`, `total` of a `paginate()` page |
| `$record` | for one record |
| `$result` | what the capability returned, pages included, as plain arrays |
| `$input` | the card's inputs |
| `$card` | the card: its `capability` and `title` |
| `$home`, `$authorized`, `$user` | the address of the application (ending with `/`), whether someone is signed in, who |

A link with `data-snap-open="<capability>"` and `data-snap-input='{"id":7}'` opens that card in the conversation
instead of leaving it. A card view is inserted as HTML: its `<script>` tags do not run (G163).
## <a name="order"></a>Reference: how a Show card looks, best first

`Caligrafy\Snap\Views` ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-views)) decides:

1. **Its card view**: `application/views/snap/<capability>.pug`, or the view the hint `card` names
   (`'card' => 'snap/list_books'`, under `application/views`); `'card' => false` for none. One that fails to render
   falls back to the designed card, and its error goes to the PHP log.
2. **The part of its page marked for it**: on the view of a `Route::page` whose first data is this capability, the
   element with `data-snap="<capability>"` is shown alone, in a frame sized to it. A whole page only when the hint
   `view` names it (`'view' => 'Bookshelf/book'`); `'view' => false` for none.
3. **A card designed for its data** (`Caligrafy\Snap\Designer`), in your design system: the `--design-*` tokens of
   [`DESIGN_STYLE`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles), else Caligrafy's. A record becomes
   a hero (its name, a line under it, badges with a tone), a few numbers, its details, its text and its tags; a list
   becomes rows. Who designs it: the hint `design` when you give one; else Claude, with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, from a
   sample of the data, once per shape of data (kept 30 days in the cache); else rules from the names of the fields.

```php
'search_books' => array('card' => 'snap/list_books'),   // the same rows as the catalog: its card view
'get_user' => array('card' => false),                     // no card view
'get_book' => array('view' => 'Bookshelf/book'),          // without a card view: this page, whole
'list_people' => array('design' => array('title' => 'name', 'subtitle' => 'role', 'meta' => array('email', 'active_cases'),
    'badge' => array('path' => 'status', 'tones' => array('away' => 'warning')))),   // a designed card, by hand
```

The `design` hint: `title`, `subtitle`, `eyebrow`, `image`, `badges` (`badge` for a list), `stats`, `fields`, `text`,
`tags` (`meta` for a list), each a field name or `array('path' => ..., 'label' => ..., 'format' => ..., 'tones' => array(...))`.
Formats: `text`, `number`, `money`, `percent`, `date`, `datetime`, `bool`, `email`, `url`; tones: `success`, `warning`,
`danger`, `info`, `neutral` (`Designer::FORMATS`, `Designer::TONES`).
## Common mistakes

+ **A card view does not show.** It must be named after a read-only capability; run `php caligrafer.php snap views`.
+ **A card looked like a whole page on 2.24, and designed since 2.25.0.** Give it a card view, or mark the part with
  `data-snap` (G163).
+ **A class of a built stylesheet does nothing.** With Tailwind, a card view can only use classes the build already has.
+ **`+` between strings** in Pug: Caligrafy renders Pug with PHP; join with `.`.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Hints -->

**Hints** make a [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) card better:
its name, the columns of a list, the words the assistant says, the numbers of Home with their actions, what Home
invites to browse, when an action applies. Cards work without any: each is built from what its capability declares.
The hints live in one file the app owns, `application/config/snap.php`, keyed by capability name. Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude writes `application/config/snap.php` for your capabilities: `about`, titles, columns, the numbers of Home with
their actions, what Home invites to browse, the card views.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap` shows `[ok] Card hints`.
+ Each key you see in the file is in the table below: a key the framework does not know is ignored silently.
## By hand

`php caligrafer.php snap install` writes a starter file when there is none. A complete one:

```php
<?php
return array(
    'about' => 'a library app: the books of a catalog, their authors, and the books lent to people',
    'cards' => array(
        'list_books' => array(
            'title' => 'The catalog',
            'columns' => array('title', 'author.name', 'published_year'),
            'empty' => 'No book yet.',
            'insight' => array('label' => 'New this month', 'since' => array('field' => 'created_at', 'days' => 30),
                'action' => array('capability' => 'list_books', 'text' => 'Browse the catalog')),
            'discover' => array('open' => 'get_book', 'key' => 'id', 'title' => 'title', 'meta' => array('author.name', 'published_year'),
                'new' => 'created_at', 'related' => 'author.id', 'opened' => array('get_book' => 'id'),
                'unavailable' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'), 'available_label' => 'On the shelf',
                'title_section' => 'On the shelf for you'),
        ),
        'lend_book' => array('done' => 'Done! {heading} is lent. Enjoy the read.',
            'applies' => array('not_in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
        'return_book' => array('applies' => array('in' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'))),
        'reading_report' => array('working' => array('Counting the books of each author…', 'Putting the report together…')),
    ),
);
```

A file that returns the cards alone (no `'cards'` key) works too. `about` (and `APP_NAME` in `.env`) tells the
assistant what it is the assistant of.
## <a name="keys"></a>Reference: every key of a card

| Key | What it does | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `title`, `lead`, `submit`, `icon` | the card's name, its line, its button, its icon (Lucide names) | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards) |
| `labels`, `icons`, `hide` | the labels and icons of fields, the fields left out | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards) |
| `values` | the labels of fixed values: `array('weekday' => array(1 => 'Monday', ...))` makes a select | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards) |
| `choices` | where a field's choices come from: `array('author_id' => 'list_authors')`, or `array('capability' => ..., 'value' => 'id', 'label' => 'name')` | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards) |
| `current` | the capability an `update_` form reads its current values from (`get_<thing>` by default) | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards) |
| `confirm`, `consequence` | a Confirm's question, the line under it | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards#confirm) |
| `undo` | what undoes it: `array('capability' => 'return_book', 'map' => array('book_id' => 'book_id'))` (each input of the undo, from an input or the result of the change), and its button `label` (*Undo*) | [Ask](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Ask-Cards#confirm) |
| `columns`, `noun`, `variant` | a list's columns, what its rows are ("authors"), its variant (`rows`) | [Show](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards) |
| `open` | which capability a list's row opens: `array('capability' => 'get_book', 'input' => 'id', 'from' => 'book_id')` | [Show](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards) |
| `full` | the page that shows the same thing in full: `'/books/{id}'` | |
| `empty`, `empty_next` | what an empty list says; what would fill it: `array('lend_book')` | [Show](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards) |
| `applies` | when an action can be done to a record: `in` or `not_in` a list | [Show](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards#answer) |
| `done` | the assistant's line once done; `{heading}` is what it was about | |
| `next` | the capabilities it leads to (suggestions after it) | |
| `alert` | an alert on Home when rows carry a flag | [Offer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Offer-Cards#alert) |
| `insight` | a number on Home, only with the action it calls for | below |
| `discover` | the things Home invites to browse | below |
| `working`, `async` | what a background task says while it runs; async without the attribute | [Track](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Go-and-Track-Cards#task) |
| `card`, `view`, `design` | its card view, the page whose `data-snap` part shows it, how its data is designed | [Card views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Card-Views) |

### <a name="insight"></a>`insight`

```php
'insight' => array('label' => 'New this month', 'icon' => 'sparkles',
    'action' => array('capability' => 'list_books', 'text' => 'Browse the catalog'),
    'since' => array('field' => 'created_at', 'days' => 30),          // count only what was added lately
    'ring' => array('of' => 'list_books', 'label' => 'of the catalog', 'invert' => false)),   // and a share of another count
```

One number per read capability with the hint, shown only when there is something to act on (a count above zero) and
the person may take its `action`. Without an `action` it is never shown (G157).

### <a name="discover"></a>`discover`

On a list capability, Home shows picks of what the app is about, each saying why it is there (6 per list at most, a different few each day):

+ **for you**: more like what this person opened (only with noticing on), sharing `related`;
+ **new**: up to 2 of what was added in the last 30 days, by the field `new`;
+ **the rule**: only what is available now, not in the `unavailable` list (`available_label` says it).

| Key | What it is |
|---|---|
| `open`, `key` | how an object opens: the capability, and the field it takes |
| `title`, `meta` | what a pick shows |
| `new` | the field that says when it was added |
| `related` | what "more like it" shares (`author.id`) |
| `opened` | the requests that mean "looked at it": `array('get_book' => 'id', 'lend_book' => 'book_id')` |
| `unavailable`, `available_label` | the business rule: `array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id')` |
| `title_section` | the section's title |
## Common mistakes

+ **Hints on `#[Capability]`.** They are keys of `application/config/snap.php`; only `async` is also a flag of the
  attribute (G157).
+ **A key with a typo** is ignored silently: copy the shapes above.
+ **The file changed and nothing did**: in a long process (the queue worker, a test) the file is read once;
  `Caligrafy\Snap\Hints::forget()` reads it again.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Snap-Assistant -->

**The assistant** of [Snap](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) answers
what a person types, says or attaches on `/assistant` with your cards. Much of it needs no model: "What can I do?", the
name of a card or of a shortcut, "delete it" on what is on screen. With an Anthropic API key, Claude understands
anything else, looks things up with the read-only capabilities the person may call, and answers with cards. It never
changes data: a change always comes back as its Confirm. Since 2.23.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant
```

Claude sets up Snap, writes `about` in `application/config/snap.php`, and asks you for an Anthropic API key if you want
the assistant to understand free text.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php snap` shows the model on the `Assistant model` line, or `[--]` without a key.
+ On `/assistant`, "What can I do?" lists every card you may use.
## By hand

1. **Without a key**, the assistant works at once: `Route::snap();` in `web.php`, `php caligrafer.php snap install`.
2. **With Claude**, add to `.env`:
    ```bash
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
    ```
   (a key from console.anthropic.com, API keys). The model is `claude-opus-5-5` at `low` effort; `SNAP_MODEL` and
   `SNAP_EFFORT` in `.env` change them. The `anthropic-ai/sdk` package must be installed: it is in Caligrafy's
   `composer.json` since 2.23.0 (after an `update`, `composer install`, or rebuild the Docker image).
3. **Say what the app is**, in `application/config/snap.php`:
    ```php
    'about' => 'a library app: the books of a catalog, their authors, and the books lent to people',
    ```
   `about` and `APP_NAME` in `.env` tell it what it is the assistant of.
## <a name="order"></a>Reference: how a request is answered

The first that fits:

1. **At once, without a model** (`Caligrafy\Snap\Shell`, [API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-shell)):
   + "What can I do?" (also `what else can i do`, `what can you do`, `help`, `menu`, `?`, `options`): the menu, every card
     this person may start, by family;
   + the title of one of their [shortcuts](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Go-and-Track-Cards#shortcut):
     that shortcut, run;
   + the title or the name of a card ("the catalog", "lend a book", "list_loans"): that card;
   + a follow-up on the record on screen, a verb and "it", "this", "that", "this one", "that one" or "this book":
     `delete`/`remove`, `change`/`edit`/`update`/`fix`, `lend`/`loan`, `return`, `open`/`show`/`see`, which open
     `delete_<thing>`, `update_<thing>`, `lend_<thing>`, `return_<thing>` or `get_<thing>` for that record. Anything
     longer ("lend it to Sam") goes to the model, with the conversation's memory.
2. **Claude** (`Caligrafy\Snap\Planner`, [API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-planner)),
   when it is on: it reads the request with the conversation so far, what is on screen and what the person chose. It
   may look things up with the read-only capabilities the person may call, as tools run with their permissions (6
   steps at most), and answers with `show_cards`: which capability, with which values, and one sentence of caption.

**What the model may never do is enforced in code, not in the prompt.** Every card it names goes through `Snap\Flow`
like any other: a read runs, a change comes back as an Ask: Confirm whose token only the person's click sends. The model
never sees a token and never runs a change. Tool results and attached files are the app's data, never instructions.

**Attachments.** The + attaches up to 3 files, 5 MB in all: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, PDF, plain text, CSV, Markdown. Without
the model, attached files get a message instead of an answer.

**The keyboard.** ⌥K / Alt+K to type, ⌥M / Alt+M to talk.
## <a name="test"></a>Testing

Fake the model with `Caligrafy\Snap\Planner::$transport` (set it back to `null` in `tearDown`), and call `snap_ask`
with `$this->action()`: it is a web-only capability. The Snap tables must be in the test database
(`platform install` with the test settings).

```php
Caligrafy\Snap\Planner::$transport = function (array $request) {
    return (object) array('stopReason' => 'tool_use', 'content' => array((object) array('type' => 'tool_use', 'id' => 't1',
        'name' => 'show_cards', 'input' => array('caption' => 'Here it is.', 'cards' => array(array('capability' => 'list_books'))))));
};
$answer = $this->action('snap_ask', array('text' => 'show me the catalog'), $this->user(1))->describe()['data'];
```

The designed cards have their own fake, `Caligrafy\Snap\Designer::$transport`, or keep to the rules with
`Caligrafy\Snap\Designer::$model = false` (since 2.24.1).
## Common mistakes

+ **The assistant only answers the names of cards** (G156): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is missing, or the `anthropic-ai/sdk`
  package is not installed.
+ **Forcing a tool in your own calls to Claude** (`toolChoice` of type `tool` or `any`) answers `400` on the current
  Claude models; Snap uses a structured output instead (G161).
+ **A test that fakes the planner on 2.24.0** also received the designer's requests: since 2.24.1 the designer has its
  own fake (G162).
+ **`/assistant` throws `LogicException`**: `Route::snap()` needs `Auth::authentication(...)` above it (G154).
