<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models -->

A **model** is a PHP class that stands for one table: one `Book` object is one row of `books`. Your capabilities
read and write rows through models and the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries)
(`Book::where('author_id', 1)->get()`, `Book::find(3)`, `Book::insert($input)`), and every page, REST
call, Vue app and AI agent reaches the data through those capabilities. This page makes the tables of the Bookshelf
(authors, books, tags, loans) and their models.

> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [CRUD operations on a database](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kNdoaSi6pcE&list=PLsJG81fLk3_UNfTuqjCbcz1S_xbram35e)
>
> An older video: it uses a controller. Today the same work goes in a capability, as below.
## With Claude

Ask for the resource with the `new-resource` skill of the Claude Code plugin, with its fields:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book title:string published_year:int summary:text author:fk
```

Claude writes:
+ `application/models/Book/create_db.sql`: the table, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, its foreign key named
  `fk_<table>_<column>`;
+ `application/models/Book/Book.php`: the model, one public property per column;
+ the capabilities `list_books`, `get_book`, `create_book`, `update_book` and `delete_book` in
  `application/services/Books/`, which use the query builder;
+ their routes in `application/config/routing/web.php` (REST, pages, forms), and the views when you want pages.

It then offers to run the SQL (`/caligrafy-quill:db application/models/Book/create_db.sql`). When the table already
holds data, it writes a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations) instead.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the primary key is `id`, each foreign key column is `<parent>_id` with the same type as the parent's `id`
  (`INT UNSIGNED` for `INT UNSIGNED`);
+ the model has a property for every column, and no `find()` method of its own;
+ the table name is the class name in lower case plus `s` (`Book` -> `books`), or the model declares
  `protected static $tableName`;
+ `php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists the new capabilities, and `php caligrafer.php call get_book id=1` answers.
## <a name="modelfundamentals"></a>By hand

You have a project made with the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) and its
Docker server. Run every command in the container: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...` (without
Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **Check the database settings.** Open `.env`. The Quickstart wrote them; they must read:
    ```text
    DB_ACTIVATE=true
    DB_CONNECTION=mysql
    DB_HOST=mysql
    DB_PORT=3306
    DB_DATABASE=caligrafy
    DB_USERNAME=root
    DB_PASSWORD=root
    ```
    `DB_HOST=mysql` and `DB_PORT=3306` are the database inside the Docker network. Without Docker, use your MySQL's
    host and port (`127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, so that the port is used). Then run
    `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only database`: every line must be `OK`.

2. **Write the tables.** Create `application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql`:
    ```sql
    /* The Bookshelf tables. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS: safe to run again, it never drops anything.
     * Run it with: php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql
     */
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authors (
        id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
        name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
        bio TEXT NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        PRIMARY KEY (id)
    ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (
        id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
        title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
        published_year SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
        summary TEXT NULL,
        author_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        PRIMARY KEY (id),
        KEY idx_books_author_id (author_id),
        CONSTRAINT fk_books_author_id FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES authors (id)
            ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
    ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tags (
        id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
        name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        PRIMARY KEY (id),
        UNIQUE KEY uq_tags_name (name)
    ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books_tags (
        id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
        book_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
        tag_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        PRIMARY KEY (id),
        UNIQUE KEY uq_books_tags (book_id, tag_id),
        CONSTRAINT fk_books_tags_book_id FOREIGN KEY (book_id) REFERENCES books (id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE,
        CONSTRAINT fk_books_tags_tag_id FOREIGN KEY (tag_id) REFERENCES tags (id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS loans (
        id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
        book_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
        borrower VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        due_on DATE NOT NULL,
        returned_at DATETIME NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        PRIMARY KEY (id),
        KEY idx_loans_book_id (book_id),
        CONSTRAINT fk_loans_book_id FOREIGN KEY (book_id) REFERENCES books (id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;
    ```
    The names follow the conventions the [relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships)
    read: a primary key `id`, a foreign key `<parent in the singular>_id` (`author_id`) of the same type as the
    parent's `id`, and the table that links books and tags named `books_tags` with `book_id` and `tag_id`. Each
    constraint name is unique in the database (`fk_<table>_<column>`).

3. **Create them.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql
    ```
    ```text
     application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql run on caligrafy
    ```
    Online, the deploy step runs this file on its own when it is new or changed. From now on, a change to one of
    these tables is a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations): never edit the
    file once it ran.

4. **Add sample rows.** Create `application/models/Bookshelf/seed.sql`:
    ```sql
    /* Sample rows for the Bookshelf. INSERT IGNORE skips the rows whose id exists, so it can run twice.
     * Run it with: php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/seed.sql
     */

    INSERT IGNORE INTO authors (id, name, bio) VALUES
        (1, 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 'American author of science fiction and fantasy, known for the Earthsea books.'),
        (2, 'Octavia E. Butler', 'American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.'),
        (3, 'Italo Calvino', 'Italian writer of playful, inventive novels and short stories.');

    INSERT IGNORE INTO books (id, title, published_year, summary, author_id) VALUES
        (1, 'A Wizard of Earthsea', 1968, 'A gifted boy learns magic and must face the shadow he set loose.', 1),
        (2, 'The Left Hand of Darkness', 1969, 'An envoy visits a planet whose people have no fixed sex.', 1),
        (3, 'Kindred', 1979, 'A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.', 2),
        (4, 'Parable of the Sower', 1993, 'In a collapsing California, a teenager starts a new belief system.', 2),
        (5, 'Invisible Cities', 1972, 'Marco Polo describes imaginary cities to the emperor Kublai Khan.', 3);

    INSERT IGNORE INTO tags (id, name) VALUES (1, 'fantasy'), (2, 'science fiction'), (3, 'classic');

    INSERT IGNORE INTO books_tags (id, book_id, tag_id) VALUES
        (1, 1, 1), (2, 1, 3), (3, 2, 2), (4, 2, 3), (5, 3, 2), (6, 4, 2), (7, 5, 3);

    INSERT IGNORE INTO loans (id, book_id, borrower, due_on, returned_at) VALUES
        (1, 1, 'Ana', '2026-11-20', NULL),
        (2, 3, 'Ben', '2026-10-30', '2026-10-28 10:00:00'),
        (3, 3, 'Chloe', '2026-11-25', NULL);
    ```
    Run it: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/seed.sql`
    (it prints ` application/models/Bookshelf/seed.sql run on caligrafy`). The deploy step never runs a `seed.sql`.

5. **Write the models.** One file per table, in `application/models/Bookshelf/`, one public property per column.

    `application/models/Bookshelf/Author.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Model;

    // One Author = one row of the authors table
    class Author extends Model
    {
        public $id;
        public $name;
        public $bio;
        public $created_at;
        public $modified_at;
    }
    ```
    `application/models/Bookshelf/Book.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Model;

    // One Book = one row of the books table
    class Book extends Model
    {
        public $id;
        public $title;
        public $published_year;
        public $summary;
        public $author_id;
        public $created_at;
        public $modified_at;
    }
    ```
    `application/models/Bookshelf/Tag.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Model;

    // One Tag = one row of the tags table
    class Tag extends Model
    {
        public $id;
        public $name;
        public $created_at;
        public $modified_at;
    }
    ```
    `application/models/Bookshelf/Loan.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Model;

    // One Loan = one row of the loans table: who borrowed which book, until when
    class Loan extends Model
    {
        public $id;
        public $book_id;
        public $borrower;
        public $due_on;
        public $returned_at;
        public $created_at;
        public $modified_at;
    }
    ```
    `Book::query()` and `Book::find()` read the table `books`: the class name in lower case plus `s`. The models need
    no relationship methods: the [relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships)
    are loaded with `with()`.

6. **<a name="modelinterface"></a>Read a row in a capability.** Only capabilities touch models. Create the
   capability `get_book` with `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/GetBook --scope books:read --read-only`,
   then make `application/services/Bookshelf/GetBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;
    use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

    // get_book: one book with its author, or "not found"
    #[Capability(
        name: 'get_book',
        description: 'Returns one book of the catalog with its author (id, name, bio), by the id of the book.',
        scope: 'books:read',
        readOnly: true,
        public: true
    )]
    class GetBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');
        public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book');

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $book = Book::with('author')->find($input['id']);
            if (!$book) {
                throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no book #{$input['id']}");
            }
            return $book;
        }
    }
    ```
    Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3`:
    ```json
    {
        "data": {
            "id": 3,
            "title": "Kindred",
            "published_year": 1979,
            "summary": "A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.",
            "author_id": 2,
            "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
            "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
            "author": {
                "id": 2,
                "name": "Octavia E. Butler",
                "bio": "American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.",
                "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
                "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48"
            }
        }
    }
    ```
    (Your dates differ.) The capability returns a `Book` with its `author` ([Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships));
    every channel gets it as plain data. `id=99` gives
    `{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "There is no book #99"}}`. Writing a capability, and serving it to
    pages, REST and agents, is on [Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service).

**Check:**
+ `docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot caligrafy -e "SHOW TABLES"` lists `authors`, `books`, `books_tags`,
  `loans` and `tags` (beside the `caligrafy_*` framework tables);
+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3` returns *Kindred*;
+ each model has exactly the columns of its table.
## <a name="modelmethods"></a>Reference

**Reading: the query builder on the model class.** Every call returns models of the class (`Book`), on its table.
The full list is on [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries).

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `Book::find(3)` | the `Book` of id 3, or `null` |
| `Book::where('author_id', 1)->get()` | a list of `Book` (empty when none) |
| `Book::where('title', 'Kindred')->first()` | the first `Book`, or `null` |
| `Book::with('author')->find(3)` | the book, with `author` (an array) |
| `Book::where('author_id', 1)->count()` | a number |
| `Book::query()->orderBy('title')->paginate(20, $page)` | `['data', 'total', 'page', 'per_page', 'pages']` |
| `Book::query()` | the query builder on `books`, to build on |

The calls a model class forwards to the query builder: `query`, `find`, `select`, `where`, `orWhere`, `whereIn`,
`whereNotIn`, `whereNull`, `whereNotNull`, `whereBetween`, `orderBy`, `latest`, `oldest`, `limit`, `offset`, `with`,
`withCount`, `first`, `value`, `pluck`, `count`, `exists`, `paginate`, `chunk`, `get`, `insert`, `input`, `arrays`.
`search()` is not one of them: write `Book::query()->search([...], $words)`.

**Writing: the query builder on the model class.** The full list is on
[Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries#write).

| Call | What it does | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `Book::insert($input)` | one `INSERT` of the values of `$input` (an array; arrays and objects in it are written as JSON) | the id of the new row |
| `Book::where('id', $id)->update($changes)` | `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ?` | how many rows changed |
| `Book::where('id', $id)->delete()` | `DELETE ... WHERE id = ?` | how many rows were deleted (`0`: no such row) |
| `Book::where('id', $id)->increment('stock', 2)` | adds to a number column (`decrement()` too) | how many rows changed |

`update()`, `delete()`, `increment()` and `decrement()` refuse to run without a `where()`, so a missing condition never
changes every row. Every value is bound. A capability that creates a book returns it read back:
`$id = Book::insert($input); return Book::with('author')->find($id);`.

**The table of a model**

| The model | `Book::query()` reads |
|---|---|
| `class Book` | `books` (the class name in lower case + `s`) |
| `class Category` | `categories` (consonant + `y` -> `ies`; `s`, `x`, `z`, `ch`, `sh` -> `es`) |
| `class BookReview` | `bookreviews` (no `_`): declare `protected static $tableName = 'book_reviews';` |
| `class Person` with `protected static $tableName = 'people';` | `people` |

**Database settings** (`.env`)

| Setting | Default in `.env.example` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DB_ACTIVATE` | `false` | `true` connects; without it every query fails with `[ERROR 2003]` |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `mysql` | the PDO driver |
| `DB_HOST` | `localhost` | `mysql` with the Docker server; `127.0.0.1` to reach a port over TCP |
| `DB_PORT` | `3306` | added to the connection unless `DB_HOST` already has `;port=` |
| `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` | `databasename`, `root`, `root` | the database and its account |
| `DB_TIMEZONE` | empty | empty: MySQL uses PHP's `SERVER_TIMEZONE`; `server` keeps MySQL's own |
## <a name="querybuilder"></a>Other ways

These still work. Use them only in older code; the prescriptive way is in brackets.

+ **A model in a controller** [a capability]: `$this->associate('Book', 'books');` then `$this->model->find(1)`. See
  [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers).
+ **The methods of a model object** [`Book::insert()`, `Book::where('id', $id)->update()` and `->delete()` above]:
  `new Book('books')` gives an object on the table you name, and its methods write one row:

    | Method | What it does | Returns |
    |---|---|---|
    | `(new Book('books'))->create($input)` | `INSERT` of the values of `$input` (an array or an object) | the new `Book`, read back |
    | `(new Book('books'))->update($changes, $id)` | `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ?`; nothing when the row does not exist or nothing is left to save | the `Book` read back, or `null` |
    | `(new Book('books'))->delete($id)` | `DELETE ... WHERE id = ?` | an empty array |
    | `$book->save()` | `update()` when `$book->id` is set, otherwise `create()` | the `Book` read back |
    | `$book->toArray()` | the object as an array | array |
    | `(new Book('books'))->find($id)` | `SELECT * ... WHERE id = ?` (the older form of `Book::find`) | `Book` or `null` |

    `create()`, `update()` and `save()` write only the columns the table has (a helper property such as
    `public $errors` is left out), and only values that are not `null` (`0`, `''` and `false` are written; `false` as
    `0`). A property left `null` keeps the column's current value or its default. Arrays and objects are written as
    JSON. Every value is bound; the column names must be letters, digits and `_`. On such an object,
    `$book->where(...)` uses the table it was given.
+ **`all()` with SQL clauses** [`Book::where(...)->orderBy(...)->limit(...)->get()`]: the clauses are added to the SQL as
  they are, so they hold their keywords, and values go in `bindings`, never in the text:
    ```php
    $books = (new Book('books'))->all(array(
        'condition' => 'WHERE author_id = ?',
        'order' => 'ORDER BY title',
        'limit' => 'LIMIT 10',
        'bindings' => array(1)
    ));
    ```
+ **`search($columns, $pattern)`** [`Book::query()->search(['title', 'summary'], $words)`]:
  `(new Book('books'))->search('title,summary', '%shadow%')` takes a `LIKE` pattern as it is (`%` and `_` are
  wildcards); the columns must be letters, digits and `_`.
+ **SQL the query builder does not write** (a join with `GROUP BY`, a subquery, a database function): a method of the
  model with `Database::execute()` and `?` placeholders:
    ```php
    public function findByIsbn($isbn)
    {
        $rows = Database::toArray(Database::execute('SELECT * FROM ' . $this->table . ' WHERE isbn = ? LIMIT 1', [$isbn]));
        return !empty($rows[0]) ? $this->arrayToModel($rows[0]) : null;
    }
    ```
+ **Relationship methods in the model** (`hasOne()`, `hasMany()`, `belongsToMany()`) [`with()`]: see
  [Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships#methods).
## Common mistakes

+ **A `find()` method in your model** (G122): `$book->find()` then runs yours, and `Book::find(3)` fails with
  "Non-static method cannot be called statically". Leave `find()` out, or call `Book::query()->find(3)`.
+ **A table name the model cannot guess** (G123): `BookReview` reads `bookreviews`. Declare
  `protected static $tableName = 'book_reviews';` (protected or public; a private one is not seen).
+ **A value written into SQL** (G2, G8): `all(['condition' => "WHERE title = '$title'"])` lets a visitor change the
  query. Use the query builder, or `?` and `bindings`.
+ **`DB_HOST=localhost` with a port** (G3): PDO then uses the MySQL socket and ignores `DB_PORT`. Use `127.0.0.1`.
+ **A foreign key of another type** (G10): `INT` toward `INT UNSIGNED` fails with "incompatible". Give it the parent's type.
+ **Editing `create_db.sql` after it ran**: a database that has the table keeps the old one. Write a
  [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations).
## Related pages

+ [Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships): authors, books, tags, loans together
+ [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries): filters, paging, counts, writes, transactions
+ [Migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations): changing a table that holds data
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)
+ [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#sql): `sql`, `migrate`, `call`


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships -->

Tables point at each other: a book has one author (`books.author_id`), an author has many books, a book has many
loans, and books and tags are linked many to many through `books_tags`. A capability loads those **related rows** with
`with()` of the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries): one query for the books,
one more per relation, never one query per book. The relations follow the names of your tables, so the models need no
code for them. This page uses the Bookshelf tables of [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models).

```php
$book    = Book::with('author', 'loans', ['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])->find(3);   // its author, its loans, its tags
$authors = Author::withCount('books')->orderBy('name')->get();                       // each author with books_count
```

> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Relationships](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o6knV88iCkw&list=PLsJG81fLk3_UNfTuqjCbcz1S_xbram35e)
>
> An older video: it shows the relationship methods of the model (under "Other ways" below).
## With Claude

Ask for the capability with the `new-capability` skill, and say which related rows it returns:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability get_book books:read read-only: one book with its author, its loans and its tags
```

Claude writes `application/services/Bookshelf/GetBook.php` (or the folder of your resource), reads the rows with
`Book::with(...)`, and never queries in a loop. For a resource with a parent (`/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book ... author:fk`),
it writes the foreign key `author_id` and its constraint in `create_db.sql`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the capability reads related rows with `with()` or `withCount()`, not a query inside a `foreach`;
+ many-to-many relations say `['pivot' => true]` (or the pivot's name);
+ `php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3` shows the related rows under their names (`author`, `loans`, `tags`).
## By hand

Run every command in the Docker container: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...` (without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **A book with its author, its loans and its tags.** Make `application/services/Bookshelf/GetBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;
    use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'get_book',
        description: 'Returns one book by its id, with its author, its tags and its loans.',
        scope: 'books:read',
        readOnly: true,
        public: true
    )]
    class GetBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');

        public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book');

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $book = Book::with('author', 'loans', array('tags' => array('pivot' => true)))->find($input['id']);
            if (!$book) {
                throw ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #' . $input['id']);
            }
            return $book;
        }
    }
    ```
    Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3`:
    ```json
    {
        "data": {
            "id": 3,
            "title": "Kindred",
            "published_year": 1979,
            "summary": "A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.",
            "author_id": 2,
            "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
            "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
            "author": {
                "id": 2,
                "name": "Octavia E. Butler",
                "bio": "American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.",
                "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48",
                "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48"
            },
            "loans": [
                {"id": 2, "book_id": 3, "borrower": "Ben", "due_on": "2026-10-30", "returned_at": "2026-10-28 10:00:00", "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48", "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48"},
                {"id": 3, "book_id": 3, "borrower": "Chloe", "due_on": "2026-11-25", "returned_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48", "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48"}
            ],
            "tags": [
                {"id": 2, "name": "science fiction", "created_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48", "modified_at": "2026-11-07 23:23:48"}
            ]
        }
    }
    ```
    (Your dates differ.) Four queries ran: the book, then its author, its loans and its tags, each with
    `WHERE ... IN (...)`.

2. **Every author with the number of their books.** Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListAuthors --scope books:read --read-only`,
   then make `application/services/Bookshelf/ListAuthors.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'list_authors',
        description: 'Lists every author of the Bookshelf, sorted by name, with books_count: how many books each one has in the catalog.',
        scope: 'books:read',
        readOnly: true,
        public: true
    )]
    class ListAuthors extends Service
    {
        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            return Author::withCount('books')->orderBy('name')->get();
        }
    }
    ```
    `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call list_authors` returns the three authors, each with
    `books_count`: Italo Calvino `1`, Octavia E. Butler `2`, Ursula K. Le Guin `2`. `withCount()` ran one
    `GROUP BY` query for all of them.

3. **Link and unlink a tag.** The rows of a many-to-many relation live in the pivot table `books_tags`: add and remove
   them with the query builder. Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/TagBook --scope books:write`, then make
   `application/services/Bookshelf/TagBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Database;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'tag_book',
        description: 'Adds a tag to a book (nothing changes when the book has it already) and returns the book with all its tags.',
        scope: 'books:write'
    )]
    class TagBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array(
            'book_id' => 'required|integer|exists,books.id',
            'tag_id' => 'required|integer|exists,tags.id'
        );

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $link = array('book_id' => $input['book_id'], 'tag_id' => $input['tag_id']);
            if (!Database::table('books_tags')->where($link)->exists()) {
                Database::table('books_tags')->insert($link);
            }
            return Book::with(array('tags' => array('pivot' => true)))->find($input['book_id']);
        }
    }
    ```
    Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/UntagBook --scope books:write`, then make
    `application/services/Bookshelf/UntagBook.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Database;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'untag_book',
        description: 'Removes a tag from a book and returns the book with the tags it has left.',
        scope: 'books:write'
    )]
    class UntagBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array(
            'book_id' => 'required|integer|exists,books.id',
            'tag_id' => 'required|integer'
        );

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            Database::table('books_tags')->where(array('book_id' => $input['book_id'], 'tag_id' => $input['tag_id']))->delete();
            return Book::with(array('tags' => array('pivot' => true)))->find($input['book_id']);
        }
    }
    ```
    Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call tag_book book_id=3 tag_id=3`: *Kindred* now has the tags
    `science fiction` and `classic`. Running it again changes nothing. `call untag_book book_id=3 tag_id=3` leaves
    `science fiction`. `call tag_book book_id=3 tag_id=9` answers `"tag_id": "There is no such tag"`.

**Check:**
+ `call get_book id=3` has `author`, `loans` and `tags`;
+ `call list_authors` gives each author a `books_count`;
+ `docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot caligrafy -e "SELECT * FROM books_tags WHERE book_id = 3"` shows
  the links you made.
## Reference

### <a name="onetoone"></a><a name="onetomany"></a>How `with()` reads a name

`with()` follows the name you give and the table it is called on:

| Name | Called on | Kind | It reads | You get |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `author` (singular) | `books` | belongs to | `books.author_id` -> `authors.id` | one row, or `null` |
| `books` (plural) | `authors` | has many | `books.author_id` = `authors.id` | a list, or `[]` |
| `loans` (plural) | `books` | has many | `loans.book_id` = `books.id` | a list, or `[]` |
| `['tags' => ['pivot' => true]]` | `books` | many to many | `books_tags.book_id` = `books.id`, `books_tags.tag_id` = `tags.id` | a list, or `[]` |
| `book.author` | `loans` | nested: the relation of a relation | `loans.book_id` -> `books.id`, then `books.author_id` -> `authors.id` | `book` with its `author` |
| `['current_loan' => ['type' => 'hasOne', 'table' => 'loans']]` | `books` | has one | `loans.book_id` = `books.id` | the first row, or `null` |

+ Singular and plural: `author` -> `authors`, `category` -> `categories`, `box` -> `boxes`. An irregular plural
  (`person`/`people`) needs `'table'`.
+ The related rows are **arrays**, also under models: `$book->author['name']`, `$book->tags[0]['name']`.
+ The key must be in the rows: `Book::select('id', 'title')->with('author')` has no `author_id`, so `author` is `null`.
+ Several names at once: `with('author', 'loans')`; one name's settings: `with(['author' => [...]])`; both:
  `with('author', ['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])`.

### <a name="manytomany"></a>Many to many: the pivot

The pivot of `books` and `tags` is `books_tags` (`<this table>_<related table>`), with `book_id` and `tag_id`. When
that table does not exist but `tags_books` does, `with()` uses `tags_books` (it tries `books_tags` first, then
remembers). `['pivot' => 'book_tag_links']` names another pivot. Write the pivot in `create_db.sql`, with a
`UNIQUE KEY` on its two columns, as on [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models). Add and
remove links with `Database::table('books_tags')->insert([...])` and `->where([...])->delete()`, as in step 3.

### <a name="override"></a>When your names differ: the settings

```php
Book::with(['writer' => ['table' => 'authors', 'foreign_key' => 'author_id']])->find(3);   // $book->writer
Book::with(['current_loan' => ['type' => 'hasOne', 'table' => 'loans', 'query' => function ($q) { $q->whereNull('returned_at'); }]])->get();
```

| Setting | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `belongsTo`, `hasOne`, `hasMany` or `belongsToMany` | singular name: `belongsTo`; plural: `hasMany`; with `pivot`: `belongsToMany` |
| `table` | the related table | the name in the plural (`belongsTo`, `hasOne`), the name itself (`hasMany`, `belongsToMany`) |
| `foreign_key` | belongs to: the column of this table; has one/many: the column of the related table; many to many: the pivot's column toward this table | `<name>_id` (belongs to), `<this table in the singular>_id` (the others) |
| `local_key` | the column of this table the others point at | `id` |
| `owner_key` | the column of the related table that is pointed at | `id` |
| `pivot` | `true` (the conventional pivot) or its name | none |
| `related_key` | the pivot's column toward the related table | `<name in the singular>_id` |
| `query` | a function that narrows the related rows: `function ($q) { $q->where('published_year', '<', 1970); }` | none |

A function alone is the `query` setting: `with(['loans' => function ($q) { $q->whereNull('returned_at'); }])`. An unknown
setting, or a name that is not letters, digits and `_`, is refused before any query runs.

### Counting: `withCount()`

```php
Author::withCount('books')->get();                                   // books_count on each author
Database::table('tags')->withCount(['books' => ['pivot' => true]])->pluck('books_count', 'name');
// ['fantasy' => 1, 'science fiction' => 3, 'classic' => 3]
Author::withCount(['books' => function ($q) { $q->where('published_year', '<', 1970); }])->pluck('books_count', 'name');
// ['Ursula K. Le Guin' => 2, 'Octavia E. Butler' => 0, 'Italo Calvino' => 0]
```

`withCount()` counts plural relations only (has many, many to many): `withCount('author')` is refused ("counts a
plural relation"). A row with nothing to count gets `0`.
## <a name="methods"></a>Other ways: the relationship methods of a model

Before 2.19, relations were methods of the model. They still work, for one model object at a time; `with()` replaces
them, for one row or a thousand.

```php
class Book extends Model
{
    // ... the properties

    public function author()   // the author: books.author_id -> authors.id
    {
        return $this->hasOne('Author', 'authors');
    }

    public function loans()    // the loans: loans.book_id = books.id
    {
        return $this->hasMany('Loan', 'loans');
    }

    public function tags()     // the tags, through books_tags (book_id, tag_id)
    {
        return $this->belongsToMany('Tag', 'tags');
    }
}

$book = (new Book('books'))->find(1);
$book->author()->name;           // 'Ursula K. Le Guin' (a model, or null)
$book->loans();                  // a list of Loan
$book->tags();                   // a list of Tag
$book->attach('tags', 2);        // adds the link 1-2 (call tags() first); returns the tags again
$book->detach('tags', 2);        // removes it
```

| Method | It reads | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `hasOne($model, $table, $foreignKey = null, $localKey = null)` | the foreign key **on this model's table**: `books.author_id` -> `authors.id` (`$foreignKey` names this table's column, `$localKey` the other table's) | a model, or `null` |
| `hasMany($model, $table, $foreignKey = null, $localKey = null)` | `<table>.<this class>_id` = this id (`$foreignKey` names that column, `$localKey` a property of this model to use instead of `id`) | a list of models |
| `belongsTo(...)` | the same as `hasMany()`: it is **not** the inverse of `hasMany()`. For a child's parent, use `hasOne()` | a list |
| `belongsToMany($model, $table, $foreignKeyLocal = null, $foreignKeyJoin = null)` | the pivot `<this table>_<table>` (or `<table>_<this table>` when that one exists); its columns are `<this class>_id` and `<model>_id`. It **creates the pivot** with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` the first time | a list of models; `$book->pivot->tags->all` holds the rows |
| `attach($table, $id)`, `detach($table, $id)` | add or remove a pivot row; call the relationship method first | the relationship again |

The method's name is up to you; it is never saved as a column. The foreign key names come from the class name in lower
case (`Book` -> `book_id`).
## Common mistakes

+ **A query inside a `foreach`** (the N+1 problem): 50 books and their authors become 51 queries. In development the
  PHP error log says "Probable N+1 query" with the file and line (G127). Load them with `with('author')`.
+ **`with('tags')` without `pivot`** (G124): `tags` is plural, so it is read as has many: `tags.book_id`, which fails
  with "Unknown column 'book_id'". Write `with(['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])`.
+ **`belongsTo()` as the inverse of `hasMany()`** (G9): it returns the children, like `hasMany()`. Use `with('author')`
  (or `hasOne()`).
+ **A foreign key of another type than the `id` it points at** (G10): MySQL refuses the constraint. Give both
  `INT UNSIGNED`.
+ **Reading `$book->author->name`**: related rows are arrays. Write `$book->author['name']`.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries -->

The **query builder** reads and writes your tables without SQL strings. You chain a few calls, and Caligrafy writes one
SQL statement with every value bound (sent apart from the SQL, so what a person types can never change the query). It
is how a capability lists, filters, pages and counts rows, and loads related rows in one query instead of one per row.
Since 2.19.0.

**Since 2.26.0** N+1 queries are prevented by default: calling a relation method on one of several rows a query returned throws `[ERROR 2004] Lazy loading prevented` in development, with the `with('<relation>')` fix, and logs a warning in production. `->lazy()`, `#[Caligrafy\Lazy]` or `STRICT_RELATIONS=false` allow it. See [eager loading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Eager-Loading).

```php
use Caligrafy\Database;

$rows  = Database::table('books')->where('published_year', '<', 1975)->orderBy('title')->limit(10)->get();   // arrays
$books = Book::where('author_id', 1)->with('author')->paginate(20);                                        // Book models
```

+ `Database::table('books')` gives **arrays**, one per row.
+ `Book::query()`, or any call on the model class (`Book::where(...)`, `Book::find(3)`, `Book::with(...)`), gives
  **`Book` models**, on the model's table ([Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models)).

The examples use the Bookshelf tables and sample rows of [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models).
## With Claude

Say what the list filters, sorts and returns:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only: the books sorted by title, 20 per page, with their author and tags; filters author_id and search (title or summary)
```

Claude writes the capability with the query builder: `Book::with(...)->orderBy(...)`, a `where()` per filter given,
`search()` for words, and `paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)` with `'page' => 'integer'` in `$rules`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ no SQL string is built from an input, and no query runs inside a loop;
+ every input `handle()` reads is in `$rules` (`page` too);
+ `update()` and `delete()` of a query have a `where()`;
+ `php caligrafer.php call list_books search=shadow` returns the right rows.
## <a name="capability"></a>By hand

Run the commands in the Docker container: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...` (without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **Create the capability.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListBooks --scope books:read --read-only
    ```
2. **Write the query.** Make `application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'list_books',
        description: 'Lists the books of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page, each with its author and its tags. Filters: author_id, search (words of the title or the summary). Returns data (the books), total, page, per_page and pages.',
        scope: 'books:read',
        readOnly: true,
        public: true
    )]
    class ListBooks extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array(
            'author_id' => 'integer',
            'search' => 'max_len,100',
            'page' => 'integer'
        );

        public $descriptions = array(
            'author_id' => 'Optional: only the books of this author',
            'search' => 'Optional: words to find in the title or the summary',
            'page' => 'Optional: the page, 1 by default (20 books per page)'
        );

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $query = Book::with('author', array('tags' => array('pivot' => true)))->orderBy('title');
            if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
                $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);
            }
            if (!empty($input['search'])) {
                $query->search(array('title', 'summary'), $input['search']);
            }
            return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
        }
    }
    ```
    A query built step by step changes as you call it: `$query->where(...)` adds to `$query`.
3. **Run it.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call list_books search=shadow
    ```
    returns one page: `"data"` holds *A Wizard of Earthsea* with its `author` and its `tags`, then
    `"total": 1, "page": 1, "per_page": 20, "pages": 1`. With `author_id=2` the page holds *Kindred* and *Parable of
    the Sower* (`"total": 2`); with `author_id=abc` the answer is
    `"author_id": "The Author Id field must be a number without a decimal"`.

One capability, and the page, the REST API, the Vue app and agents all get the same filtered, paged list
([Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#web)).

**Check:**
+ `call list_books search=shadow` gives `"total": 1`;
+ `call list_books search=50%` gives `"total": 0`: `%` is a character to find, not a wildcard;
+ `call list_books page=2` gives `"data": []` with `"page": 2` (there are fewer than 21 books).
## <a name="read"></a>Reference: building a query

```php
Book::where('author_id', 1)->get();                               // author_id = 1
Book::where('published_year', '<', 1975)->where('author_id', 1)->get();   // AND
Book::where('published_year', '<', 1970)->orWhere('author_id', 3)->get(); // OR
Book::where(['author_id' => 1, 'published_year' => 1968])->get(); // several equalities, in parentheses
Book::where(function ($q) {                                       // a group in parentheses
    $q->where('published_year', '<', 1970)->orWhere('author_id', 3);
})->where('summary', '!=', null)->get();

Book::whereIn('id', [1, 2, 3])->get();                            // whereNotIn too
Book::whereNull('summary')->get();                                // whereNotNull too
Book::whereBetween('published_year', [1960, 1980])->get();        // both ends included
Book::query()->search(['title', 'summary'], $words)->get();       // title or summary contains the words
Book::query()->latest()->limit(5)->offset(5)->get();              // newest first (created_at); oldest() the other way
Book::query()->select('id', 'title as name')->arrays()->get();    // two columns, renamed
```

The SQL they write (`toSql()` and `getBindings()` show it, without running it):

| Query | SQL | Bindings |
|---|---|---|
| `Book::where(['author_id' => 1, 'published_year' => 1968])` | ``SELECT * FROM `books` WHERE (`author_id` = ? AND `published_year` = ?)`` | `[1, 1968]` |
| the group above | ``... WHERE (`published_year` < ? OR `author_id` = ?) AND `summary` IS NOT NULL`` | `[1970, 3]` |
| `Book::whereIn('id', [1, 2, 3])->whereNull('summary')->whereBetween('published_year', [1960, 1980])` | ``... WHERE `id` IN (?, ?, ?) AND `summary` IS NULL AND `published_year` BETWEEN ? AND ?`` | `[1, 2, 3, 1960, 1980]` |
| `Book::query()->search(['title', 'summary'], 'shadow 50%')` | ``... WHERE (`title` LIKE ? OR `summary` LIKE ?)`` | `['%shadow 50\%%', '%shadow 50\%%']` |
| `Book::query()->latest()->limit(5)->offset(5)` | ``SELECT * FROM `books` ORDER BY `created_at` DESC LIMIT 5 OFFSET 5`` | `[]` |
| `Book::query()->select('id', 'title as name')` | ``SELECT `id`, `title` AS `name` FROM `books` `` | `[]` |

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `where($column, $value)` | `=`; `where($column, null)` is `IS NULL` |
| `where($column, $operator, $value)` | operators `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `like`, `not like`; `where($column, '!=', null)` is `IS NOT NULL` |
| `where([$column => $value, ...])`, `where(function ($q) {...})` | equalities joined by `AND`, a group; both in parentheses |
| `orWhere(...)` | the same forms, joined by `OR` |
| `whereIn($column, $list)`, `whereNotIn($column, $list)` | an empty list: `whereIn` matches no row, `whereNotIn` adds no condition |
| `whereNull($column)`, `whereNotNull($column)`, `whereBetween($column, [$from, $to])` | |
| `search($columns, $words)` | `(c1 LIKE ? OR c2 LIKE ?)` with `%words%` bound; `%` and `_` in the words are escaped; empty words add no condition |
| `orderBy($column, 'asc' or 'desc')`, `latest($column = 'created_at')`, `oldest($column = 'created_at')` | |
| `limit($n)`, `offset($n)` | whole numbers >= 0 |
| `select(...$columns)` | `'id'`, `'books.*'`, `'title as name'`; one array works too |
| `arrays()` | rows stay arrays (undoes the models of `Book::query()`) |
| `input($array)` | where `paginate()` reads `page` instead of the query string |
| `with(...)`, `withCount(...)` | related rows and counts: [Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships) |

**Names are checked, values are bound.** A table or column name must be letters, digits and `_` (or `table.column`);
anything else is refused before any SQL runs: `[ERROR 2001] Invalid table or column name 'name; DROP': letters, digits
and _ only, with one optional prefix (table.column)`. Another operator gives `[ERROR 2001] Operator not allowed: use
=, !=, <>, <, >, <=, >=, like or not like`. A boolean is bound as `0`/`1`, a `DateTime` as `Y-m-d H:i:s`; an array
value is refused (use `whereIn`).

**Selected columns and models.** A model has every property its class declares, so
`Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->get()` gives `Book` models whose other columns are `null` (and a capability
returns them, `null`s included). For only the columns you selected (a CSV export, a small list), add `arrays()`:
`Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->arrays()->get()` gives `[['id' => 1, 'title' => 'A Wizard of Earthsea'], ...]`,
as `Database::table('books')->select('id', 'title')->get()` does.
## Reference: getting the rows

| To get | Call | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| every row | `get()` | a list (empty when none) |
| the first row | `first()` | one row, or `null` |
| one row by id | `find(3)`, `find($value, 'isbn')` | one row, or `null` |
| one value | `value('title')` | `'Kindred'`, or `null` |
| one column | `pluck('title')`, `pluck('title', 'id')` | `['A Wizard of Earthsea', ...]`, `[1 => 'A Wizard of Earthsea', ...]` |
| how many | `count()` | a number (order and limit ignored) |
| whether any | `exists()` | `true` or `false` |
| a page | `paginate(20, $page)` | `['data', 'total', 'page', 'per_page', 'pages']` |
| many rows, in parts | `chunk(500, function ($rows, $part) { ... })` | `true`, or `false` when the function returned `false` |

`pluck()` also takes a count of `withCount()` or a relation of `with()`:
`Author::withCount('books')->pluck('books_count', 'name')` gives `['Ursula K. Le Guin' => 2, ...]`. `chunk()` reads in
`id` order unless the query has an order.

### <a name="paging"></a>Paging

```php
$page = Book::query()->orderBy('title')->paginate(2, 2);
// ['data' => [Kindred, Parable of the Sower], 'total' => 5, 'page' => 2, 'per_page' => 2, 'pages' => 3]
```

+ Without a page number, `paginate()` reads `page` from the query string (`?page=2`). In a capability, pass the page
  of its input, as in the steps above: REST, an agent or the command line have no query string.
+ A page number that is not a whole number >= 1 is page 1. A page past the last one gives `'data' => []` (and runs
  no second query). `pages` is at least 1.

### <a name="eager"></a>Related rows: `with()` and the N+1 problem

Listing 50 books and then reading each one's author runs 51 queries (the N+1 problem). `with()` runs two: one for the
books, one for all their authors (`WHERE id IN (...)`).

```php
$books   = Book::with('author', ['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])->get();   // author: a row or null; tags: a list
$authors = Author::withCount('books')->get();                            // books_count on each
$loan    = Database::table('loans')->with('book.author')->first();       // the loan, its book, the book's author
```

The names, the conventions and the settings are on
[Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships).

**The N+1 warning.** While you develop (`APP_ENV` other than `production`), when the same query runs 10 times in one
request, Caligrafy writes one line in the PHP error log:

```text
[Caligrafy] Probable N+1 query: the same SELECT ran 10 times in this request (select * from `books` where `id` = ? limit ?), from <the file>:<the line>. Load the rows once with with(): Database::table('books')->with('author')->get() or Book::with('author')->get().
```

Add a `with()` where it says. Production does not count.
## <a name="write"></a>Reference: writing rows

```php
$id = Database::table('tags')->insert(['name' => 'poetry']);                    // the new id, as a string: "4"
Database::table('tags')->insert([['name' => 'essay'], ['name' => 'travel']]);   // several rows, one statement

Database::table('tags')->where('id', $id)->update(['name' => 'poems']);         // 1: the rows changed
Book::where('id', 1)->increment('published_year');                              // also decrement('stock', 2)
Database::table('tags')->whereIn('name', ['essay', 'travel', 'poems'])->delete(); // 3: the rows deleted
```

+ `insert()` takes one row, or a list of rows that all have the same columns. Arrays and objects are written as JSON,
  booleans as `0`/`1`.
+ `update()`, `delete()`, `increment()` and `decrement()` need a `where...()`. Without one they refuse to run, so a
  missing condition never empties a table:
  `delete() needs a where(): ->where('id', $id)->delete(...). For every row of the table, write the SQL with Database::execute()`.
  `increment('stock', 5, ['restocked_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s')])` sets other columns at the same time.

### <a name="transactions"></a>Transactions

```php
$id = Database::transaction(function () use ($input) {
    // the book changes hands: close its open loan, then open the new one
    Database::table('loans')->where('book_id', $input['book_id'])->whereNull('returned_at')->update(['returned_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s')]);
    return Database::table('loans')->insert(['book_id' => $input['book_id'], 'borrower' => $input['borrower'], 'due_on' => $input['due_on']]);
});
```

All of it is saved, or none of it: an exception rolls everything back and is thrown again; otherwise
`transaction()` returns what the function returns. A transaction inside another one (or inside a test, which runs in
a transaction) is part of the outer one: catching its exception inside the outer one does not undo its rows. MySQL
saves a `CREATE` or an `ALTER` at once, which ends a transaction early: keep table changes in
[migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations).
## <a name="sql"></a>Under the hood: when to keep SQL

The builder writes one table's `SELECT` (with its relations), `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE`. Keep SQL, with `?`
placeholders, for joins with `GROUP BY`, subqueries, database functions and changes to every row of a table:

```php
$rows = Database::execute('SELECT author_id, MAX(published_year) AS latest FROM books GROUP BY author_id HAVING latest > ?', [1970]);
// [['author_id' => 2, 'latest' => 1993], ['author_id' => 3, 'latest' => 1972]]
```

The model's own methods of before 2.19 keep working too: `(new Book('books'))->create($input)`,
`->update($changes, $id)`, `->delete($id)`, `$book->save()`
([Models: other ways](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models#querybuilder)). New code writes with
`Book::insert()`, `Book::where('id', $id)->update()` and `->delete()`.

`Query::useExecutor($object)` sends the builder's queries to another object with `execute($sql, $bindings)` (a test
double); `Query::useExecutor(null)` goes back to the database.
## <a name="models"></a>Common mistakes

+ **`Book::find()` with a `find()` of your own in the model** (G122): it fails. Leave it out, or `Book::query()->find(3)`.
+ **A table the class name does not give** (G123): `BookReview` reads `bookreviews`; declare
  `protected static $tableName = 'book_reviews';`.
+ **`Book::search(...)`**: not forwarded; write `Book::query()->search(...)`. And the model's own
  `(new Book('books'))->search('title', '%x%')` takes `%` as a wildcard, the builder's `search()` does not (G126).
+ **`paginate(20)` in a capability**: it reads the query string, which REST, agents and the command line do not send.
  Write `paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)` with `'page' => 'integer'` in `$rules`.
+ **`update()` without `where()`** (G125): refused. `whereNotIn('id', [])` and `search($columns, '')` add no condition,
  so they do not count as one.
+ **Selected columns with models**: the other properties come back `null`; add `arrays()`.
+ **The N+1 warning in a worker** (G127): `APP_ENV` is read once per process, so a long worker counts across jobs;
  call `Query::watch(null)` between jobs.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Filters-and-Order -->

The [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) narrows the rows with `where()`,
`whereIn()`, `whereNull()`, `whereBetween()` and `search()`, picks the columns with `select()`, and sorts and limits
them with `orderBy()`, `latest()`, `limit()` and `offset()`. Every value is bound (sent apart from the SQL), and every
name is checked, so what a person types can never change the query. Since 2.19.0.

```php
Book::where('published_year', '<', 1975)->where('author_id', 1)->orderBy('title')->limit(10)->get();
```

The examples use the Bookshelf tables of [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models).
## With Claude

Say what the list filters and sorts:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only: the books sorted by title, 20 per page; filters author_id and search (title or summary)
```

Claude adds a `where()` per filter given and `search()` for words, each input declared in `$rules`.

**Check** before you say OK: no SQL string is built from an input, and `php caligrafer.php call list_books search=50%`
gives `"total": 0` (`%` is a character to find, not a wildcard).
## By hand

A query built step by step changes as you call it: `$query->where(...)` adds to `$query`. In a capability, add a
condition only for a filter that was given:

```php
public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
{
    $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
    if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
        $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);
    }
    if (!empty($input['search'])) {
        $query->search(array('title', 'summary'), $input['search']);
    }
    return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
}
```

`toSql()` and `getBindings()` show the SQL and its values without running it:

```php
$query = Book::whereIn('id', [1, 2, 3])->whereNull('summary');
$query->toSql();        // SELECT * FROM `books` WHERE `id` IN (?, ?, ?) AND `summary` IS NULL
$query->getBindings();  // [1, 2, 3]
```
## <a name="where"></a>Reference: conditions

```php
Book::where('author_id', 1)->get();                               // author_id = 1
Book::where('published_year', '<', 1975)->where('author_id', 1)->get();   // AND
Book::where('published_year', '<', 1970)->orWhere('author_id', 3)->get(); // OR
Book::where(['author_id' => 1, 'published_year' => 1968])->get(); // several equalities, in parentheses
Book::where(function ($q) {                                       // a group in parentheses
    $q->where('published_year', '<', 1970)->orWhere('author_id', 3);
})->where('summary', '!=', null)->get();

Book::whereIn('id', [1, 2, 3])->get();                            // whereNotIn too
Book::whereNull('summary')->get();                                // whereNotNull too
Book::whereBetween('published_year', [1960, 1980])->get();        // both ends included
Book::query()->search(['title', 'summary'], $words)->get();       // title or summary contains the words
```

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [`where($column, $value)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-where) | `=`; `where($column, null)` is `IS NULL` |
| `where($column, $operator, $value)` | operators `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `like`, `not like`; `where($column, '!=', null)` is `IS NOT NULL` |
| `where([$column => $value, ...])`, `where(function ($q) {...})` | equalities joined by `AND`, a group; both in parentheses |
| [`orWhere(...)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-orwhere) | the same forms, joined by `OR` |
| [`whereIn($column, $list)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-wherein), `whereNotIn($column, $list)` | an empty list: `whereIn` matches no row, `whereNotIn` adds no condition |
| `whereNull($column)`, `whereNotNull($column)` | `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL` |
| [`whereBetween($column, [$from, $to])`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-wherebetween) | both ends included |
| [`search($columns, $words)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-search) | `(c1 LIKE ? OR c2 LIKE ?)` with `%words%` bound; `%` and `_` in the words are escaped; empty words add no condition |

| Query | SQL | Bindings |
|---|---|---|
| `Book::where(['author_id' => 1, 'published_year' => 1968])` | ``SELECT * FROM `books` WHERE (`author_id` = ? AND `published_year` = ?)`` | `[1, 1968]` |
| the group above | ``... WHERE (`published_year` < ? OR `author_id` = ?) AND `summary` IS NOT NULL`` | `[1970, 3]` |
| `Book::query()->search(['title', 'summary'], 'shadow 50%')` | ``... WHERE (`title` LIKE ? OR `summary` LIKE ?)`` | `['%shadow 50\%%', '%shadow 50\%%']` |
## <a name="order"></a>Reference: columns, order and limits

```php
Book::query()->latest()->limit(5)->offset(5)->get();              // newest first (created_at); oldest() the other way
Book::query()->select('id', 'title as name')->arrays()->get();    // two columns, renamed
```

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [`select(...$columns)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-select) | `'id'`, `'books.*'`, `'title as name'`; one array works too |
| [`orderBy($column, 'asc' or 'desc')`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-orderby) | several calls sort by several columns |
| `latest($column = 'created_at')`, `oldest($column = 'created_at')` | newest or oldest first |
| `limit($n)`, `offset($n)` | whole numbers >= 0 |

``Book::query()->latest()->limit(5)->offset(5)`` writes ``SELECT * FROM `books` ORDER BY `created_at` DESC LIMIT 5 OFFSET 5``.

**Names are checked, values are bound.** A table or column name must be letters, digits and `_` (or `table.column`);
anything else is refused before any SQL runs: `[ERROR 2001] Invalid table or column name 'name; DROP': letters, digits
and _ only, with one optional prefix (table.column)`. Another operator gives `[ERROR 2001] Operator not allowed: use
=, !=, <>, <, >, <=, >=, like or not like`. A boolean is bound as `0`/`1`, a `DateTime` as `Y-m-d H:i:s`; an array
value is refused (use `whereIn`).
## Common mistakes

+ **`Book::search(...)`** is not forwarded to the builder: write `Book::query()->search(...)`. The model's own
  `(new Book('books'))->search('title', '%x%')` takes `%` as a wildcard; the builder's `search()` does not (G126).
+ **Selected columns with models**: `Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->get()` gives `Book` models whose other
  columns are `null`; add `arrays()` (G138).
+ **A filter read from `$input` that `$rules` does not declare**: only the inputs of `$rules` reach `handle()`.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Getting-Rows -->

A [query](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) runs when you ask for its rows: `get()` for every
row, `first()` and `find()` for one, `value()` and `pluck()` for a value or a column, `count()` and `exists()` for a
number or a yes, `chunk()` for many rows in parts, `paginate()` for a page. What you get is **arrays** from
`Database::table()` and **models** from a model class. Since 2.19.0.

```php
use Caligrafy\Database;

$rows  = Database::table('books')->where('author_id', 2)->get();   // arrays
$book  = Book::find(3);                                            // a Book, or null
$count = Book::where('author_id', 2)->count();                     // 2
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability get_book books:read read-only: one book by its id, not found when there is none
```

Claude reads the row with `Book::find($input['id'])` (or `with(...)->find(...)`) and throws
`ServiceError::notFound(...)` when it is `null`.

**Check:** `php caligrafer.php call get_book id=999` answers `not_found`, not an empty `data`.
## By hand

1. **Arrays or models.** `Database::table('books')` gives arrays, one per row. `Book::query()`, or a call of the query
   builder on the model class (`Book::where(...)`, `Book::find(3)`, `Book::with(...)`, `Book::first()`,
   `Book::paginate(20)`...), gives `Book` models, on the model's table: the class name in lower case plus `s`
   (`Book` -> `books`), unless the class declares `protected static $tableName = 'book_reviews';`.
2. **Switch between them.** `arrays()` keeps a model query's rows as arrays; `models(Book::class)` turns a
   `Database::table()` query's rows into models:
    ```php
    Book::query()->select('id', 'title')->arrays()->get();        // [['id' => 1, 'title' => 'A Wizard of Earthsea'], ...]
    Database::table('books')->models(Book::class)->get();         // Book models
    ```
3. **One row or nothing.** In a capability, a missing row is a refusal:
    ```php
    $book = Book::find($input['id']);
    if (!$book) {
        throw ServiceError::notFound('There is no book #' . $input['id']);
    }
    return $book;
    ```
## <a name="get"></a>Reference: getting the rows

| To get | Call | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| every row | [`get()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-get) | a list (empty when none) |
| the first row | [`first()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-first) | one row, or `null` |
| one row by id | [`find(3)`, `find($value, 'isbn')`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-find) | one row, or `null` |
| one value | [`value('title')`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-value) | `'Kindred'`, or `null` |
| one column | [`pluck('title')`, `pluck('title', 'id')`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-pluck) | `['A Wizard of Earthsea', ...]`, `[1 => 'A Wizard of Earthsea', ...]` |
| how many | [`count()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-count) | a number (order and limit ignored) |
| whether any | [`exists()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-exists) | `true` or `false` |
| a page | [`paginate(20, $page)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Pagination) | `['data', 'total', 'page', 'per_page', 'pages']` |
| many rows, in parts | [`chunk(500, function ($rows, $part) { ... })`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-chunk) | `true`, or `false` when the function returned `false` |

+ `pluck()` also takes a count of `withCount()` or a relation of `with()`:
  `Author::withCount('books')->pluck('books_count', 'name')` gives `['Ursula K. Le Guin' => 2, ...]`.
+ `chunk()` reads in `id` order unless the query has an order; the function gets the rows and the number of the part
  (from 1), and returning `false` stops.
+ `count()`, `exists()`, `value()` and `pluck()` of a column run one small query, without the relations and without
  models.
## <a name="models"></a>Reference: models and arrays

| Query | Rows |
|---|---|
| `Database::table('books')` | arrays |
| `Book::query()`, `Book::where(...)`, `Book::find(3)` | `Book` models, related rows (`with()`) as arrays |
| `->arrays()` | arrays (undoes the models) |
| `->models(Book::class)` | instances of a class that extends `Caligrafy\Model` (another class is refused) |

A model has every property its class declares: with `select()`, the other columns are `null`, and a capability returns
them, `null`s included. For only the columns you selected, add `arrays()`.
## Common mistakes

+ **`Book::find()` with a `find()` of your own in the model** (G122): `Book::find(1)` then fails with "Non-static method
  cannot be called statically". Leave it out, or write `Book::query()->find(1)`.
+ **A table the class name does not give** (G123): `BookReview` reads `bookreviews`; declare
  `protected static $tableName = 'book_reviews';`.
+ **Selected columns with models** (G138): add `arrays()`.
+ **A query inside a `foreach`** over rows: load the related rows with
  [`with()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Eager-Loading) instead.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Pagination -->

`paginate()` gives one page of a [query](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries)'s rows with the
numbers a page needs: the rows, how many there are in all, which page it is and how many pages there are. It runs two
queries (a count, then the page), and one when the page is past the last. A capability that returns a page serves it
the same way to web pages, REST, the JS client, agents and Snap's lists. Since 2.19.0.

```php
$page = Book::query()->orderBy('title')->paginate(2, 2);
// ['data' => [Kindred, Parable of the Sower], 'total' => 5, 'page' => 2, 'per_page' => 2, 'pages' => 3]
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability list_books books:read read-only: the books sorted by title, 20 per page, with their author
```

Claude writes `paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)` with `'page' => 'integer'` in `$rules`.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php call list_books page=2` gives `"page": 2` (and `"data": []` when there
are fewer than 21 books).
## By hand

1. **The capability** pages with the page of its input: REST, an agent and the command line have no query string.
    ```php
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer', 'page' => 'integer');

    public $descriptions = array(
        'author_id' => 'Optional: only the books of this author',
        'page' => 'Optional: the page, 1 by default (20 books per page)'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
        if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
            $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);
        }
        return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
    }
    ```
2. **The page**, in `application/config/routing/web.php`: the query string reaches the capability as its inputs
   (`?page=2`, `?author_id=2`), and the `query` option gives the view `$author_id` to keep in the links:
    ```php
    Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books', 'authors' => 'list_authors'], 'query' => ['author_id']]);
    ```
3. **The links**, in `application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug`
   ([the whole view](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)):
    ```pug
    //- the next and previous pages keep the author of the address (?author_id=2)
    - $filter = $author_id !== '' ? '&author_id=' . (int) $author_id : '';
    p.cq-auth-note
        | Page #{$books['page']} of #{$books['pages']}, #{$books['total']} books
        if $books['page'] > 1
            |  · 
            a(href="{$home}books?page=" . ($books['page'] - 1) . $filter) Previous
        if $books['page'] < $books['pages']
            |  · 
            a(href="{$home}books?page=" . ($books['page'] + 1) . $filter) Next
    ```
   The rows are `$books['data']`. Pug in Caligrafy is PHP: strings join with `.`.
## <a name="reference"></a>Reference

[`paginate($perPage = 20, $page = null)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-paginate)
returns:

| Key | What it is |
|---|---|
| `data` | the rows of the page (arrays or models, with their relations) |
| `total` | the rows of the whole query |
| `page` | the page number used |
| `per_page` | the rows per page |
| `pages` | the number of pages, at least 1 |

+ **Without a page number**, `paginate()` reads `page` from [`input($array)`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-input)
  when you gave one, else from the query string (`?page=2`).
+ A page number that is not a whole number >= 1 is page 1. A page past the last one gives `'data' => []` and runs no
  second query.
+ `$perPage` must be a whole number >= 1: anything else throws `paginate() needs a number of rows per page >= 1`.
+ Elsewhere a page keeps its shape: [`Route::download`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#download)
  exports the rows of that page only; a [Snap Show: List](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Show-Cards)
  shows its pages; a [card view](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Card-Views) gets `$rows` and
  `$page`.
## Common mistakes

+ **`paginate(20)` in a capability**: it reads the query string, which REST, agents and the command line do not send.
  Write `paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)` with `'page' => 'integer'` in `$rules`.
+ **`page` missing from `$rules`**: undeclared inputs never reach `handle()`, so every page is page 1.
+ **Reading `$_GET` in the view**: the view gets the query string only through the `query` option of `Route::page`.

+ [Views: a page of a list](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Query-Builder-Eager-Loading -->

**Eager loading** reads the related rows of a [query](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) in
one more query per relation, instead of one query per row. Listing 50 books and then reading each one's author runs 51
queries (the N+1 problem); `with('author')` runs two: one for the books, one for all their authors
(`WHERE id IN (...)`). `withCount()` adds a count per row in one `GROUP BY` query. While you develop, Caligrafy warns
you when the same query runs 10 times in a request. Since 2.19.0.

**Since 2.26.0** a relation method called on one of several rows read by a query throws `[ERROR 2004] Lazy loading prevented` in development (a warning in production): load the relation with `with()` and read it as a property. `$book->lazy()->author()` or `#[Caligrafy\Lazy]` on the method allow a call that is meant; `STRICT_RELATIONS=false` makes it a warning.

```php
$books   = Book::with('author', ['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])->get();   // author: a row or null; tags: a list
$authors = Author::withCount('books')->get();                            // books_count on each
$loan    = Database::table('loans')->with('book.author')->first();       // the loan, its book, the book's author
```
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability get_book books:read read-only: one book with its author, its loans and its tags
```

Claude reads the rows with `Book::with(...)`, and never queries in a loop.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ related rows come from `with()` or `withCount()`, not a query inside a `foreach`;
+ many-to-many relations say `['pivot' => true]` (or the pivot's name);
+ `php caligrafer.php call get_book id=3` shows the related rows under their names (`author`, `loans`, `tags`).
## By hand

1. **Name the relations.** `with()` follows the name you give and the table it is called on, so the models need no code:
    ```php
    $book = Book::with('author', 'loans', array('tags' => array('pivot' => true)))->find($input['id']);
    ```
   Four queries run: the book, then its author, its loans and its tags, each with `WHERE ... IN (...)`.
2. **Count instead of loading.**
    ```php
    return Author::withCount('books')->orderBy('name')->get();   // each author with books_count
    ```
3. **Narrow the related rows** with a function:
    ```php
    Book::with(['loans' => function ($q) { $q->whereNull('returned_at'); }])->get();
    ```
## <a name="names"></a>Reference: how `with()` reads a name

| Name | Called on | Kind | It reads | You get |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `author` (singular) | `books` | belongs to | `books.author_id` -> `authors.id` | one row, or `null` |
| `books` (plural) | `authors` | has many | `books.author_id` = `authors.id` | a list, or `[]` |
| `['tags' => ['pivot' => true]]` | `books` | many to many | `books_tags.book_id` = `books.id`, `books_tags.tag_id` = `tags.id` | a list, or `[]` |
| `book.author` | `loans` | nested | `loans.book_id` -> `books.id`, then `books.author_id` -> `authors.id` | `book` with its `author` |
| `['current_loan' => ['type' => 'hasOne', 'table' => 'loans']]` | `books` | has one | `loans.book_id` = `books.id` | the first row, or `null` |

+ The related rows are **arrays**, also under models: `$book->author['name']`, `$book->tags[0]['name']`.
+ The key must be in the rows: `Book::select('id', 'title')->with('author')` has no `author_id`, so `author` is `null`.
+ The pivot of `books` and `tags` is `books_tags`; when it does not exist but `tags_books` does, `with()` uses that one.
+ Keys are read in chunks of 1000 (`Query::IN_CHUNK`); the main rows are never repeated by a join.
## <a name="settings"></a>Reference: the settings of a relation

```php
Book::with(['writer' => ['table' => 'authors', 'foreign_key' => 'author_id']])->find(3);   // $book->writer
Book::with(['current_loan' => ['type' => 'hasOne', 'table' => 'loans', 'query' => function ($q) { $q->whereNull('returned_at'); }]])->get();
```

| Setting | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `belongsTo`, `hasOne`, `hasMany` or `belongsToMany` | singular name: `belongsTo`; plural: `hasMany`; with `pivot`: `belongsToMany` |
| `table` | the related table | the name in the plural (`belongsTo`, `hasOne`), the name itself (`hasMany`, `belongsToMany`) |
| `foreign_key` | belongs to: the column of this table; has one/many: the column of the related table; many to many: the pivot's column toward this table | `<name>_id` (belongs to), `<this table in the singular>_id` (the others) |
| `local_key` | the column of this table the others point at | `id` |
| `owner_key` | the column of the related table that is pointed at | `id` |
| `pivot` | `true` (the conventional pivot) or its name | none |
| `related_key` | the pivot's column toward the related table | `<name in the singular>_id` |
| `query` | a function that narrows the related rows | none |

An unknown setting, or a name that is not letters, digits and `_`, is refused before any query runs. All of it:
[Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships#override).

### `withCount()`

```php
Database::table('tags')->withCount(['books' => ['pivot' => true]])->pluck('books_count', 'name');
Author::withCount(['books' => function ($q) { $q->where('published_year', '<', 1970); }])->pluck('books_count', 'name');
```

It counts plural relations only (has many, many to many): `withCount('author')` is refused. A row with nothing to count
gets `0`.
## <a name="nplusone"></a>Reference: the N+1 warning

While you develop (`APP_ENV` other than `production`), when the same `SELECT` shape runs 10 times in one request,
Caligrafy writes one line in the PHP error log, with the first file and line outside `framework/`:

```text
[Caligrafy] Probable N+1 query: the same SELECT ran 10 times in this request (select * from `books` where `id` = ? limit ?), from <the file>:<the line>. Load the rows once with with(): Database::table('books')->with('author')->get() or Book::with('author')->get().
```

+ It counts every query run through `Database::execute()`, models included. Production does not count.
+ `Query::$threshold` (10) is the count; `Query::$logger` (a callable) receives the line instead of `error_log()`;
  `Query::watch(true)` or `watch(false)` forces it on or off, `watch(null)` decides from `APP_ENV` again and forgets the
  shapes counted ([API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Query#query-watch)).
## Common mistakes

+ **Relations follow names, not the database** (G124): irregular plurals (`person`/`people`) need `table` or `type`; a
  `limit()` in a `query` constraint limits the whole relation query, not each parent; a constraint on a many-to-many
  relation runs on the join: qualify columns (`tags.label`).
+ **`select()` without the key column**: the relation is `null`.
+ **The N+1 warning in a worker** (G127): `APP_ENV` is read once per process, so a long worker counts across jobs;
  call `Query::watch(null)` between jobs.
+ **A pivot inside `Database::transaction()` on PostgreSQL**: a failed query aborts the transaction; name the pivot
  (G124).
