---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.4-OpenAI%3A-ChatGPT%2C-GPTs%2C-DALL.E -->

Your application can ask OpenAI's models to write text (GPT) and to draw images (GPT image models; DALL.E was shut down
on May 12, 2026). The class `Caligrafy\OpenAI` sends the request; your key stays on the server. You put the call in a
**capability**, so the same feature reaches a web page, a Vue app, the REST API and AI agents (MCP) without a second
line of AI code. In the Bookshelf example, the capability `write_blurb` writes the back-cover blurb of a book, and
`draw_cover` draws a cover.

This page is about your application calling a model. The other direction, AI agents such as Claude using your
application, is [MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#mcp).

API calls cost money: create a key on [platform.openai.com/api-keys](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) and add
credits to its project first.
## With Claude

Ask for the feature and name the capability:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability write_blurb ai:use read-only
Write a two-sentence back-cover blurb for a book from its title and author, with OpenAI. Show it on a /blurb page with a form.
```

Claude scaffolds `application/services/Bookshelf/WriteBlurb.php` with `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service`, fills its `$rules` and
`handle()`, adds the routes to `application/config/routing/web.php` (`Route::page`, `Route::form`, and
`Route::capabilities`, `Route::mcp` when the project does not have them), writes the Pug view and a test in `tests/`.
For a chat app in Vue, `/caligrafy-quill:new-app app chat` follows the plugin's AI chat recipe.

**Check**
- `OPEN_AI_KEY` is in `.env`, never in a file of `public/` or in git; `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai` says OK.
- The capability is not `public: true` (anyone could spend your credits) and has a scope (`ai:use`).
- `handle()` checks `$result['response']['error']` (OpenAI's own errors) and `api_success` (no answer at all).
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test` passes without a real key: the test replaces the OpenAI client.
## By hand

The steps below add `write_blurb` (text) and `draw_cover` (image) to a project of the
[Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) that has sign-in
([`Route::auth`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#routeauth)), `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')`
and `Route::mcp('/mcp')` in `web.php`. Run the commands in the project folder. Without Docker (Composer with MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP), run the same commands without `docker compose exec dev-box` and open your own address.

### Step 1: Add the key

Open `.env` and set the key (keep the other lines as they are):

```text
OPEN_AI_KEY=sk-proj-...
OPEN_AI_MODEL=
OPEN_AI_IMAGE_MODEL=
```

Empty models mean the defaults: `gpt-6-luna` for text, `gpt-image-2` for images. Run:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai
```

It checks, without spending anything, that the key is accepted and that the default models are allowed for its
project. Without a key it prints `SKIP  OpenAI: OPEN_AI_KEY is not set`.

### Step 2: Create the capability

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/WriteBlurb --scope ai:use --read-only
```

Expected: `Created application/services/Bookshelf/WriteBlurb.php: capability 'write_blurb' (scope ai:use)`. Replace the
content of **`application/services/Bookshelf/WriteBlurb.php`** with:

```php
<?php
/**
 * WriteBlurb: writes the back-cover blurb of a book with OpenAI
 */

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\OpenAI;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'write_blurb',
    description: 'Writes a two-sentence back-cover blurb for a book from its title and author. Returns {blurb}.',
    scope: 'ai:use',
    readOnly: true
)]
class WriteBlurb extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'title' => 'required|max_len,255',
        'author' => 'max_len,255',
    );

    public $filters = array(
        'title' => 'trim',
        'author' => 'trim',
    );

    public $descriptions = array(
        'title' => 'The title of the book',
        'author' => 'The author of the book',
    );

    // the OpenAI client comes through the constructor: a test can replace it ($this->fake(OpenAI::class, ...))
    public function __construct(private OpenAI $openai)
    {
    }

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $book = $input['title'] . (!empty($input['author']) ? ' by ' . $input['author'] : '');
        $result = $this->openai->delegate(
            $book,
            'Write a back-cover blurb of two sentences. No spoilers.',
            CONVERSE
        );

        $response = $result['response'] ?? null;
        if (empty($result['api_success']) || !is_array($response)) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI did not answer: try again in a moment');
        }
        if (isset($response['error'])) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI refused: ' . ($response['error']['message'] ?? 'unknown error'));
        }

        return array('blurb' => trim($response[0]['message']['content'] ?? ''));
    }
}
```

What it does:
+ `readOnly: true`: it changes none of your data (agents may call it without asking).
+ The constructor gets a new `OpenAI` object (type `TEXT`) from the [container](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection).
+ `delegate($input, $outcome, $command)` sends `CONVERSE` as the system prompt and the title with the instructions as
  the user message, with the default model.
+ The answer is in `$response[0]['message']['content']`. When OpenAI refuses (wrong key, no credits, unknown model),
  `$response['error']['message']` says why; when nothing comes back (timeout, network), `api_success` is `false`.
  Both become a `conflict` refusal with that message: a page shows it in `flash('error')`, REST answers 409.

Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities`: the list now has
`write_blurb  ai:use  read  Writes a two-sentence back-cover blurb...`.

### Step 3: Call it from the command line

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call write_blurb title=Kindred author="Octavia E. Butler"
```

Expected (the text varies):

```json
{
    "data": {
        "blurb": "..."
    }
}
```

Without a title it answers `{"error": {"code": "invalid", ..., "fields": {"title": "The Title field is required"}}}`.

### Step 4: A page with a form

Add the routes to **`application/config/routing/web.php`**, before `Route::run();`:

```php
Route::page('/blurb', 'Bookshelf/blurb', ['signedIn' => true]);
Route::form('/blurb', 'write_blurb', ['success' => '/blurb', 'back' => '/blurb', 'flash' => '{blurb}']);
```

`Route::form` calls `write_blurb` with the form's fields, as the signed-in person, then goes back to `/blurb` with the
blurb as the `success` message (`{blurb}` is filled from the result). Create **`application/views/Bookshelf/blurb.pug`**:

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display Write a blurb

  section.cq-band.cq-band--tight
    .cq-inner.cq-inner--narrow
      if flash('error')
        .cq-alert.cq-alert--error(role='alert')= flash('error')
      if flash('success')
        p.cq-lead(role='status')= flash('success')
      form(method='POST', action="{$home}blurb")
        =csrf()
        .cq-field
          label(for='title') Title
          input#title.form-control(type='text', name='title', value=old('title'))
          if errors('title')
            p.cq-field-error= errors('title')
        .cq-field
          label(for='author') Author
          input#author.form-control(type='text', name='author', value=old('author'))
          if errors('author')
            p.cq-field-error= errors('author')
        button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Write
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/blurb`. Signed out, you go to `/login`. Signed in, type a title and click **Write**: the
page comes back with the blurb above the form. With an empty title it comes back with *The Title field is required*
under the field and the author you typed still there.

### Step 5: REST and AI agents

Nothing to add: `Route::capabilities` and `Route::mcp` serve every capability. Create a token for a program or an agent:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "blurb agent" --scopes ai:use --user 1
```

It prints `cq_...` once: store it as a secret. Then:

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_..." \
  -d '{"title": "Kindred", "author": "Octavia E. Butler"}' \
  http://localhost:8080/capabilities/write_blurb
```

Expected: `200` and `{"data":{"blurb":"..."}}`. Without the token: `401`. An agent connected to `/mcp` with this token
sees the tool `write_blurb` and calls it with the same inputs.

### Step 6: Test it without a key

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test make WriteBlurb
```

Replace **`tests/WriteBlurbTest.php`** with:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\OpenAI;
use Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase;

/**
 * php caligrafer.php test WriteBlurb
 */
final class WriteBlurbTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testItWritesABlurb(): void
    {
        // a stand-in for OpenAI: no request leaves the computer
        $this->fake(OpenAI::class, new class extends OpenAI {
            public function delegate($input = '', $outcome = '', $command = CONVERSE, $context = array(), $parameters = array())
            {
                return array('api_success' => true, 'type' => 'text',
                    'response' => array(array('message' => array('role' => 'assistant', 'content' => "A blurb for $input."))));
            }
        });

        $answer = $this->call('write_blurb', array('title' => 'Kindred', 'author' => 'Octavia E. Butler'), $this->user(1));

        $this->assertSame('A blurb for Kindred by Octavia E. Butler.', $answer['blurb']);
    }

    public function testItNeedsATitle(): void
    {
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'write_blurb', array(), $this->user(1));
    }

    public function testGuestsCannotUseIt(): void
    {
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('unauthenticated', 'write_blurb', array('title' => 'Kindred'), 'guest');
    }
}
```

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test WriteBlurb
```

Expected: `OK (3 tests, 3 assertions)`.

### Step 7: Images

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/DrawCover --scope ai:use --read-only
```

Replace **`application/services/Bookshelf/DrawCover.php`** with:

```php
<?php
/**
 * DrawCover: draws a book cover with an OpenAI image model
 */

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\OpenAI;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'draw_cover',
    description: 'Draws a book cover from a title and a short description. Returns {image}: a PNG as a data URL.',
    scope: 'ai:use',
    readOnly: true
)]
class DrawCover extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'title' => 'required|max_len,255',
        'idea' => 'max_len,1000',
        'quality' => 'contains_list,low;medium;high',
    );

    public $filters = array(
        'title' => 'trim',
        'idea' => 'trim',
    );

    public $descriptions = array(
        'title' => 'The title of the book',
        'idea' => 'What the cover should show',
        'quality' => 'low (fastest), medium (default) or high',
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $prompt = 'A book cover for "' . $input['title'] . '". ' . ($input['idea'] ?? '') . ' No text on the cover.';
        $openai = new OpenAI(IMAGE);
        $result = $openai->delegate($prompt, '', ANALYZE, array(), array(
            'size' => '1024x1536',
            'quality' => $input['quality'] ?? 'medium',
        ));

        $response = $result['response'] ?? null;
        if (empty($result['api_success']) || !is_array($response)) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('No image: OpenAI did not answer in time, try the low quality');
        }
        if (isset($response['error'])) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI refused: ' . ($response['error']['message'] ?? 'unknown error'));
        }

        return array('image' => 'data:image/png;base64,' . ($response[0]['b64_json'] ?? ''));
    }
}
```

GPT image models answer with a **base64 image**, never a URL: the capability returns it as a `data:` URL that an `img`
shows as it is. For an image, `delegate()` sends the input as the `prompt` and ignores the command. (The container
always builds a `TEXT` client, so this capability creates its `IMAGE` client itself.)

An image is too large for a flash message, so the page calls the capability from the browser with the generated
JavaScript client. Write the client (run it again after every capability change):

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client
```

Expected: `public/js/capabilities.js written: ... capabilities`. Add the page to **`web.php`**:

```php
Route::page('/cover', 'Bookshelf/cover', ['signedIn' => true]);
```

**`application/views/Bookshelf/cover.pug`**:

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display Draw a cover

  section.cq-band.cq-band--tight
    .cq-inner.cq-inner--narrow
      p#error.cq-alert.cq-alert--error(role='alert', hidden)
      form#cover(method='POST')
        .cq-field
          label(for='title') Title
          input#title.form-control(type='text', name='title', required)
        .cq-field
          label(for='idea') What the cover shows
          input#idea.form-control(type='text', name='idea')
        button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Draw
      img#image(alt='The cover', width='512', hidden)

  script(type='module', src="{$home}public/js/cover.js")
```

**`public/js/cover.js`**:

```js
import { drawCover, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'

const form = document.getElementById('cover')
const image = document.getElementById('image')
const error = document.getElementById('error')
const button = form.querySelector('button')

form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault()
  error.hidden = true
  button.disabled = true
  button.textContent = 'Drawing...'
  try {
    const answer = await drawCover({ title: form.elements.title.value, idea: form.elements.idea.value, quality: 'low' })
    image.src = answer.image
    image.hidden = false
  } catch (e) {
    error.textContent = e instanceof CapabilityError ? (Object.values(e.fields || {}).join(' ') || e.message) : 'Something went wrong.'
    error.hidden = false
  } finally {
    button.disabled = false
    button.textContent = 'Draw'
  }
})
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/cover`, type a title and click **Draw**: the button says *Drawing...* and the cover
appears under the form. The client sends the session cookie and its CSRF token: no key in the page.

**Check**
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists `write_blurb` and `draw_cover` with the scope `ai:use`.
- `/blurb` and `/cover` send signed-out visitors to `/login`.
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test WriteBlurb` passes with no key in `.env`.
- `curl` without a token on `/capabilities/write_blurb` answers `401`.
- `grep -r OPEN_AI_KEY public/` finds nothing.
## Reference

### `new OpenAI($mode = TEXT)`

| Mode | Endpoint | Default parameters |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `model` = `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` only |
| `IMAGE` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations` | `model` = `OPENAI_DEFAULT_IMAGE_MODEL`, `n` 1, `size` `1024x1024`, `quality` `medium`, `output_format` `png` |

Only the model is sent by default for text: current reasoning models reject `temperature`, `top_p` and `max_tokens`.
Add the parameters your model supports (`max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`, `response_format`...).

### `delegate($input = '', $outcome = '', $command = ANALYZE, $context = array(), $parameters = array())`

+ **TEXT**: sends `messages` = the `$context` messages, then `{role: system, content: $command}`, then
  `{role: user, content: "$input\n\n$outcome\n"}`. `$outcome` may be an array (sent as `| a | b |`).
  `$context` is the earlier conversation (`['role' => 'user'|'assistant'|'system', 'content' => '...']`).
+ **IMAGE**: sends `prompt` = `$input` with `$parameters`; `$outcome`, `$command` and `$context` are not used.
+ `$parameters` are merged over the defaults.

| Command | System prompt sent |
|---|---|
| `CONVERSE` | `You are a helpful assistant:` |
| `SUMMARIZE` | `Summarize the following:` |
| `ANALYZE` (default) | `Analyze the following:` |
| `CORRECT` | `Fix the following:` |
| `CLASSIFY` | `Classify the following:` (the categories in `$outcome`) |
| `COMPLETE` | `Complete the following:`; with `[insert]` in the input, the model writes only the text that replaces it |
| `PREDICT` | `Predict based on the following:` |
| `RECOMMEND` | `Recommend about the following:` |
| `CUSTOM` | empty: put your own system message first in `$context` |

### The answer

```php
array(
    'api_success' => true,     // false only when nothing came back (timeout, network): response is then a message
    'response' => array(...),  // TEXT: the choices, the text in [0]['message']['content']
                               // IMAGE: the data, the base64 PNG in [0]['b64_json']
                               // or OpenAI's error body: ['error' => ['message' => ..., 'code' => ...]]
    'type' => 'text'           // 'text' or 'image', when something came back
)
```

`api_success` is `true` for an error body too: always check `isset($result['response']['error'])`.

### Other methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `converse($parameters = array(), $attachments = array(), $method = 'POST', $additionalHeaders = array())` | sends the parameters as they are to the endpoint of the mode (`delegate()` uses it); same answer shape |
| `OpenAI::command($name)` | `'summarize'` -> `SUMMARIZE`... (`OpenAI::COMMANDS`), anything else -> `null` |
| `OpenAI::type($name)` | `'text'` -> `TEXT`, `'image'` -> `IMAGE`, anything else -> `null` |

When a command or a type comes from a form, resolve it with `OpenAI::command()` / `OpenAI::type()`, never with
`constant()`: `constant()` would accept the name of any constant, `.env` secrets included.

An `OpenAI` object keeps the parameters of its earlier calls (`converse()` merges each call's parameters into it): use
a new object per request, as the container does for each capability call.

### Models

| Constant | Model |
|---|---|
| `GPT6_LUNA` | `gpt-6-luna`: fastest, cheapest; the default (`OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL`, or `OPEN_AI_MODEL`) |
| `GPT6_SOL` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `GPT6_ASTRA` | `gpt-6-astra`: the flagship (`GPT4_LATEST` and `GPT4_LATEST_VISION` point to it) |
| `GPT_IMAGE` | `gpt-image-2`: the image default (`OPENAI_DEFAULT_IMAGE_MODEL`, or `OPEN_AI_IMAGE_MODEL`) |
| `GPT_IMAGE_BEST` | `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| `GPT_IMAGE_FAST` | `gpt-image-2.5-flare` |
| `GPT3`, `GPT4`, `GPT4_32` | shut down by OpenAI |
| `GPT4O`, `GPT4OMINI` | retire on January 14, 2027 |

Pass another model with `$parameters`: `array('model' => GPT6_ASTRA)`. Image options: `size` (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`,
`1024x1536`, `auto`), `quality` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `auto`), `output_format` (`png`, `jpeg`, `webp`), `background`, `n`.

### `.env`

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| `OPEN_AI_KEY` | none: required |
| `OPEN_AI_MODEL` | `gpt-6-luna` |
| `OPEN_AI_IMAGE_MODEL` | `gpt-image-2` |

The constants of `OpenAI.php` (`TEXT`, `CONVERSE`, `GPT6_LUNA`...) exist once the class is loaded: a file that uses one
before any `OpenAI` (for example in a property default) stops with *Undefined constant*.
## Other ways

**The example controller.** `web.php` ships two commented routes to a demo page that sends a form to `delegate()`:

```php
Route::get('/ai', 'Caligrafy\\Controllers\\AIController');
Route::post('/ai', 'Caligrafy\\Controllers\\AIController@query');
```

The controller is `application/controllers/core/AI/AIController.php`, its view `application/views/AI/openai.pug`. The
routes are open to anyone who reaches the site and every request is billed to you: use them to explore, then write a
capability as above, which has a scope, a sign-in check, validation and every channel.

**An answer that is not JSON.** For streaming or custom headers, serve a web-only capability with
[`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action), and keep the AI call in a plain capability that it calls with
`$this->capability('write_blurb', $input, $context)`. A controller that creates `new OpenAI()` reaches only its one route.
## Common mistakes

+ **Reading only `api_success`.** It is `true` when OpenAI answers with an error (rejected key, no credits, unknown
  model). Check `$result['response']['error']`. A `429 insufficient_quota` means the project has no credits.
+ **Sending `temperature` or `max_tokens`** to a reasoning model: OpenAI refuses the request. Use `max_completion_tokens`.
+ **Looking for an image URL.** GPT image models return base64 in `[0]['b64_json']`.
+ **Slow images.** The HTTP client gives up after 30 seconds (`httpRequest()`): a `high` quality image can take longer
  and comes back with `api_success` false. Use `low` or `medium`.
+ **A public capability.** `public: true` lets anyone spend your credits. Keep a scope and sign-in.
+ **The key in the browser.** Never put `OPEN_AI_KEY` in a page, `public/` or a Vue build: the browser calls the
  capability, the server calls OpenAI.
+ **`form.title` in a script.** It is the form's own `title` attribute: read inputs with `form.elements.title`.
+ **`constant($_POST['command'])`.** Use `OpenAI::command()`.

+ [Open source agents (Llama, Mistral...)](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.6-Open-Source-Agents-(llama,-Mistral-etc.)): the same with open models
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.5-Open-AI%3A-Assistants -->

An **assistant** holds a conversation: it remembers what was said, follows your instructions and can answer from your
own files. `Caligrafy\Assistant` runs on OpenAI's Responses and Conversations APIs (OpenAI shut down its Assistants API
on August 26, 2026; see [Migrating from version 1](#migrating)). You put it in a capability, so the same assistant
answers a web page, a Vue app, the REST API and AI agents. In the Bookshelf example, the capability `ask_librarian`
answers questions about the books, from a catalog file, and remembers the conversation.

Nothing is stored on OpenAI for the assistant itself: its model, instructions and tools live in your code and are sent
with every answer. OpenAI keeps the **conversation** (`conv_...`) and, when you give files, a **vector store** (`vs_...`)
that indexes them.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability ask_librarian ai:use read-only
A librarian assistant (Caligrafy\Assistant) that answers questions about the books from application/files/catalog.md and
continues a conversation when it gets the conversation id back. A /librarian page to chat with it.
```

Claude scaffolds the services in `application/services/`, a page (Pug view and a script that calls the generated
client), the routes in `web.php` and a test that replaces the assistant.

**Check**
- `OPEN_AI_KEY` is in `.env` only; `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai` says OK.
- The conversation id goes back to the caller and comes in again as an input: the capability keeps nothing in the session.
- The capability that uploads files is not reachable by agents (`mcp: false`) and needs an administrator (`level: 1`).
- Answers are shown as text (`textContent`, `{{ }}`), never as HTML.
## By hand

The project is the one of the [OpenAI page](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.4-OpenAI:-ChatGPT,-GPTs,-DALL.E):
`OPEN_AI_KEY` in `.env`, sign-in, `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` and `Route::mcp('/mcp')`. Without Docker (Composer with MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP), run the same commands without `docker compose exec dev-box` and open your own address.

### Step 1: Write the catalog

Create **`application/files/catalog.md`** (the `application` folder is never served to browsers):

```text
# Bookshelf catalog

- Kindred, Octavia E. Butler, 1979. Shelf B, 2 copies.
- The Dispossessed, Ursula K. Le Guin, 1974. Shelf A, 1 copy.
```

### Step 2: A capability that indexes it

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/IndexCatalog --scope ai:admin
```

Replace **`application/services/Bookshelf/IndexCatalog.php`** with:

```php
<?php
/**
 * IndexCatalog: uploads the catalog file to OpenAI so that the librarian answers from it
 */

use Caligrafy\Assistant;
use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'index_catalog',
    description: 'Uploads application/files/catalog.md to OpenAI and returns the id of its vector store, for LIBRARIAN_STORE in .env.',
    scope: 'ai:admin',
    level: 1,
    mcp: false
)]
class IndexCatalog extends Service
{
    public $rules = array();

    public function __construct(private Assistant $assistant)
    {
    }

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $file = APP_PATH . 'files/catalog.md';
        if (!is_file($file)) {
            throw ServiceError::notFound('Write the catalog in application/files/catalog.md first');
        }

        $this->assistant->name = 'Bookshelf catalog';
        $uploaded = $this->assistant->uploadAssistantFiles(array($file));
        if (empty($uploaded) || $this->assistant->vector_store_id === '') {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI did not take the file: check OPEN_AI_KEY (php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai)');
        }

        return array('vector_store_id' => $this->assistant->vector_store_id, 'file_ids' => $uploaded);
    }
}
```

`uploadAssistantFiles()` sends the file to OpenAI (`POST /v1/files`) and creates a vector store named after the
assistant with it. Run it once from the command line (it has full access there):

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call index_catalog
```

Expected:

```json
{
    "data": {
        "vector_store_id": "vs_...",
        "file_ids": [
            "file-..."
        ]
    }
}
```

Copy the `vs_...` id into **`.env`**:

```text
LIBRARIAN_STORE=vs_...
```

Every `.env` line becomes a constant: the capability below reads `LIBRARIAN_STORE`. Run `index_catalog` again after you
change the catalog (it creates a new store: put its id in `.env`).

### Step 3: The librarian

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/AskLibrarian --scope ai:use --read-only
```

Replace **`application/services/Bookshelf/AskLibrarian.php`** with:

```php
<?php
/**
 * AskLibrarian: a conversation with an OpenAI assistant that knows the bookshelf
 */

use Caligrafy\Assistant;
use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'ask_librarian',
    description: 'Asks the bookshelf librarian a question. Send the conversation id it returns to continue the same conversation. Returns {conversation, answer}.',
    scope: 'ai:use',
    readOnly: true
)]
class AskLibrarian extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'question' => 'required|max_len,4000',
        'conversation' => 'alpha_numeric_dash|max_len,100',
    );

    public $filters = array(
        'question' => 'trim',
        'conversation' => 'trim',
    );

    public $descriptions = array(
        'question' => 'The question for the librarian',
        'conversation' => 'The conversation id of an earlier answer, to continue that conversation',
    );

    // the assistant comes through the constructor: a test can replace it ($this->fake(Assistant::class, ...))
    public function __construct(private Assistant $assistant)
    {
    }

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $assistant = $this->assistant;
        $assistant->instructions = 'You are the librarian of a small bookshelf. Answer in three sentences at most.';
        if (defined('LIBRARIAN_STORE') && LIBRARIAN_STORE !== '') {
            $assistant->vector_store_id = LIBRARIAN_STORE;   // answer from the catalog (index_catalog)
        }

        if (!empty($input['conversation'])) {
            $assistant->thread_id = $input['conversation'];  // continue that conversation
        } else {
            $assistant->start();                              // a new conversation on OpenAI
            if ($assistant->thread_id === '') {
                throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI did not start the conversation: check OPEN_AI_KEY (php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai)');
            }
        }

        $assistant->createMessage($input['question'])->run();
        if ($assistant->status !== 'completed') {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('OpenAI did not answer: ' . ($assistant->last_response['error']['message'] ?? $assistant->status));
        }

        return array('conversation' => $assistant->thread_id, 'answer' => $assistant->text());
    }
}
```

What it does:
+ The container gives a new `Assistant` with no settings (creating it calls nothing on OpenAI); `handle()` sets its
  instructions and, when `LIBRARIAN_STORE` is set, its vector store, which the default `file_search` tool searches.
+ The first question opens a conversation (`start()`, `POST /v1/conversations`). The caller sends its id back with the
  next question, so the capability keeps nothing between calls and works the same for a page, REST and an agent.
+ `run()` sends the question with the instructions, the tools and the conversation (`POST /v1/responses`) and returns
  when the answer is there; `text()` is its text.

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call ask_librarian question="Where is Kindred?"
```

Expected (the answer varies):

```json
{
    "data": {
        "conversation": "conv_...",
        "answer": "Kindred is on shelf B; there are 2 copies."
    }
}
```

Continue the same conversation:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call ask_librarian question="Who wrote it?" conversation=conv_...
```

### Step 4: A page to chat

The conversation id lives in the page, so the page calls the capability with the generated client. Write it:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client
```

Add to **`application/config/routing/web.php`**, before `Route::run();`:

```php
Route::page('/librarian', 'Bookshelf/librarian', ['signedIn' => true]);
```

**`application/views/Bookshelf/librarian.pug`**:

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display Ask the librarian

  section.cq-band.cq-band--tight
    .cq-inner.cq-inner--narrow
      ul#answers.cq-rows
      p#error.cq-alert.cq-alert--error(role='alert', hidden)
      form#ask(method='POST')
        .cq-field
          label(for='question') Your question
          input#question.form-control(type='text', name='question', required)
        button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Ask

  script(type='module', src="{$home}public/js/librarian.js")
```

**`public/js/librarian.js`**:

```js
import { askLibrarian, CapabilityError } from './capabilities.js'

const form = document.getElementById('ask')
const answers = document.getElementById('answers')
const error = document.getElementById('error')
const button = form.querySelector('button')
let conversation = ''   // the conversation id of the first answer: the next questions continue it

function add (who, text) {
  const row = document.createElement('li')
  row.className = 'cq-row'
  row.textContent = who + ': ' + text   // text, never HTML: the answer comes from a model
  answers.append(row)
}

form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault()
  const question = form.elements.question.value.trim()
  if (!question) return
  error.hidden = true
  button.disabled = true
  add('You', question)
  try {
    const input = conversation ? { question, conversation } : { question }
    const answer = await askLibrarian(input)
    conversation = answer.conversation
    add('Librarian', answer.answer)
    form.reset()
  } catch (e) {
    error.textContent = e instanceof CapabilityError ? (Object.values(e.fields || {}).join(' ') || e.message) : 'Something went wrong.'
    error.hidden = false
  } finally {
    button.disabled = false
  }
})
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/librarian`, sign in, ask *Where is Kindred?* then *How many copies?*: both questions and
answers appear in the list, and the second answer knows the first.

### Step 5: Test it without a key

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test make AskLibrarian
```

Replace **`tests/AskLibrarianTest.php`** with:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Assistant;
use Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase;

/**
 * php caligrafer.php test AskLibrarian
 */
final class AskLibrarianTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testItAnswersAndKeepsTheConversation(): void
    {
        // a stand-in for the OpenAI assistant: no request leaves the computer
        $this->fake(Assistant::class, new class extends Assistant {
            public function start() { $this->thread_id = 'conv_test'; return $this; }
            public function run($additional_instructions = '', $instructions = null, $tools = [], $model = '', $metadata = null)
            {
                $this->status = 'completed';
                $this->response_text = 'Kindred is on shelf B.';
                return $this;
            }
        });

        $answer = $this->call('ask_librarian', array('question' => 'Where is Kindred?'), $this->user(1));

        $this->assertSame(array('conversation' => 'conv_test', 'answer' => 'Kindred is on shelf B.'), $answer);
    }

    public function testItNeedsAQuestion(): void
    {
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'ask_librarian', array(), $this->user(1));
    }
}
```

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test AskLibrarian
```

Expected: `OK (2 tests, 2 assertions)`.

**Check**
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists `ask_librarian` (`ai:use`, read) and `index_catalog` (`ai:admin`, writes).
- An MCP `tools/list` does not show `index_catalog`.
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call ask_librarian question=x conversation="conv/../x"` is refused: *The Conversation field may
  only contain letters, numbers, dashes and underscores*.
- The page shows the answers as plain text.
## Reference

### `new Assistant($parameters = array())`

Creating an assistant calls nothing on OpenAI, unless you give it files.

| Parameter | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | none | the name (also the name of its vector store) |
| `description` | none | kept in the object only |
| `instructions` | none | the system prompt sent with every answer |
| `model` | `ASSISTANT_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`gpt-6-luna`, or `OPEN_AI_MODEL`) | `ASSISTANT_GPT6_LUNA`, `ASSISTANT_GPT6_SOL`, `ASSISTANT_GPT6_ASTRA` |
| `tools` | `array(['type' => 'file_search'])` | add `['type' => 'code_interpreter']` to let it run code on the files |
| `metadata` | none | up to 16 string pairs, sent with the conversation and every answer |
| `file_paths` | none | local files: uploaded and indexed in a new vector store at once |
| `file_ids` | none | files already on OpenAI: indexed in a new vector store at once |
| `vector_store_id` | `''` | an existing vector store: reuse its files without uploading them again |

`file_search` gets `vector_store_ids` = the assistant's store (it is left out when there is no store);
`code_interpreter` gets `container: {type: auto, file_ids}`; the old tool name `retrieval` becomes `file_search`.

### Methods

| Method | Chainable | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `start()` | yes | creates a conversation (`POST /v1/conversations`): `thread_id` = `conv_...` |
| `createMessage($content, $file_ids = [], $metadata = null, $role = "user")` | yes | queues a message for the next `run()`; `$role`: user, assistant, system or developer; `$file_ids` go to the code interpreter; `$metadata` is not used |
| `run($additional_instructions = '', $instructions = null, $tools = [], $model = '', $metadata = null)` | yes | sends the queued messages (`POST /v1/responses`) and waits for the answer; the arguments override the settings for this answer only |
| `retrieveResponse($timeout = 120, $interval = 2)` | yes | for version 1 code: polls only while the answer is `queued` or `in_progress` |
| `end()` | yes | deletes the conversation |
| `retrieve()` | yes | does nothing (version 1 code) |
| `text()` | no | the text of the last answer (`response_text`) |
| `listMessages()` | no | the items of the conversation stored on OpenAI |
| `uploadAssistantFiles($specified_paths = [])` | no | uploads files, adds them to the vector store (creates it when there is none), returns their ids |
| `deleteAssistantFile($file_id)` | no | removes a file from the store and deletes it on OpenAI; `true` when deleted |
| `delete()` | no | deletes the vector store: `true` when deleted (otherwise the assistant itself) |

### Properties

| Property | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `name`, `description`, `instructions`, `tools`, `metadata` | the settings (public: change them after creation) |
| `file_ids`, `file_paths`, `vector_store_id` | the files and their store |
| `thread_id` | the conversation id (`conv_...`): set it to continue a conversation |
| `run_id` | the last answer id (`resp_...`) |
| `status` | the last answer's status: `completed`, `failed`, `incomplete`... |
| `messages` | the messages of this object: `['id', 'role', 'content' => [['type' => 'input_text'|'output_text', 'text']]]` |
| `response_text` | the text of the last answer |
| `last_response` | the last raw answer from OpenAI, with `error.message` when it failed |
| `assistant_id` | not used (version 1) |
## <a name="migrating"></a>Migrating from version 1

| Version 1 (Assistants API) | Version 2 (Responses + Conversations) |
|---|---|
| `new Assistant([...])` created an assistant on OpenAI | nothing is created: the settings live in the object |
| `assistant_id` | not used: keep the name, instructions, model and tools in your code |
| thread (`thread_id`) | conversation (`thread_id` holds the `conv_...` id) |
| run (`run_id`) | response (`run_id` holds the `resp_...` id) |
| `run()` then `retrieveResponse()` | `run()` returns with the answer; `retrieveResponse()` only waits for background answers |
| `messages` held thread messages (`content[0]['text']['value']`) | `['role', 'content' => [['type', 'text']]]`; use `text()` for the last answer |
| files attached to the assistant | files indexed in a vector store (`vector_store_id`) |
| `retrieval` tool | `file_search` (`retrieval` is still accepted and converted) |

Threads of version 1 can no longer be read. To keep a history, send the stored messages with `createMessage()` before
the first `run()` of a new conversation.
## Other ways

**With the conversation in the session.** `$assistant->start()->createMessage('Hi')->run()->text()` works in a web-only
capability ([`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action)) or a controller you keep, with the conversation id kept in the session. It
serves that one route only, and a REST client or an agent has no session: keep the assistant in a capability and pass the
conversation id, as above.

**Plain chat without OpenAI's memory.** `OpenAI::delegate()` with the earlier messages in `$context` (see the
[OpenAI page](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.4-OpenAI:-ChatGPT,-GPTs,-DALL.E)) keeps the history
on your side, without conversations or files on OpenAI.
## Common mistakes

+ **Expecting the answer in `messages[...]['content'][0]['text']['value']`** (version 1). Use `text()`.
+ **Polling in a loop after `run()`.** `run()` already waits for the answer.
+ **Uploading the files on every question.** Upload once (`index_catalog`), keep the `vector_store_id`, pass it next time.
+ **`alpha_dash` for the conversation id.** In GUMP it refuses digits: use `alpha_numeric_dash`.
+ **Trusting a conversation id from anyone.** Anyone who has an id can continue that conversation: ids are long and
  random, but do not put secrets in a conversation that several people share.
+ **A missing key.** `start()` leaves `thread_id` empty and `run()` ends with `status` `failed`: check them, and run
  `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only openai`.

+ [Open source agents (Llama, Mistral...)](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.6-Open-Source-Agents-(llama,-Mistral-etc.))

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.1-Creating-Bots-with-Watson -->

A **bot** is a chat window where people talk to an assistant in plain language. Caligrafy connects to
[IBM watsonx Assistant](https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/assistant/assistant-v2): you design the conversation (intents,
answers, choices) in IBM's interface, and Caligrafy gives you the chat app (a small Vue 3 app in `public/<name>`) and
the server side (`Caligrafy\Watson`), which keeps your key on the server. In the Bookshelf example, the help desk
answers questions such as opening hours and loans: people use it in the chat window, and the capability `ask_helpdesk`
gives the same answers to pages, the REST API and AI agents.

You need an [IBM Cloud account](https://cloud.ibm.com/registration) with a watsonx Assistant on the **Plus plan or
higher** (the v2 API that Caligrafy uses needs it).
> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Creating Bots with Caligrafy](https://youtu.be/TVajzJIDwfA)
>
> The video shows how Caligrafy connects to IBM Watson to build your own bot.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app bot helpdesk
```

Claude checks the name, runs `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php bot helpdesk`, and tells you the address to open
(`/bot/helpdesk?botSkillId=<assistant id>`) and the `.env` settings to fill. To reach the same assistant from pages,
REST and agents, ask for a capability too:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability ask_helpdesk ai:use read-only
Ask the watsonx help desk one question and return its text answer.
```

**Check**
- `WATSON_API_KEY`, `WATSON_URL` and `WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID` are in `.env`; `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only watson` says OK.
- The chat page answers your first message; without `?botSkillId=` it says *No assistant here: add ?botSkillId=<assistant id> to the address of this page.*
- The bot's script calls the data routes with `apiHeaders()` (the session and its CSRF token), never an API key.
## By hand

Run the commands in the project folder of the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart).
Without Docker (Composer with MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP), run the same commands without `docker compose exec dev-box` and
open your own address.

### Step 1: Create the assistant on IBM Cloud

In watsonx Assistant, create an assistant and build its conversation (try it in IBM's preview first). Then collect:

+ the **API key** and the **instance URL** (IBM Cloud > your Assistant service > Service credentials):
  `https://api.<region>.assistant.watson.cloud.ibm.com/instances/<instance_id>`;
+ the **assistant id** and, for recent assistants, the **environment id** (Assistant settings, or Environments >
  API details).

### Step 2: Add the settings

Open `.env` and fill the Watson lines (add `WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID`, which is not in `.env.example`):

```text
WATSON_API_KEY=...
WATSON_URL=https://api.us-south.assistant.watson.cloud.ibm.com/instances/<instance_id>
WATSON_ENVIRONMENT_ID=
WATSON_API_VERSION=2024-08-25
WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID=<assistant id>
```

`WATSON_URL` has no `/v2` at the end: Caligrafy adds the path. Run:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only watson
```

Expected: `OK    Watson: key and assistant accepted ...` (with `WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID` it opens and closes a test session).

### Step 3: Create the chat app

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php bot helpdesk
```

Expected:

```text
 Project created in the public folder.
 Type cd public/helpdesk to access it anytime
```

It copies `framework/plugins/bot` to `public/helpdesk`: `index.php` (the chat markup) and `scripts/main.js` (the Vue
app); the style is `public/css/bot.css`. The template's `application/config/routing/web.php` already serves it, with one
page line and three data lines that name the example controllers. Since 2.21.0 they are two lines (replace them, or leave
them: they do the same):

```php
// BOT PAGE ROUTE: a botSkillId is given in the URL, for example ?botSkillId=62196ce3-0b22-4aea-b2f2-d39730c03797
Route::page('/bot/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index', 'botSkillId']]);

// BOT DATA ROUTES: POST /__bots__/{appName}/communicate, POST /__bots__/{appName}/{appId}, DELETE /__bots__/{appName}
Route::bots();
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/bot/helpdesk?botSkillId=<assistant id>`. The chat says *Hi there!*; type a message and
press **Go**: the assistant's answer appears below it. Without `?botSkillId=`, or when the assistant cannot be reached
(wrong URL, key or plan), the chat says so under *Hi there!*.

### Step 4: The same assistant for pages, REST and agents

The chat app keeps a Watson session in the PHP session, which only a browser has. For one question at a time, from any
channel, write a capability:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/AskHelpdesk --scope ai:use --read-only
```

Replace **`application/services/Bookshelf/AskHelpdesk.php`** with:

```php
<?php
/**
 * AskHelpdesk: one question to the watsonx Assistant of the bookshelf
 */

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;
use Caligrafy\Watson;

#[Capability(
    name: 'ask_helpdesk',
    description: 'Asks the bookshelf help desk (a watsonx Assistant) one question. Returns {answer, replies}: the text, and every reply as Watson sent it.',
    scope: 'ai:use',
    readOnly: true
)]
class AskHelpdesk extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'question' => 'required|max_len,2000',
    );

    public $filters = array(
        'question' => 'trim',
    );

    public $descriptions = array(
        'question' => 'The question for the help desk',
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if (!defined('WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID') || WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID === '') {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('The help desk is not set up: add WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID to .env');
        }

        try {
            $watson = new Watson(WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID);   // opens a session (WATSON_URL, WATSON_API_KEY)
        } catch (Exception $e) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict('Watson could not be reached: ' . $e->getMessage());
        }

        $replies = $watson->communicate($input['question'])->getResponse() ?? array();
        $watson->closeSession();

        $texts = array();
        foreach ($replies as $reply) {
            if (($reply['response_type'] ?? '') === 'text') {
                $texts[] = $reply['text'];
            }
        }

        return array('answer' => implode("\n", $texts), 'replies' => $replies);
    }
}
```

Each call opens a session, sends the question and closes the session, so the assistant does not remember earlier
questions here. Run:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call ask_helpdesk question="When are you open?"
```

Expected (the text is your assistant's):

```json
{
    "data": {
        "answer": "We are open from 9 to 6, Monday to Saturday.",
        "replies": [
            {
                "response_type": "text",
                "text": "We are open from 9 to 6, Monday to Saturday."
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

With `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` and `Route::mcp('/mcp')` in `web.php`, it is also
`POST /capabilities/ask_helpdesk` and the agent tool `ask_helpdesk`. A page shows it with a form, as on the
[OpenAI page](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.4-OpenAI:-ChatGPT,-GPTs,-DALL.E):
`Route::form('/helpdesk', 'ask_helpdesk', ['success' => '/helpdesk', 'back' => '/helpdesk', 'flash' => '{answer}'])`.

**Check**
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only watson` is OK.
- The chat at `/bot/helpdesk?botSkillId=<assistant id>` answers.
- `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call ask_helpdesk question=Hi` answers `data`; with `WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID` empty it answers
  `conflict`, *The help desk is not set up: add WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID to .env*.
## Reference

### `Caligrafy\Watson`

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `new Watson($watson_assistant_id, $environment_id = null)` | opens a session; `$environment_id` defaults to `WATSON_ENVIRONMENT_ID`. Throws without `WATSON_URL` (*Set WATSON_URL to your watsonx Assistant instance URL...*) or when no session opens (*The session could not be initialized*) |
| `communicate($messageText, $skillVariables = null)` | sends a message; `$skillVariables` (an array) are the context variables of the main skill. Returns the object |
| `getResponse()` | the replies of the last message (the `output.generic` list) |
| `getLastExchange()` | the last turn: `['turn_count', 'user', 'response']` |
| `getConversation()` | every turn, by turn number |
| `getExchangeAt($turnCount)` | one turn, or `[]` |
| `getContext()`, `getSkillVariables()`, `getContextVariable($variable)` | the context Watson returned, its user-defined variables, one of them |
| `getSessionId()` | the session id |
| `closeSession()` | deletes the session on Watson |

`getResponse()` and `getLastExchange()` take the last turn **out** of the log: call one of them once per message.

Requests go to `{WATSON_URL}/v2/assistants/{assistant_id}[/environments/{environment_id}]/sessions...?version={WATSON_API_VERSION}`
with the key as `apikey` basic authentication.

### `.env`

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| `WATSON_API_KEY` | none: required |
| `WATSON_URL` | none: required, the instance URL without `/v2` |
| `WATSON_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | none: sessions are created on the assistant itself |
| `WATSON_API_VERSION` | `2024-08-25` |
| `WATSON_ASSISTANT_ID` | none: read by `doctor` and by your own code (the capability above) |

### Replies

| `response_type` | What the chat app does |
|---|---|
| `text` | shows `text`, then waits for typed input |
| `option` | shows `title` and one button per option (`label`; the value sent is `value.input.text`) |
| `image` | shows the image (`source`, `title`) |
| `pause` | when the context has an `action` and the page defines `window.executeBotAction(context)`, shows the `text` it returns and sends its `variables` with the next answer |

### The chat app

`public/<name>/scripts/main.js` keeps the conversation (`messages`) and what the bot waits for (`action`: a `text`
input or `button` options) and calls the data routes with axios and `{ headers: apiHeaders() }`:

| Route | Body | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST __bots__/<name>/<assistant id>` | `{}` | `true` once the session is open (kept in the PHP session) |
| `POST __bots__/<name>/communicate` | `{text, variables?}` | `{action_success: true, response: [replies], context: {variables}}` |
| `DELETE __bots__/<name>` | | closes the session |

Messages are always shown as text, never as HTML. To change the look, edit `public/<name>/index.php` and keep the ids
and Vue bindings; the page route can be any path that ends with the app name, and `?app=<file>` opens another
`public/<name>/<file>.php` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`).
## Under the hood

`Route::bots()` declares the three data routes on the example controller `Caligrafy\Controllers\WatsonController`
(`application/controllers/core/AI/WatsonController.php`): `connect()` creates `new Watson($appId)` and keeps it,
serialized, in the session; `communicate()` sends the text and the variables and answers the replies and the context;
`end()` closes the session. The conversation lives in the PHP session, which only the browser has. Everything else (one
question from a page, REST or an agent) goes through a capability such as `ask_helpdesk`.
## Common mistakes

+ **`WATSON_URL` with `/v2` at the end**, or the URL of the IBM Cloud dashboard instead of the instance URL.
+ **A Lite plan.** The v2 API needs Plus or higher: sessions are refused.
+ **No `?botSkillId=` in the page address.** The chat cannot connect.
+ **An old bot client that sends the API key.** Since 2.7.0 the client sends `apiHeaders()`; a bot that sends the key
  gets `[ERROR 1004] Access Denied` once `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` (Caligrafy Cloud). Copy `framework/plugins/bot/scripts/main.js` again.
+ **A bot folder name that is reserved**: `app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`,
  `ml`, `resources`, `uploads`.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.3-Machine-Learning -->

**ML Core** brings machine learning to the browser: it detects body poses in a camera, learns from pictures, and
trains small neural networks of your own. It is a JavaScript class, `MlCore` (`public/js/services/mlcore.js`), built
on [ml5.js](https://docs.ml5js.org) 1.4 (itself on TensorFlow.js), with [p5.js](https://p5js.org/reference/) 2.x for
drawing and controls. Everything runs in the browser: nothing is sent to your server unless your code sends it.

In the Bookshelf example, a page learns how many hours a book takes to read from its number of pages.
> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Creating and training an AI with Caligrafy](https://youtu.be/hBSWkaaBbNM)
>
> The video builds neural networks and computer vision with Caligrafy to detect people and objects and to predict outcomes.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app ml reading
```

Claude checks the name, runs `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ml reading` and gives you the addresses of the four example pages.
Then describe what to learn: *"a page that learns the reading time of a book from its number of pages"*.

**Check**
- The page loads ml5 (and p5 when it draws) before `mlcore.js`, as the scaffolded pages do.
- A page without a camera gives `media: 'none'`: a `<video id="video">` without a source starts the camera.
- Callbacks take `(results, error)`, in that order (ml5 1.x).
## By hand

Run the commands in the project folder of the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart).
Without Docker (Composer with MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP), run the same commands without `docker compose exec dev-box` and
open your own address.

### Step 2: Try the examples

| Address | Example | Pattern |
|---|---|---|

| `http://localhost:8080/ml/reading?app=posedetector` | learns poses you label with the buttons, then names them | learning with a person |

### Step 3: Your own neural network

Create **`public/reading/readingtime.php`** (opened with `?app=readingtime`):

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
        <title>Reading time</title>
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/tokens.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/layout.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/look.css';?>">
        <script src="https://unpkg.com/ml5@1.4.0/dist/ml5.min.js"></script>
    </head>
    <body class="cq-site">
        <section class="cq-hero cq-hero--page">
            <h1 class="cq-display">Reading time</h1>
        </section>
        <section class="cq-band cq-band--tight">
            <div class="cq-inner cq-inner--narrow">
                <p id="status" class="cq-note">Training...</p>
                <form id="guess" method="POST">
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="pages">Pages</label>
                        <input id="pages" class="form-control" type="number" name="pages" min="1" value="350" required>
                    </div>
                    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit" disabled>Guess</button>
                </form>
                <p id="answer" class="cq-lead"></p>
            </div>
        </section>

        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
        <script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'mlcore.js'; ?>"></script>
        <script>loadVue({ scripts: ['readingtime'] });</script>
    </body>
</html>
```

`loadVue({ scripts: [...] })` adds `public/reading/scripts/<name>.js` to the page. Create
**`public/reading/scripts/readingtime.js`**:

```js
// A neural network that learns the hours a book takes to read from its number of pages (regression)
const myMl = new MlCore({
    media: 'none',    // no camera: the page has no <video id="video">
    canvas: 'none',
    brain: { type: 'neuralnetwork', options: { inputs: ['pages'], outputs: ['hours'], task: 'regression' } }
});

const status = document.getElementById('status');
const form = document.getElementById('guess');
const answer = document.getElementById('answer');

myMl.ready.then(() => {
    // the examples: pages read -> hours it took
    [[120, 3], [200, 5], [300, 7.5], [400, 10], [500, 12.5], [640, 16]]
        .forEach(([pages, hours]) => myMl.brain.addData({ pages: pages }, { hours: hours }));
    myMl.brain.normalizeData();
    myMl.brain.train({ epochs: 60 }, () => {
        status.textContent = 'Trained on 6 books.';
        form.querySelector('button').disabled = false;
    });
});

form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const pages = Number(form.elements.pages.value);
    myMl.brain.predict({ pages: pages }, (results, error) => {
        answer.textContent = error ? 'No guess: ' + error : 'About ' + results[0].value.toFixed(1) + ' hours';
    });
});
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/ml/reading?app=readingtime`. *Training...* becomes *Trained on 6 books.* after a few
seconds and **Guess** turns on. Click it: *About 8.7 hours* (the number varies a little from one training to the next).
Training pauses while the browser tab is hidden.

To keep what a network learned, `myMl.brain.save('reading')` downloads its files (the model `.json`, its
`_meta.json` and its `.weights.bin`); put them in `public/reading/resources/` and load them with
`myMl.brain.load(<the address of the model .json>, callback)` instead of training. To keep data on
the server (the readers' own reading times, for example), send it to a capability with the
[JS client](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#client).

**Check**
- The four example addresses open (with the camera allowed, the pose page draws on you).
- `?app=readingtime` shows *Trained on 6 books.* and a guess.
- The browser console has no errors.
## Reference

### `new MlCore(settings)`

| Setting | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `media` | `'video'` | the id of the `<video>` or `<img>`; a `<video>` without `src` starts the camera |
| `canvas` | `'canvas'` | the id of the drawing canvas |
| `brain` | `{ type: 'neuralnetwork', options: { inputs: 34, outputs: 2, debug: true, task: 'classification' } }` | the brain (below) |
| `filter` | `false` | `true`: keeps only the person and removes the background (ml5 `bodySegmentation`) |
| `hideVideo` | `false` | hides the video under the drawing |
| `backend` | `'webgl'` | the TensorFlow.js backend of the neural networks |

| `brain.type` | What it is | `brain.options` |
|---|---|---|
| `neuralnetwork` | an ml5 neural network | `inputs`, `outputs` (numbers or names), `task` (`classification` or `regression`), `debug`... |
| `featureextractor` | MobileNet, retrained on your labeled pictures | `epochs`, `batchSize` (for training); `version`, `alpha`, `task` (for MobileNet) |

`myMl.ready` is a promise that resolves when the brain and the camera are ready; `myMl.brain` is the ml5 object.

### Body poses

```js
var myMl = new MlCore();
myMl.detect((myMl) => {
    myMl.drawKeypoints(myMl);   // the 17 points
    myMl.drawSkeleton(myMl);    // the lines between them
    // myMl.poses: the poses of this frame
});
myMl.stopDetection();
```

`detect(callback, ...args)` runs ml5 `bodyPose` (MoveNet) on the media and calls `callback(myMl, ...args)` at every
frame. Each pose of `myMl.poses` has both shapes, scaled to the canvas:

```js
let pose = myMl.poses[0];
pose.keypoints        // 17 keypoints {x, y, confidence, name}: nose, left_eye, right_eye, left_ear, right_ear,
                      // left_shoulder, right_shoulder, left_elbow, right_elbow, left_wrist, right_wrist,
                      // left_hip, right_hip, left_knee, right_knee, left_ankle, right_ankle
pose.nose             // {x, y, confidence}, the same for every name
pose.box              // the box around the person
pose.pose.keypoints   // the earlier shape: [{part: 'leftEye', position: {x, y}, score}, ...]
pose.pose.leftEye     // camelCase names
pose.skeleton         // [[keypointA, keypointB], ...] for the visible connections
```

### Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `drawKeypoints(myMl)`, `drawSkeleton(myMl)` | draw the pose |
| `drawFeature(myMl, ['nose', 'left_eye'])` | draw some keypoints (snake_case or camelCase names) |
| `addData(myMl, label)` | body poses: adds the 34 coordinates of the current pose with a label |
| `addImage(myMl, label)` | feature extractor: adds the current frame with a label |
| `train(myMl, options = {})` | trains (`{ epochs, batchSize }`), then classifies continuously |
| `classify(myMl)` | classifies the current pose or frame; the best label is in `myMl.brain.results`, e.g. `Happy (93)%` |
| `save(name, callback, myMl)`, `load(fileOrPath, callback, myMl)` | download the model, load a saved one |
| `toP5(myMl)` | hands the canvas to p5 (call it in `setup()`): `draw()` then runs at every frame |
| `startStream()` | starts the camera (called by the constructor for a `<video>` without a source) |

On a neural network you can call ml5 directly: `myMl.brain.addData(inputs, outputs)`, `normalizeData()`,
`train(options, callback)`, `classify(input, (results, error) => ...)` (classification: `results[0].label`,
`results[0].confidence`), `predict(input, (results, error) => ...)` (regression: `results[0].value`), `save()`, `load()`.

### Drawing with p5

```js
function setup() {
    myMl.toP5(myMl);            // p5 now draws on the canvas
}

function draw() {               // runs only after toP5()
    if (myMl.poses.length > 0) {
        let nose = myMl.poses[0].nose;
        fill(255, 0, 0);
        ellipse(nose.x, nose.y, 50);
    }
}
```

p5 2.x has no `preload()`: use `async function setup()` to wait for something. Its DOM functions (`createButton`,
`createElement`) are part of p5 itself.

### Scripts of a page

```html
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/p5.js/2.3.4/p5.min.js"></script>   <!-- when the page draws -->
<script src="https://unpkg.com/ml5@1.4.0/dist/ml5.min.js"></script>
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
<script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'mlcore.js'; ?>"></script>
<script>loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] });</script>
```

The camera pages fill the screen (`public/css/camera.css`, 2.11.0+): the video and the canvas share one size
(640 x 480), the title and messages float at the top (`.cq-camera-top`, `#infobar`), the buttons at the bottom
(`.cq-camera-bottom`, `#apps`). See [the FaceDetect screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition#facedetect-markup-components).
## Common mistakes

+ **ml5 0.x code.** ML Core 2.0 follows ml5 1.x: `poseNet` became `bodyPose`, callbacks are `(results, error)`, models
  load asynchronously (wait for `myMl.ready`).
+ **`preload()` with p5 2.x.** It no longer exists.
+ **A page without a camera that keeps `<video id="video">`.** It asks for the camera: remove it and give `media: 'none'`.
+ **Training in a hidden tab.** The browser pauses it until the tab is visible again.
+ **An app folder with a reserved name**: `app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`, `ml`,
  `resources`, `uploads`.

+ [ml5.js reference](https://docs.ml5js.org) and [p5.js reference](https://p5js.org/reference/)
