<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.7-Phone-and-Tablet-Apps -->

A Caligrafy project can have its own **iOS and Android app** (Caligrafy Quill 2.27.0+): the same capabilities as its
web pages, REST API and AI agents, on a phone or a tablet, signed in with the same accounts and reached by the same
notifications. One command creates it, one line of `web.php` lets people sign in to it, and the store builds go to
TestFlight and Google Play from a Mac or from GitHub.

With Claude Code, `/caligrafy-quill:mobile` does all of it, and walks you through the Apple and Google accounts. Step
by step: the course's [lesson 18](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/18-Bookshelf-in-the-Stores)
turns Bookshelf into an iOS and Android app.

## What it is made of

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `php caligrafer.php mobile <name>` | Creates `public/<name>`: a Vue app (Vite, Vue Router, Caligrafy's look) that [Capacitor](https://capacitorjs.com) 8 wraps into an Xcode project (`ios/`) and an Android Studio project (`android/`) |
| `Route::mobile([...])` | People sign in to the app through the site's own sign-in page; the app gets a token of that person and calls the capabilities with it |
| `Notify::user()` | The notifications you already send reach the person's iPhones, iPads and Android phones too |
| `fastlane/Fastfile`, `.github/workflows/mobile-<name>.yml` | The store builds: iOS to TestFlight, Android to the internal testing track of Google Play |

The app is never a second backend: every screen reads and writes through the project's capabilities, as the person
signed in, under the same rules (scopes, levels, validation) as the web pages, REST and MCP.

## Create it

Node.js 22+ on your computer (the Docker server has none), then at the root of the project (from the Docker server,
`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php mobile ...` with `--id` and `--url`, then the `npm` and `npx cap` lines
it prints, on your computer):

```bash
php caligrafer.php mobile bingo --id com.holidaybingo.app --display "Holiday Bingo" --url https://holidaybingo.caligrafy.com
```

+ `--id`: the app id. It is the bundle id of iOS, the package of Android and the address the sign-in returns to the
  app through. Lowercase letters and digits in two or more parts separated by dots (no `-` or `_`). It cannot change
  once the app is in a store. Default: `com.<project folder>.<name>`.
+ `--display`: the name under the icon (30 characters). Default: the folder's name.
+ `--url`: the site the store builds call. Default: `APP_URL` when it is https, else `https://<project folder>.caligrafy.com`.

It installs the packages, adds the iOS and Android projects, sets up their sign-in address and notifications, makes the
icons from the Caligrafy mark (replace `assets/icon-only.png` and run `npm run icons`), and writes the GitHub workflow.

## Sign people in

In `application/config/routing/web.php`, after `Route::auth()` and `Route::capabilities()`:

```php
Route::auth(['home' => '/']);
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');
Route::mobile(['scheme' => 'com.holidaybingo.app']);
```

1. The app opens `https://<site>/mobile/authorize` in the phone's browser.
2. The person signs in on the site's own page, or creates an account, then allows the app on that device.
3. The site sends them back to the app with a one-time code. The app trades the code for a personal access token of
   that person: "Mobile: Maya's iPhone" in the tokens list.

A project without accounts (2.27.2+) keeps the same line: it then declares no sign-in address and only lets its apps
call the public capabilities, with no sign-in and no token.

The app never sees a password. The exchange is protected with PKCE, so a code is useless to any other app that
intercepts it. Signing out of the app revokes the token.

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scheme` | (required) | The app id (or a list of ids, one per app) |
| `scopes` | `['*']` | What the app may call. `['*']` is whatever the person may do; narrow it with `['books:read', 'books:write']` |
| `days` | `90` | How long the app stays signed in |
| `origins` | `[]` | Other origins allowed to call with a token (the app's own are always allowed) |
| `name` | `APP_NAME` | The app's name on the consent page |

The routes: `GET`/`POST /mobile/authorize`, `POST /mobile/token`, `GET /mobile/session`, `POST /mobile/signout`.

## Build its screens

`src/components/pages/` and `src/router/index.js`. A page reads and writes through `call()`:

```js
import { call } from '../../mobile/session.js'

const books = await call('list_books', { page: 1 })
try {
  await call('create_book', { title: this.title })
} catch (error) {
  this.errors = error.fields      // { title: 'The Title field is required' }
}
```

`currentUser()`, `signIn()`, `signOut()` and `onSessionChange()` come from the same file. A `webOnly: true` capability
needs the browser's session, so the app cannot call it: give the app a capability of its own.

```bash
npm run dev        # in a browser, against the Docker server (sign-in works the same, on this computer only)
npm run ios        # a development build, then Xcode: run it on an iPhone simulator
npm run android    # the same in Android Studio: an Android emulator
```

These development builds call your local site (`.env.development`, `http://localhost:8080`): the iPhone simulator
reaches it at `localhost`, the Android emulator at `10.0.2.2` (the app switches by itself), and plain http is allowed
to this computer's addresses only. The store builds, `npm run release:ios` and `npm run release:android`, call the site
online (`.env.production`, https); the workflow and fastlane use them. To try the app on a real phone, use a release
build against the site online.

Tested on an iPhone 18 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2) and a Pixel emulator (Android 16): sign-in through the site, the
return to the app, a restart, notifications turned on and shown, and sign-out.

## Notifications

The `Notify::user($id, ['title' => ..., 'body' => ..., 'url' => ...])` you send for the browsers and email
([Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)) reaches the phones once the person turns them
on in the app (`enablePush()`), with these settings on the site:

| Setting | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `APNS_KEY`, `APNS_KEY_ID`, `APNS_TEAM_ID` | Apple Developer, Keys: a key with Apple Push Notifications service (the `.p8` text, or that text in base64), its id, your team id |
| `APNS_TOPIC` | The app id |
| `APNS_ENVIRONMENT` | `sandbox` while you run the app from Xcode; leave it out for TestFlight and the App Store |
| `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Firebase console, Project settings, Service accounts: the private key's JSON (or that JSON in base64) |

In the app: the Push Notifications capability in Xcode (Signing & Capabilities, once), and
`android/app/google-services.json` from Firebase for Android. Check with `php caligrafer.php notify status <user id>`
and `php caligrafer.php notify test <user id>`. Online, set them with `php caligrafer.php cloud secret set <app> NAME=value`.

## Publish it

What you do once, as the owner of the accounts:

1. **Apple**: the [Apple Developer Program](https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/) (99 USD a year), the app in
   App Store Connect, and an App Store Connect API key with the Admin role. Xcode signs the builds with that key:
   there is no certificate or provisioning profile to keep.
2. **Google**: a [Google Play developer account](https://play.google.com/console/signup) (25 USD once), the app in
   Play Console, an upload key (`keytool`), and a service account allowed to release. Google needs the first build
   uploaded by hand. A new personal account must also run a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days before its first
   production release.
3. **The secrets of the repository** (GitHub, Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions): `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `ASC_KEY_ID`,
   `ASC_ISSUER_ID`, `ASC_KEY_P8`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`,
   `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD`, `PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` and, for Android notifications, `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON`. The README of
   `public/<name>` says where each one comes from.

Then each release: change `version` in `public/<name>/package.json`, push, and run the workflow (`/caligrafy-quill:ship`
does it, or `gh workflow run mobile-<name>.yml -f platform=both`). iOS arrives in TestFlight, Android on the internal
testing track; you send it to review from App Store Connect and Play Console. On a Mac with Xcode, the same lanes run
locally: `bundle exec fastlane ios beta`, `bundle exec fastlane android beta`.

Before the first review: Apple asks an app with accounts to let people delete their account inside the app, a
privacy policy address and the privacy labels; both stores ask for screenshots.


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.8-Languages -->

A Caligrafy project can speak several languages (Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0+): its pages, its form messages and its
numbers, dates and amounts follow each visitor's language, and Arabic, Hebrew or Persian pages are laid out right to
left. One file per language holds the app's words; one setting lists the languages.

## What it is made of

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `APP_LOCALES=en,fr,ar` in `.env` | The app's languages, in order. Empty means English only |
| `APP_LOCALE=en` | The language of a visitor who asks for none. Empty means the first of `APP_LOCALES` |
| `application/lang/<code>.json` | The words of one language, as nested objects: `{"home": {"title": "Good food"}}` is the key `home.title` |
| `t('home.title')` in a view | The word in the visitor's language |
| `html(lang=locale(), dir=lang_dir())` | The page's language and direction: `rtl` for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and a few others |
| `lang_url('fr')` | This page in another language, for a language menu |
| `Caligrafy\Lang` | The same in PHP, plus `money()`, `number()` and `date()` in each language's way |

The master layouts of a new project (`site.pug`, `layout.pug`) already set `lang` and `dir`, and Caligrafy's
stylesheets use logical properties, so a right-to-left page mirrors by itself.

## The files

`application/lang/en.json`:

```json
{
  "home": {
    "title": "Good food. Better hours.",
    "hello": "Hello {name}"
  },
  "tables_left": "{count} table left|{count} tables left",
  "fields": { "email": "Email" },
  "validation": { "required": "Please fill in {field}" }
}
```

`application/lang/ar.json`:

```json
{
  "home": { "title": "أكل طيّب، بأوقات أحلى", "hello": "أهلاً {name}" },
  "tables_left": "بقيت طاولة واحدة|بقي {count} طاولات",
  "fields": { "email": "البريد الإلكتروني" },
  "validation": { "required": "الحقل {field} مطلوب", "valid_email": "{field} غير صالح" }
}
```

- `{name}` is replaced by the variable of that name: `t('home.hello', ['name' => $user->name])`.
- With a `count`, `"one|other"` or `"zero|one|other"` picks the form: `t('tables_left', ['count' => 3])`.
- A word missing in a language shows in `APP_LOCALE`'s language, then as its key: a page never shows nothing.
- `php caligrafer.php doctor` says when a language has no file, a file is not valid JSON, or words are missing.

## The visitor's language

In this order:

1. `?lang=fr` in the address: used, and remembered in the cookie `lang` for a year.
2. The cookie `lang`, from an earlier visit.
3. The browser's languages (`Accept-Language`): `fr-CA` matches `fr`.
4. `APP_LOCALE`.

Only the codes of `APP_LOCALES` are ever used. The command line, scheduled jobs and background jobs use `APP_LOCALE`;
a job that writes to a person in their language calls `Lang::set($person->language)` first.

A language menu:

```pug
nav.cq-lang
  each $code in locales()
    a(href=lang_url($code), aria-current=$code === locale() ? 'true' : null)= strtoupper($code)
```

## In a view

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block content
  section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
    h1.cq-display= t('home.title')
    p.cq-lead= t('tables_left', ['count' => $deal['tables_left']])
```

A page's script gets the words it needs as JSON, kept small with a prefix:

```pug
script window.LANG = !{lang_json('app')}
```

## Form messages

The capabilities' validator speaks the visitor's language when its library (GUMP) has it: French, Spanish, German,
Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Hebrew and others. It has no Arabic: put the messages in the file's
`validation` object, keyed by rule (`required`, `valid_email`, `max_len`, `min_len`...), with `{field}` and `{param}`.
Any message there replaces GUMP's, in every language. The `fields` object names the fields in each language.

## Money, numbers and dates

```php
use Caligrafy\Lang;

Lang::money(1234.5, 'USD');          // $1,234.50 in English, 1 234,50 $US in French
Lang::money(45, 'AED', 'ar');        // in Arabic numerals and its currency's way
Lang::number(1234.5, 1);             // 1,234.5 / 1 234,5
Lang::date('2026-11-25', 'long');    // November 25, 2026 / 25 novembre 2026
```

They use PHP's `intl` extension (in the Docker image); without it, plain `1,234.50 USD` and `25 Nov 2026`.

## Good to know

- Caligrafy's own pages (sign-in, sign-up, the welcome page) are in English: an app that needs them in other
  languages copies them into its views with `t()`. `Route::auth`'s `messages` option takes `t(...)` values.
- A project made before 2.28.0 keeps its own `site.pug`: change `html(lang="en")` to
  `html(lang=locale(), dir=lang_dir())` there.
- The helpers `t`, `locale`, `locales`, `lang_dir`, `lang_url` and `lang_json` are only defined when the app has not
  defined a function of the same name.


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.3-Metadata-%26-Social-Rich-Cards -->

When someone shares an address of your app on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Slack or iMessage, those apps show a **rich
card**: a title, a line of description and an image, read from the page's `og:` and `twitter:` meta tags. Every page
built on `default/master/site` prints the card of your app (2.16.2+); you set it once with `metadata()`, and a page can
have its own.
> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Creating Rich Cards with Caligrafy](https://youtu.be/qgzufCEcg_I)
>
> In this video, we show how we can create Rich Cards that give search engines, social media networks and collaboration tools the ability to have more information about your site, application or product from the URL alone.
## With Claude

```text
Give Bookshelf its social card: "Bookshelf: your books, lent and returned", and each book page its own title
```

Claude fills the `metadata(...)` call of `application/config/config.php` and, for a page of its own, sets `$metadata`
in that view.

**Check**

+ The page source of `/books` has `og:title`, `og:description` and `og:image`.
+ The image is 1200 by 630 and its address is a full `https://` address.
+ The card shows in [opengraph.xyz](https://www.opengraph.xyz/) once the app is online.
## By hand

**1. The card of the app.** In `application/config/config.php`, replace the commented `metadata(...)` example with:

```php
metadata(array(
    'site_name' => 'Bookshelf',
    'title' => 'Bookshelf: your books, lent and returned',
    'description' => 'Know who has your books and when they come back.',
    'image' => 'https://bookshelf.example.com/public/images/resources/social-card.png',
    'image_alt' => 'Bookshelf',
));
```

Put a 1200 by 630 image at `public/images/resources/social-card.png`.

**2. Look at it.** Open the source of any page of `default/master/site` (`/books`, `/login`...). The `head` has, among the
image size, its `alt` and the other `twitter:` lines:

```text
<meta name="description" content="Know who has your books and when they come back."/>
<meta property="og:type" content="website"/>
<meta property="og:site_name" content="Bookshelf"/>
<meta property="og:title" content="Bookshelf: your books, lent and returned"/>
<meta property="og:description" content="Know who has your books and when they come back."/>
<meta property="og:image" content="https://bookshelf.example.com/public/images/resources/social-card.png"/>
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image"/>
```

With `APP_URL` set (Caligrafy Cloud sets it), `og:url` is that address plus the page's path.

**3. A card per book.** Each book page shows its own title and summary. It uses the Bookshelf page of one book
(`application/views/Bookshelf/book.pug`, [lesson 04](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/04-Your-First-Capabilities)
of the course), whose route in `application/config/routing/web.php` gives it `$book` (`get_book`: the book with its
`author` nested) and `$authors` (`list_authors`):

```php
    Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book', 'authors' => 'list_authors'], 'notFound' => 'Bookshelf/notfound']);
```

In `application/views/Bookshelf/book.pug`, make the first block set `$metadata` (the layout's `head` reads it):

```pug
block title
    - $metadata = array('title' => $book['title'] . ' on Bookshelf', 'description' => $book['summary']) + (array) metadata()
    = $book['title'] . ' · Bookshelf'
```

Leave the rest of the view (its `block content`) as it is.

Open the source of `http://localhost:8080/books/3`: `<meta property="og:title" content="Kindred on Bookshelf"/>` and
`<meta name="description" content="A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland."/>`; the image and
the rest come from `metadata()`. `$metadata` set outside a block (below `extends`) is not seen by the layout.

**4. Share links.** To show *Share: Facebook X LinkedIn Pinterest* under a page, add `'site_url' =>
'https://bookshelf.example.com'` to the `metadata(...)` of step 1 (the address the links share), and replace the
page's footer:

```pug
block footer
  footer.cq-footer
    include ../default/modules/share
```

The links share `site_url`, the app's address, not the page's.

**5. Test the card online.** Platforms read the card from the internet: on your computer, use a tunnel such as
[ngrok](https://ngrok.com/), or try it once the app is online. Then paste the address in
[opengraph.xyz](https://www.opengraph.xyz/), the [Facebook debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/sharing/)
or the [LinkedIn post inspector](https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/). Platforms keep a card for days: after a
change, press **Scrape again** in Facebook's debugger. X has no validator any more: preview a post with the address.

**Check**

+ `og:title` and `og:image` are in the source of every page.
+ `/books/3` has its own title.
+ A debugger shows the image, the title and the domain.
## <a name="card"></a>Reference: the card

`metadata(array $pairs)` keeps the pairs for the request (in the session) and returns them all; `metadata()` returns
them. A `null` value is ignored. `default/modules/metadata.pug` prints the card from the view's `$metadata`, else from
`metadata()`, and prints nothing without a `title`.

| Key | Becomes | |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `og:title`, `twitter:title` | Required |
| `description` | `description`, `og:description`, `twitter:description` | Under 125 characters; X and LinkedIn do not show it |
| `image` | `og:image`, `twitter:image` (a large card) | A full address, 1200x630 |
| `image_width`, `image_height` | `og:image:width`, `og:image:height` | `1200` and `630` by default |
| `image_alt` | `og:image:alt`, `twitter:image:alt` | What the image shows |
| `site_name` | `og:site_name` | |
| `site_url` | `og:url`: this address plus the page's path; the address the share links share | `APP_URL` by default |

X and LinkedIn show only the image, the title and the domain: say what the app does in the title.

**`$metadata` in a view also prints a product block.** When a view of `site.pug` has `$metadata`, the layout adds
`default/modules/metadata_body.pug` to the page: hidden schema.org `Product` data (name, description, image, a price from
`amount`, `0.00` by default, a rating from `ratingValue` and `reviewCount`). It is meant for a page that sells one
product; give those keys their real values on such a page.

| Module | |
|---|---|
| `default/modules/metadata.pug` | the card, in the `head` of `site.pug` |
| `default/modules/metadata_body.pug` | the schema.org `Product` data, when the view has `$metadata` |
| `default/modules/share.pug` | share links for the footer of `site.pug` pages |
| `default/modules/social.pug` | share links of the older `layout.pug` |
## Other ways

**A controller you keep** passes the card to its view: `view('Bookshelf/book', array('book' => $book, 'authors' =>
$authors, 'metadata' => array('title' => $book['title']) + metadata()))`. `Route::page` and `$metadata` in the view replace it.

**The older masters** (`default/master/layoutblocks.pug`, `layout.pug`) print the card only when the view gets
`'metadata'`, and the share links when it also gets `'social' => true`:
`view('default/index', array('metadata' => metadata(), 'social' => true))`.
## Common mistakes

+ **No card at all.** `metadata()` has no `title`: nothing is printed without one.
+ **The image does not show.** The address is relative (`/public/...`) or the server is not reachable from the
  internet: use a full `https://` address of a server online.
+ **An old card keeps showing.** The platform kept it: *Scrape again* in Facebook's debugger.
+ **The per-page title is ignored.** `$metadata` was set outside a block: set it in the first block of the view.
+ **Share links share nothing.** `site_url` is not in `metadata()`.
## Related pages

+ [Search referencing and analytics](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.4-Search-Referencing-and-Analytics)
+ [Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)
+ [Routing: pages](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.4-Search-Referencing-and-Analytics -->

Search engines read three things Caligrafy helps with: the **description** of each page (the line under its title in
the results), the proof that the site is yours (**Google Search Console**), and, once people come, **Google
Analytics**. The description comes from `metadata()` ([rich cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.3-Metadata-&-Social-Rich-Cards));
analytics is one setting of `.env`.
## With Claude

```text
Make Bookshelf ready for Google: a description for every page, and Google Analytics with the id G-XXXXXXX in production
```

Claude sets the `description` of `metadata()` in `application/config/config.php` and tells you to put
`GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID` in the production `.env` (on Caligrafy Cloud: `php caligrafer.php cloud secret set <app>
GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID=G-...`). It does not sign in to Google for you.

**Check**

+ The page source has `<meta name="description" ...>`.
+ Online, with `APP_ENV=production`, the source has `googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-...`; locally it has none.
## By hand

**1. A description for every page.** Set `description` in the `metadata(...)` call of `application/config/config.php`
(the whole call is in [rich cards](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.3-Metadata-&-Social-Rich-Cards)):

```php
metadata(array(
    'site_name' => 'Bookshelf',
    'title' => 'Bookshelf: your books, lent and returned',
    'description' => 'Know who has your books and when they come back.',
));
```

Every page of `default/master/site` then has
`<meta name="description" content="Know who has your books and when they come back."/>`. A page gets its own
description as in [a card per book](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.3-Metadata-&-Social-Rich-Cards#card).

**2. Prove the site is yours to Google.** In [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console), add a
**URL prefix** property with the app's address (`https://bookshelf.example.com`) and choose **HTML file**. Download the
file Google gives (`google<code>.html`), put it at the **root of the project** (next to `index.php`), commit it and
deploy. Apache serves a file that exists as it is, so `https://bookshelf.example.com/google<code>.html` answers the
file; press **Verify**. A **Domain** property is verified with a DNS record at your domain's registrar instead.

**3. Google Analytics.** Create a Google Analytics property and copy its measurement id (`G-...`). In the `.env` of
the production server:

```text
APP_ENV=production
GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID=G-XXXXXXX
```

Every page of `default/master/site` then loads `https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-XXXXXXX`. With
`APP_ENV=local` the tag is never printed, so your own visits while you develop are not counted.

**Check**

+ The source of `/` has the description.
+ Search Console says *Ownership verified*.
+ Online, the source has the `gtag` script with your id; Analytics shows your visit in its real-time view.
## Reference

| What | Where it comes from | Printed by |
|---|---|---|
| `<meta name="description">` | `metadata()`'s `description`, or the view's `$metadata` | `default/modules/metadata.pug`, in every master |
| Google Analytics (`gtag`) | `GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID`, only with `APP_ENV=production` | `site.pug` always; `layoutblocks.pug` when the view gets `'google_analytics' => true` |
| `keywords()` | `keywords('books, lending')` | not printed in pages; given to Vue apps as `env.keywords` |
| Search Console proof | an HTML file at the root of the project, or DNS | Apache, as a file |

+ `keywords($value)` keeps a string of keywords for the request and returns it. Google ignores the `keywords` meta tag,
  so the masters do not print one.
+ The layouts print no `google-site-verification` meta tag: use the HTML file or DNS.
+ Files at the root of the project, such as `robots.txt` or a `sitemap.xml` you write, are served as they are, except
  dotfiles, `caligrafer.php`, `composer.*`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `package*.json` and `.sql`, `.log`, `.bak`, `.ini`,
  `.sh`, `.env` files, which `.htaccess` denies.
## Other ways

**The older masters.** A view on `default/master/layoutblocks.pug` gets analytics only when its route passes it:
`view('default/index', array('metadata' => metadata(), 'google_analytics' => true))`. Pages on `site.pug` need nothing.
## Common mistakes

+ **No analytics online.** `APP_ENV` is not `production`, or `GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID` is empty in the server's `.env`
  (on Caligrafy Cloud, set it with `cloud secret set`, then deploy). Since 2.26.2 `php caligrafer.php doctor` warns when
  the id is set and `APP_ENV` is not `production`, and when it is an old Universal Analytics id (`UA-`), which Google
  stopped collecting in 2023: use the `G-` id of a Google Analytics 4 web stream (G174).
+ **The verification file answers the app's 404.** It is in `public/` or `application/`: put it at the root of the
  project.
+ **Search results show an old description.** Google reads the page again on its own schedule: ask for a new crawl in
  Search Console (URL inspection).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online -->

You built your capabilities, pages and apps on your computer. This page puts the same project online: one production
image (the `Dockerfile` of every project), one command that prepares the database at each start
(`php caligrafer.php deploy`), and two ways to run it, [Caligrafy Cloud](#cloud) (`https://<name>.caligrafy.com`, a
free first half hour) or [your own server](#ownserver). Since Caligrafy Quill 2.4.0.

**Since 2.26.0** the production image tunes itself to its container (processes, database connections, preloading, a response cache): see [performance and deployment](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Performance-and-Deployment). An app that uses an optional SDK (payments, push, passkeys, Groq, the assistant with Claude) must have added it with `php caligrafer.php add <feature>` and committed `composer.lock`.
## With Claude

| You want | Ask |
|---|---|
| the app online at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com` | `/caligrafy-quill:ship bookshelf` |
| a readiness check only, or your own server | `/caligrafy-quill:deploy` or `/caligrafy-quill:deploy --own-server` |
| to sell the app on the marketplace of caligrafy.com | `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace bookshelf` |

`/caligrafy-quill:ship` commits, creates the GitHub repository and pushes (your SSH key, else HTTPS with the GitHub
CLI, else a code to approve in your browser), signs in to Caligrafy Cloud with an approval in your browser (no token
to copy), creates the app, adds its deploy key, deploys it and checks it online. You approve in your browser, and say
yes before credits are spent. `/caligrafy-quill:deploy --own-server` prepares the project for Coolify or Docker and
deploys nothing: the server is yours.

**Check**

+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud status bookshelf` says `running`, with the time left.
+ `https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com` opens; sign-in and a form work there.
+ `git ls-files` lists no `.env`, `.env.php` or `.env.production`.
## By hand: Caligrafy Cloud

Run these commands on your computer, in the project's folder, with its Docker server up (without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`). Run on the Docker server, `cloud login` cannot open your browser: open the address it
prints.

**1. Check the project.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php version                        # 2.4.0 or later
ls Dockerfile Dockerfile.dockerignore composer.lock
git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)\.env($|\.)' | grep -v '\.env\.example$' | grep -v '^framework/settings/'   # must print nothing
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only project          # no FAIL
```

Every `application/models/<folder>/create_db.sql` must be safe to run again (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, no `DROP`
or `DELETE`). `composer.lock` must be committed. The project's `.gitignore` already leaves out `.env`, `.env.php` and,
since 2.19.1, every other `.env.*` file (`.env.testing`, `.env.production`...) except `.env.example`. A single page
application made with `php caligrafer.php create` is online only once built: run `npm run build` in `public/<name>`
and commit its `dist/` folder (the image does not run `npm`; since 2.19.1 the template no longer ignores `dist/`).

**2. An account.** Create it at [deploy.caligrafy.com](https://deploy.caligrafy.com/signup) (your email is your
username; the same account signs in to caligrafy.com) and open the link of the confirmation email.

**3. Your code on GitHub.** Commit and push the project, with its `Dockerfile`:

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "Bookshelf"
git push
```

**4. Sign in, create the app, deploy.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud login                 # approve, in the browser page it opens, the code it shows
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud create bookshelf      # the repository of this project (git origin), branch main
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf      # builds and starts it, and follows the build
```

A **private** repository needs the app's read-only deploy key: `cloud create` saves it in
`.caligrafy/bookshelf-deploy-key.pub`; add it with
`gh repo deploy-key add .caligrafy/bookshelf-deploy-key.pub -R <owner>/<repo> --title "Caligrafy Cloud"` (or in GitHub,
*Settings, Deploy keys*, *Allow write access* off) before `cloud deploy`.

**5. The settings of your services.** The database settings, the keys, `APP_URL` and `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` are
written for the app. Set the others, then deploy again:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud secret set bookshelf PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_PRODUCTION=sk_live_...
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud secret set bookshelf STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf
```

**6. Check it.** Open `https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com`, sign in, send a form. Then:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud status bookshelf      # running, the time left
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud logs bookshelf        # the deploy step's lines, then what the app prints
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud jobs bookshelf        # the scheduled jobs, their last and next runs
```

The log of a start shows the deploy step:

```text
 Caligrafy deploy
  OK    Settings: .env compiled to .env.php (read without parsing on every request)
  OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache, migrations, scripts
  OK    application/models/Auth/create_db.sql: run
  OK    application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql: run
  OK    application/models/Loans/create_db.sql: run
```

**7. Keep it online.** The first 30 minutes are free; then add time:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud credits 10            # opens the Stripe payment page
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud extend bookshelf month   # 5 credits; a paused app starts again
```

**Check**

+ `cloud status` says `running`.
+ The pages, the sign-in and a form work online.
+ `cloud jobs` lists your scheduled jobs, if the app has some.
## <a name="image"></a>Reference: the production image

Every project has a `Dockerfile` at its root. Hosts that build from a Dockerfile use it as it is:

+ PHP 8.5 and Apache (`mod_rewrite`, `mod_headers`), with the extensions Caligrafy uses (`bcmath`, `exif`, `gd`, `intl`,
  `mysqli`, `pdo_mysql`, `zip`) and the production `php.ini`;
+ the libraries of your `composer.lock`, without the development packages;
+ no Node.js and no `npm`: client apps are served as they are in the repository (a Vite app from its committed `dist/`);
+ your code, without what must not be online: `Dockerfile.dockerignore` leaves out `.env` and `.env.*` (but
  `.env.example`), `.git`, `vendor`, `node_modules`, `qa`, `tests`, `backups`, the Claude plugin, `public/uploads/*` and
  `.caligrafy`;
+ PHP sessions in `/var/lib/php/sessions`: a volume there keeps people signed in across deploys;
+ at start, `php caligrafer.php deploy --wait ${CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT:-60}`, then Apache (a database that is not ready
  does not keep the site down).

**Settings are not in the image.** The running container reads its `.env` as a file at `/var/www/html/.env`, not plain
environment variables: the host must let you mount a file. In production it has `APP_ROOT=` (empty), `APP_ENV=production`,
`APP_DEBUG=false`, `APP_PROTOCOL=https`, its own `APP_KEY` and `API_KEY` (`php caligrafer.php generatekeys`),
`DB_ACTIVATE=true` and the production `DB_*`, and the keys of your services. The list and the reasons are in
[Security: the production settings](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading).

`docker/Dockerfile` is another file: the development image of `docker-compose.yaml`.

## <a name="deploy"></a>Reference: `php caligrafer.php deploy`

What the image runs before Apache starts:

1. prints the scheduled jobs on one line (`caligrafy-schedule {...}`), which Caligrafy Cloud reads;
2. compiles `.env` to `.env.php` (2.19.0): pages then read the settings without parsing `.env` (`env cache`); a `.env`
   changed later is read as it is until the next start;
3. waits for the database (60 seconds by default, `--wait <seconds>` or `CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT`);
4. creates the framework tables (tokens, the audit log, job runs, notifications, jobs, the cache, migrations), safe to
   run again;
5. runs every `application/models/<folder>/create_db.sql` that is **new or changed** since its last run, in folder
   order, and records it in `caligrafy_scripts`;
6. runs the [migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations) of `application/migrations`
   that never ran on this database, in order (2.18.0).

+ A changed script that drops, deletes or truncates (`DROP TABLE`, `DELETE FROM`, `TRUNCATE`...) is never run again on
  its own: the log says so, and you run it by hand when you mean it (`php caligrafer.php sql <file>`). `seed.sql` and
  other scripts are never run. Without `DB_ACTIVATE=true` there is nothing to do for the database.
+ A statement that adds a column, an index or a foreign key already there is skipped, so a `create_db.sql` keeps its
  `ALTER TABLE ... ADD` lines. Change a table that holds data with a migration.
+ It exits with `1` when the database could not be prepared, after saying why.

```bash
php caligrafer.php deploy                 # what the image runs at start
php caligrafer.php deploy --wait 120      # wait up to 2 minutes for the database
```

## <a name="cloud"></a>Reference: Caligrafy Cloud

[Caligrafy Cloud](https://deploy.caligrafy.com) builds your project from its GitHub repository and gives it a MySQL
database, its keys and an address: `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Free time | every new app is free for its first 30 minutes online, from its first deploy |
| Credits | 1 credit = 1 USD, in packs of 5, 10, 25 or 50, paid with Stripe |
| Time online | a week: 2 credits; a month: 5; a year: 50. Time is added to what is left |
| When the time ends | the app is paused (its address shows a paused page) and you get an email. Its data is kept 7 days, then deleted |
| Limits | 5 apps per account, 256 MB of memory and a quarter of a CPU per app |

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cloud login [--no-browser]` | prints a code and opens `https://deploy.caligrafy.com/cli?code=...`: approve it there. `--token cq_...` or `--paste` take a token of the dashboard. The token is kept in `.caligrafy/cloud.json` (ignored by git); `CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_TOKEN` overrides it |
| `cloud account` | your email and credits |
| `cloud create <name> [--repo <url>] [--branch <b>]` | the app, from this project's GitHub repository |
| `cloud key <name>` | the read-only deploy key of a private repository |
| `cloud deploy <name> [--no-wait]` | builds and starts it |
| `cloud apps`, `cloud status <name>`, `cloud logs <name> [--jobs]` | your apps, one app's state and time left, its logs |
| `cloud jobs <name> [run <job> \| history <job>]` | its scheduled jobs, one run now, a job's runs |
| `cloud secret set <name> KEY=value`, `secret list <name>`, `secret delete <name> KEY` | a setting of its `.env`, applied at the next deploy; stored encrypted, never shown again |
| `cloud extend <name> week\|month\|year` | 2, 5 or 50 credits (an account with no limit spends none and its apps have no end date) |
| `cloud credits 5\|10\|25\|50` | buy credits on Stripe |
| `cloud submit <name> [--no-deploy]` | sends the marketplace listing, then deploys |
| `cloud delete <name> --yes` | the app, its database and files, for good |
| `cloud logout` | |

+ Every `cloud` command exits with `1` when Caligrafy Cloud refuses; a pipe (`| tail`) hides it.
+ The database settings and the keys of the app are written for you, and your settings cannot replace them;
  `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=false` are the defaults.
+ **Pages online.** Caligrafy Cloud turns the shared legacy API key off (`LEGACY_API_KEY=false`). Pages call their
  routes with the session and its CSRF token (`apiHeaders()`, the generated JS client); a page that still sends the key
  gets `[ERROR 1004] Access Denied: the legacy API key is turned off`. Programs and agents use
  [personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP).
+ **A password until it is on the marketplace.** The app's page has a *Password* section that locks the app with a
  password you share (off by default). Everyone types it once per browser; it lasts 30 days. While locked, pages send
  visitors to `https://deploy.caligrafy.com/unlock/<name>`, API and agent calls get `401`, and `cloud apps` and
  `cloud status` print `[password protected]`. Locking or unlocking restarts the app (2 to 5 minutes). Offering the app
  to the marketplace removes the password for good.
+ **On the marketplace: 15-minute trials.** Once its listing is published, visitors try the app for 15 minutes (one
  try per browser without an account, 3 per account, then the app's page on caligrafy.com with its Buy panel open).
  Its owner, its maker, its buyers and the administrators are never limited. The limit applies to everyone else who
  opens the app, its own users included (G172): an app people really use belongs on the marketplace only if that is
  what you want for them. Webhooks, REST clients and agents are not limited.
+ **AI agents.** Caligrafy Cloud is itself a Caligrafy application: an agent connects to
  `https://deploy.caligrafy.com/mcp` with a token of the dashboard (*Command line and AI agents*) and can list, deploy
  and extend your apps.
+ Every command is also in [Caligrafer: cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#cloud).

## <a name="marketplace"></a>Selling your app on the marketplace

An app online on Caligrafy Cloud can be offered on the [marketplace of caligrafy.com](https://caligrafy.com/marketplace):
Caligrafy sells a prompt that recreates it with Caligrafy, using Claude, and you earn 25% of every sale.

1. On the app's page in the App console (deploy.caligrafy.com), **Marketplace**: say where we pay you (your country;
   wire details where Stripe does not pay out), then **Offer it to the marketplace**.
2. In Claude Code, in the app's folder, run `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace bookshelf`. It reads the whole code, runs the
   app on your computer and walks through it to screenshot its key features (5 at most), writes the title, the
   description, the prompt that recreates the app and an estimated price window in one private file,
   `.caligrafy/marketplace.json` (ignored by git), then sends it to Caligrafy and redeploys the app. It often takes 15 to
   30 minutes. Without Claude Code, write the file yourself and send it: `php caligrafer.php cloud submit bookshelf`.
3. Caligrafy reviews the listing, sets the final price and publishes it, or turns it down with a reason (offer it again
   after the changes). On caligrafy.com, **Listings** follows each listing (offered, to fix, published), **Earnings** its
   sales and your payouts (from 50 USD, once a month, 14 days after each sale), and **Tasks** what waits for you.
4. Once published, the app's own address is limited to 15-minute trials for everyone but you, its buyers and the
   administrators: **Try the app free · 15 min** on its page starts one (G172).

Each app on Explore comes three ways: its **prompt**, which recreates it with Caligrafy, using Claude; its **code**,
reproduced from the prompt into a private GitHub repository of the buyer; or **managed for you**, online at
`<name>.caligrafy.com` for a monthly or yearly price. You earn 25% of the prompt's price on each of them. What people buy
is in **Library** (prompts and code), and managed apps are in **Apps** (the App console), under *Managed for you*.

**Submitting an idea.** No code at all: on [caligrafy.com/ideas/new](https://caligrafy.com/ideas/new), describe the app
(what it does, who it is for, its powers) and get an estimate, free. Caligrafy reviews it, builds a proof of concept and
gives it to you to try, privately, for 3 days; ask for fixes once, then take it in one of the three ways or drop it.
Your ideas are in **Ideas** on caligrafy.com.

## <a name="ownserver"></a>Your own server

The same image runs on any host that builds a Dockerfile and lets you give it a file and a database.

+ **[Coolify](https://coolify.io)** (open source, on your own server): a *Dockerfile* application from your repository,
  a MySQL database, the `.env` as a *file storage* mounted at `/var/www/html/.env`, and volumes at
  `/var/www/html/public/uploads` and `/var/lib/php/sessions`. MySQL 8.4 with its defaults needs more than 256 MB of
  memory: give the database more, or a smaller configuration.
+ **Any server with Docker:**

```bash
docker build -t bookshelf .
docker run -d -p 80:80 \
  -v "$(pwd)/.env.production:/var/www/html/.env:ro" \
  -v bookshelf-uploads:/var/www/html/public/uploads \
  -v bookshelf-sessions:/var/lib/php/sessions \
  bookshelf
```

Put HTTPS in front of it (a load balancer, Coolify's proxy, Caddy...). Hosts that offer only environment variables and
no file (Railway, Render, DigitalOcean App Platform) are not supported yet.

**Without Docker** (files copied to a PHP 8.3+ server with Apache): run `php caligrafer.php env cache` after each change
to `.env` (never commit `.env.php`), and `php caligrafer.php deploy` for the database. After copying files that keep
their old modification times (`rsync -a`, `cp -p`), run `php caligrafer.php cache clear`: it empties the compiled views
and the class map (which otherwise finds new classes by itself within a minute with `APP_ENV=production`).

**Scheduled jobs** ([Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)): run a second
container from the same image and `.env` with `php caligrafer.php schedule work` (on Coolify, a second application with
that start command), or `php caligrafer.php schedule due` from the server's cron every minute. One of the two.

**Background jobs** ([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)): a job on
`queue_work` in `schedule.php` runs them with the scheduler, or a container of its own runs `php caligrafer.php queue
work` for longer jobs.

**Notifications:** the web push keys made once (`php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject https://<the address>`) and
kept across deploys, `APP_URL`, `MAIL_*`, and HTTPS.
## <a name="troubleshooting"></a>Common mistakes

| You see | Why, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| The build fails | `cloud logs <name>` shows the build: usually `composer.lock` missing or out of date (`composer update`, commit the lock file) |
| `caligrafer deploy: the database is not prepared` | the line above it says why: the database is not reachable (the `DB_*` settings, or `--wait` longer), or a SQL error in a `create_db.sql` or a migration (it names the statement that failed) |
| `Host ... is not allowed to connect` | the database was created but its user was not: on your own server, create the database again (it has no data yet) |
| Caligrafy Cloud cannot read a private repository | the deploy key is not added on GitHub |
| The address shows a paused page | its time ended (`cloud extend <name> week`), or it is deploying, or there is no app with that name |
| `deploy` answers *has no time left (its free 30 minutes are used)* | `cloud extend <name> week` (2 credits), then deploy again; `cloud credits 5` to buy credits |
| The page works locally, its calls get `[ERROR 1004] Access Denied` online | the page sends the legacy API key, off on Caligrafy Cloud: call the routes with `apiHeaders()` or the JS client. A single page application made before 2.19.1 sends `VITE_API_KEY`: give it the session headers of the 2.19.1 template (`apiHeaders()` of `src/common/app.js`) |
| `cloud login` waits and nothing opens | it runs in the Docker server: open the address it printed, approve the code |
| Everyone is signed out after a deploy | no volume at `/var/lib/php/sessions` |
| Uploaded files disappear after a deploy | no volume at `/var/www/html/public/uploads` |
| Pages are slow online | `APP_DEBUG=true` in the production `.env` |
| A setting changed on your own server seems ignored | run `php caligrafer.php env cache` again (or restart the container: the deploy step compiles `.env`) |

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Caligrafy-Cloud -->

[Caligrafy Cloud](https://deploy.caligrafy.com) puts a project online at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`: it builds the
project from its GitHub repository with its own `Dockerfile`, gives it a MySQL database, its keys, its `.env` and the
volumes it needs, and runs its scheduled jobs. Every new app is free for its first 30 minutes online. Since 2.4.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:ship bookshelf
```

It commits, creates the GitHub repository and pushes (your SSH key, else HTTPS with the GitHub CLI, else a code to
approve in your browser), signs in to Caligrafy Cloud with an approval in your browser, creates the app, adds its deploy
key, deploys it and checks it online. You approve in the browser, and say yes before credits are spent.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `php caligrafer.php cloud status bookshelf` says `running`, with the time left;
+ `https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com` opens; sign-in and a form work there;
+ `git ls-files` lists no `.env`, `.env.php` or `.env.production`.
## By hand

Run the commands on your computer, in the project's folder, with its Docker server up (without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`).

**1. Check the project.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php version                        # 2.4.0 or later
ls Dockerfile Dockerfile.dockerignore composer.lock
git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)\.env($|\.)' | grep -v '\.env\.example$' | grep -v '^framework/settings/'   # must print nothing
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only project          # no FAIL
```

Every `create_db.sql` must be safe to run again ([The deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step#scripts)),
`composer.lock` committed, and a Vite single page application built (`npm run build` in `public/<name>`, `dist/`
committed).

**2. An account.** Create it at [deploy.caligrafy.com](https://deploy.caligrafy.com/signup) (your email is your
username; the same account signs in to caligrafy.com) and open the link of the confirmation email.

**3. Your code on GitHub.**

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "Bookshelf"
git push
```

**4. Sign in.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud login
```

```text
 To sign in, approve this code in your browser: <code>
 https://deploy.caligrafy.com/cli?code=...
```

Open the address (in the Docker server the browser does not open by itself), check that the code is the same, approve.
The command then prints ` Signed in as you@example.com (... credits). The token is in .caligrafy/cloud.json (git-ignored).`

**5. Create the app.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud create bookshelf
```

```text
 Created https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com from https://github.com/you/bookshelf (main).
 Next: php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf
```

It reads the repository from the project's `origin` remote (`--repo <url>` names another, `--branch <b>` another
branch). A **private** repository gets a read-only deploy key, printed and saved in
`.caligrafy/bookshelf-deploy-key.pub`: add it on GitHub before deploying,

```bash
gh repo deploy-key add .caligrafy/bookshelf-deploy-key.pub -R <owner>/<repo> --title "Caligrafy Cloud"
```

or in the repository's *Settings, Deploy keys*, with *Allow write access* off.

**6. Its settings.** The database settings, the keys, `APP_URL`, `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false` and
`LEGACY_API_KEY=false` are written for the app. Add the keys of your services:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud secret set bookshelf PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_PRODUCTION=sk_live_...
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud secret list bookshelf
```

Each one is stored encrypted, never shown again, and applied at the next deploy.

**7. Deploy.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf
```

```text
 Deploying https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com (a few minutes)...
 Online: https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com
```

It follows the build for up to 15 minutes (`--no-wait` returns at once). A failed build prints the last 30 lines of
its log.

**8. Check it.** Open `https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com`, sign in, send a form. Then:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud status bookshelf      # running, the time left
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud logs bookshelf        # the deploy step, then what the app prints
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud jobs bookshelf        # the scheduled jobs, their last and next runs
```

**9. Keep it online.** After the free 30 minutes, add time:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud credits 10               # prints the Stripe page to pay on
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud extend bookshelf month   # 5 credits; a paused app starts again
```
## <a name="reference"></a>Reference

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Free time | every new app, its first 30 minutes online from its first deploy |
| Credits | 1 credit = 1 USD, in packs of 5, 10, 25 or 50, paid with Stripe |
| Time online | a week: 2 credits; a month: 5; a year: 50; added to what is left |
| When the time ends | the app is paused (its address shows a paused page) and you get an email; its data is kept 7 days, then deleted |
| Limits | 5 apps per account, 256 MB of memory and a quarter of a CPU per app |
| Settings | `.env` written by Cloud, with your `cloud secret` values; yours cannot replace the database settings and keys |
| Scheduled jobs | read at each deploy from the `caligrafy-schedule` line of the deploy step; `cloud jobs` shows them |
| Sign-in for the command line | `.caligrafy/cloud.json`, or `CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_TOKEN`; `CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_URL` for another service |
| AI agents | `https://deploy.caligrafy.com/mcp` with a token of the dashboard (*Command line and AI agents*): list, deploy and extend your apps |

Every `cloud` command is on [Caligrafer: deploy commands](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Deploy-Commands#cloud).

**A password until it is on the marketplace.** The app's page has a *Password* section that locks the app with a
password you share (off by default). Each browser types it once, for 30 days. While locked, pages send visitors to
`https://deploy.caligrafy.com/unlock/<name>`, API and agent calls get `401`, and `cloud apps` and `cloud status` print
`[password protected]`. Locking or unlocking restarts the app (2 to 5 minutes). Offering the app to the marketplace
removes the password for good ([Selling your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#marketplace)).

**On the marketplace: 15-minute trials.** Once its listing is published, visitors try the app for 15 minutes (one try
per browser without an account, 3 per account, then the app's page on caligrafy.com with its Buy panel open). Its
owner, its maker, its buyers and the administrators are never limited. The limit applies to everyone else who opens
the app, its own users included (G172): an app people really use belongs on the marketplace only if that is what you
want for them. Webhooks, REST clients and agents are not limited.
## Common mistakes

| You see | Why, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| The build fails | `cloud logs <name>`: usually `composer.lock` missing or out of date (G69): `composer update`, commit it |
| Cloud cannot read a private repository | the deploy key is not added on GitHub (`cloud key <name>` prints it again) |
| `deploy` answers *has no time left (its free 30 minutes are used)* | `cloud extend <name> week` (2 credits), then deploy again (G90) |
| `cloud deploy ... \| tail` says nothing went wrong | a pipe hides the exit code (G89): run it whole |
| Pages work locally, their calls get `[ERROR 1004] Access Denied` online | the legacy API key is off on Cloud (G87): call the routes with `apiHeaders()` or the JS client |
| The address shows a paused page | its time ended, it is deploying, or there is no app with that name |
| `cloud login` waits and nothing opens | it runs in the Docker server: open the address it printed |
| Stripe emails about failing test-mode webhooks once live | a test-mode endpoint still points at the production address (G115): create the endpoint in live mode, set its `whsec_...` as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and remove the test one |

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Your-Own-Server -->

The [production image](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Production-Image) of a project runs on
any host that builds a Dockerfile and lets you give the container a file and a database: Coolify on your own server, or
any server with Docker. A PHP server without Docker works too. This page sets up each one, with the scheduled jobs, the
background jobs and the notifications. Since 2.4.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:deploy --own-server
```

It checks that the project is ready, writes `.env.production` for the host with your OK (its own keys from
`generatekeys`, `DB_ACTIVATE=true` and the production `DB_*`; never committed), and says what to set up on the host. It deploys nothing:
the server is yours.

**Check** before you say OK: `curl -I https://<your-host>/.env` answers `403` or `404`, and sign-in and a form work.
## By hand

### <a name="coolify"></a>Coolify

[Coolify](https://coolify.io) is open source and runs on your own server.

1. A **MySQL** database resource. MySQL 8.4 with its defaults needs more than 256 MB of memory (G71): give it more, or
   a smaller configuration (`performance_schema = OFF`, `innodb_buffer_pool_size = 64M`, about 384 MB).
2. A **Dockerfile** application from your repository (it uses the `Dockerfile` at the root).
3. The production `.env` as a **file storage** mounted at `/var/www/html/.env`, with the database's host, name, user
   and password in `DB_*` and `DB_ACTIVATE=true`.
4. Two **volumes**: `/var/www/html/public/uploads` and `/var/lib/php/sessions`.
5. Deploy. The application's log starts with [the deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step).

Coolify's proxy gives it HTTPS.

### <a name="docker"></a>Any server with Docker

```bash
docker build -t bookshelf .
docker run -d -p 80:80 \
  -v "$(pwd)/.env.production:/var/www/html/.env:ro" \
  -v bookshelf-uploads:/var/www/html/public/uploads \
  -v bookshelf-sessions:/var/lib/php/sessions \
  bookshelf
```

Put HTTPS in front of it (a load balancer, Caddy...). `-e CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT=120` gives a database that starts
slowly two minutes.

### <a name="nodocker"></a>Without Docker

Files copied to a PHP 8.3+ server with Apache (`mod_rewrite`, `AllowOverride FileInfo` or `All` for the `.htaccess`
files) and the extensions the image has (`bcmath`, `exif`, `gd`, `intl`, `mysqli`, `pdo_mysql`, `zip`):

```bash
composer install --no-dev
php caligrafer.php env cache      # after each change to .env (never commit .env.php)
php caligrafer.php deploy         # the database: framework tables, scripts, migrations
php caligrafer.php cache clear    # after copying files that keep their old modification times (rsync -a, cp -p)
```

`cache clear` empties the compiled views and the class map; with `APP_ENV=production` the class map otherwise finds new
classes by itself within a minute (G117). On nginx, write the rules of the `.htaccess` files yourself: they deny
dotfiles, the server-side folders and scripts in `public/uploads`.
## <a name="jobs"></a>Scheduled jobs, background jobs, notifications

+ **Scheduled jobs** ([Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs)): one of the
  two, not both:
  + a second container from the same image and `.env`, with the command `php caligrafer.php schedule work` (on Coolify,
    a second application with that start command);
  + or the server's cron, every minute: `* * * * * cd /var/www/html && php caligrafer.php schedule due`.
+ **Background jobs** ([Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)): a job of
  `application/config/schedule.php` on the framework's `queue_work` capability runs them with the scheduler; for longer
  jobs, a container of its own runs `php caligrafer.php queue work`.
+ **Notifications** ([Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)): the web push
  keys made once (`php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject https://<the address>`) and kept across deploys, `APP_URL`,
  the `MAIL_*` settings, and HTTPS.
## <a name="checklist"></a>Before you open it to people

+ `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `APP_ROOT=` (empty), `APP_PROTOCOL=https`, keys of its own
  (`php caligrafer.php generatekeys`).
+ `curl -I https://<your-host>/.env` answers `403` or `404`.
+ Personal access tokens for programs and agents, then `LEGACY_API_KEY=false`.
+ `php caligrafer.php doctor --env .env.production` from your computer, when it can reach the database.

The whole list, and why: [the production checklist](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading#checklist).
## Common mistakes

| You see | Why, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| The settings are ignored | the host gives environment variables, not a file (G67): mount the `.env` at `/var/www/html/.env`. Railway, Render and DigitalOcean App Platform are not supported yet |
| `Host ... is not allowed to connect` | MySQL was killed while it initialized (G71): more memory, then recreate its volume while it has no data |
| Everyone is signed out after a deploy | no volume at `/var/lib/php/sessions` (G70) |
| Uploaded files disappear after a deploy | no volume at `/var/www/html/public/uploads` (G70) |
| A changed view still shows the old page | files copied with old modification times (G117): `php caligrafer.php cache clear` |
| A job's `Cache::forget()` does not reach the pages | `CACHE_STORE=file`: the web server and the command line have their own folders (G119). Keep the `database` store |
| Jobs run twice | both a `schedule work` container and a cron line |
| A setting changed on the server seems ignored | run `php caligrafer.php env cache` again, or restart the container |
## Related pages

+ [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online)
+ [The production image](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Production-Image) · [The deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step)
+ [Deploying to Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Caligrafy-Cloud)
+ [Security and upgrading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Production-Image -->

Every Caligrafy project has a **production image**: the `Dockerfile` at its root. Caligrafy Cloud, Coolify and any
host that builds from a Dockerfile use it as it is. This page says what is in it, what is left out, what runs when it
starts, and what the container needs from the host. Since 2.4.0.

**Since 2.26.0** the image starts with `docker/production/start.sh`: it sizes Apache to the container (`PHP_PROCESSES`), turns keep-alive off, keeps database connections, preloads the framework, compiles the views, keeps public answers in memory and can run the async server (`ASYNC=on`). Every setting is on [performance and deployment](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Performance-and-Deployment).

> `docker/Dockerfile` is another file: the development image of `docker-compose.yaml` (the `dev-box` and `scheduler`
> containers).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:deploy
```

The `deploy` skill checks that the project is ready for the image (the `Dockerfile`, `composer.lock`, no `.env` in git,
safe `create_db.sql` scripts, a built SPA) and says what to fix. It deploys nothing.

**Check** before you say OK: `docker build -t myapp .` finishes, and `git ls-files` lists no `.env`, `.env.php` or
`.env.production`.
## By hand

Build and run the image on your computer, with a production-like `.env` of your own:

```bash
docker build -t bookshelf .
docker run --rm -p 8090:80 -v "$(pwd)/.env.production:/var/www/html/.env:ro" bookshelf
```

The container's log starts with the [deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step),
then Apache's. A `.env.production` whose database cannot be reached prints
` FAIL  Database: not reachable after 60 s: check the DB_* settings` and
`caligrafer deploy: the database is not prepared (see above)`, and the site starts anyway.
## <a name="contents"></a>What is in it

| Layer | What the `Dockerfile` does |
| --- | --- |
| Base | `php:8.5-apache` |
| System | Debian packages over `https`, the libraries for `gd`, `zip` and `intl`, `unzip` and `git`; Apache's `rewrite` and `headers` modules |
| PHP | the extensions `bcmath`, `exif`, `gd` (FreeType, JPEG), `intl`, `mysqli`, `pdo_mysql` and `zip`; the production `php.ini` |
| Sessions | `session.save_path = "/var/lib/php/sessions"`, a folder owned by `www-data` |
| Libraries | Composer 2, then `composer install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist --no-scripts --no-autoloader --no-plugins` from `composer.json` and `composer.lock` alone, so a code change does not install them again |
| Code | `COPY . .` (less what `Dockerfile.dockerignore` leaves out), `composer dump-autoload --optimize --no-dev --no-plugins`, `public/uploads` and `backups/` created, `public/uploads` owned by `www-data` |
| Port | `80` |

No Node.js and no `npm`: client apps are served as they are in the repository, a Vite app from its committed `dist/`.
Composer runs with `--no-plugins` (2.22.1), so no Composer plugin tries to run `npm` during the build.
## <a name="ignore"></a>What is left out

`Dockerfile.dockerignore` keeps these out of the image:

| Left out | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `.env`, `.env.*` (but `.env.example`) | secrets: the host gives the settings |
| `.git`, `.github` | history and CI |
| `vendor`, `**/node_modules` | installed in the image, or not needed |
| `qa`, `tests`, `backups` | development, tests and update backups |
| `claude-plugin`, `.claude`, `.claude-plugin`, `framework/design` | tools for Claude Code and the design styles' sources |
| `*.log`, `.DS_Store` | |
| `public/uploads/*` (but its `.gitignore`) | uploads live in a volume |
| `.caligrafy` | the Cloud sign-in and the marketplace listing |
## <a name="start"></a>What runs at start

```sh
php caligrafer.php deploy --wait ${CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT:-60} || echo 'caligrafer deploy: the database is not prepared (see above)'; exec apache2-foreground
```

1. [`php caligrafer.php deploy`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step): the scheduled jobs
   line, `.env` compiled to `.env.php`, then the database (it waits up to `CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT` seconds, 60 by
   default, for a database that starts at the same time).
2. Apache in the foreground, whatever the deploy step said: a database that is not ready does not keep the site down.
## <a name="host"></a>What the container needs from the host

+ **Its settings as a file** at `/var/www/html/.env` (G67): Caligrafy reads `.env`, and its values replace plain
  environment variables of the same name. Coolify mounts it as a *file storage*, `docker run` with
  `-v .env.production:/var/www/html/.env:ro`, and Caligrafy Cloud writes it. Hosts that only offer environment
  variables (Railway, Render, DigitalOcean App Platform) are not supported yet.
+ **The production settings** in that file: `APP_ROOT=` (empty), `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`,
  `APP_PROTOCOL=https`, its own `APP_KEY` and `API_KEY` (`php caligrafer.php generatekeys`), `DB_ACTIVATE=true` and the
  production `DB_*`, and the keys of your services. The list and the reasons:
  [Security: the production settings](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading).
+ **A MySQL database** it can reach.
+ **Two volumes** (G70): `/var/lib/php/sessions` (people stay signed in across deploys) and
  `/var/www/html/public/uploads` (uploads survive a deploy).
+ **HTTPS in front of it**: a load balancer, Coolify's proxy, Caddy... The session cookie is `Secure` behind a proxy
  that sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`.
## Common mistakes

+ **The build fails on Composer** (G69): `composer.lock` is missing or older than `composer.json`. Run
  `composer update` and commit it.
+ **A Vite app is blank online**: its `dist/` is not committed. Run `npm run build` in `public/<name>` and commit
  `dist/`.
+ **Everyone is signed out after a deploy, uploads are gone** (G70): no volume at `/var/lib/php/sessions` or
  `/var/www/html/public/uploads`.
+ **Settings given as environment variables are ignored** (G67): give the container its `.env` as a file.
+ **`APP_ROOT=bookshelf` online**: the site's links point to `/bookshelf/...`. `APP_ROOT=` is empty in production.
+ **Pages are slow online**: `APP_DEBUG=true` in the production `.env`.
## Related pages

+ [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online)
+ [The deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step)
+ [Deploying to Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Caligrafy-Cloud) · [your own server](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Your-Own-Server)
+ [Security and upgrading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step -->

**The deploy step** is `php caligrafer.php deploy`: what a project runs each time it starts in production, before
Apache serves it. The [production image](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Production-Image) runs it
for you. It compiles the settings and brings the database up to date: the framework tables, your `create_db.sql`
scripts when they are new or changed, then your migrations. Since 2.4.0 (migrations 2.18.0, `.env.php` 2.19.0).
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:deploy
```

Before a deploy, the skill checks what the deploy step will run: every `create_db.sql` safe to run twice, the
migrations in order, the schedule file valid. After one, `/caligrafy-quill:ship` reads the start-up log.

**Check** before you say OK: the log of the start has only `OK` and `SKIP` lines, and no `FAIL`.
## By hand

On a server without Docker (files copied to PHP and Apache), run it yourself after each copy:

```bash
php caligrafer.php deploy
php caligrafer.php deploy --wait 120      # wait up to 2 minutes for the database
```

On your computer, run it against a production-like settings file to see what it would do:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php deploy --env .env.staging
```

```text
 Caligrafy deploy
 caligrafy-schedule {"version":1,"jobs":[]}
  OK    Settings: .env compiled to .env.php (read without parsing on every request)
  OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache, migrations, scripts
  OK    application/models/Auth/create_db.sql: up to date
  OK    application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql: changed: run again
  OK    Migrations: 1 run: 20261107232335_add_books_isbn.sql
```

> `--env` reads the database settings of that file; the `Settings` line always compiles the project's own `.env`.
## <a name="steps"></a>What it does, in order

From [`Caligrafy\Deployer::run()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#deployer-run):

1. **The scheduled jobs line.** `caligrafy-schedule <json>`: the listing of `schedule list --json`, which Caligrafy
   Cloud reads from the log to run the jobs. A schedule file with problems prints
   `caligrafy-schedule-invalid <the problems>` instead, and its jobs do not run. Without the file the list is empty.
2. **The settings.** `.env` compiled to `.env.php`
   ([`Deployer::cacheEnv()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#deployer-cacheenv), the same
   as `env cache`): pages read the settings without parsing `.env` while `.env` keeps that content. Without `.env`:
   `SKIP  Settings: no .env to compile`.
3. **`DB_ACTIVATE`.** Not `true`: `SKIP  Database: DB_ACTIVATE is not true: nothing to prepare`, and it stops there with
   exit code `0`.
4. **The database.** It tries to connect every 2 seconds until `--wait` seconds have passed (60 by default; the image
   passes `CALIGRAFY_DEPLOY_WAIT`). Never reached:
   `FAIL  Database: not reachable after 60 s: check the DB_* settings`, exit code `1`.
5. **The framework tables.** `framework/settings/platform.sql` (every table `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`: tokens, the
   audit log, job runs, notifications, jobs, the cache, migrations, Snap), and `caligrafy_scripts`, which records the
   scripts that ran.
6. **The `create_db.sql` scripts.** Every `application/models/<folder>/create_db.sql`, in folder order:

    | The script | Line | What happens |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | never ran here | `OK  <path>: run` | it runs, and its SHA-256 is recorded |
    | ran, and has not changed | `OK  <path>: up to date` | nothing |
    | changed since it ran | `OK  <path>: changed: run again` | it runs again, and the new SHA-256 is recorded |
    | changed, and drops, deletes or truncates | `WARN  <path>: changed, but it drops or deletes data: not run (php caligrafer.php sql <path> runs it)` | nothing: run it by hand when you mean it |

    "Drops or deletes" is `DROP TABLE`, `DROP DATABASE`, `DROP SCHEMA`, `DROP VIEW`, `DROP COLUMN`, `DELETE FROM` or
    `TRUNCATE`, comments left aside ([`Deployer::destructive()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#deployer-destructive)).
    A statement that fails only because what it adds is already there (a duplicate column, key name or foreign key:
    MySQL errors 1060, 1061, 1826) is skipped, so a script keeps its `ALTER TABLE ... ADD` lines and runs again.
    Other files (`seed.sql`...) are never run.
7. **The migrations.** When `application/migrations` has files, the ones that never ran, in order:
   `OK  Migrations: 1 run: <file>`, or `OK  Migrations: up to date`. A migration edited after it ran:
   `WARN  Migrations: <file>: changed after it ran, not run again (write a new migration for the change)`.

Any SQL error in steps 5 to 7 prints `FAIL  Database: <the error>` (a migration names its file and statement) and the
exit code is `1`. The image starts Apache anyway, after `caligrafer deploy: the database is not prepared (see above)`.
## <a name="scripts"></a>Writing scripts it can run again

Because a changed script runs again on the next start, each `create_db.sql` must be safe to run twice:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `books` (
    `id` INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

-- added later: skipped once the column is there
ALTER TABLE `books` ADD COLUMN `isbn` VARCHAR(20) NULL;
```

For a change to a table that holds data, prefer a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations):
it runs once, in order, and says so.
## Common mistakes

+ **A script that drops its table first** (G68): it ran once; changed, it is never run again (`WARN`), and run by hand it
  deletes the data. Use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and added statements.
+ **`caligrafer deploy: the database is not prepared`**: the line above it says why: the database is not reachable (the
  `DB_*` settings, or a longer `--wait`), or a SQL error that names the statement.
+ **`Host ... is not allowed to connect`** (G71): the database was created but its user was not, often a MySQL killed for
  lack of memory while it initialized. Give it more memory, and recreate its volume while it holds no data.
+ **A setting changed on your own server is ignored**: `.env.php` was compiled from the old `.env`, and is used only
  while `.env` has that content; an edited `.env` is read again. Restart the container, or run `env cache`.
+ **Scheduled jobs do not run on Cloud**: the log has `caligrafy-schedule-invalid`: run `php caligrafer.php schedule list`
  to see the problems.
## Related pages
