<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Updating-Caligrafy -->

**Updating** moves a project to a newer release of Caligrafy Quill in one command, `php caligrafer.php update`: the
framework, the release's other files, the settings and packages it adds, then the untouched files of `application/`
(`upgrade --apply`). Your code is never overwritten: a file you changed is kept, with the release's version next to it to
merge. This page is the how-to, then what each command does. `update` since 2.9.0; `upgrade` looks for a newer
release since 2.10.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:update
```

The `update` skill runs `update --check`, shows what changes, runs `update`, merges every `.caligrafy-new` file into
yours, runs `platform install`, `doctor` and the tests, reads the release notes of every version passed, and refreshes
Claude Code's copy of the plugin.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `php caligrafer.php version` is the new version;
+ `find . -name '*.caligrafy-new' -not -path './vendor/*' -not -path './backups/*'` prints nothing;
+ `php caligrafer.php doctor` has no `FAIL`, and sign-in and the forms work from a private window.
## By hand

The commands run in the project's Docker server; without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`.

**1. Start from a clean state.** `git status --short`: commit what is there, so that the update is one change you can
review. With uncommitted changes `update` stops (`--yes` goes on anyway).

**2. See what changes.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update --check
```

```text
 Updating Caligrafy Quill 2.24.1 to 2.25.0 (check: nothing is changed)

  replaced    framework/ (will be replaced)
  replaced    claude-plugin/ (will be replaced)
  replaced    caligrafer.php (will be replaced)
  customized  Dockerfile: kept, the new version will be written in Dockerfile.caligrafy-new
  setting     .env: <NEW_SETTING> will be added with its default

 Nothing was changed. php caligrafer.php update applies it.
```

(an example: the files and settings listed are those your two releases differ by). Already on the latest:
` Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0 is the latest: nothing to update. php caligrafer.php upgrade checks application/.`

**3. Update.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update            # the latest release
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update 2.25.0     # or one release
```

Run it whole, not through `| tail` (G89): it exits with `1` when something did not finish, and its last lines run
`upgrade --apply`. It ends with
` Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0 is in place. ... Check the project with php caligrafer.php doctor; the release notes: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-2.25.0`.

**4. Merge every `.caligrafy-new`.**

```bash
find . -name '*.caligrafy-new' -not -path './vendor/*' -not -path './backups/*'
```

For each one, `diff <file> <file>.caligrafy-new`, write your changes plus the release's into `<file>`, then delete the
`.caligrafy-new`.

**5. Check.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php version
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install   # the framework tables of the new release
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php upgrade --local    # nothing outdated left in application/
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test
```

Read the release notes of every version you passed
(`https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-<version>`), and the "From X to Y" notes of
[Security and upgrading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading#upgrading).

**6. Commit and deploy.** Commit (`Caligrafy Quill <from> to <to>`), push, deploy. Delete `backups/` once you are done:
git ignores it and the production image leaves it out.
## <a name="update"></a>What `update` does

From [`Caligrafy\Updater`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#updater). It downloads, from
GitHub, the project's own release (`Framework::VERSION`) and the target (the latest by default), and compares your
files with your own release, so it can tell what you changed:

1. **`framework/` and `claude-plugin/`** are the framework's: replaced whole, the files the release dropped included.
   `framework/librairies/app/.env` (written by `initialize`) is kept. Framework files you changed by hand are listed at
   the end; your copies are in the backup.
2. **Every other file of the release** (`caligrafer.php`, `.bin/`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `index.php`,
   `public/css`, `public/js`...):

    | Your file | What happens | Report |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | missing | added | `added` |
    | the same as your release's | replaced | `replaced` |
    | changed by you | kept; the new version written next to it as `<file>.caligrafy-new` | `customized` |

   Your documents (`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `LICENSE`) are replaced only when untouched, left alone without a `.caligrafy-new` when you changed them, and never
   added. Never touched here: `application/`, `tests/`, `qa/`, `public/uploads/`, `composer.lock`, the CI files, and the
   project's plugin source files.
3. **Merged** instead of compared: `composer.json` gets the new packages and versions you did not change (then
   `composer update` for them; `--no-composer` prints the command), `.gitignore` the new lines, `.env` the new settings
   with their defaults (existing values are never changed).
4. **The plugin.** The project's plugin source keeps its own name, and Claude Code's copy of the plugin is registered,
   installed or refreshed when `claude` is on this computer.
5. **`application/`**: `php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply --local`, from the new release.

Everything it replaces is copied first to `backups/caligrafy-update-<from>-to-<to>-<time>/`. It refuses a version lower
than the project's (` This project runs <from>: going back to <to> is not supported (restore a backup instead)`).

**A project before 2.9.0** has no `update`: get the command once (G94), then run it.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/master/framework/core/Updater.php -o framework/core/Updater.php
php -r "require 'framework/core/Updater.php'; exit((new Caligrafy\Updater('.'))->run());"
```
## <a name="upgrade"></a>What `upgrade` does

`application/` was copied from `framework/settings/application` when the project was made, and is yours. `upgrade`
(from [`Caligrafy\Upgrader`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#upgrader)) brings its
untouched files up to date. Without `--local`, `--force` or `--keep`, it first asks GitHub for a newer release (G96):
when there is one, `upgrade` is `update --check` and `upgrade --apply` is `update`.

```bash
php caligrafer.php upgrade                                      # dry run
php caligrafer.php upgrade --local                              # this release's templates only
php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply                              # replace the files you never changed
php caligrafer.php upgrade --force application/views/Auth/login.pug          # replace one file you changed
php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply --keep application/views/default/index.pug   # keep a template copy that is now yours
```

It tells your files from untouched copies with `application/.caligrafy-manifest.json` (written by `initialize`) and the
history of every template version (`framework/settings/template-history.json`). Each template file is:

| State | Means | With `--apply` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `missing` | not in `application/` | added |
| `identical` | the same as the template | nothing |
| `outdated` | an untouched copy of an older template | replaced, with a backup in `backups/caligrafy-upgrade-<time>/` |
| `customized` | changed by you | kept; the new version written next to it as `.caligrafy-new` |
| `kept` | named with `--keep` (remembered in the manifest) | kept; the new version next to it |
| `held` | not added, with the reason: the user capabilities when the project manages users its own way (G80), `AuthController` or `AdminController` when its routes do not need them | nothing; `--force` adds one |
| `routes` | `application/config/routing/web.php`, your routes | never replaced |

It also reports, without changing them: client apps in `public/` that differ from their template, settings of
`.env.example` missing from `.env` and obsolete ones, and Bootstrap 3 classes left in views and apps.
## Common mistakes

+ **`update | tail`** (G89): the pipe hides a failed `composer update` or `upgrade`. Run it whole.
+ **A `.caligrafy-new` left behind**: the release's fixes in that file are not in yours. Merge each one, then delete it.
+ **A new skill is missing in Claude Code after the update** (G103): Claude Code runs its own copy of the plugin. Run
  `php caligrafer.php plugin` on your computer, then restart `claude` in the folder.
+ **`upgrade` on an old project says nothing changes** (G96): before 2.10.0 it compared `application/` with the
  templates of the release the project already ran. Run `update`.
+ **The new framework tables are missing**: an update that adds tables needs `platform install` (the deploy step runs
  it online).
+ **The user capabilities are `held`** (G80): the project manages users its own way; `--force` adds them when you
  want them.
## Related pages

+ [Security and upgrading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading)
+ [Caligrafer: maintenance commands](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Maintenance-Commands)

# Performance and deployment

Since 2.26.0 the production image (`Dockerfile`) is tuned for the container it runs in, and a project can go further
with a response cache and, experimentally, an async server. Every setting below is a line of `.env` (or a variable of
the container's environment); nothing in the application's code changes.

## What the production image does at start

`docker/production/start.sh` runs before Apache:

1. **PHP processes**: `PHP_PROCESSES`. By default it follows the app: **2 per CPU** the container may use (read
   from its cgroup quota, at least 4), or **6 per CPU** (at least 16) when an AI key is set (`OPEN_AI_KEY`,
   `GROQ_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AGENT_API_KEY`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY`, `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`,
   `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `WATSON_API_KEY`). Apache's own default (up to 150) makes processes fight over a few CPUs;
   too few, and a page waits behind requests that wait on something else.
2. **Keep-alive off** (`KEEP_ALIVE=on` keeps it). With a fixed number of processes, an idle open connection would hold
   one. The proxy in front (Caligrafy Cloud, Traefik, a load balancer) keeps the visitors' connections open.
3. **The response cache** (`CACHE=off` turns it off) and **OPcache preloading** (`PRELOAD=off`).
4. `php caligrafer.php deploy` (framework tables, SQL scripts, migrations), then `php caligrafer.php optimize` (every
   Pug view compiled, the class map built) as the web server's user: the first visitor of a new container compiles
   nothing.

OPcache keeps the compiled code and stops checking the files for changes (`docker/production/php.ini`): a new version
is a new image.

## How many processes

A process answers one request at a time. A page that only computes is fastest with one process per CPU; a request
that waits (the database, an AI service, an outside API) holds its process while it waits.

| Your app | `PHP_PROCESSES` |
|---|---|
| Pages and the database | leave it empty: 2 per CPU, at least 4 (database waits last milliseconds) |
| Calls an AI service (an AI key is set) | leave it empty: 6 per CPU, at least 16; more if more AI requests can wait at the same time (about 3 MB each when idle) |
| Calls another slow service (a payment API, an SMTP server) from its pages | set it: more than the requests that can wait at the same time |

Measured on 2 CPUs (HTML pages per second while other visitors wait 1 s on an outside call): 4 processes answer
8,051 pages a second when nothing waits, but 32 when 4 visitors wait at once; 8 processes answer 4,180, then 7,550
with 4 waiting, then 14 with 16 waiting. The async server answers AI calls without holding a page's process.

`php caligrafer.php doctor` warns when an app that has AI keys runs fewer than 16 processes, and when the database
allows fewer connections than the processes keep open.

## Persistent database connections

`DB_PERSISTENT` (empty means on, for MySQL and PostgreSQL in a web server): each process keeps its database
connection between requests instead of opening one per request. Before it is reused, a transaction the last request
left open is rolled back and the session time zone is set again. The command line (tests, migrations, the queue)
never keeps one. Each process holds one connection: the database must allow `PHP_PROCESSES` connections plus the
command line and the queue (`doctor` checks it). `DB_PERSISTENT=false` connects on every request.

## The response cache

A capability or a page whose answer is the same for every visitor can say how long that answer may be shared:

```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_books', description: 'The catalog', readOnly: true, public: true, cache: 30)]
class ListBooks extends Service { /* ... */ }
```

```php
Route::page('/about', 'Site/about', ['cache' => 300]);
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // GET /capabilities/list_books (a read-only capability may be called with GET)
```

A GET or HEAD from a visitor with no session cookie and no token gets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=30`, and the
production image's Apache keeps the answer in memory: the next visitors get it without PHP. Never kept:

- an answer to a signed-in person or to a token (it is not marked);
- an answer that sets a cookie, such as a page with a form (its CSRF token starts a session): `HttpCache::guard()`
  turns it into `Cache-Control: private, no-store` just before the headers go out;
- any answer other than a 200.

`cache` needs `readOnly: true` and `public: true`. Choose a few seconds for data that changes: a cached answer is not
cleared when the data changes, it expires.

## The async server (experimental)

```bash
php caligrafer.php add async        # Workerman
php caligrafer.php async check      # which capabilities may run there, and why the others may not
```

With `ASYNC=on`, the production image listens with the async server: processes that keep the application in memory
(`ASYNC_WORKERS`, one per CPU by default) answer the capabilities channel (`GET /capabilities`,
`/capabilities/{name}`), and every other request (pages, forms, sign-in, files) goes to Apache unchanged. A request
that brings the session cookie always goes to Apache.

A capability runs there only when its class uses no session, cookie or superglobal (`$_SESSION`, `$_GET`, `$_SERVER`...),
prints nothing, never calls `exit`, keeps no static state, is not `webOnly` and takes no file: `async check` names
what stops each one, and Apache answers the others as before. After each request, what it left in memory is
forgotten (the cache copies, a transaction, container instances). Its callers are tokens and visitors only.

Development: `php caligrafer.php async start --listen http://0.0.0.0:8081` answers on its own port.

## Capability calls

Since 2.26.1 a call of a capability by name (`/capabilities/{name}`, MCP, the JS client) reads the registry of
capabilities from a file kept next to the class map instead of building it on every request: it loads only the file of
the capability it calls. On 2 CPUs through Apache, a public read-only capability answered 2,816 calls a second on
2.26.0 and 4,948 on 2.26.1 (a plain route: about 6,900). Nothing to set: it follows the class map
([How the attribute is found](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Capability-Attribute#registry)).

## Measured

The numbers of the benchmark (Docker, 2 CPUs and 1 GB for the app) are on the
[benchmark dashboard](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill#performance) and in the release notes of
[2.26.0](Release-notes:-2.26.0).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Security-Defaults -->

# Security defaults

What Caligrafy Quill does for every project without a line of code (2.26.0), and what one line turns on.

| Protection | How | Since |
|---|---|---|
| CSRF on forms | `Request` checks `_token` on every POST, PUT and DELETE of a form; `=csrf()` in a view; session-authenticated JSON writes need `X-CSRF-Token`; `Route::webhook` is exempt by itself | default |
| SQL injection | the query builder binds every value and checks identifiers | default |
| Mass assignment | only the inputs listed in a capability's `$rules` reach `handle()` | default |
| Passwords | `password_hash` in the shipped sign-up, `password_verify` at sign-in | default |
| Session fixation | `Route::auth` gives a new session id and a new CSRF token at sign-in and sign-out | default |
| Session cookie | `HttpOnly`, and `Secure` on HTTPS (also behind a load balancer that says so) | default |
| Token scopes | a write capability without a `scope` needs a token with the scope named after it, or `*`; read-only and public ones need none; REST, MCP and command-line tokens are all checked, 403 otherwise; `doctor` lists the unscoped writes | **default since 2.26.0** |
| N+1 queries | calling a relation method on one of several rows a query read throws `[ERROR 2004]` in development with the `with()` fix, and logs a warning in production; `->lazy()` or `#[Caligrafy\Lazy]` allow one | **default since 2.26.0** |
| Shared caches | an answer that sets a cookie, goes to a signed-in person or a token, or is not a 200 is never marked public | default (2.26.0) |
| Webhook signatures | `Route::webhook` refuses to register without `verify` (`'stripe'` checks `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) | one line |
| Personal access tokens | shown once, stored as SHA-256, revocable, with an expiry | one command |

Settings that turn a default off, for a migration period only:

- `TOKEN_DEFAULT_SCOPES=false` (deprecated): any token may call a write capability without a scope, as before 2.26.0.
- `STRICT_RELATIONS=false`: the N+1 check warns instead of throwing in development.

`php caligrafer.php doctor` reports both, with the fix.


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Support-and-Release-Policy -->

Which versions of Caligrafy Quill get fixes, and for how long. Since 2.26.0.

## Versions

Caligrafy Quill follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org): a **major** version (3.0) can break projects, a
**minor** version (2.26) adds features, a **patch** version (2.26.1) only fixes. Each release is a git tag `v<version>`
on [GitHub](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/releases) and
[Packagist](https://packagist.org/packages/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill), and its changes are in the
[changelog](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).

## What is supported

| Release | Bug fixes | Security fixes |
|---|---|---|
| The latest minor (today 2.26) | yes | yes |
| The minor before it | no | for 12 months after the next minor shipped |
| Older minors | no | no |

- **Security fixes** are released as patch versions of each supported minor (2.25.x while it is supported).
- **Bug fixes** go to the latest minor only: move up with `php caligrafer.php update`, which updates the framework,
  the plugin and your templates and keeps your code (see [updating Caligrafy](Updating-Caligrafy)).
- **There is no long-term support (LTS) release yet.** It will be announced here when there is one.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue: use GitHub's
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/security/advisories/new) for the
repository. You get an answer, and the fix ships as a patch release of every supported minor.

## Upgrading

Each minor release has its release notes (linked from the sidebar), with what changed and what to check after
`php caligrafer.php update`; `php caligrafer.php doctor` reports what a project should change.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/10.-Claude-Code-Plugin -->

Caligrafy Quill ships with its own **[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) plugin**, `caligrafy-quill`, in the [`claude-plugin/`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/tree/master/claude-plugin) folder of every project. When you open a project in Claude Code, Claude knows the framework from its source: capabilities, the declarative routes, the query builder, models, Pug views, authentication, payments, Vue apps, bots, face detection, machine learning and the AI integrations. It builds the Caligrafy way, **build once, experience everywhere**: a feature becomes a capability, and every experience (pages, Vue apps, REST, AI agents) calls it. With `/caligrafy-quill:idea` it goes from your idea to an app online: **Describe it. Approve it. Ship it.**

Current version: **1.40.0**, for Caligrafy Quill v2.28.0.
## <a name="whatyouget"></a>What the plugin gives Claude

| Component | Name | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skill (automatic) | `caligrafy` | The framework knowledge: every page of this wiki, an API reference and 148 verified gotchas (G1-G148) written from the framework source, UI guidelines for every new page, and recipes for AI chat apps and face login. Claude Code loads it whenever it works in a Caligrafy project |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:idea` | Your idea turned into a complete app online, with one confirmation: the plan, the project, every feature as a capability, the checks, then GitHub and Caligrafy Cloud |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:new-capability` | One capability, served to the channels you need (REST, the JavaScript client, pages and forms, MCP), with a token and tests |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:new-resource` | A table, its model, its five CRUD capabilities, their REST routes, pages and forms |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:assistant` | Snap Cards and the assistant: every capability as a card, a Home that shows what needs you, a conversation that answers with cards (`Route::snap()`, 2.23.0) |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:new-app` | A client app in `public/<name>` (Vue as a library, a Vite SPA, a Watson bot, face detection, machine learning) and its routes |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:server` | Starts, stops or checks the Docker development server |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:db` | Runs SQL scripts and migrations, lists tables, runs queries |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:mobile` | An iOS and Android app of the project (2.27.0): created, signed in through the site, with notifications, checked on a simulator, and published to TestFlight and Google Play; it walks you through the Apple and Google accounts |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:design` | Restyles every page after a design style (`DESIGN_STYLE`), with one stylesheet |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:ship` | Puts the project on GitHub and Caligrafy Cloud by itself |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:deploy` | Checks the project is ready for production, then deploys it to Caligrafy Cloud or prepares it for your own server |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace` | Packages an app on Caligrafy Cloud for the marketplace of caligrafy.com and submits it |
| Command | `/caligrafy-quill:update` | Updates the project to the latest release and merges every `.caligrafy-new` file |
| Agent | `caligrafy-reviewer` | Reviews your Caligrafy code for framework bugs and security issues; it never edits files |
| Hook | `php -l` | After Claude writes or edits a `.php` file, checks its syntax and sends an error back to Claude (skipped when PHP is not installed) |

Claude also runs `php caligrafer.php doctor` first when something does not work. The [plugin changelog](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/claude-plugin/README.md#changelog) lists what each version added, and each [release note](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-2.19.0) names the plugin version that follows it.
## <a name="install"></a>Installing the plugin

### With a project (recommended)

Every project has a `.claude/settings.json` that registers the plugin's source (a "marketplace": the project folder, through `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) and enables the plugin. `initialize` (and so `quickstart`) gives that source the project's own name, `caligrafy-<folder>-<4 letters>`, and `.bin/caligrafer quickstart` registers it with Claude Code when the `claude` command is installed. Open the project and accept the **"trust this folder"** prompt:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --docker
claude
```

**Check:** type `/caligrafy-quill:` in Claude Code: the commands of the table above are listed. `php caligrafer.php doctor` has a line `Claude Code plugin: caligrafy-quill@caligrafy-<name>`.

### From GitHub, in any folder

In Claude Code:
```text
/plugin marketplace add caligrafy/caligrafy-quill
/plugin install caligrafy-quill@caligrafy
```
or in a terminal:
```bash
claude plugin marketplace add caligrafy/caligrafy-quill
claude plugin install caligrafy-quill@caligrafy
```
The source from GitHub is named `caligrafy` and the plugin `caligrafy-quill`, hence `caligrafy-quill@caligrafy`.

### When a command such as `/caligrafy-quill:design` is unknown

Claude Code keeps one plugin source per name for the whole computer. Projects made before 2.10.1 all named their source `caligrafy`: the first project opened won, the others got its (older) plugin, and none got one once that folder was deleted. In the project, on your computer:
```bash
php caligrafer.php plugin
```
It gives the source the project's own name, registers it (`claude plugin marketplace add`), installs the plugin for the project (`claude plugin install ... --scope project`), and prints `Plugin source: caligrafy-<name>, plugin caligrafy-quill@caligrafy-<name>`. Restart `claude` in the folder. `doctor` warns when a project still shares the name or its plugin is read from another folder.

### When a new skill is missing after an update

Claude Code runs a copy of the plugin made when it was installed, not the project's `claude-plugin/` folder. `php caligrafer.php update` and `php caligrafer.php plugin` refresh that copy when the project's plugin is newer, and `doctor` warns while it is older (`Claude Code runs caligrafy-quill X, this project has Y`). When the update ran in Docker, where `claude` is not installed, run `php caligrafer.php plugin` on your computer in the project folder. Then restart `claude`.
## <a name="commands"></a>Commands

### `/caligrafy-quill:idea <your idea>`
The [Quickstart with Claude](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude). Claude:
1. **Describe it**: turns the idea into a plan (a name, 1 to 3 tables, 4 to 12 capabilities, who may do what, one page per main table, sample data; jobs, alerts and background work only when the idea needs them) and waits for your OK.
2. **Approve it**: sets the project up (`.bin/caligrafer quickstart`, after checking Docker and the ports), writes each table's `create_db.sql` and model, each capability with `php caligrafer.php service`, sign-in with `Route::auth` (a username by default; an email when the plan says so, [kept in the `username` column](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#emailsignin)), the pages with `Route::page` and `Route::form`, the REST routes, the JavaScript client, a card where signed-in people create a token for their AI agents, and tests; then checks every capability (`call`), REST, the page at desktop and phone width, MCP, `test`, `doctor` and a review by `caligrafy-reviewer`, and shows you the app locally.
3. **Ship it**: follows `/caligrafy-quill:ship`.

Your OK at the plan covers everything after it, the framework's `.git` included. You only approve sign-ins in the browser pages Claude opens, and say yes before credits are spent. "Stop before putting it online" makes it wait after the checks.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:idea A reading list: I add books I want to read, mark them as read, and rate them from 1 to 5.
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:new-capability <capability_name> [scope] [read-only|destructive]`
Scaffolds the class with `php caligrafer.php service <Folder>/<Name> --scope <scope>`, writes its description for agents, its `$rules`, `$filters` and `$descriptions`, and a `handle()` that reads with the query builder and refuses with `ServiceError`. It adds the channels you ask for in `web.php`: `Route::capability`, `Route::capabilities` and the JavaScript client, `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::download`, `Route::webhook`, `Route::action` (a web-only capability, for what a page or a form cannot say), `Route::mcp`. It creates a token when an agent needs one, checks every channel (`capabilities`, `call`, REST with and without the scope, MCP `tools/list` and `tools/call`, `audit`), writes a test, and asks `caligrafy-reviewer` to review. Learn more in [Build Once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:new-resource <Entity> [field:type ...]`
Capabilities first, every request declared:
+ `application/models/<Entity>/create_db.sql`: the table, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, an `id` primary key, `<model>_id` foreign keys with unique constraint names;
+ `application/models/<Entity>/<Entity>.php`: the model, one public property per column, its relationships;
+ `list_`, `get_`, `create_`, `update_` and `delete_` capabilities in `application/services/<Entities>/`, the only code that touches the model;
+ their REST routes (`Route::capability`), the pages (`Route::page` with their data from the capabilities) and the forms (`Route::form`) in `web.php`, and the views when you want HTML pages.

Then it offers to run the SQL (`/caligrafy-quill:db`), calls each capability, writes a test and asks for a review. Field types: `string`, `text`, `int`, `decimal`, `bool`, `date`, `datetime`, `json`; `name:fk` is a foreign key to the model `Name`.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book title:string author:string publisher:fk
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:new-app <app | create | bot | facedetect | ml> <name>`
Runs the Caligrafer scaffold into `public/<name>`, adds its page route, prefers capabilities and the JavaScript client for its data, and opens it to check the browser console.
+ `app`: Vue 3 as a library
+ `create`: a Vite Vue single page application (Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ on your computer)
+ `bot`: an IBM Watson bot
+ `facedetect`: face detection and recognition (`@vladmandic/face-api` 1.7.15)
+ `ml`: ML Core (ml5 and p5)

The names `app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`, `ml`, `resources` and `uploads` are reserved. The `caligrafy` skill carries two complete recipes Claude follows: **AI chat apps** (OpenAI, Groq, or an open model on OpenRouter or Ollama) and **face login** (face prints checked on the server, with a lockout; a photo can pass, so use it as a convenience or a second factor).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app facedetect faceauth
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:assistant [what the app is about]`
Gives the project [Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant) (2.23.0): adds `Route::snap();` to `web.php`, runs `php caligrafer.php snap install`, writes the hints of `application/config/snap.php` from your capabilities (names, columns, the assistant's lines, Home's numbers with their actions, what Home invites to browse, when an action applies), marks slow capabilities `async: true` (a Track card: Task in the background), adds the queue and routines jobs, asks before setting an Anthropic API key (you type it in a hidden prompt), and checks `/assistant` and `/snap`.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:assistant a library app: books, authors and loans
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:server <start | stop | status>`
Checks that Docker runs, that the ports (8080, 8077, 3306) are free, and that `.env` has the Docker settings (`DB_HOST=mysql`, an empty `APP_ROOT`), then starts or stops the server and checks the site answers. When a port is taken it gives the project other ports with a `docker-compose.override.yml`; behind a company proxy that inspects TLS ("self-signed certificate in certificate chain"), it gives the container the company's root certificate. See [Getting Started](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/1.-Getting-Started#using-docker).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:server start
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:db <script.sql | tables | query "SQL">`
Runs SQL on the project's MySQL: in the Docker `mysql` container, or a local MySQL with the `DB_*` settings of `.env` (never printing the password).
+ `<script.sql>`: a script such as `application/models/Book/create_db.sql` (the one `new-resource` writes) or `application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql`. Scripts with `DROP`, `TRUNCATE` or `DELETE` are shown first and need your OK. A change to a table that holds data becomes a migration (`php caligrafer.php migrate make <name>`, then `migrate`).
+ `tables`: the tables and their row counts.
+ `query "SQL"`: read-only queries; Claude asks before a statement that writes.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:db application/models/Book/create_db.sql
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:design [style | off]`
Reads a whole `DESIGN.md` (84 styles from VoltAgent/awesome-design-md in `framework/design/vendor/`, `interstellar` in `framework/design/local/`, or yours in `application/design/<name>/`), writes one stylesheet, `public/css/designs/<style>.css`, loaded after the Caligrafy stylesheets, sets `DESIGN_STYLE` in `.env`, and checks the sign-in pages and your pages in a browser at desktop and phone width. Caligrafy's files and your views are not edited. `off` brings the Caligrafy look back. Without a style it asks which one. See [Design styles](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:design linear.app
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:ship [app-name] [--public]`
Checks the project is ready (no `.env` in git, the scripts safe to run again, the tests), commits, then creates the GitHub repository (private unless `--public`) and pushes it: with your SSH key when GitHub knows it, else over HTTPS with the GitHub CLI, else after installing the GitHub CLI and a code you approve on GitHub's page. It signs in to Caligrafy Cloud with a code you approve on deploy.caligrafy.com (sign up there the first time), creates the app, adds its read-only deploy key to the repository, deploys, and checks the address answers. It never asks for or prints a password, token or key, and asks before spending credits. Run it again after a change: it pushes and deploys again.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:ship myapp
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:deploy [app-name] [--own-server]`
First a read-only check, point by point: Caligrafy Quill 2.4.0 or later, `Dockerfile` and `composer.lock`, no secrets in git, `create_db.sql` scripts safe to run again, no changed migration, the tests, the payment keys, everything committed and pushed. Then it deploys to [Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#cloud) with `php caligrafer.php cloud` (`cloud login` approved in your browser), or, with `--own-server`, prepares the project for [Coolify or Docker](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#ownserver). For a deploy without any hand-off, use `/caligrafy-quill:ship`.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:deploy myapp
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace [app-name]`
For an app on Caligrafy Cloud that you offered on its page. Claude reads the whole code, runs the app on your computer as a separate Docker project with invented data, and takes screenshots of its key features (5 at most, all different, 1280x800). It writes the title, the description, the prompt that recreates the app with Caligrafy and an estimated price window from a short market study into one private file, `.caligrafy/marketplace.json`, then sends it with `php caligrafer.php cloud submit` and redeploys the app. It often takes 15 to 30 minutes. Caligrafy reviews the listing, sets the final price and publishes it; you earn 25% of every sale. See [the marketplace](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#marketplace).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:marketplace myapp
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:mobile [name] [publish]`
Gives the project its iOS and Android app (Caligrafy Quill 2.27.0+). Claude agrees the app id with you (it is for life), runs `php caligrafer.php mobile`, adds `Route::mobile` to `web.php`, builds the screens on your capabilities and checks them in a browser at phone size and on a simulator, then sets up notifications. With `publish` it goes through what the stores need with you, one step at a time: the Apple Developer and Google Play accounts, the apps in App Store Connect and Play Console, the keys, and the repository's secrets, which you type yourself. Then `/caligrafy-quill:ship` sends each release to TestFlight and Google Play. See [Phone and tablet apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.7-Phone-and-Tablet-Apps).
```text
/caligrafy-quill:mobile bingo
/caligrafy-quill:mobile bingo publish
```

### `/caligrafy-quill:update [version]`
Asks you to commit uncommitted work first, shows what [`php caligrafer.php update`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#update) will change, applies it, then merges every `.caligrafy-new` file into your version: your changes kept, the release's added, and a note where both rewrote the same lines. It ends with `version`, `doctor` and `upgrade --local`. A project before 2.9.0 gets the command first.
```text
/caligrafy-quill:update
```
## <a name="reviewer"></a>The `caligrafy-reviewer` agent

It reads the files you name (or your latest changes under `application/`, `tests/`, `public/<app>/` and the SQL scripts), with the framework source and the gotchas as ground truth, and reports findings by severity, each with `file:line`, the failure, the gotcha and a fix. It checks, among others: SQL built from input, CSRF and request header mistakes, route problems, unsafe uploads, outdated templates and libraries, foreign key and pivot schemas, exposed secrets, model code outside capabilities, and since 2.19 a new controller where a declarative route fits, `where` strings the query builder should write, and N+1 loops. It only reads (tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash). Ask in plain words:
```text
Review the Books capabilities and web.php with the caligrafy-reviewer agent
```
## <a name="tryit"></a>Try it

A first session in a project set up with the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart):
```text
/caligrafy-quill:server status
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Author name:string bio:text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book title:string published_year:int summary:text author:fk
/caligrafy-quill:db application/models/Author/create_db.sql
/caligrafy-quill:db application/models/Book/create_db.sql
Turn on sign-in with Route::auth, and let only signed-in people add books
Review the Books capabilities with the caligrafy-reviewer agent
```
`new-resource` writes one folder per entity (`application/models/Book/`, `application/services/Books/`, `application/views/Books/`). The by-hand pages and the [course](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course) keep the same Bookshelf in `application/models/Bookshelf/`, `application/services/Bookshelf/` and `application/views/Bookshelf/`: both work, the folders are only for you.

**Check** what Claude wrote before you say OK: the capabilities in `php caligrafer.php capabilities` with the scopes you expect, no `public: true` on a capability that changes data unless you want it, `Route::form` for each form and `Route::action` for what a page or a form cannot say, no new controller, and the page in your browser.
## <a name="knowledge"></a>How the plugin's knowledge is maintained

For contributors to the framework:
+ The numbered files of `skills/caligrafy/reference/` and `wiki-sidebar.md` mirror the pages of this wiki, with a link to the source page at the top of each. Refresh them with `python3 claude-plugin/scripts/sync-wiki.py <wiki clone>`; `--check` exits with `1` when a mirror is stale.
+ `api-reference.md` and `gotchas.md` are written by hand from the framework source. When they and the wiki disagree, the source-verified files win.
+ After a change to `framework/`: update them, run the [QA suite](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Caligrafy#qa), bump `version` in `claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and the "Current version" line of this page, and follow the [release process](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Caligrafy#release).
+ Load the plugin from a folder with `claude --plugin-dir ./claude-plugin`; validate it with `claude plugin validate ./claude-plugin --strict`.
> **Safety notes**
> + `php caligrafer.php initialize --yes` deletes the `.git` folder (without `--yes` it asks in a terminal and keeps it otherwise). Claude asks before running it in a git repository.
> + Claude never prints or commits the secrets of your `.env`, and approvals for GitHub and Caligrafy Cloud happen in your browser.

# API reference

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0: every public class, method and helper function of the framework, generated from the source at each release by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`. Each method shows its signature, its doc comment as written in the code, its parameters, what it returns and the line of the source it is on.

The guides of the wiki explain how to use these classes; start with [How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works).

<a name="action"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Action

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Action
```

Source: [framework/core/Action.php:27](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Action.php#L27)

Class Action (2.21.0)
Route::action('/connect', 'cloud_connect') answers a request with a capability declared webOnly: true, for what a
page or a form cannot say: a sign-in between two sites, a session that decides where to go, a gate, a payment page.
1. access: the 'signedIn', 'level', 'comeBack' and 'visitorsOnly' options of Route::page
2. the capability is called with the query string or the form, and the route variables (which win), as the person who sent it, with its rules, permissions and audit log like any capability
3. its answer goes to the browser: a Caligrafy\Web (a view, a redirect, JSON, text), or JSON of the plain data A JSON call needs the page's X-CSRF-Token or an API token, signed in or not ([ERROR 1004], 401)
4. a refusal it does not answer itself is treated as in Route::form: invalid input or a conflict goes back with errors(), old() and flash('error'); a visitor goes to sign in; forbidden is 403, anything else 404. JSON requests get the REST error.
Unlike every other capability, it may read the session and the request and may sign people in, and a GET may change
data: so a webOnly capability is reachable through Route::action only, never through REST, MCP, the JS client,
Route::page, Route::form or a controller.

### Methods

+ [`Action::handle()`](#action-handle)
+ [`Action::answer()`](#action-answer)

<a name="form"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Form

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Form
```

Source: [framework/core/Form.php:29](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Form.php#L29)

Class Form (2.19.0)
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' =&gt; '/books/{id}', 'flash' =&gt; 'Book added']) answers the form's POST
(or its PUT / DELETE through \_method) with a capability, without a controller:
1. the CSRF token of the form is checked by the request, as for every form (error 3000, 403)
2. the capability is called with the form fields, the files of its `file` inputs (Uploads) and the route variables (which win), as the person who sent the form (Context::fromRequest(..., 'web'))
3. success: a redirect to 'success' (a path whose {placeholders} are filled from the result, then from the route variables, or a callable($result) returning the path; without it, back to the form), with the 'flash' message (also with placeholders) for flash('success')
4. invalid input (or a conflict): back to the form ('back', else the Referer of this site, else /) with the field errors, the message and the old input for the next request: errors($field), old($field), flash('error')
5. a visitor where the capability needs someone: to the sign-in page ('signIn', default /login) when Auth is active, else 403; forbidden: 403 (error 1006); not found: 404 (error 1005)
A JSON request (Accept: application/json) gets the REST answer instead of redirects: {"data": ...} with 200 (201 for a
POST that changes data), or {"error": ...} with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422. Sent with the session cookie, it needs the
X-CSRF-Token header, as REST.

### Constants

+ `SECRET = '/pass|secret|token|card|cvc|cvv|iban/i'`: fields never kept as old input

### Methods

<a name="download"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Download

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Download
```

Source: [framework/core/Download.php:32](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Download.php#L32)

Class Download (2.19.0)
Route::download('/books.csv', 'list_books', ['as' =&gt; 'csv', 'filename' =&gt; 'books.csv']) answers a GET with the result
of a read-only capability as an attachment, without a controller:

- inputs: the query string and the route variables (which win), as the person who opens the link (Context::fromRequest(..., 'web')); the capability must be readOnly (a link must not change data)
- 'as' =&gt; 'csv' (default): RFC 4180 (CRLF, fields with a comma, a quote or a line break in double quotes, quotes doubled), UTF-8, the header row from the first row's keys; 'bom' =&gt; true starts the file with a UTF-8 BOM (Excel); text cells that start with = + - @ or a tab are prefixed with ' so that spreadsheets do not run them as formulas ('formulas' =&gt; true keeps them as they are); arrays in a cell are written as JSON, booleans as true / false. 'as' =&gt; 'json': the result, pretty-printed
- 'as' =&gt; 'zip' (2.22.0): the files the capability lists, in one ZIP archive streamed from a temporary file. Each item is a path (the file keeps its name) or ['file' =&gt; path, 'name' =&gt; 'folder/name in the archive']; a page of paginate() gives its rows. Paths are relative to 'root', a folder of the project (default 'public/uploads'): a file outside it, or missing, is left out, so a link never reaches other files. Duplicate names get " (2)". Images, video, audio and archives are stored as they are, other files compressed. No file at all: 404 (error 1005). Needs the PHP zip extension (in Caligrafy's Docker images and on Caligrafy Cloud)
- 'filename': a name, or a callable($result, $input) returning one (default: the capability's name)
- refusals as Route::page: a visitor is sent to sign in when Auth is active, else 403 (error 1006); forbidden 403; anything else 404 (error 1005)

### Constants

+ `FORMATS = array('csv', 'json', 'zip')`
+ `STORED = ...`

### Methods

+ [`Download::columns()`](#download-columns)
+ [`Download::format()`](#download-format)

<a name="webhook"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Webhook

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Webhook
```

Source: [framework/core/Webhook.php:24](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Webhook.php#L24)

Class Webhook (2.19.0)
Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_payment', ['verify' =&gt; 'stripe']) answers the POSTs of another service with
a capability, without a controller:

- no CSRF token (the sender has no session): the signature of the body proves who sent it. 'verify' is required: 'stripe' checks the Stripe-Signature header with \Stripe\Webhook::constructEvent and the secret in the variable 'secret_env' names (default STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), with 'tolerance' seconds (default 300); a callable function (string $rawBody, array $headers): bool checks anything else (headers with lower-case names)
- the raw body (php://input) must be JSON; the capability gets ['event' =&gt; the decoded body], as the system (Context::system('webhook', $path)): declare public $rules = ['event' =&gt; 'required']
- answers: 200 {"received": true}; 400 for a bad signature or a body that is not JSON; the status of a ServiceError; 500 for anything else (written to the PHP error log)

### Public properties

+ `public static $logger = null`: callable|null replaces error_log() (tests)

### Methods

+ [`Webhook::handle()`](#webhook-handle)
+ [`Webhook::process()`](#webhook-process)
+ [`Webhook::verify()`](#webhook-verify)

<a name="uploads"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Uploads

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Uploads
```

Source: [framework/core/Uploads.php:28](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Uploads.php#L28)

Class Uploads (2.19.0)
A capability declares a file input with the rule `file`, an optional allow-list and an optional maximum size:

```
public $rules = ['cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'];
```

- web pages (Route::form) and REST (Route::capability, Route::capabilities) take the field from $_FILES once the caller is allowed to call the capability, check it (one file, the allow-list - never an executable type, see isAllowedUpload() - and the size), save it in public/uploads under a new random name with uploadFile() (the name the client sent is never used) and give handle() the saved file's public URL, a string. A value sent in that field without a file is dropped. The saved file is deleted when the call fails afterwards.
- MCP and the command line cannot send files: the field is a URL or a path string; its extension is checked against the allow-list.

The file rules (file, extension, max_size, required_file) are never given to GUMP: Service::validate() strips them.
A field with required_file (or required) and no file is invalid: 'The &lt;Field&gt; field needs a file' (2.19.1).
Without `extension` the allow-list is DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXTENSIONS.

### Constants

+ `RULES = array('file', 'extension', 'max_size', 'required_file')`

### Methods

<a name="throttle"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Throttle

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Throttle
```

Source: [framework/core/Throttle.php:19](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Throttle.php#L19)

Class Throttle (2.19.0)

```
$throttle = new Throttle(5, 900);          // 5 failures within 15 minutes lock the key for the rest of them
if ($throttle->locked($key)) ...; $throttle->fail($key); $throttle->clear($key);
```

The counts are kept in the Cache (CACHE_STORE: the caligrafy_cache table or a private folder, shared by every
session, so that a new cookie does not start again), or in the session when the cache is off.
Each failure keeps the count for $seconds more.

### Public properties

+ `public $max`: int
+ `public $seconds`: int

### Methods

## class Caligrafy\Flash

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Flash
```

Source: [framework/core/Flash.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Flash.php#L20)

Class Flash (2.19.0)
Route::form() puts the field errors, the old input and a message here before it redirects; the page of the next
request reads them with the view helpers errors($field), old($field) and flash($key), then they are gone.
Route::run() ages them when there are some: what the previous request put becomes this request's, and leaves the
session (without Route::run, the first read does).

Kept in $_SESSION['__flash'] as ['errors' =&gt; [field =&gt; message], 'old' =&gt; [field =&gt; value], 'messages' =&gt; [key =&gt; text]].

+ `KEY = '__flash'`

<a name="context"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Context

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Context
```

Source: [framework/core/Context.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Context.php#L23)

Class Context
Built by the channel adapters (web pages, REST, MCP, CLI) and read by the services: a service never looks at the
request, the session or the headers itself.

The actor is one of:

- user: a signed-in user (session), or the owner of a token
- token: a personal access token (Tokens), with its scopes
- key: the legacy API key (every generated key is the same key: full access, as before 2.1)
- cli: a script or the command line (full access); a scheduled job is a system context on this channel
- guest: nobody: only public capabilities

### Constants

+ `CHANNELS = array('web', 'rest', 'mcp', 'cli')`

### Public properties

+ `public static $levelAttribute = 'permissions'`: Name of the users column that holds the permission level compared with a capability's level (Auth::guard)
+ `public $channel`: string web, rest, mcp or cli
+ `public $viaAction = false`: bool the call comes from Route::action() (2.21.0): the only way to a webOnly capability
+ `public $user`: object|null the user model (signed in, or the owner of the token)
+ `public $token`: array|null the token row (id, name, scopes, user_id...)

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#context-construct)
+ [`Context::cli()`](#context-cli)
+ [`Context::local()`](#context-local)

<a name="route-resolvecontroller"></a>
### `Route::resolveController()`

```php
public static function resolveController($name)
```

Resolves the controller part of a 'Controller@action' route to a declared class name

- fully qualified names are accepted, with or without a leading backslash: 'Shop\OrderController', '\Shop\OrderController'
- a declared class always wins (a project's own global AIController is used as is)
- a short name that is not a declared class falls back to the framework example controllers namespace (Caligrafy\Controllers), so routes written before 1.6 such as 'AIController@query' keep working

**Parameters**

+ `$name` `string`: defines the controller part of the route

**Returns** `string|null`: the class name, or null when no such controller exists

Source: [framework/core/Route.php:268](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Route.php#L268)

<a name="route-page"></a>
### `Route::page()`

```php
public static function page($route, $view, array $options = array())
```

A page: renders a view through the framework's page controller, which gives every page who is signed in and,
optionally, an access rule and data from capabilities (pages never read models):

```
Route::page('/books', 'Books/index');
Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Books/show', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']]);
Route::page('/admin/books', 'Books/admin', ['level' => 1, 'data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
```

Options: 'signedIn' (bool), 'level' (int), 'data' (name =&gt; read-only capability, or [capability, inputs]),
'with' (fixed values), 'notFound' (a view shown with a 404 when a data capability finds nothing);
2.20.0: 'visitorsOnly' (a path: signed-in people are sent there), 'comeBack' (true: a visitor goes to
/login?return=&lt;this page&gt;), 'query' (the names of the query string the view gets)

**Parameters**

+ `$route` `string`: the uri
+ `$view` `string`: the view, as for view()
+ `$options` `array`, default `array()`: see PageController::render()

Source: [framework/core/Route.php:357](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Route.php#L357)

```php
public static function pages()
```

The pages declared with Route::page (2.24.0): each with its route, its view and its options (its data
capabilities), so that a capability can be shown through the page designed for it

**Returns** `array`: of ['route' =&gt; 'books/{id}', 'view' =&gt; 'Bookshelf/book', 'options' =&gt; [...]]

<a name="route-action"></a>
### `Route::action()`

```php
public static function action($route, $capability, array $options = array())
```

A request answered by a web-only capability (2.21.0, Caligrafy\Action): for what Route::page and Route::form
cannot say, such as a sign-in between two sites, a gate or a payment page. The capability is declared
#[Capability(..., webOnly: true)] and may return a Caligrafy\Web.

```
Route::action('/connect', 'cloud_connect');
Route::action('/unlock/{name}', 'unlock_app', ['method' => 'POST']);
```

Options: 'method' ('GET' by default, 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE' or a list), 'signedIn', 'level', 'comeBack',
'visitorsOnly' (as Route::page), 'back', 'error' and 'signIn' (as Route::form, for a refusal it does not answer)

**Parameters**

+ `$route`
+ `$capability`
+ `$options` `array`, default `array()`

Source: [framework/core/Route.php:382](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Route.php#L382)

<a name="route-snap"></a>
### `Route::snap()`

```php
public static function snap(array $options = array())
```

Snap Cards and the assistant (2.23.0, Caligrafy\Snap): every capability of the app as a card, and an assistant
that answers with them, in one line of web.php:

```
Route::snap();
Route::snap(['assistant' => '/help', 'cards' => '/cards']);
```

It declares, for the signed-in person:

```
/assistant              Home (what needs you, insights, things to browse, shortcuts) and the task space
/assistant/ask          what they typed, said, attached or clicked (snap_ask)
/assistant/noticed      what the assistant noticed, and their routines (a settings page)
/snap                   every card they may use (a gallery), /snap/c/{capability} one card at its own address
/snap/run, /snap/call/  a card sent (snap_run), and the snap_* capabilities the pages call
```

The tables come with php caligrafer.php platform install; card hints are in application/config/snap.php; the
assistant uses Claude when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set (else it answers from the cards' names, without a model).
Changes only ever run from a Confirm the person clicks (Caligrafy\Snap\Consent).

**Parameters**

+ `$options` `array`, default `array()`: 'assistant' (the path of the assistant, '/assistant'), 'cards' (the path of the cards, '/snap')

<a name="route-form"></a>
### `Route::form()`

```php
public static function form($route, $capability, array $options = array())
```

A form without a controller (2.19.0, Caligrafy\Form): the form's POST calls a capability, then redirects

```
Route::page('/books/new', 'Books/new');
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Book added']);
Route::form('/books/{id}', 'update_book', ['method' => 'PUT', 'success' => '/books/{id}']);
```

GET stays a Route::page. Options: 'method' (POST, PUT or DELETE, or a list; default POST), 'success' (a path with
{placeholders} from the result and the route, or a callable($result) returning one; default back), 'flash' (a
message for flash('success'), or [key =&gt; message]), 'back' (where invalid input goes; default the Referer of this
site), 'error' (the message for flash('error') instead of the capability's), 'signIn' (default /login);
2.20.0: 'visitorsOnly' (a path: signed-in people are sent there), 'same' ([field =&gt; [other field, message]]),
'accepted' ([field =&gt; message]: a box that must be ticked), 'inputs' (values only the server sets: an array or a
callable($input)), 'signsIn' (the field of the answer that holds the id of the person to sign in), 'signsInWith'
(how: 'password' by default, what AuthRoutes::signedInBy() answers).
'success' may be a full address, or a callable returning one (a payment page).
Invalid input goes back with errors($field), old($field) and flash('error') for the next page. JSON requests get
the REST answer.

**Parameters**

+ `$route`
+ `$capability`
+ `$options` `array`, default `array()`

Source: [framework/core/Route.php:520](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Route.php#L520)



Options: prefix, home ('/'), logout ('/'), register (true, false or the capability), attempts (5), lock (900
seconds), views, passkeys (false), identifier ('username', or the users column people sign in with: 'email'),
signInAfterRegister (false: true signs the new account in and goes 'home'). See AuthRoutes.

# Caligrafy\AuthRoutes

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

Part of [Routing and requests](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Routing).

<a name="authroutes"></a>
```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class AuthRoutes
```

Source: [framework/core/AuthRoutes.php:40](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/AuthRoutes.php#L40)

Class AuthRoutes (2.19.0)
Route::auth() (after Auth::authentication('User', 'users') in web.php) registers, with the views of the
authentication module (application/views/Auth/login.pug and register.pug):

```
GET  /login           the sign-in page (a signed-in person goes to 'home')
POST /login           signs in: the username (or 'identifier') and passcode fields, checked with the model's
                      findByUsername() (another identifier: its findBy($column, $value), else the query builder)
                      and verifyPassword() (an old encrypted passcode is upgraded to a hash); a new session id
                      (session_regenerate_id(true)) and a new CSRF token; then 'home'
GET|POST /logout      signs out: a new session id and CSRF token, then 'logout'
GET  /notAuthorized   where Auth::guard() sends people below the level a page needs (403)
GET|POST /register    the sign-up page and the register_user capability (every input its rules declare), then the
                      sign-in page, or signed in and 'home' with 'signInAfterRegister' ('register' => false: none)
with 'passkeys' => true, the JSON endpoints of Caligrafy\Passkey (the passkeys table of the face login recipe, the
page sends the X-CSRF-Token header; public/js/services/passkey.js in the browser):
POST /passkey/register/options, /passkey/register (signed in), /passkey/login/options, /passkey/login
```

Failed sign-ins are counted per IP and username (Throttle, in the Cache): after 'attempts' (5) within 'lock' seconds
(900) that username is refused from that address (429) until the window ends.
Options: prefix (''), home ('/'), logout ('/'), register (true, or the name of the capability), attempts, lock,
views (['login' =&gt; 'Auth/login', 'register' =&gt; 'Auth/register']), passkeys (false), identifier ('username': the
users column people sign in with and the name of its field, 'email' for instance), signInAfterRegister (false),
attemptsPerUser (2.19.6: failures of one username from any address before it is locked, 0 = off), level (2.19.5: the lowest permission level that may sign in, 0 by default; below it, the sign-in is refused like a
wrong password), messages (what sign-in and sign-up say: 'invalid', 'locked' ({minutes} is the wait), 2.19.3; 'mismatch',
'register_invalid', 'register_taken', 'registered', 2.19.4; see AuthRoutes::MESSAGES).
A failed sign-in shows the page again with what the person typed in the identifier field (never the password).
A JSON request (Accept: application/json) gets JSON answers and needs the X-CSRF-Token header.
Not provided by the framework, so refused with a LogicException: 'face' (the face login recipe has its own
controller and tables) and 'reset' (password reset: the users table has no email address).

## Constants

+ `RETURN_TO = '__auth_return'`: the session key of the page to go back to after signing in (2.20.0)
+ `SIGNED_IN_BY = '__auth_signed_in_by'`: the session key of how this session signed in (2.21.3)
+ `DUMMY_HASH = '$2y$10$B0NLUgDUK3CbImwrVfa/FuOtSOKrb7DZTGG3USPSF4Comn4cy5RtG'`
+ `MESSAGES = ...`

## Public properties

+ `public static $signUp = null`: bool|null whether a Route::auth of this request has a sign-up page (null: no Route::auth)
+ `public static $regenerate = null`: callable|null replaces session_regenerate_id(true) (tests)

<a name="pagecontroller"></a>
## class Caligrafy\PageController

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class PageController extends Controller
```

Source: [framework/core/PageController.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/PageController.php#L25)

Class PageController
Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Books/show', ['data' =&gt; ['book' =&gt; 'get_book']]) renders a view through this controller:
1. access: 'signedIn' =&gt; true sends visitors to /login; 'level' =&gt; N also sends people below level N to /notAuthorized (Auth::guard on Context::$levelAttribute)
2. data: each 'data' entry calls a read-only capability as the person who opens the page ($this-&gt;call(): the same rules as REST and MCP), with the query string and the route variables as inputs (the route variables win), or with the inputs it lists (['book' =&gt; ['get_book', ['id' =&gt; 3]]]). A refusal becomes the page's answer: a visitor is sent to sign in; otherwise 403 (error 1006) or 404 (error 1005), or the 'notFound' view (route variables, 'with', 'message', who opens it) with a 404 status
3. the view gets the route variables, 'with' values, the data, 'authorized' and 'user' (id, username, level) - never the query string
Pages never read models: capabilities do, so a page, REST and AI agents follow the same rules.

### Constants

+ `RESERVED = array('authorized', 'user')`

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#pagecontroller-construct)
+ [`->render()`](#pagecontroller-render)

#### `View::cache()`

```php
public static function cache()
```

Compiled templates are kept between requests: a view is compiled to PHP once, then again only when it or a file
it includes or extends changes. On by default; VIEW_CACHE=false compiles every view on every request. A project
that sets Phug's cache_dir itself keeps its own. Returns the folder used, or null (no cache). Also sets Phug's
debug mode from APP_DEBUG.

<a name="designs"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Designs

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Designs
```

Source: [framework/core/Designs.php:21](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Designs.php#L21)

Class Designs
A style is a DESIGN.md and the override stylesheet written from it, public/css/designs/&lt;name&gt;.css. DESIGN.md files
are looked up in this order, the first one wins on a name clash:

```
application/design/<name>/                the project's own styles
framework/design/local/<name>/            styles added to Caligrafy itself
framework/design/vendor/<vendor>/<name>/  collections copied from elsewhere (awesome-design-md...), by vendor name
```

The layout loads that stylesheet after the Caligrafy stylesheets when DESIGN_STYLE names it; an empty DESIGN_STYLE,
an unknown name or a style without its stylesheet keeps Caligrafy's own look.

### Constants

+ `VENDOR = 'framework/design/vendor'`
+ `LOCAL = 'framework/design/local'`
+ `APPLICATION = 'application/design'`
+ `STYLESHEETS = 'public/css/designs'`

<a name="httpcache"></a>
## class Caligrafy\HttpCache

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class HttpCache
```

Source: [framework/core/HttpCache.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/HttpCache.php#L23)

Class HttpCache
A capability declared with cache (#[Capability(..., readOnly: true, public: true, cache: 30)]) answered over REST, or
a page declared with Route::page(..., ['cache' =&gt; 30]), is sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=30 when the
request is a GET or HEAD with no session cookie and no Authorization header: the production image's Apache cache
(docker/production/cache.conf), a CDN or a proxy then answer the next visitors from memory, without PHP.

Never kept: an answer to a signed-in person or a token (it is not marked), an answer that sets a cookie (a session
started while answering: a form's CSRF token) and any answer other than 200: guard() turns them into
Cache-Control: private, no-store just before the headers are sent. Vary: Cookie, Authorization keeps the copy for
visitors without them.

### Constants

+ `MAX = 86400`

### Methods

+ [`HttpCache::publicFor()`](#httpcache-publicfor)
+ [`HttpCache::shareable()`](#httpcache-shareable)
+ [`HttpCache::guard()`](#httpcache-guard)
+ [`HttpCache::reset()`](#httpcache-reset)


Marks the current answer public for $seconds when this request may share it

**Parameters**

+ `$seconds`

**Returns** `bool`: whether it was marked

Source: [framework/core/HttpCache.php:33](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/HttpCache.php#L33)

## abstract class Caligrafy\Service

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

abstract class Service
```

Source: [framework/core/Service.php:34](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Service.php#L34)

Class Service
Extend it in application/services/, declare the inputs and implement handle():

```
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book', scope: 'books:write')]
class CreateBook extends Service {
    public $rules = ['title' => 'required|max_len,255', 'author_id' => 'required|integer'];
    public $filters = ['title' => 'trim|sanitize_string'];
    public $descriptions = ['title' => 'The title of the book'];
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        return (new Book('books'))->create($input);
    }
}
```

- $rules: GUMP validation rules per input. Only the inputs listed here reach handle(); use '' for an input without a rule. They also give the JSON Schema that agents and clients see (Capabilities::schema()). A file input takes the rule 'file' (2.19.0): 'cover' =&gt; 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'. Web pages and REST save the uploaded file and give handle() its public URL; MCP and the command line send a URL or a path (Caligrafy\Uploads).
- $filters: GUMP filters applied before validation.
- handle() returns data (an array, a model, a list of models, a scalar) and throws ServiceError to refuse. It never renders a view, redirects, prints or reads the request or the session: the context says who calls.

### Public properties

+ `public $rules = array()`: array input =&gt; GUMP rules
+ `public $filters = array()`: array input =&gt; GUMP filters
+ `public $descriptions = array()`: array input =&gt; description, for the schema

### Methods

+ [`->handle()`](#service-handle)
+ [`->validate()`](#service-validate)
+ [`->capability()`](#service-capability)
+ [`->run()`](#service-run)

## class Caligrafy\Capability

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Capability
```

Source: [framework/core/Capability.php:17](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Capability.php#L17)

Attribute Capability
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book to the catalog', scope: 'books:write')]
on a class that extends Caligrafy\Service. Its name is how REST, MCP, the JS client and the CLI call it.

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#capability-construct)

<a name="capability-construct"></a>
#### `->__construct()`

```php
public function __construct(
    public string $name,
    public string $description = '',
    public string $scope = '',
    public int $level = 0,
    public bool $readOnly = false,
    public bool $destructive = false,
    public bool $public = false,
    public bool $mcp = true,
    public bool $webOnly = false,
    public bool $async = false,
    public int $cache = 0
)
```

**Parameters**

+ `$name` `string`: snake_case, unique in the application (create_book)
+ `$description` `string`, default `''`: one or two sentences: what it does and returns (shown to agents as the tool description)
+ `$scope` `string`, default `''`: the token scope it needs (books:write); '' = none for a read-only one, its own name for a write one (2.26.0: a token needs the scope create_book, or \*; TOKEN_DEFAULT_SCOPES=false, deprecated: none)
+ `$level` `int`, default `0`: the minimum value of the users permission column (0 = any signed-in user)
+ `$readOnly` `bool`, default `false`: true when it changes nothing (not audited when it succeeds; agents may call it freely)
+ `$destructive` `bool`, default `false`: true when it deletes or overwrites data (agents ask before calling it)
+ `$public` `bool`, default `false`: true when anyone may call it without signing in or a token
+ `$mcp` `bool`, default `true`: false keeps it out of the MCP tools (one only a browser can use, such as a push subscription)
+ `$webOnly` `bool`, default `false`: true (2.21.0): only Route::action() reaches it: it may read the session and sign people in
+ `$async` `bool`, default `false`: true (2.23.0): Snap cards run it in the background as a task; REST, MCP, pages and call run it directly
+ `$cache` `int`, default `0`: seconds (2.26.0): a GET of it over REST by a visitor with no session cookie and no token may be kept by shared caches (the production image's own cache, a CDN) for that long; needs readOnly and public, and an answer that is the same for every visitor

Source: [framework/core/Capability.php:35](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Capability.php#L35)

<a name="capabilities"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Capabilities

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Capabilities
```

Source: [framework/core/Capabilities.php:29](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Capabilities.php#L29)

Class Capabilities
A capability is a class of application/services/ that extends Service and carries #[Capability(...)].
Every channel calls it through call(), which always does the same, in order:
1. finds it (not_found)
2. checks the context: public, or signed in / a token (unauthenticated), with the scope and level (forbidden); a token needs the declared scope, or for a write capability that declares none its own name (scopeOf(), 2.26.0)
3. keeps, filters and validates the declared inputs (invalid)
4. runs handle()
5. writes the audit log: every refusal, and every success of a capability that is not read-only
and returns plain data (models become arrays of their columns).

The registry is built from the classes declared once the capability files are loaded. With the class map (2.26.1)
a call by name (get(), so call(), REST, MCP, the JS client) reads a cache of it instead, kept next to the class map
and out of date as soon as the class map is (a file added, removed or edited) or a file of framework/services
changes: it saves finding and reflecting every service on every request. A name the cache does not have (a class
declared elsewhere, registered by hand) builds the registry as before.

### Constants

+ `CACHE_VERSION = 1`

### Public properties

+ `public static $defaultScopes = null`: bool|null whether a write capability declared without a scope needs the scope named after it from a token (2.26.0): null until the first use reads TOKEN_DEFAULT_SCOPES (false, deprecated: any token, as before)

### Methods

+ [`Capabilities::scopeOf()`](#capabilities-scopeof)
+ [`Capabilities::unscopedWrites()`](#capabilities-unscopedwrites)
+ [`Capabilities::register()`](#capabilities-register)
+ [`Capabilities::all()`](#capabilities-all)
+ [`Capabilities::get()`](#capabilities-get)
+ [`Capabilities::available()`](#capabilities-available)
+ [`Capabilities::call()`](#capabilities-call)
+ [`Capabilities::schema()`](#capabilities-schema)
+ [`Capabilities::schemaFromRules()`](#capabilities-schemafromrules)
+ [`Capabilities::describe()`](#capabilities-describe)

## class Caligrafy\Container

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Container
```

Source: [framework/core/Container.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Container.php#L25)

Class Container (2.18.0)
Capabilities are made by the container, so a service asks for what it uses in its constructor:

```
public function __construct(private Mailer $mailer) {}
```

A class the container has no binding for is built with its constructor's parameters resolved the same way (a class
or interface type -&gt; Container::get, else the parameter's default). Bindings go in application/config/container.php:

```
Container::singleton(PaymentGateway::class, fn () => new StripeGateway(getenv('STRIPE_SECRET')));
Container::bind(Clock::class, SystemClock::class);
```

A test swaps one with Container::instance(Mailer::class, $fake), then Container::reset() forgets it.

### Constants

+ `FILE = 'config/container.php'`

### Methods

+ [`Container::bind()`](#container-bind)
+ [`Container::singleton()`](#container-singleton)
+ [`Container::instance()`](#container-instance)
+ [`Container::has()`](#container-has)

+ [`Container::boot()`](#container-boot)

<a name="tokens"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Tokens

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Tokens
```

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L20)

Class Tokens
A token is `cq_<id>_<secret>`: shown once when it is created, stored only as a SHA-256 hash in caligrafy_tokens
with a name, an optional owner (users.id), its scopes, an optional expiry, the last use and a revocation date.

Scopes are `<resource>:<action>` strings (books:read, books:write). A token scope `*` grants everything and
`books:*` grants every action on books. A capability's own name (create_book) is a scope too (2.26.0): the one a write
capability declared without a scope needs (Capabilities::scopeOf()). Tables: framework/settings/platform.sql (php caligrafer.php platform install).

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_tokens'`
+ `PREFIX = 'cq_'`

### Methods

<a name="tokens-expiresat"></a>
#### `Tokens::expiresAt()`

```php
public static function expiresAt($expiresAt)
```

The expires_at value of an expiry given as a Unix time. Dates are stored in local time (SERVER_TIMEZONE), and when
the clocks fall back the repeated hour names two instants: strtotime() reads its first one. A token created at
01:21 EDT to expire an hour later (01:21 EST) would be refused at once, so an instant of the second occurrence
is stored as the first local time after the repeated hour (02:00): it never stops early, at worst an hour late.

**Parameters**

+ `$expiresAt` `int|string|null`: a Unix time, a local 'Y-m-d H:i:s' (kept as given) or null (never expires)

**Returns** `string|null`

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:96](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L96)
