<a name="migrations"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Migrations

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Migrations
```

Source: [framework/core/Migrations.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Migrations.php#L23)

Class Migrations
application/migrations/&lt;number&gt;_&lt;name&gt;.sql: php caligrafer.php migrate runs, in number order, the files that never
ran on this database, and records each one in caligrafy_migrations (its name, its sha256, when). A file is never run
twice: change the database with a new file, not by editing one that ran (status shows it as "changed", and deploy
warns). The deploy step (php caligrafer.php deploy) runs them after the create_db.sql scripts. Forward only: undo a
change with a new migration.

The statements of a file are split on ; outside quotes and comments. A file stops at its first failing statement:
it is not recorded, the statements before it stay applied (MySQL commits a CREATE or ALTER at once), so write each
file so that it can run again (IF NOT EXISTS), or keep one change per file.

### Constants

+ `FOLDER = 'application/migrations'`
+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_migrations'`
+ `PATTERN = '/^(\d{1,14})_([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\.sql$/'`

### Methods

<a name="cache"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Cache

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Cache
```

Source: [framework/core/Cache.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Cache.php#L25)

Class Cache (2.18.0)

```
$rates = Cache::remember('exchange-rates', 600, fn () => $this->fetchRates());   // at most once every 10 minutes
Cache::put('report:2026-11', $rows, 3600);  Cache::get('report:2026-11', []);  Cache::forget('report:2026-11');
```

CACHE_STORE in .env: database (the default with DB_ACTIVATE=true: the caligrafy_cache table, which the deploy step
and php caligrafer.php platform install create, shared by the web server, the queue, scheduled jobs and every
server), file (the default without a database: a private folder of the temporary directory, of one server and one
system user, so the command line and the web server each have their own) or off (nothing is kept, remember()
always runs its function). Values are stored as JSON: strings, numbers, booleans,
null and arrays (an object comes back as an array). $seconds null keeps a value until it is forgotten or flushed.
php caligrafer.php cache clear empties the store.

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_cache'`
+ `STORES = array('file', 'database', 'off')`

### Methods

+ [`Cache::store()`](#cache-store)
+ [`Cache::get()`](#cache-get)

+ [`Cache::forget()`](#cache-forget)
+ [`Cache::flush()`](#cache-flush)
+ [`Cache::clearMemory()`](#cache-clearmemory)

Source: [framework/core/Model.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Model.php#L20)

Class Model is the base model from which the application models can be extended

## Public properties

+ `public $table`
+ `public static $strictRelations = null`: Lazy loading of relations (2.26.0). A model the query builder read among several rows (Book::where(...)-&gt;get(), paginate(), chunk()) that runs a relation method (hasOne, hasMany, belongsTo, belongsToMany) would run one query per row (N+1): in development that throws [ERROR 2004]; in production (or with STRICT_RELATIONS=false) it logs a warning once per request and relation. $book-&gt;lazy()-&gt;author() allows one call, #[Caligrafy\Lazy] on the relation method allows it always. A model read alone (find(), first(), the instance find() and all()) is not guarded.

# Caligrafy\Query

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

Part of [Data](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Data).

<a name="query"></a>
```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Query
```

Source: [framework/core/Query.php:29](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Query.php#L29)

Class Query
Builds one SQL statement with bound values only. Table and column names are validated against IDENTIFIER and
quoted with backticks, operators come from an allow-list, values are never written into the SQL.

```
Database::table('books')->where('price', '<', 20)->orderBy('title')->limit(10)->get();   // arrays
Book::where('author_id', 3)->with('author', 'tags')->paginate(20);                       // Book models
```

Eager loading (with(), withCount()) runs one more query per relation (WHERE key IN (...), in chunks of 1000 keys)
and attaches its rows under the relation's name; it never joins in a way that repeats the main rows.
In development (APP_ENV other than production) the same SELECT shape run 10 times in one request is logged once
as a probable N+1 query (error_log), with the file and line that ran it.
The models of a result of several rows are guarded (2.26.0): a relation method run on one of them throws [ERROR 2004]
in development and logs a warning in production (Model::strictRelations(), STRICT_RELATIONS=false, $model-&gt;lazy()).

## Constants

+ `IDENTIFIER = '/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?$/'`
+ `NAME = '/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/'`
+ `IN_CHUNK = 1000`
+ `NO_LIMIT = '9223372036854775807'`

## Public properties

+ `public static $threshold = 10`: int identical SELECT shapes in a request before the N+1 warning
+ `public static $logger = null`: callable|null receives the N+1 warning instead of error_log()
+ `public static $watching = null`: bool|null null until the first query decides it from APP_ENV (see watching())

Validates an identifier (column, table, or table.column) and returns it quoted: `books`.`title`

<a name="query-relation"></a>
### `Query::relation()`

```php
public static function relation($parent, $name, $config = null)
```

How a relation of $parent is read, by convention unless $config says otherwise:

- singular name (author) on books: belongsTo, books.author_id -&gt; authors.id
- plural name (books) on authors: hasMany, books.author_id = authors.id
- ['pivot' =&gt; true|'name'] or type belongsToMany (tags on books): the pivot Model::belongsToMany() creates, books_tags (&lt;this table&gt;_&lt;related table&gt;), or tags_books when only that one exists (tried when books_tags fails, then remembered); books_tags.book_id = books.id, books_tags.tag_id = tags.id

**Parameters**

+ `$parent`
+ `$name`
+ `$config`, default `null`

**Returns** `array`: type, table, foreign_key, local_key, owner_key, pivot, related_key, query

Source: [framework/core/Query.php:641](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Query.php#L641)

# Sign-in

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

Users and sessions, passkeys, face login and the sign-in of the phone apps.

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`Caligrafy\Auth`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#auth) | Class that defines the properties and methods of an authentication mechanism for UI and API |
| [`Caligrafy\Passkey`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#passkey) | Passkey wraps lbuchs/webauthn (MIT, no dependencies besides ext-openssl). |
| [`Caligrafy\PasskeyException`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#passkeyexception) | (no doc comment) |
| [`Caligrafy\FaceLogin`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#facelogin) | Face login checks used with FaceDetector.liveness() (public/js/services/detect.js) |
| [`Caligrafy\FaceLoginException`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#faceloginexception) | (no doc comment) |
| [`Caligrafy\Mobile`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Auth#mobile) | Route::mobile(['scheme' =&gt; 'com.example.books']) (after Route::auth() in web.php) lets the iOS and Android apps of php caligrafer.php mobile &lt;name&gt; sign their user in and call the capabilities as that user |

<a name="passkey"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Passkey

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Passkey extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/Passkey.php:34](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Passkey.php#L34)

Passkey wraps lbuchs/webauthn (MIT, no dependencies besides ext-openssl). The browser side is
public/js/services/passkey.js (PasskeyClient.create() / PasskeyClient.get()).

Registration (logged-in user):  registrationOptions($id, $username) -&gt; navigator.credentials.create() -&gt; register($response, $id)
Authentication:                  authenticationOptions([$id])        -&gt; navigator.credentials.get()    -&gt; authenticate($response) returns the user id

The challenge of each ceremony is kept in the session: single use, it expires after $timeout seconds.
Relying party: PASSKEY_RP_ID (the domain, ex: example.com) and PASSKEY_ORIGIN (ex: https://www.example.com) in .env.
Without them the request host is used, which is fine in development: set both in production.
Passkeys need https, except on localhost.

Table (see the face login recipe / wiki 9.9.2):

```
passkeys (id, user_id, credential_id, public_key, sign_count, name, transports, aaguid, created_at, last_used_at)
```

### Constants

+ `SESSION_KEY = '__passkey_challenge'`

### Public properties

+ `public $timeout = 120`
+ `public $userVerification = 'required'`
+ `public $residentKey = 'required'`

<a name="facelogin"></a>
## class Caligrafy\FaceLogin

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class FaceLogin extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/FaceLogin.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/FaceLogin.php#L30)

Face login checks used with FaceDetector.liveness() (public/js/services/detect.js)

1. challenge($username) issues a nonce and $count of the CHALLENGES in a random order, kept in the session
2. the browser runs detector.liveness({ challenges }) and posts { nonce, liveness, prints }
3. verify($response, $username) consumes the nonce (single use, short lived) and checks the liveness result and the prints: enough of them, consistent with each other (same face) and not identical (a replayed static print)
4. match($prints, $enrolled) finds the account whose enrolled prints are close to every print

Face prints are computed in the browser: these checks stop photos, naive replays and stolen requests, they do not
stop a determined attacker who controls the browser. Use a passkey (Caligrafy\Passkey) for sensitive accounts.

Distances are euclidean between 128-number face-api descriptors: same person usually &lt; 0.5, others &gt; 0.6

### Constants

+ `SESSION_KEY = '__face_challenge'`
+ `CHALLENGES =['turn-left', 'turn-right', 'smile']`

### Public properties

+ `public static $match = 0.5`
+ `public static $spread = 0.6`
+ `public static $distinct = 0.001`
+ `public static $minPrints = 3`
+ `public static $maxPrints = 12`
+ `public static $count = 2`
+ `public static $ttl = 60`
+ `public static $clock = null`

### Methods

+ [`FaceLogin::challenge()`](#facelogin-challenge)
+ [`FaceLogin::consume()`](#facelogin-consume)
+ [`FaceLogin::verify()`](#facelogin-verify)
+ [`FaceLogin::checkPrints()`](#facelogin-checkprints)

<a name="mobile"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Mobile

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Mobile
```

Source: [framework/core/Mobile.php:33](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Mobile.php#L33)

Class Mobile
Route::mobile(['scheme' =&gt; 'com.example.books']) (after Route::auth() in web.php) lets the iOS and Android apps of
php caligrafer.php mobile &lt;name&gt; sign their user in and call the capabilities as that user:

```
GET  /mobile/authorize   opened by the app in the system browser: sign in (the site's own /login), then a page asks
                         "Sign in to <app> on this device?". Allow sends the browser to <scheme>://auth?code=...&state=...
POST /mobile/authorize   that page's answer (the session's CSRF token): Allow or Not now
POST /mobile/token       the app trades the code (one use, 5 minutes) and its PKCE verifier for a personal access
                         token of that user (Tokens::create: "Mobile: <device>", the 'scopes', 'days' days)
GET  /mobile/session     who the app's token signs in (401 when it no longer works)
(redirect=http://localhost:5173 instead of a scheme: the app in a browser while it is built, only when this site is
served on this computer: the code comes back to <redirect>/?mobile_auth=1&state=...&code=...)
POST /mobile/signout     revokes the app's own token, and forgets the phone's push registration
```

The app sends Authorization: Bearer cq_... to /capabilities (Route::capabilities) like any program; no cookie and no
CSRF token. The browsers of the app (capacitor://localhost, https://localhost, http://localhost[:port]) and the
'origins' option get CORS headers, never Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: the session cookie never leaves the site.
A project without accounts (no Auth::authentication, 2.27.2) gets the CORS only: its apps call the public
capabilities, with no sign-in and no token.
Codes: PKCE S256 (RFC 7636), the challenge given to /authorize, the verifier only to /token. Tables
caligrafy_mobile_codes (php caligrafer.php platform install; the deploy step creates them).

### Constants

+ `CODES = 'caligrafy_mobile_codes'`
+ `CODE_SECONDS = 300`
+ `DEFAULT_DAYS = 90`
+ `APP_ORIGINS = array('capacitor://localhost', 'ionic://localhost', 'https://localhost', 'http://localhost')`
+ `VIEW = '../../framework/views/mobile/authorize'`

### Public properties

+ `public static $options = null`: array|null the options of Route::mobile (null: no Route::mobile, no CORS)
+ `public static $respond = null`: callable|null replaces header() and exit in tests: fn(int $status, array $headers)

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

|---|---|
| [`Caligrafy\Scheduler`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#scheduler) | An app declares its jobs in application/config/schedule.php: each one calls one capability with fixed inputs on a fixed rhythm (every: 1m...1d, or a five-field cron in a timezone). |
| [`Caligrafy\Queue`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#queue) | A job is a capability and its input, kept in the caligrafy_jobs table (php caligrafer.php platform install, or the deploy step, creates it). |
| [`Caligrafy\Notify`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Notify#notify) | Notify::user($userId, ['title' =&gt; ..., 'body' =&gt; ..., 'url' =&gt; ..., 'tag' =&gt; ..., 'urgency' =&gt; ...]) sends to every channel the user turned on and logs the result (caligrafy_notifications: never the body; kept 30 days): ... |
| [`Caligrafy\Mail`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#mail) | The Mail class handles all emails sent from the framework |

Source: [framework/core/Scheduler.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Scheduler.php#L22)

Class Scheduler
An app declares its jobs in application/config/schedule.php: each one calls one capability with fixed inputs on a
fixed rhythm (every: 1m...1d, or a five-field cron in a timezone). The framework validates the file, runs the jobs
locally (php caligrafer.php schedule due / work) and prints the listing Caligrafy Cloud runs in production
(schedule list --json, version 1).

A run: one at a time per job (a database lock), in a child process stopped at its timeout, with full access like the
command line (Context::system: actor type schedule, actor id the job's name), recorded in caligrafy_job_runs (kept 30
days). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the capability failed or timed out, 2 the schedule file is invalid, 3 skipped.

### Constants

+ `FILE = 'application/config/schedule.php'`
+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_job_runs'`
+ `LISTING_VERSION = 1`
+ `EVERY = ...`
+ `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 55`
+ `MAX_TIMEOUT = 300`
+ `KEEP_DAYS = 30`
+ `FIELDS = array('name', 'capability', 'input', 'every', 'cron', 'timezone', 'timeout', 'enabled')`
+ `OK = 0`
+ `FAILED = 1`
+ `INVALID = 2`
+ `SKIPPED = 3`

<a name="queue"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Queue

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Queue
```

Source: [framework/core/Queue.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Queue.php#L26)

Class Queue (2.18.0)

```
Queue::push('send_welcome_email', ['user_id' => $id]);                       // as soon as a worker is free
Queue::push('build_report', ['month' => '2026-11'], ['delay' => 600, 'attempts' => 5, 'timeout' => 120]);
```

A job is a capability and its input, kept in the caligrafy_jobs table (php caligrafer.php platform install, or the
deploy step, creates it). A worker runs each one in its own process, stopped at its timeout, with full access, as a
scheduled job (Context::system('queue', '&lt;capability&gt; #&lt;id&gt;')): check who may ask for the work before pushing it.

Workers: php caligrafer.php queue work (a loop, on your computer or your own server), or the scheduler: a job of
application/config/schedule.php on the framework's capability queue_work, every minute, which Caligrafy Cloud runs
too. A failed run is tried again after 30 s, 1 min, 2 min... until its attempts are used; an input the capability
refuses (invalid, not found) fails at once. Jobs are kept 7 days after they finish.

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_jobs'`
+ `DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS = 3`
+ `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60`
+ `MAX_TIMEOUT = 900`
+ `RETRY_SECONDS = 30`
+ `KEEP_DAYS = 7`
+ `NAME = '/^[a-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/'`

### Methods

+ [`Queue::push()`](#queue-push)
+ [`Queue::work()`](#queue-work)
+ [`Queue::execute()`](#queue-execute)
+ [`Queue::jobs()`](#queue-jobs)

# Caligrafy\Notify

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

Part of [Jobs, notifications and mail](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs).

<a name="notify"></a>
```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Notify
```

Source: [framework/core/Notify.php:32](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Notify.php#L32)

Class Notify
Notify::user($userId, ['title' =&gt; ..., 'body' =&gt; ..., 'url' =&gt; ..., 'tag' =&gt; ..., 'urgency' =&gt; ...]) sends to every
channel the user turned on and logs the result (caligrafy_notifications: never the body; kept 30 days):

- push: each browser the user subscribed (caligrafy_push_subscriptions), with the VAPID keys of .env (php caligrafer.php notify keys), 5 seconds per push service, the message kept 24 hours for a device that is off; a 404 or 410 deletes the subscription, so do 5 failures in a row
- push to the phone apps (2.27.0, php caligrafer.php mobile): each iPhone or iPad the user turned it on in, through Apple (APNS_KEY, APNS_KEY_ID, APNS_TEAM_ID, APNS_TOPIC), and each Android device through Firebase (FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT), registered in caligrafy_push_devices (notify_register_device); a device Apple or Firebase says is gone is deleted, so is one after 5 failures in a row. Signing out of the app (/mobile/signout) forgets it
- email: the user's confirmed address only (caligrafy_notify_emails), through MAIL_*, with a one-click unsubscribe link (a signed URL) and the List-Unsubscribe headers

A delivery failure never throws; a bad message throws ServiceError::invalid. At most NOTIFY_RATE_PER_HOUR messages per
user and hour (30): above it nothing is sent ('skipped' =&gt; 'rate'). In-page alerts stay the app's job.
Without the tables (php caligrafer.php platform install) nothing is sent and nothing fails.

## Constants

+ `CHANNELS = array('push', 'email')`
+ `SUBSCRIPTIONS = 'caligrafy_push_subscriptions'`
+ `DEVICES = 'caligrafy_push_devices'`
+ `PROVIDERS = array('apns', 'fcm')`
+ `EMAILS = 'caligrafy_notify_emails'`
+ `PREFS = 'caligrafy_notify_prefs'`

<a name="cryptopayment"></a>
## class Caligrafy\CryptoPayment

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class CryptoPayment extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/CryptoPayment.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/CryptoPayment.php#L26)

CryptoPayment accepts crypto payments (USDC) through the Coinbase Business Checkouts API.

Coinbase Commerce (api.commerce.coinbase.com, CRYPTO_PAY_KEY) shut down on March 31, 2026. Its successor is the
Checkouts API of Coinbase Business (https://business.coinbase.com/api/v1/checkouts), available to merchants in the
supported countries. Requests are authenticated with a short-lived JWT signed with a CDP API key:

- COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME: the key name, e.g. organizations/{org_id}/apiKeys/{key_id}
- COINBASE_API_KEY_SECRET: the Ed25519 secret (base64) or the ECDSA private key (PEM, legacy keys)

### Methods

<a name="agent"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Agent

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Agent extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/Agent.php:33](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Agent.php#L33)

The Agent class talks to open models through OpenAI-compatible providers:
Groq (default, through groq-php), Together AI, Fireworks AI, OpenRouter, a local Ollama or any custom endpoint.

Choose the provider in .env with AGENT_PROVIDER (groq|together|fireworks|openrouter|ollama|custom).
Key: the provider key (GROQ_API_KEY, TOGETHER_API_KEY, FIREWORKS_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) or AGENT_API_KEY.
AGENT_API_BASE overrides the endpoint (required for custom), AGENT_MODEL and AGENT_VISION_MODEL the default models.
The GROQ_* settings and constants keep working as before.

Groq keeps groq-php: its audio endpoints (multipart uploads) and behavior stay unchanged. The other providers
only need chat completions and the model list, sent with cURL (no extra dependency).

### Constants

+ `PROVIDERS = ...`: Providers: label, default endpoint, key setting, default models (October 2026), audio support, where to get a key and where the models are listed. Ollama needs no key; custom needs AGENT_API_BASE and AGENT_MODEL. Serverless Llama (October 2026): OpenRouter and Ollama only. Groq retired its Llama chat models in August 2026, Together and Fireworks only serve Llama on dedicated/on-demand deployments: their defaults are gpt-oss-120b. Preview models: Groq qwen/qwen3.8-27b.
+ `TIMEOUT = 120`

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#agent-construct)
+ [`Agent::settings()`](#agent-settings)

+ [`->provider()`](#agent-provider)

<a name="assistant"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Assistant

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Assistant extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/Assistant.php:29](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Assistant.php#L29)

The Assistant class runs conversations with OpenAI models through the Responses and Conversations APIs.

OpenAI shut down the Assistants API on August 26, 2026. Version 2.0 of this class keeps the same chainable
methods (start, createMessage, run, retrieveResponse, end) on top of the APIs that replace it:

- the assistant (model, instructions, tools) is configuration kept in this object and sent with every response
- a conversation (POST /v1/conversations) replaces the thread
- a response (POST /v1/responses) replaces the run
- files are searched through a vector store (file_search tool)

### Public properties

+ `public $name`: string the name of the assistant (used for the vector store name and metadata)
+ `public $description`: string what the assistant does (local description)
+ `public $instructions`: string the instructions (system prompt) sent with every response
+ `public $tools = array(["type" => "file_search"])`: array the tools: ["type" =&gt; "file_search"] is completed with the vector store, ["type" =&gt; "code_interpreter"] gets an automatic container with the uploaded files
+ `public $file_ids =[]`: array ids of the files uploaded for the assistant
+ `public $file_paths =[]`: array local paths of the files to upload
+ `public $metadata`: array metadata sent with every response (up to 16 string pairs)
+ `public $vector_store_id = ''`: string the vector store that holds the files searched by file_search
+ `public $assistant_id = ''`: string kept for backward compatibility: the Assistants API no longer exists, nothing is created on OpenAI
+ `public $thread_id = ''`: string the active conversation id (conv_...). Kept under its old name for backward compatibility
+ `public $run_id = ''`: string the last response id (resp_...)
+ `public $status = 'queued'`: string the status of the last response: completed, failed, in_progress, queued, incomplete, cancelled
+ `public $messages =[]`: array the messages of the conversation: the user messages added and the assistant messages received. Every message is ['id', 'role', 'content' =&gt; [['type' =&gt; 'input_text'|'output_text', 'text' =&gt; '...']]]
+ `public $response_text = ''`: string the text of the last assistant answer
+ `public $last_response =[]`: array the last raw response returned by OpenAI (useful for errors and usage)

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#assistant-construct)
+ [`->retrieve()`](#assistant-retrieve)
+ [`->delete()`](#assistant-delete)
+ [`->start()`](#assistant-start)
+ [`->end()`](#assistant-end)
+ [`->createMessage()`](#assistant-createmessage)
+ [`->listMessages()`](#assistant-listmessages)
+ [`->run()`](#assistant-run)
+ [`->retrieveResponse()`](#assistant-retrieveresponse)

<a name="rest"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Rest

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Rest
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Rest.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/interfaces/Rest.php#L25)

Class Rest
Answers HTTP requests with capabilities, in JSON:

- Route::capability('POST', '/books', 'create_book') maps one route to one capability
- Route::capabilities('/capabilities') adds GET /capabilities (what the caller may call, with the input schemas, and the CSRF token of the session in "csrf") and POST /capabilities/{name} (call any capability by name: the JS client of the Vue apps uses it)

Who calls: a personal access token (Authorization: Bearer cq_...), the legacy API key, or the signed-in user. Calls
made with the session cookie need the CSRF token in an X-CSRF-Token header (or \_token) unless they only read.
Inputs: the JSON body (or form fields, or the query string for GET), then the route variables, which win.
Responses: 200 with the result ({"data": ...}), 201 when a POST creates, or {"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}
with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422.

### Methods

+ [`Rest::respond()`](#rest-respond)
+ [`Rest::answer()`](#rest-answer)
+ [`Rest::listing()`](#rest-listing)
+ [`Rest::input()`](#rest-input)

## class Caligrafy\Mcp\Http

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Mcp;

class Http
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Mcp/Http.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/interfaces/Mcp/Http.php#L22)

Class Http
One JSON-RPC message per POST, answered with application/json (no event stream: every tool answers at once).

- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer &lt;personal access token&gt;. Without a valid token: 401 with WWW-Authenticate.
- Origin: a browser request from another site is refused (403), against DNS rebinding. Allowed: no Origin header (agents), the application's own host, and the origins listed in MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma separated).
- Notifications are answered 202 with no body. GET and DELETE answer 405 (no server-initiated stream, no sessions).

### Methods

<a name="mcp-server"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Mcp\Server

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Mcp;

class Server
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Mcp/Server.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/interfaces/Mcp/Server.php#L26)

Class Server
JSON-RPC 2.0 messages of MCP, independent of the transport (Http for Streamable HTTP, caligrafer mcp for stdio):
initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call; notifications get no answer.

The tools are the capabilities the context may call, with their input schema and the hints agents use to decide
when to ask the user first (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint). A tool call goes through Capabilities::call(): the same
permission checks, validation and audit as every other channel. A refused call (invalid input, forbidden...) is a
tool result with isError, so the agent can read the reason and correct itself; protocol errors are JSON-RPC errors.

### Constants

+ `PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = array('2025-11-25', '2025-06-18', '2025-03-26', '2024-11-05')`
+ `PARSE_ERROR = -32700`
+ `INVALID_REQUEST = -32600`
+ `METHOD_NOT_FOUND = -32601`
+ `INVALID_PARAMS = -32602`
+ `INTERNAL_ERROR = -32603`

<a name="async-kernel"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Async\Kernel

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Async;

class Kernel
```

Source: [framework/core/Async/Kernel.php:34](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Async/Kernel.php#L34)

Class Kernel
What the async server runs, whatever server it is: boot() once per process (settings, constants, the class map, the
application's config and container, the capabilities), then handle() for each request, one at a time per process.

It answers the capabilities channel only, as Route::capabilities() does on the web server:

```
GET  {prefix}         the capabilities the caller may call
POST {prefix}/{name}  a call (GET too for a read-only capability), inputs in the JSON body or the query string
```

The caller is known from its token (Authorization: Bearer cq_...), or is a visitor. There is no session and no
cookie here: a request that brings the session cookie is the web server's (handles() says so), as is a capability
that Eligibility refuses. Between requests, everything a request may leave behind is forgotten (endRequest()).

### Methods

+ [`Kernel::boot()`](#async-kernel-boot)
+ [`Kernel::handles()`](#async-kernel-handles)
+ [`Kernel::handle()`](#async-kernel-handle)
+ [`Kernel::eligible()`](#async-kernel-eligible)
+ [`Kernel::endRequest()`](#async-kernel-endrequest)

<a name="async-eligibility"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Async\Eligibility

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Async;

class Eligibility
```

Source: [framework/core/Async/Eligibility.php:28](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Async/Eligibility.php#L28)

Class Eligibility
The async server keeps the application in memory and answers many requests from one process, so a capability it runs
must not keep anything from one caller to the next, nor talk to the web server's request directly. A capability is
eligible when its class's own source (read as PHP tokens: comments and strings do not count) uses none of:

- the request and the session: $_SESSION, $_COOKIE, $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_FILES, $_SERVER, session(), request(), Auth::, redirect(), view() (the async channel knows its caller only from a token, or as a visitor);
- output and the end of the process: echo, print, printf, var_dump, header(), setcookie(), http_response_code(), exit, die, ob_*() (it returns data; the server sends it);
- state kept between calls: global, static variables, assignments to static properties;

and it is not webOnly and takes no file input (the `file` rule).
Anything else (classes it calls) is not read: the isolation test (php caligrafer.php async check) runs each eligible
capability for two callers in one process and compares. A capability that is not eligible is answered by the web
server as before: being unsafe makes it slower, never shared.

### Constants

+ `SUPERGLOBALS = array('$_SESSION', '$_COOKIE', '$_GET', '$_POST', '$_REQUEST', '$_FILES', '$_SERVER', '$GLOBALS')`
+ `FUNCTIONS = ...`

### Methods

<a name="async-workermanserver"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Async\WorkermanServer

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Async;

class WorkermanServer
```

Source: [framework/core/Async/WorkermanServer.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Async/WorkermanServer.php#L25)

Class WorkermanServer
Workerman (pure PHP, composer require workerman/workerman: php caligrafer.php add async) keeps a few processes
that each hold the application in memory (Kernel::boot) and many open connections, answering one request at a time
per process. In front of the web server (ASYNC=on in the production image: docker/production/start.sh), it answers
the capabilities channel itself (Kernel::handles) and passes every other request, unchanged, to Apache on
127.0.0.1:&lt;backend port&gt;, adding X-Forwarded-For; without a backend (development), others get a 404.

### Methods

+ [`WorkermanServer::run()`](#async-workermanserver-run)


Runs the server (this call does not return)

**Parameters**

+ `$listen` `string`: e.g. http://0.0.0.0:80
+ `$workers` `int`: processes (each holds one copy of the application)
+ `$backend` `string|null`, default `null`: the web server for everything else, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080
+ `$prefix`, default `'/capabilities'`

Source: [framework/core/Async/WorkermanServer.php:33](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Async/WorkermanServer.php#L33)

<a name="snap-hints"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Hints

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Hints
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Hints.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Hints.php#L30)

Class Hints
Snap Cards work without any hint: every card is built from what a capability declares (its rules, descriptions,
readOnly and destructive). Hints only make them better, from one file the app owns, application/config/snap.php:

```
return [
    'about' => 'a library app',                       // what the assistant is the assistant of (the planner)
    'cards' => [                                      // keyed by capability name
        'list_books' => ['title' => 'The catalog', 'columns' => ['title', 'author.name'], 'empty' => 'No book yet.'],
        'reading_report' => ['async' => true, 'working' => ['Counting the books…']],
    ],
];
```

A file that returns the cards alone (no 'cards' key) works too. The keys of a card are in the wiki page
"Snap Cards and the Assistant": title, lead, submit, columns, labels, hide, values, choices, open, full, empty,
variant, noun, icon, done, undo, next, applies, empty_next, alert, insight, discover, working, async, consequence,
confirm, card (2.25.0: its card view, 'Folder/view' under application/views, or false), view (2.24.0: the page whose
part marked data-snap shows it, or false) and design (2.24.0: how its data is shown without a card view or a page).
A capability is async when #[Capability(async: true)] says so, or its hint does.

### Methods

+ [`Hints::for()`](#snap-hints-for)
+ [`Hints::about()`](#snap-hints-about)
+ [`Hints::forget()`](#snap-hints-forget)

<a name="snap-views"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Views

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Views
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Views.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Views.php#L25)

Class Views
How a Show card looks, best first (2.25.0):
1. its card view: application/views/snap/&lt;capability&gt;.pug, a Pug view made for the card, in the app's own markup and classes, rendered on the server into the card (the hint 'card' =&gt; 'Folder/view' names another, false none). It gets $result (what the capability returned), $rows and $page for a list, $record for one record, $input, $card, $home, $authorized and $user. A link with data-snap-open="&lt;capability&gt;" and data-snap-input='{"id":7}' opens that card in the conversation. Written by Claude from the app's views (the assistant skill); its first line names the page it was made from and that page's fingerprint, so `php caligrafer.php snap views` says when it is stale.
2. the part of its page marked data-snap="&lt;capability&gt;" (a Route::page whose first data it is), embedded in the card (?snap-embed: no frame, sized to it); a whole page only when the hint 'view' names it
3. a card designed for its data in the app's design system (Snap\Designer)

### Methods

<a name="snap-designer"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Designer

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Designer
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Designer.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Designer.php#L23)

Class Designer
A capability shown through its own page uses that page (Snap\Views). Without one, its card is designed, never dumped:
a design says which of the data makes the title, the line under it, the badges, the numbers that stand out, the
details, the longer text and the tags of a record, or the title, line, details and badge of each row of a list.
The page then draws it with the app's own design tokens (its DESIGN_STYLE), so it looks like the rest of the app.

Who designs it: the hint 'design' of application/config/snap.php when the app gives one; else Claude (when the
assistant has its key), once for each shape of data, kept in the cache; else rules from the names of the fields.

### Constants

+ `FORMATS = array('text', 'number', 'money', 'percent', 'date', 'datetime', 'bool', 'email', 'url')`
+ `TONES = array('success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info', 'neutral')`
+ `CACHE_DAYS = 30`

### Public properties

+ `public static $model = true`: bool false: rules only, never the model (tests, and a design asked for while answering)
+ `public static $transport = null`: Tests fake Claude's design here (a callable that takes the request and returns the response), apart from the planner's: a test that fakes the planner never sees the designer's requests

### Methods

+ [`Designer::record()`](#snap-designer-record)
+ [`Designer::rows()`](#snap-designer-rows)
+ [`Designer::spec()`](#snap-designer-spec)
+ [`Designer::paths()`](#snap-designer-paths)
+ [`Designer::format()`](#snap-designer-format)

<a name="snap-planner"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Planner

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Planner
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Planner.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Planner.php#L25)

The Snap shell's planner (2.23.0): Claude reads what the person typed or said and answers with cards.

What the model may do, enforced here, not in the prompt:

- look things up with the read-only capabilities this person may call (as tools, run with their permissions);
- answer with show_cards: which capability, with which values, and one sentence of caption.

Every card it names goes through Snap\Flow like any other: a read runs, a change comes back as an Ask: Confirm
whose token only the person's click sends. The model never sees a token and never runs a change.
Tool results are the app's data: the system prompt says so, and nothing in them can reach a change anyway.

Claude through the official PHP SDK (anthropic-ai/sdk), claude-opus-5-5 at low effort (a quick turn in a UI),
server-side refusal fallbacks on. Without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the planner is off and the shell uses its fast path.

### Constants

+ `MODEL = 'claude-opus-5-5'`
+ `MAX_STEPS = 6`
+ `RESULT_BYTES = 12000`
+ `FILE_TYPES = array('image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain', 'text/csv', 'text/markdown')`
+ `FILE_BYTES = 5242880`
+ `FILES = 3`

### Public properties

+ `public static $transport = null`: callable|null tests: fn (array $request): object  (a response with -&gt;stopReason and -&gt;content)

### Methods

+ [`Planner::on()`](#snap-planner-on)
+ [`Planner::files()`](#snap-planner-files)
+ [`Planner::plan()`](#snap-planner-plan)
+ [`Planner::send()`](#snap-planner-send)

<a name="snap-flow"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Flow

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Flow
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Flow.php:16](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Flow.php#L16)

The next card for a capability and its inputs, the same whoever asks (a card that is sent, the shell's fast path,
the model's choice): one place decides, so the planner can never take a shortcut around consent.

```
read:        inputs missing -> its Ask card; complete -> runs -> Show card
write/destroy: inputs missing -> its Ask card; refused by its rules -> Ask with errors; else -> Ask: Confirm
```

A change runs only in SnapRun, with the token of that Confirm.

## class Caligrafy\Snap\Consent

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Consent
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Consent.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Consent.php#L20)

Snap consent (2.23.0): nothing that changes data runs from a card until the person confirms it.

- snap_run answers a change with an Ask: Confirm: what will change (before -&gt; after), and a one-time token bound to this person, this capability and these exact inputs, for 10 minutes, kept in the session (never in the card's address). Only the person's click on that card sends it back; a model, a page or a link cannot make one.
- A confirmed change is recorded in Caligrafy's audit log (capability snap_confirm, detail: what was confirmed).
- What the change can be undone with is decided here, from what was true before (update_), what was created (create_ -&gt; delete_), or a hint ('undo' in application/config/snap.php). Undoing is a change too: it gets its own Confirm.

### Constants

+ `TTL = 600`
+ `KEEP = 20`
+ `KEY = 'snap_consent'`

### Methods

+ [`Consent::ask()`](#snap-consent-ask)
+ [`Consent::take()`](#snap-consent-take)
+ [`Consent::undo()`](#snap-consent-undo)

<a name="snap-offers"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Offers

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Offers
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Offers.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Offers.php#L26)

Offer: Suggestion and Offer: Routine (2.23.0): the assistant notices what a person does again and again,
only if they turned noticing on, and offers to help. Built to stay quiet rather than noisy:

- opt-in per person (snap_settings.noticing), off by default; "What I've noticed" shows every pattern, each deletable, and turning noticing off deletes what was noticed
- a pattern is the same request (capability + inputs) on 3 different days or more, on the same weekday (weekly) or around the same hour (daily); anything weaker says nothing
- every offer says why ("you did this 4 Mondays in a row"), has Not now and Don't suggest this again, and at most MAX_OFFERS are shown at a time
- Offer: Suggestion: it is the usual moment and it was not done yet today: do it now (through Snap\Flow, so a change still asks for its Confirm)
- Offer: Routine: do it on that rhythm, at a level the person picks: suggest (a Suggestion at that moment), confirm (its Confirm ready at that moment), auto (it runs as a task and they are told). Accepting a routine is itself a change with its Ask: Confirm. A delete is never automatic.

### Constants

+ `MIN_DAYS = 3`
+ `MAX_OFFERS = 2`
+ `WINDOW_DAYS = 42`
+ `LEVELS = array('suggest', 'confirm', 'auto')`
+ `DAYS = array(1 => 'Monday', 2 => 'Tuesday', 3 => 'Wednesday', 4 => 'Thursday', 5 => 'Friday', 6 => 'Saturday', 7 => 'Sunday')`

### Public properties

+ `public static $now = null`: int|null tests: the time "now" is

<a name="snap-tasks"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Tasks

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Tasks
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Tasks.php:24](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Tasks.php#L24)

Track: Task cards (2.23.0): work that runs in the background for one person.

A capability declared #[Capability(async: true)] (or with the hint 'async' in application/config/snap.php) does not run
in the request: a read starts as a task at once, a change after its Ask: Confirm. The task is a row of snap_tasks and
a job of Caligrafy's queue (snap_task_run). The worker runs the capability AS THE PERSON who asked (their user, the
web channel: their permissions, not the queue's full access), keeps the card of what came out, and notifies them:

```
done        -> the Show card of the result
needs_input -> the Ask card of what the capability refused (the person answers it, a new task starts)
failed      -> a notice, after the queue's retries
```

The Track card shows where it is: queued, running, then the card it ended with.

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_snap_tasks'`
+ `LABELS = ...`

### Methods

<a name="snap-discover"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Discover

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Discover
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Discover.php:28](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Discover.php#L28)

Discover (2.23.0): Home surfaces the things this application is about, to
invite browsing, the way a shop surfaces products. Out of the box, from one hint on a list capability ('discover'):

- for you      more like what this person looked at (only when they turned noticing on: what they opened is in snap_events), e.g. another book by the author of a book they opened
- new          what was added last
- the rule     a business rule of the app: only what is available now (not in another list, e.g. not lent)

Each pick is a Home card that opens the object in the task space; each says why it is there.

The hint: 'discover' =&gt; array(

```
'open' => 'get_book', 'key' => 'id',                     how an object opens (capability, the field it takes)
'title' => 'title', 'meta' => array('author.name', ...),   what a pick shows
'new' => 'created_at',                                   the field that says when it was added
'related' => 'author.id', 'by' => 'author.name',          what "more like it" shares, and its name
'opened' => array('get_book' => 'id', 'lend_book' => 'book_id'),   the requests that mean "looked at it"
'unavailable' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'),   the business rule
'title_section' => 'On the shelf for you')
```

### Constants

```php

class Cards
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Cards.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Snap/Cards.php#L22)

Snap Cards (2.23.0): every card is built from what a capability already declares

Families and types (marketing names the family with the type):

```
Ask: Form, Choice, Confirm   Show: Answer, List   Go: Shortcut   Track: Task   Offer: Suggestion, Routine
```

Phase 1 builds Ask: Form, Ask: Choice, Show: Answer and Show: List from:

- the capability's rules and descriptions (fields, types, limits, choices, required)
- the shape of its result (a page, a list, a record, a value)
- optional hints in application/config/snap.php (Snap\Hints)

The model, later, only picks a card and fills it; it never invents a card's structure.

## Constants

+ `VERSION = 1`
+ `MAX_OPTIONS = 50`
+ `THING_ICONS = ...`
+ `VERB_ICONS = ...`
+ `FIELD_ICONS = ...`

+ `HIDDEN = '/^(snap_|notify_|queue_work$)/'`

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

The Snap shell's two spaces (2.23.0):

```
Home       the starting workspace: the agent's message for the situation, prompt suggestions (and "What else can
           I do"), the input; then the cards: Needs you (alerts, tasks waiting on you, changes to confirm),
           For you (offers), In progress (tasks), Shortcuts. Only the sections that have something.
Task space the engagement: the conversation minimized to the agent's latest answer (back and forth, history,
           rating, a different answer, the input on demand); only the cards of that answer.
```

Each turn is kept (snap_turns): what was asked, the caption, the cards, the suggestions, how it was answered.

### `Conversation::home()`

```php
public static function home(Context $context)
```

Home, for this person, now: an orchestrator of what to concentrate on, in this order:

```
Needs you      alerts, tasks waiting on the person, changes to confirm (the focus)
insights       numbers, each with the action it calls for (none without one)
For you        offers (what they usually do now, routines)
In progress    running tasks
discover       the things this app is about, to browse: more like what they looked at, new, available
Just done, Your shortcuts
```

The message says the focus and nudges the conversation on; the suggestions start with the focus's action and a
pick to look at. One card per capability (the latest task of a capability is its only card) and per object.
Each card carries its key: opening it (snap_ask open) shows it in the task space.

# Testing

> Caligrafy Quill 2.28.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

The base class of the tests of an application (tests/, php caligrafer.php test).

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Testing#testing-testcase) | Test what the app does through its capabilities, as the pages, REST, the JS client and agents reach them |

<a name="testing-testcase"></a>
## abstract class Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Testing;

abstract class TestCase extends \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase
```

Source: [framework/testing/TestCase.php:41](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/testing/TestCase.php#L41)

Test what the app does through its capabilities, as the pages, REST, the JS client and agents reach them:

```
final class BooksTest extends Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase
{
    public function testAReaderAddsABook(): void
    {
        $book = $this->call('create_book', ['title' => 'Dune'], $this->user(1));
        $this->assertSame('Dune', $book['title']);
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'create_book', [], $this->user(1));
        $this->assertCapabilityFails('unauthenticated', 'create_book', ['title' => 'Dune'], 'guest');
        $this->assertStringContainsString('Dune', $this->render('Books/list', ['books' => [$book]]));
    }
}
```

Each test runs in a database transaction that is rolled back at its end (with DB_ACTIVATE=true), so tests leave the
database as they found it; a CREATE, ALTER or DROP ends the transaction (MySQL commits it). Use a database of its own
for tests: DB_TEST_DATABASE in .env, or the settings of .env.testing. Bindings of the container, the cache's copies
and the query shapes the N+1 warning counts (Query::forgetShapes) are forgotten between tests.

## class Caligrafy\Features

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Features
```

Source: [framework/core/Features.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Features.php#L30)

Class Features (2.26.0)
The SDKs that only some applications use are no longer in Caligrafy's composer.json (they are suggested): a project
adds the one it needs with php caligrafer.php add &lt;feature&gt;, which runs composer require with the pinned constraint.
The framework classes that use an SDK call Features::need() first: without it they throw FeatureMissing, whose
message names the command, never a fatal "class not found".

FaceDetect's models (@vladmandic/face-api 1.7.15) and the pictures of its recognition example are not in the release
either: php caligrafer.php add facedetect (and php caligrafer.php facedetect &lt;app&gt;) download them from pinned,
versioned sources and check the SHA-256 of each file before anything is written.

used() tells which features a project uses (its .env settings and its application/ code): doctor reports the ones
whose SDK is missing, update keeps (or adds back) their packages in composer.json.

### Constants

+ `SINCE = '2.26.0'`
+ `FEATURES = ...`
+ `CLASSES = ...`
+ `PLACEHOLDERS = array('pk_test_1234', 'sk_test_1234', 'pk_live_1234', 'sk_live_1234')`
+ `FACE_API = '1.7.15'`
+ `MODELS_DIR = 'public/resources/models'`
+ `MODELS = ...`
+ `MODEL_SOURCES = array('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@vladmandic/face-api@1.7.15/model/', 'https://unpkg.com/@vladmandic/face-api@1.7.15/model/',)`
+ `PICTURES_DIR = 'recognition/Flash'`
+ `PICTURES = ...`
+ `PICTURE_SOURCES = ...`

### Public properties

+ `public static $absent = array()`: array tests: packages treated as not installed
+ `public static $fetcher = null`: callable|null tests: fn (string $url): ?string, the body of a download (null when it failed)

<a name="classmap"></a>
## class Caligrafy\ClassMap

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class ClassMap
```

Source: [framework/core/ClassMap.php:24](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/ClassMap.php#L24)

Class ClassMap (2.18.0)
Before 2.18.0 the first unknown class of a request loaded every PHP file of framework/core, framework/database,
framework/interfaces, application/ and tests/. Now a map of class =&gt; file (namespaced or not, interfaces, traits and
enums too) is built once from those folders (application/config, application/views and tests/ left out) and kept in a
private folder of the temporary directory; a class is loaded when it is first used.

Kept as before: a file that does more than declare classes (it declares functions, or runs code at the top level, or
declares a class inside an if) is loaded at start, as every file used to be. A class missing from the map, and the
list of capabilities, make the map check its files (once per request; with APP_ENV=production at most once a
minute): a file added, removed or changed since the map was built rebuilds it, so a new class works at once while
you develop. A new container starts with no map. CLASS_MAP=false in .env goes back to loading every file.

### Constants

+ `VERSION = 3`
+ `PRODUCTION_CHECK = 60`

### Methods

+ [`ClassMap::enabled()`](#classmap-enabled)
+ [`ClassMap::register()`](#classmap-register)
+ [`ClassMap::load()`](#classmap-load)
+ [`ClassMap::capabilityFiles()`](#classmap-capabilityfiles)
+ [`ClassMap::refresh()`](#classmap-refresh)
+ [`ClassMap::scanned()`](#classmap-scanned)
+ [`ClassMap::registered()`](#classmap-registered)
+ [`ClassMap::map()`](#classmap-map)
+ [`ClassMap::rebuild()`](#classmap-rebuild)
+ [`ClassMap::declarations()`](#classmap-declarations)
+ [`ClassMap::tempFolder()`](#classmap-tempfolder)

<a name="updater"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Updater

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Updater
```

Source: [framework/core/Updater.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Updater.php#L26)

Class Updater
php caligrafer.php update [&lt;version&gt;] downloads the project's release (Framework::VERSION) and the target release
(the latest by default), then:
1. framework/ and claude-plugin/ are the framework's: replaced whole (files the release dropped go too), except the files initialize writes there (KEEP). Framework files changed by hand are named in the report
2. every other file of the release (caligrafer.php, .bin/, Dockerfile, index.php, public/css, public/js...) is compared with the project's release: an untouched copy is replaced, a missing one added, a changed one kept with the new version written next to it (&lt;file&gt;.caligrafy-new). Documents (DOCS) changed by hand are left alone
3. composer.json gets the new packages and versions the project did not change (then composer update for them), .gitignore the new lines, .env the new settings with their defaults (existing values are never changed)
4. php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply, from the new release, brings application/ up to date
Everything replaced is copied first to backups/caligrafy-update-&lt;from&gt;-to-&lt;to&gt;-&lt;time&gt;/. --check reports only.
application/, .env values, public/uploads and vendor/ are never replaced.

### Constants

+ `REPOSITORY = 'caligrafy/caligrafy-quill'`
+ `WHOLE = array('framework', 'claude-plugin')`
+ `KEEP = array('framework/librairies/app/.env')`
+ `SKIP = ...`
+ `MERGED = array('composer.json', '.gitignore')`
+ `DOCS = array('README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md', 'CONTRIBUTING.md', 'CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md', 'ARCHITECTURE.md', 'LICENSE')`
+ `NEW_SUFFIX = '.caligrafy-new'`
+ `ENV_EXAMPLE = 'framework/settings/.env.example'`

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#updater-construct)
+ [`->run()`](#updater-run)
+ [`->newerRelease()`](#updater-newerrelease)
+ [`->download()`](#updater-download)

<a name="deployer"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Deployer

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Deployer
```

Source: [framework/core/Deployer.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Deployer.php#L23)

Class Deployer
1. waits for the database (a new server starts its database at the same time as the app)
2. creates the framework tables (framework/settings/platform.sql, safe to run again)
3. runs every application/models/&lt;folder&gt;/create_db.sql that is new or changed since its last run, and records it in caligrafy_scripts. A script that drops, deletes or truncates is never run again once it ran: run it by hand (php caligrafer.php sql &lt;file&gt;) when you mean it. seed.sql and other scripts are never run. A statement that adds a column, an index or a foreign key already there (the script's earlier run added it) is skipped, so a script keeps its ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements.
4. runs the migrations of application/migrations that never ran (Migrations, 2.18.0)
Without DB_ACTIVATE=true there is nothing to do.

### Constants

+ `SCRIPTS_TABLE = 'caligrafy_scripts'`
+ `DESTRUCTIVE = '/\b(DROP\s+(TABLE|DATABASE|SCHEMA|VIEW|COLUMN)|DELETE\s+FROM|TRUNCATE)\b/i'`

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#deployer-construct)
+ [`->run()`](#deployer-run)

+ [`->schedule()`](#deployer-schedule)
+ [`->scripts()`](#deployer-scripts)

+ [`Deployer::alreadyApplied()`](#deployer-alreadyapplied)

<a name="cloudclient"></a>
## class Caligrafy\CloudClient

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class CloudClient
```

Source: [framework/core/CloudClient.php:19](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/CloudClient.php#L19)

Class CloudClient
Calls the capabilities of Caligrafy Cloud (POST &lt;url&gt;/capabilities/&lt;name&gt;) with a personal access token of the
account. `cloud login` gets it by itself: it opens &lt;url&gt;/cli?code=..., the owner approves the code shown in the
terminal, and the command collects the token (start_cli_login, poll_cli_login). --token or --paste take one created
on the dashboard instead. The token is kept in .caligrafy/cloud.json of the project (git-ignored, never in the
image), or given with CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_TOKEN. CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_URL points to another service.

### Constants

+ `DEFAULT_URL = 'https://deploy.caligrafy.com'`
+ `PERIODS = array('week', 'month', 'year')`

Source: [framework/core/Quickstart.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/Quickstart.php#L23)

Class Quickstart
Every step can be run again: it only does what is missing.
1. application/ (initialize; it deletes the .git folder of the framework, so it needs --yes when one exists)
2. .env: the database of the Docker server (DB_ACTIVATE=true, DB_HOST=mysql, a database name), or, on a local server (MAMP, XAMPP, LAMP), the address of the project in its web folder (APP_ROOT) and its MySQL settings (asked with the stack's defaults; without a terminal to confirm them, skipped unless --db-defaults)
3. the database and the framework tables (tokens, audit log)
4. web.php: Route::capabilities('/capabilities') for the JS client, Route::mcp('/mcp') for AI agents and Route::notifications() for the links of notification emails
5. with --example: the Tasks example (capabilities, page, REST routes, table, JS client)

### Constants

+ `EXAMPLE = 'framework/settings/examples/tasks'`
+ `LOCAL_STACKS = ...`
+ `DEFAULT_DATABASE = 'caligrafy'`
+ `DOCKER_SERVICES = array('dev-box' => array(80, '8080'), 'prod-box' => array(80, '8080'), 'phpmyadmin' => array(80, '8077'), 'mysql' => array(3306, '3306'))`: Runs the steps
+ `COMPOSE_FILES = ...`

<a name="pluginsource"></a>
## class Caligrafy\PluginSource

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class PluginSource
```

Source: [framework/core/PluginSource.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/PluginSource.php#L22)

Class PluginSource
A project enables the Claude Code plugin of its own claude-plugin/ folder through .claude/settings.json: a plugin
source (a "marketplace", declared in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json) at "./", and the plugin caligrafy-quill@&lt;name&gt;.
Claude Code keeps one source per name for the whole computer: when every project calls it "caligrafy", the first
project opened wins, every other project gets that project's plugin (an older one), and none gets any once that
folder is deleted. initialize and update give the project its own name: caligrafy-&lt;folder&gt;-&lt;4 hex&gt;.
The framework's own repository keeps "caligrafy": it is the source people add from GitHub.
Claude Code runs a copy of the plugin it makes at install time (~/.claude/plugins/cache), not the project's folder:
after an update brings a newer claude-plugin/, connect() refreshes that copy, and doctor warns while it is older.

### Constants

+ `SHARED = 'caligrafy'`
+ `PLUGIN = 'caligrafy-quill'`
+ `SETTINGS = '.claude/settings.json'`
+ `MARKETPLACE = '.claude-plugin/marketplace.json'`
+ `MANIFEST = 'claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'`

### Methods

Source: [framework/core/MobileApp.php:21](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.28.0/framework/core/MobileApp.php#L21)

Class MobileApp
Creates public/&lt;name&gt; from framework/librairies/mobile: the Vite Vue app of `create`, wrapped by Capacitor 8 into an
iOS and an Android project, that signs its user in through the site (Route::mobile) and calls the capabilities with
that user's token, turns push notifications on (Notify), and builds for TestFlight and Google Play with fastlane, on
a Mac or on GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/mobile-&lt;name&gt;.yml, written next to the project's own workflows).
Options: --id (the app id: com.example.books, the bundle id of iOS, the package of Android and the URL scheme of the
sign-in), --display (the name under the icon), --url (the site it calls once online). Node.js 22+ installs it and adds
ios/ and android/ (npx cap add); without it, the folder is created and the README says what to run.

### Constants

+ `TEMPLATE = 'framework/librairies/mobile'`
+ `RESERVED = array('app', 'bot', '__bots__', 'css', 'facedetect', 'fonts', 'images', 'js', 'ml', 'resources', 'uploads', 'snap', 'mobile')`
+ `PLACEHOLDERS = array('package.json', 'package-lock.json', 'capacitor.config.json', 'index.html', '.env.production', 'README.md')`

### Public properties

+ `public static $shell = null`: callable|null replaces the shell in tests: fn(string $command, string $cwd) =&gt; int exit status
