<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Agent-Commands -->

The **agent commands** of [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer) are for programs
and AI agents that call your capabilities: `token` creates, lists and revokes personal access tokens, `mcp` serves the
capabilities to an agent on this computer, and `audit` shows what was called and refused.
## With Claude

```text
create a token for my reporting agent with books:read, valid 90 days
connect Claude Code to this app's capabilities
```

The `new-capability` skill runs `token create` (and shows the token once, without keeping it), and adds the app to
Claude Code with `claude mcp add ... php caligrafer.php mcp`.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php token list` shows the token `active` with only the scopes you asked
for, and `php caligrafer.php audit` shows the agent's calls.
## By hand

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install        # the token and audit tables, once
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "books agent" --scopes books:read,books:write
claude mcp add bookshelf -- docker compose exec -T dev-box php caligrafer.php mcp
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit --limit 20
```

(without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`, and `-T`).
## <a name="token"></a>`token`

```text
 Usage:
 php caligrafer.php token create <name> --scopes <a:read,b:write | *> [--user <id>] [--expires <days>]
 php caligrafer.php token list
 php caligrafer.php token revoke <id>
```

### `token create`

```bash
php caligrafer.php token create "books agent" --scopes books:read,books:write
php caligrafer.php token create "Reporting job" --scopes books:read --expires 90
php caligrafer.php token create "Sam's agent" --scopes "books:*" --user 7
```

```text
 Token #2 "books agent" created with books:read books:write

 cq_2_...

 It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--scopes` (required) | `resource:action` values, separated by commas or spaces; `books:*` for every action on books; `*` for everything. A value of another shape is left out; with none left: ` A token needs scopes: --scopes books:read,books:write (or * for everything)` |
| `--expires <days>` | the token stops working after that many days (at least 1); the line says `, expires <date>` |
| `--user <id>` | the token acts for that user, so a capability's `level` applies to them and `$context->user` is that user. A user that does not exist: ` There is no user #<id>: no token was created.` |

Only the token's SHA-256 hash is stored: the token itself is printed once. A program sends it as
`Authorization: Bearer cq_...`.

### `token list`

```text
 #2    active   books agent                    books:read books:write  last used 2026-11-07 23:17:49
 #3    expired  Reporting job                  books:read  user 7  never used
```

The number, the state (`active`, `expired` or `revoked`), the name, the scopes, the user it acts for, and when it was
last used. With none: ` No tokens yet: php caligrafer.php token create <name> --scopes <scopes>`.

### `token revoke`

```bash
php caligrafer.php token revoke 2
```

```text
 Token #2 revoked
```

It takes the number without `#`, and stops the token at once. A number with no active token:
` No active token #<id>`.

Every `token` command needs the database and the framework tables: without them,
` The token table does not exist yet: run php caligrafer.php platform install`. The class behind them is
[`Caligrafy\Tokens`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#tokens).
## <a name="mcp"></a>`mcp`

```text
mcp [--token <token>]: MCP server over stdio for local AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor...): php caligrafer.php mcp
```

```bash
claude mcp add myapp -- php caligrafer.php mcp                                  # your own PHP
claude mcp add myapp -- docker compose exec -T dev-box php caligrafer.php mcp   # Docker
CALIGRAFY_TOKEN=cq_... php caligrafer.php mcp                                   # only what the token allows
```

+ **The protocol.** One JSON-RPC message per line on standard input, one answer per line on standard output; empty
  lines are skipped, notifications get no answer. The messages are those of
  [`Caligrafy\Mcp\Server`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces#mcp-server): `initialize`,
  `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. PHP errors go to standard error, so they never break the stream.
+ **The tools** are the capabilities, with their input schemas and the hints agents read before acting
  (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`). A call goes through the same checks, validation and audit as every other
  channel (channel `mcp`).
+ **Without a token** it has full access, like any script you run, and says so on standard error:
  `caligrafer mcp: no token, full local access (set CALIGRAFY_TOKEN to limit it)`.
+ **With a token** (`--token <token>`, or `CALIGRAFY_TOKEN`) it sees and calls only what the token's scopes allow. It
  needs the database (`caligrafer mcp: A token needs the database: set DB_ACTIVATE=true`), and a token that is unknown,
  revoked or expired stops it with exit code `1`.
+ **Agents on another computer** reach the application over HTTP: `Route::mcp('/mcp')` and a token. See
  [AI agents: MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#mcp).
## <a name="audit"></a>`audit`

```text
audit [--limit 50] [--capability <name>]: the latest capability calls
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php audit
php caligrafer.php audit --capability create_book --limit 200
```

```text
 2026-11-07 23:17:49  rest  token  2            create_book                  ok
 2026-11-07 23:17:49  rest  guest  -            create_book                  unauthenticated  Sign in or send a personal access token
```

| Column | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| when | `occurred_at`, in the server's time zone |
| channel | `web`, `rest`, `mcp` or `cli` (scheduled and background jobs run on `cli`) |
| who | `user`, `token`, `key`, `cli`, `guest`, or the system that ran it (`schedule`, `queue`) |
| id | the user's or the token's id, the job's name for a system, `-` for nobody |
| capability | its name |
| outcome | `ok`, `invalid`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict` or `error`, and a short detail |

Every call that changes data and every refusal is recorded; a successful read is not, and inputs never are. With no
rows: ` The audit log is empty (or php caligrafer.php platform install was not run)`. The class behind it is
[`Caligrafy\Audit`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#audit).
## Common mistakes

+ **`token revoke #2`** (G77): `#2` is read as `0` and nothing is revoked (` No active token #0`). Write
  `token revoke 2`.
+ **Tokens for an app online** (G79): an app on Caligrafy Cloud or your own server has no shell for `token create`.
  Give the app a page where signed-in people create their own tokens (a capability that calls `Tokens::create()` and
  refuses token contexts).
+ **A wrong token is a visitor** (G140): REST treats an unknown, revoked or expired `Bearer` token as no token, so a
  public capability still answers `200` (MCP over HTTP answers `401`). Check with `token list` that it is `active`.
+ **A token without `--user` passes any `level`** (G140): the level is a check on people. Keep the scopes of
  administrator capabilities off application tokens, or check the person in `handle()`.
+ **`mcp` with full access for an agent you do not control**: give it `CALIGRAFY_TOKEN` with the scopes it needs.
+ **A scope with a typo**: `--scopes book:read` creates a token for `book:read`, which no `books:read` capability
  accepts. Read the scopes `token create` prints.
## Related pages

+ [Caligrafer: every command](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer)
+ [Personal access tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#tokens) · [the audit log](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#audit)
+ [Sign-in, users and tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#agents)
+ [API reference: interfaces](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Interfaces)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Job-Commands -->

The **job commands** of [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer) run work outside
a page: `schedule` runs capabilities on a timer, `queue` runs the background jobs your capabilities pushed, `notify`
sets up web push and sends a test, and `test` runs the app's tests.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability check_prices prices:write: run it every hour
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability send_welcome_email users:write: run it in the background after sign-up
```

The `new-capability` skill writes the job in `application/config/schedule.php` (or the `Queue::push(...)` call), runs
`schedule list` or `queue work --once` to check it, and writes its test.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php schedule list` lists the job with the rhythm you asked for, and
`php caligrafer.php test` ends with `OK (...)`.
## By hand

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule list
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule run check-prices
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php queue work --once
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test
```

(without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`). The Docker server's `scheduler` container already runs
`schedule work` while it is up.
## <a name="schedule"></a>`schedule`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php schedule <list [--json] | run <job> | due | work | history [<job>] [--limit 50]>
 Jobs are declared in application/config/schedule.php
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `schedule list` | checks `schedule.php` (every job, its capability, its rhythm) and lists the jobs |
| `schedule list --json` | the same as one line of JSON (version 1): what Caligrafy Cloud reads at each deploy |
| `schedule run <job>` | runs one job now; `--if-due`: only when it is due this minute |
| `schedule due` | runs the jobs due this minute (for a cron line every minute) |
| `schedule work` | runs `due` every minute until stopped: ` Running the scheduled jobs every minute (Ctrl-C to stop)` |
| `schedule history [<job>] [--limit 50]` | the latest runs: when, the job, the outcome and its detail |

```text
 check-prices             every 1h       check_prices             UTC, timeout 55s
 nightly-report           0 2 * * *      build_report             Europe/Paris, timeout 120s (disabled)
```

+ A job calls one capability with fixed inputs, `every` one of `1m`, `5m`, `10m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `6h`, `12h`,
  `1d` (in UTC) or a five-field `cron` in its `timezone`, with a `timeout` (55 seconds by default, 300 at most).
+ One run at a time per job: a run that starts while the last one is still going is ` <job>: skipped, the previous run is still running`.
+ Each run is a child process stopped at its timeout, with full access like the command line, recorded in
  `caligrafy_job_runs` (kept 30 days).
+ Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` a job failed or timed out, `2` the file is invalid (every problem is printed, one per line),
  `3` skipped.
+ With no `schedule.php`: ` No scheduled jobs (application/config/schedule.php declares them)`.

Learn more in [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs) and
[`Caligrafy\Scheduler`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#scheduler).
## <a name="queue"></a>`queue`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php queue <work [--queue default] [--for <seconds>] [--once] [--sleep 3] | status | list [--status failed] [--limit 50] | failed | retry <id | all>>
 Background jobs pushed with Caligrafy\Queue::push('<capability>', [...])
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php queue work --once      # what is due, then stops
php caligrafer.php queue work --for 300   # for 5 minutes
php caligrafer.php queue work             # until Ctrl+C
php caligrafer.php queue status
php caligrafer.php queue list --status failed
php caligrafer.php queue retry 42         # retry all: every failed job
```

```text
 Working the queue default until it is empty
 #12 send_welcome_email: done
 1 done, 0 to try again, 0 failed
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `queue work` | runs the jobs of a queue (`--queue`, `default` by default): `--once` until it is empty, `--for <seconds>` for a while, else until stopped; `--sleep` is the pause when there is nothing to do (3 seconds) |
| `queue status` | ` 0 pending, 0 running, 0 done, 0 failed` |
| `queue list [--status <s>] [--limit 50]` | one line per job: its id, queue, capability, status, attempts, and when it may run or when it finished, with its last error |
| `queue failed` | `queue list --status failed` |
| `queue retry <id \| all>` | puts a failed job, or all of them, back in the queue: ` 1 failed job(s) back in the queue` |

+ Each job runs in its own process (`queue exec <id>`, internal), stopped at its timeout, with full access (G121): the
  capability that pushes the work checks who may ask for it.
+ A failed run is tried again after 30 s, 1 min, 2 min... until its attempts are used (3 by default); an input the
  capability refuses (invalid, not found) fails at once. Jobs are kept 7 days after they finish.
+ Online, a scheduled job on the framework's `queue_work` capability runs them every minute (Caligrafy Cloud runs it
  too), or a container of its own runs `queue work` for longer jobs.

Learn more in [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) and
[`Caligrafy\Queue`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs#queue).
## <a name="notify"></a>`notify`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php notify <keys [--subject mailto:you@example.com] | test <user id> | status <user id>>
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject mailto:you@example.com   # the web push keys, once
php caligrafer.php notify test 7                                  # a test notification to user 7
php caligrafer.php notify status 7                                # user 7's channels
```

+ **`keys`** writes `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` and `VAPID_SUBJECT` to `.env`:
  ` Web push keys written to .env (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT=mailto:you@example.com). Keep them: new keys cut off every subscribed browser`.
  It refuses to replace keys that are there (exit `1`). The subject is a `mailto:` address or an `https://` address;
  without `--subject` it uses `MAIL_FROM` or `MAIL_USERNAME` when it is an email address, else `APP_URL`.
+ **`test <user id>`** sends ` Notifications work` (` A test from php caligrafer.php notify test.`) to the user's
  channels, and prints the result as JSON.
+ **`status <user id>`** prints, as JSON, the channels offered, then `push` (`configured`, `public_key`, the number of
  `browsers`, `enabled`) and `email` (`configured`, `address`, `confirmed`, `enabled`) for that user.

Learn more in [Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications) and
[`Caligrafy\Notify`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Notify).
## <a name="test"></a>`test`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php test make <Name>   (writes tests/<Name>Test.php)
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php test make Books   # writes tests/BooksTest.php
php caligrafer.php test              # every tests/*Test.php and tests/*/*Test.php
php caligrafer.php test Books        # only the tests whose class or method name matches
```

```text
 tests/BooksTest.php written: php caligrafer.php test Books
```

+ **`make <Name>`** writes a class that extends `Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase` with one test and commented examples of
  `$this->call(...)` and `$this->assertCapabilityFails(...)`. A trailing `Test` in the name is dropped; an existing file
  is refused. It also writes `tests/.gitignore` when the folder had none, or one that ignored every file (projects made
  before 2.18.0).
+ **`test [<filter>]`** runs PHPUnit with `framework/testing/bootstrap.php`, no configuration file,
  `--display-warnings` and `--fail-on-warning`: a warning fails the run. Its exit code is PHPUnit's.
+ With no tests: ` No tests yet: php caligrafer.php test make <Name> writes tests/<Name>Test.php` (exit `0`). Without
  PHPUnit (`composer install --no-dev`): ` PHPUnit is not installed: composer install (with the development packages), then php caligrafer.php test`
  (exit `1`).

How to write the tests: [Testing capabilities](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Capabilities),
[Testing pages, forms and actions](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Pages-Forms-and-Actions)
and [The test database](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Test-Database).
## Common mistakes

+ **A scheduled job expects someone signed in** (G108): a job runs with nobody signed in, as the system. Give it the
  ids it works on in its inputs.
+ **A background job trusts its input** (G121): it runs with full access. Check who may ask in the capability that
  pushes it.
+ **`skipped` read as a failure** (G150): it is a run that started while the same job was still going.
+ **New web push keys**: every browser that turned push on stops receiving. `notify keys` refuses to replace them;
  keep them across deploys.
+ **A test that creates a table** (G121): MySQL commits the `CREATE` and ends the test's transaction, so its rows stay.
## Related pages

+ [Caligrafer: every command](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer)
+ [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs) · [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) · [Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications)
+ [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App)
+ [API reference: jobs, notifications and mail](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Jobs)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Maintenance-Commands -->

The **maintenance commands** of [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer) check and
keep a project current: `doctor` checks it, `design` picks its look, `update` and `upgrade` move it to a new release,
`plugin` connects its Claude Code plugin, and `snap` says what Snap Cards and the assistant need.
## With Claude

| You want | Ask |
| --- | --- |
| the latest release, with your changes merged | `/caligrafy-quill:update` |
| another look for every page | `/caligrafy-quill:design linear.app` |
| card views for the assistant | `/caligrafy-quill:assistant` |
| to know what is wrong | "run doctor and fix what fails" |

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php doctor` has no `FAIL`, and after an update no `.caligrafy-new` file is
left.
## By hand

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update --check
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php design list
```

(without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`). Run `doctor` first whenever something does not work.
## <a name="doctor"></a>`doctor`

```text
doctor [--only openai,groq] [--json] [--env <file>]: read-only health check of the project and of the services configured in .env
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php doctor
php caligrafer.php doctor --only database,mail
php caligrafer.php doctor --env .env.production
php caligrafer.php doctor --json
```

```text
Caligrafy doctor (read-only): Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0

 Database
  OK    Database: connected to mysql://mysql:3306/caligrafy (server 8.4.13)
  OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache and migrations installed
  OK    Migrations: 1 ran, none pending

 3 OK, 0 WARN, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP
```

+ **The groups** (`--only`, separated by commas): `project`, `database`, `openai`, `groq`, `agent`, `stripe`,
  `coinbase`, `watson`, `mail`. An unknown name lists the valid ones.
+ **`project`** checks PHP (8.3 or later) and its extensions, `vendor/`, the keys (`APP_KEY`, `API_KEY`), `APP_DEBUG`,
  the legacy API key and the pages that still send it, the Claude Code plugin, `public/uploads`, the web app manifest and
  the service worker, the design style, forms without a method and Pug pitfalls in views, the schedule file,
  notifications, Snap's card views, changed framework files, and whether the templates of `application/` are up to
  date. **`database`** checks the connection, the framework tables, Snap's tables and the migrations. The others check each service configured in `.env`; a service that is not configured is
  `SKIP`.
+ **Each line** is `OK`, `WARN`, `FAIL` or `SKIP`, with `-> <fix>` under it when there is something to do.
+ **Read-only**: it lists, reads or connects, and never creates, charges or sends anything (Watson only opens and
  closes a session when its assistants cannot be listed). It never creates `.env`.
+ **Secrets** are never printed: at most a known prefix and the last 4 characters.
+ **Exit code** `1` when a check fails. `--json` prints the results for a script.
+ **With Docker**, run it in the container (`docker compose exec dev-box ...`) so that the host `mysql` resolves.

The class behind it is [`Caligrafy\Doctor`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#doctor).
## <a name="design"></a>`design`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php design <list [--json] | show <name> | use <name> | off | status>
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `design list` | the styles of `application/design`, `framework/design/local` and `framework/design/vendor/*` (the first wins on a name clash): ` 85 styles (* selected, + stylesheet written)` |
| `design list --json` | `{"selected": ..., "styles": [...]}` |
| `design show <name>` | its source, description, `DESIGN.md` and stylesheet, and the copies a clash hides |
| `design use <name>` | `DESIGN_STYLE=<name>` in `.env` |
| `design off` | `DESIGN_STYLE=` in `.env`: Caligrafy's own look; the stylesheets are kept |
| `design status` | the selected style, and whether its stylesheet exists |

`use` changes nothing on the pages until `public/css/designs/<name>.css` exists (G92):
` DESIGN_STYLE=<name> in .env. Its stylesheet public/css/designs/<name>.css is not written yet: pages keep Caligrafy's own look until it is.`
`/caligrafy-quill:design` writes it. Learn more in [Design styles](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles).
## <a name="update"></a>`update`

```text
update [<version>] [--check] [--yes] [--no-composer]: moves the project to another release of Caligrafy Quill (the latest by default) and applies everything
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `<version>` | a release (`2.21.6` or `v2.21.6`); the latest by default. A lower version than the project's is refused |
| `--check` | says what it would replace, add and keep, the new settings and packages; writes nothing |
| `--yes` | goes on although git has uncommitted changes |
| `--no-composer` | prints the `composer update` command instead of running it |

On the latest release: ` Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0 is the latest: nothing to update. php caligrafer.php upgrade checks application/.`
What it replaces, keeps and merges, and how to finish an update, is in
[Updating Caligrafy](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Updating-Caligrafy).
## <a name="upgrade"></a>`upgrade`

```text
upgrade [--apply] [--local] [--force <application/path>] [--keep <application/path>]: brings the project up to date (dry run by default)
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| (none) | a dry run: when a newer release is out, the same as `update --check`; else what it would change in `application/` |
| `--apply` | when a newer release is out, `update` to it; else replaces the files of `application/` you never changed |
| `--local` | compares `application/` with this release's templates only, without looking for a newer release |
| `--force <application/path>` | replaces one file you changed (a backup is kept) |
| `--keep <application/path>` | keeps an untouched template copy that is now yours (remembered in the manifest); can be given more than once |

Each template file is reported as `missing`, `identical`, `outdated`, `customized`, `kept`, `held` or `routes`. The
states, and what to do with each, are in [Updating Caligrafy](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Updating-Caligrafy#upgrade).
## <a name="plugin"></a>`plugin`

```text
plugin: gives this project's Claude Code plugin its own source name and says where Claude Code reads it
```

```text
 Plugin source: caligrafy-7df2, plugin caligrafy-quill@caligrafy-7df2
 Claude Code reads the plugin from /Users/me/www/bookshelf/claude-plugin: restart claude in this folder to load it
```

1. It renames the plugin source of `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `.claude/settings.json` from the shared
   `caligrafy` to the project's own name (` (renamed from the shared "caligrafy")`). One name for every project gave
   them all the first one's plugin (G97).
2. When the `claude` command is on this computer, it registers the source (`claude plugin marketplace add`), installs
   `caligrafy-quill@<name>` for the project (`--scope project`), and, when Claude Code's copy of the plugin is older than
   the project's, refreshes it: ` Claude Code's copy of the plugin: <old>, now <new>`.
3. Without `claude` (in Docker) it says to run it on your computer.

A project with no `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: ` No .claude-plugin/marketplace.json: this project has no Claude Code plugin source (php caligrafer.php update brings it)`.
Run it when a `/caligrafy-quill:...` command is unknown, then restart `claude` in the folder. The class behind it is
[`Caligrafy\PluginSource`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#pluginsource).
## <a name="snap"></a>`snap`

```text
 Usage: php caligrafer.php snap [install | status | views]
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php snap install   # Snap's tables, and application/config/snap.php when there is none
php caligrafer.php snap           # what is ready (snap status)
php caligrafer.php snap views     # how each card that shows data looks (2.25.0)
```

```text
 Snap Cards and the assistant
  [ok] Tables            caligrafy_snap_*
  [ok] Route             Route::snap(); in application/config/routing/web.php
  [ok] Card hints        application/config/snap.php (optional: cards work without it)
  [--] Assistant model   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env (without it the assistant answers from the cards' names)

 Then open /assistant (signed in), and /snap for every card.
```

`snap views` lists every read-only capability's card:

```text
 Card views (application/views/snap/<capability>.pug)
  [ok] get_book                   from Bookshelf/book.pug
  [!!] list_books                 Bookshelf/books.pug changed since its card view was made: write it again
  [--] get_user                   no card view: a card designed from its data
  [??] old_report                 no read-only capability of that name: the file is not used
```

It exits with `1` when a card view is stale. `install` and `status` need the database. Learn more in
[Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#looks),
[`Snap\Views`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-views) and
[`Snap\Setup`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Snap#snap-setup).
## Common mistakes

+ **`doctor | tail` says nothing failed** (G89): a pipe hides the exit code. Read the summary line, or use
  `set -o pipefail`.
+ **A new skill is missing after an update** (G103): Claude Code runs its own copy of the plugin. `php caligrafer.php plugin`
  on your computer refreshes it.
+ **`upgrade` says nothing changes on an old project** (G96): before 2.10.0 it never looked for a newer release. Run
  `update`.
+ **`design use` and the pages look the same** (G92): the style's stylesheet is not written yet.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Deploy-Commands -->

The **deploy commands** of [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer) put a project
online: `deploy` prepares the database at each start in production, `cloud` runs the project on Caligrafy Cloud, and
`generatekeys` and `generateapikey` make keys for another environment.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:ship bookshelf
/caligrafy-quill:deploy --own-server
```

`ship` commits, creates the GitHub repository, pushes, signs in to Caligrafy Cloud with an approval in your browser,
runs `cloud create`, adds the deploy key, runs `cloud deploy` and checks the app online. `deploy --own-server` checks the
project and prepares it for your own server, and deploys nothing.

**Check** before you say OK: `php caligrafer.php cloud status bookshelf` says `running`, and
`https://bookshelf.caligrafy.com` opens.
## By hand

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud login
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud create bookshelf
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy bookshelf
```

(without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`). The whole walk-through is
[Deploying to Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Caligrafy-Cloud).
## <a name="deploy"></a>`deploy`

```text
deploy [--wait <seconds>]: prepares the database in production: framework tables, every new or changed application/models/<folder>/create_db.sql (never one that drops or deletes data twice), then the pending migrations
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php deploy                 # what the production image runs at start
php caligrafer.php deploy --wait 120      # wait up to 2 minutes for the database (default 60)
```

```text
 Caligrafy deploy
 caligrafy-schedule {"version":1,"jobs":[]}
  OK    Settings: .env compiled to .env.php (read without parsing on every request)
  OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache, migrations, scripts
  OK    application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql: run
  OK    Migrations: up to date
```

The production image runs it before Apache starts. What it does, line by line, is
[The deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step). It exits with `1` when the
database could not be prepared, and `0` when it is ready or `DB_ACTIVATE` is not `true`.
## <a name="cloud"></a>`cloud`

`php caligrafer.php cloud` (or `cloud help`) prints the list. Every command calls a capability of Caligrafy Cloud
(`POST https://deploy.caligrafy.com/capabilities/<name>`) with the account's token, and exits with `1` when Cloud
refuses, with its message.

### Signing in

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud login` | prints a code and opens `https://deploy.caligrafy.com/cli?code=...` in your browser: approve the code there, and the command collects the token |
| `cloud login --no-browser` | the same without opening the browser: open the address it prints |
| `cloud login --token cq_...` | takes a token created on the dashboard |
| `cloud login --paste` | asks for that token at a prompt |
| `cloud account` | your email and credits |
| `cloud logout` | removes `.caligrafy/cloud.json` |

```text
 To sign in, approve this code in your browser: <code>
 https://deploy.caligrafy.com/cli?code=...
 Signed in as you@example.com (10 credits). The token is in .caligrafy/cloud.json (git-ignored).
```

The token is kept in `.caligrafy/cloud.json` (ignored by git, never in the image). `CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_TOKEN` gives one
instead, and `CALIGRAFY_CLOUD_URL` points to another service. In the Docker `dev-box` the browser does not open: open the
address it printed.

### Apps

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud create <name> [--repo <url>] [--branch <b>]` | the app, built from a GitHub repository: the project's `origin` remote when `--repo` is missing (read from `.git/config` in the `dev-box`, which has no `git`) |
| `cloud key <name>` | the read-only deploy key of an app built from a private repository, printed alone (for `> key.pub`) and saved in `.caligrafy/<name>-deploy-key.pub` |
| `cloud deploy <name> [--no-wait]` | builds and starts it, and follows the build up to 15 minutes unless `--no-wait` |
| `cloud apps` | your apps: name, status, address and time left |
| `cloud status <name>` | one app's status and time left, and `[password protected]` when it is locked |
| `cloud logs <name>` | the deploy step's lines, then what the app prints |
| `cloud logs <name> --jobs` | the latest runs of every scheduled job |
| `cloud jobs <name>` | its scheduled jobs, their last and next runs |
| `cloud jobs <name> run <job>` | runs one now (it starts within a minute) |
| `cloud jobs <name> history <job> [--limit 20]` | the runs of one job, with their output |
| `cloud delete <name> --yes` | the app, its database and files, for good; without `--yes` it only says what it would delete |

A private repository: `create` prints the deploy key and the command that adds it,
`gh repo deploy-key add .caligrafy/<name>-deploy-key.pub --title "Caligrafy Cloud"`. Add it before `cloud deploy`.
A failed build prints the last 30 lines of its log.

### Settings

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud secret set <name> KEY=value` | a setting of the app's `.env`, applied at the next deploy |
| `cloud secret list <name>` | the names of its settings (never their values) |
| `cloud secret delete <name> KEY` | removes one, applied at the next deploy |

The database settings, the keys, `APP_URL` and `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` are written for the app; your settings cannot
replace them.

### Time and credits

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud extend <name> week\|month\|year` | 2, 5 or 50 credits of time online, added to what is left; a paused app starts again |
| `cloud credits 5\|10\|25\|50` | prints the Stripe page that buys credits (1 credit = 1 USD) |

### The marketplace

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud submit <name> [--file .caligrafy/marketplace.json] [--no-deploy] [--no-wait]` | sends the listing the `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace` skill wrote, then deploys the app again for the screenshots of its key pages |

The class behind them is [`Caligrafy\CloudClient`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Tooling#cloudclient).
## <a name="keys"></a>`generatekeys`, `generateapikey`

```text
generatekeys: generates an APP and an API pair of keys that you can put in your app's environment variable 
generateapikey: generates an API key that you can provide to any third party desiring to access your services
```

```bash
php caligrafer.php generatekeys       #  APP_KEY=...  API_KEY=...
php caligrafer.php generateapikey     #  API_KEY=... for the APP_KEY of .env
```

+ `generatekeys` makes a new `APP_KEY` (32 random bytes, base64) and the `API_KEY` encrypted from it. Use it for another
  environment (a production `.env`), or to replace a leaked `APP_KEY`: changing it signs everyone out and revokes every
  legacy API key.
+ `generateapikey` gives the `API_KEY` of the `APP_KEY` in `.env`. Legacy API keys are all the same key and cannot be
  revoked one by one: for programs and agents, use [`token`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer-Agent-Commands#token).
+ Both print the keys and write nothing. `initialize` already writes the keys of a new project.
## Common mistakes

+ **`cloud deploy <name> | tail` looks fine** (G89): the pipe hides the exit code of a refused deploy. Run it whole.
+ **`deploy` answers *has no time left*** (G90): every new app is free for its first 30 minutes from its first deploy;
  then `cloud extend <name> week`.
+ **The build fails** (G69): `composer.lock` is missing or older than `composer.json`. Run `composer update` and commit
  the lock file.
+ **Pages get `[ERROR 1004]` online** (G87): Caligrafy Cloud turns the legacy API key off. Pages call their routes with
  the session (`apiHeaders()`, the JS client).
+ **A password-protected app answers a redirect** (G114): until it is offered to the marketplace, a locked app sends
  visitors to the unlock page and API calls get `401`.
## Related pages

+ [Caligrafer: every command](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer)
+ [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online)
+ [Deploying to Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Caligrafy-Cloud) · [your own server](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Deploying-to-Your-Own-Server)
+ [The deploy step](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Deploy-Step) · [the production image](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/The-Production-Image)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/1.-Getting-Started -->

This page is the reference for installing Caligrafy Quill: what it needs, the recommended setup with Docker, the other setups (MAMP, XAMPP, LAMP, your own Apache), the address of a project (`APP_ROOT`), the server rules that protect your files, and the concepts and folders of a project. **New to Caligrafy?** Follow the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart): with Git and Docker, one command sets everything up.
## <a name="requirements"></a>Requirements

| | Needed |
| --- | --- |
| With Docker (recommended) | Git and Docker Desktop. PHP 8.5, Apache, MySQL 8.4 and phpMyAdmin 5.2.3 run in containers |
| On your own server | PHP 8.3 or higher (8.5 recommended) with `curl`, `json`, `mbstring`, `openssl` and `pdo_mysql` (and `gd`, `sodium`, `intl`, `zip`, `bcmath` for the features that use them); Apache with `mod_rewrite`, `mod_headers` and `mod_mime`, and `AllowOverride FileInfo` (or `All`); MySQL 8.4 (or another database PDO supports); Composer |
| For the Vue single page application template | Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ on your computer |

`php caligrafer.php doctor` checks the PHP version and extensions of a project.
## With Claude

Open the project folder in Claude Code and ask, or use the skill:
```text
/caligrafy-quill:server start
```
The `server` skill checks that Docker is running, that the ports 8080, 8077 and 3306 are free (it proposes other ports with a `docker-compose.override.yml` when one is taken) and that `.env` has the Docker settings (`DB_HOST=mysql`, an empty `APP_ROOT`), then starts the server and checks that the site answers. For a project from an idea, `/caligrafy-quill:idea` sets it up for you ([Quickstart with Claude](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude)).

**Check:** `http://localhost:8080` opens, and `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor` ends with `0 FAIL`.
## Installation

### <a name="quickstart"></a><a name="using-docker"></a>With Docker (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --docker
```
Answer `y` when it asks to delete the framework's `.git`. Add `--example` for the Tasks example. The command installs the PHP libraries, builds and starts the Docker server, initializes the project, points `.env` at the Docker database, creates the database and the framework tables, and adds the `/capabilities` and `/mcp` routes. The full output and the troubleshooting are in the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart#start).

The Docker server (`docker-compose.yaml`):

| Service | Address | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dev-box` | http://localhost:8080 | PHP 8.5 with Apache, your project folder mounted in it: a change to a file is live |
| `phpmyadmin` | http://localhost:8077 | phpMyAdmin, user `root`, password `root` |
| `mysql` | `127.0.0.1:3306` from your computer, `mysql:3306` from `dev-box` | MySQL 8.4, user `root`, password `root` |
| `scheduler` | | runs the scheduled jobs every minute (started by `server start`) |

Every day: `.bin/caligrafer server start` and `.bin/caligrafer server stop`. Run Caligrafer in the container: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php <command>`. The first start builds the PHP image (it compiles the PHP extensions: from under a minute to about 5 minutes); later starts take seconds; `.bin/caligrafer server rebuild` builds it again after a change to `docker/Dockerfile`. Stop with `stop`, not `docker compose down`: the `mysql` container has no volume, and removing it removes the data.

**Without PHP on your computer**, `.bin/caligrafer server start` on a project that is not set up runs `.bin/server`: the `prod-box` container, with the code copied into the image and rebuilt when files change, at `http://localhost:8080/caligrafy-quill`. Use `quickstart --docker` instead: it serves your folder as it is.

### <a name="composer"></a>With Composer, on MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP

> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Installing Caligrafy](https://youtu.be/21Lazd38FfQ)
>
> A video of the installation on a local Apache, MySQL and PHP server.

In the web folder of your running local server (MAMP: the folder of its Apache settings, `htdocs` by default; XAMPP: `htdocs`; LAMP: `/var/www/html`):
```bash
composer create-project caligrafy/caligrafy-quill myapp
cd myapp
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --local
```
`composer create-project` installs the latest release (see the [changelog](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md); `-s dev` takes the unreleased `master` branch) and prints the next command. `quickstart --local` gives the project its address (`APP_ROOT`, from its place in the web folder; MAMP's own settings are read), asks for the MySQL settings with the server's defaults, and creates the database, the framework tables and the routes. On Windows: `php caligrafer.php quickstart`. Details: [Quickstart, with Composer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart#composer).

**Check:** open the address it prints, for example `http://localhost:8888/myapp` with a default MAMP.

### <a name="manual"></a>By hand, on your own Apache

1. Get the code in the web folder of your server (or in a folder a virtual host points to):
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
    cd myapp
    composer install
    ```
2. Initialize the project:
    ```bash
    php caligrafer.php initialize --yes
    ```
    ```text
     .git deleted: git init starts your project's own history
     Application initialized successfully
    ```
    It creates `.env` from `framework/settings/.env.example`, writes a new `APP_KEY` and `API_KEY`, sets `APP_ROOT=myapp` (the folder name), copies the templates to `application/` and makes `public/uploads` writable. For a site at the root of its address (a virtual host), run `php caligrafer.php initialize off --yes` instead: `APP_ROOT` is then empty.
3. Point `.env` at your database:
    ```text
    DB_ACTIVATE=true
    DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
    DB_PORT=3306
    DB_DATABASE=myapp
    DB_USERNAME=root
    DB_PASSWORD=<your password>
    ```
    Use `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`: with `localhost`, PDO uses the MySQL socket and ignores `DB_PORT`.
4. Create the database, the framework tables and the routes:
    ```bash
    php caligrafer.php quickstart --url http://localhost/myapp
    ```
    It finds the database settings already set, so it asks nothing, and ends with `Ready. Next:`.
5. Check:
    ```bash
    php caligrafer.php doctor
    ```
    and open `http://localhost/myapp` (your server's port and path).

`php caligrafer.php generatekeys` prints a new key pair when you need one for another environment.

### <a name="different-root-folder"></a>The project's address: `APP_ROOT`

`APP_ROOT` in `.env` is the path of the project under the address of the server, without slashes:

| The project is served at | `APP_ROOT` |
| --- | --- |
| `http://localhost:8080/` (Docker), or a virtual host | empty |
| `http://localhost/myapp/` | `myapp` |
| `http://localhost/clients/myapp/` | `clients/myapp` |

`initialize` sets it to the folder name (`initialize off`: empty), and `quickstart` sets it from the project's place in the web folder of MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP. Rename the folder, or move it, and change `APP_ROOT` to match.

### <a name="virtualhosts"></a>Virtual hosts

A virtual host is optional. It must allow the project's `.htaccess` files:
```text
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName bookshelf.test
    DocumentRoot "/path/to/myapp"
    <Directory "/path/to/myapp">
       Options FollowSymLinks
       AllowOverride All
       Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```
Add `127.0.0.1 bookshelf.test` to `/etc/hosts`, restart Apache, and set `APP_ROOT=` (empty).
## <a name="protecting-your-server-files"></a>Protecting your server files

Only `index.php` and the `public` folder are meant to be reached from a browser. The `.htaccess` file at the root of the project answers `403` for existing:
+ dotfiles and dot folders, such as `.env`, `.env.php`, `.git` and `.claude` (`.well-known` stays reachable);
+ the folders `application`, `framework`, `vendor`, `tests`, `qa`, `docker`, `claude-plugin`, `archives`, `backups` (2.19.1) and `node_modules`;
+ the files `caligrafer.php`, `composer.json`, `composer.lock`, `docker-compose.yaml` (or `.yml`), `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, and any `.sql`, `.log`, `.bak`, `.ini`, `.sh` or `.env` file.

Every other address goes to `index.php?uri=<path>`, the front controller. A second `.htaccess` in `public/uploads` stops any script that ends up there from running or being downloaded. The rules are case-insensitive (macOS and Windows file systems).

Keep these files when you deploy. They need `mod_rewrite`, `mod_headers` (CORS, cookies, the service worker scope) and `mod_mime` (the web app manifest type), and `AllowOverride FileInfo` (or `All`): without `mod_headers`, Apache answers `500`. Check a server with `curl -I http://<your-host>/.env`: the answer must be `403` or `404`.

**nginx** ignores `.htaccess`. Use equivalent rules, for example:
```text
location ~ /\.(?!well-known) { deny all; }
location ~ ^/(application|framework|vendor|tests|qa|docker|claude-plugin|archives|node_modules|backups)/ { deny all; }
location ~ ^/(caligrafer\.php|composer\.(json|lock)|docker-compose\.ya?ml|package(-lock)?\.json)$ { deny all; }
location ~* \.(sql|log|bak|ini|sh|env)$ { deny all; }
location = /public/sw.js { add_header Service-Worker-Allowed "/"; }
types { application/manifest+json webmanifest; }
location ~* ^/public/uploads/.*\.(php\d*|phtml|phar|cgi|pl|py|sh)$ { deny all; }
location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?uri=$uri&$args; }
```

PHP's built-in server (`php -S`) reads no `.htaccess`: it neither routes the pages nor protects these files. Use Docker or Apache.
## <a name="caligrafer"></a>Caligrafer, the command line tool

`php caligrafer.php <command>` (with Docker: `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php <command>`). **Every command is on one page: [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer).** The ones you use most:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `quickstart [--example]` | sets a project up in one step ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#quickstart)) |
| `service <Folder/Name> --scope <scope>` | creates a capability ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#service)) |
| `call <capability> key=value` | calls a capability and prints its answer ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#call)) |
| `sql <file.sql>` | runs a SQL script, such as a model's `create_db.sql` ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#sql)) |
| `migrate [status \| make <name>] [--env <file>]` | changes tables that hold data ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#migrate)) |
| `client` | writes the JavaScript client of the capabilities ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#client)) |
| `token create <name> --scopes ...` | a token for a program or an AI agent ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#token)) |
| `test [make <Name>]` | runs your app's tests, or writes one ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#test)) |
| `doctor` | checks the project and its services ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#doctor)) |
| `update` | moves the project to a newer release ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#update)) |

+ <a name="version"></a>The version of a project: `php caligrafer.php version` prints `Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0` ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#version)).
+ <a name="buildoncecommands"></a>Capabilities, tokens, MCP and the audit log: `service`, `capabilities`, `call`, `client`, `platform install`, `token`, `mcp`, `audit` ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#service)).
+ <a name="doctor"></a>Something does not work: `php caligrafer.php doctor` checks the project, the database and every service of `.env`, with a fix for each problem ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#doctor)).
## <a name="architecture"></a>How a project is built

Caligrafy is a Model-View-Controller framework with one more layer on top, so that a feature is **built once and experienced everywhere**:

| Layer | What it holds | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Capabilities** | the features, written once: inputs and their rules, who may use them, the work, the result | `application/services/` (a `Caligrafy\Service` with `#[Capability]`) |
| **Experiences** | every way to reach a capability | Pug pages (`Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::action`), Vue apps (the JavaScript client), REST (`Route::capability`, `Route::capabilities`), AI agents (`Route::mcp`) |
| **Models** | one class per table, read and written by capabilities only | `application/models/` |
| **Views** | the Pug pages | `application/views/` |
| **Controllers** | older code and the examples a new project ships; a new request never needs one | `application/controllers/` |

### <a name="buildonce"></a>Build once, experience everywhere

A capability is called the same way by every experience, so its rules never drift between the web pages, the apps, the API and the agents. [How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works) explains it in 5 minutes; [Build Once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP) has every option.

### <a name="namespace"></a>The `Caligrafy` namespace

The framework's classes are in the namespace `Caligrafy`. Your classes are global (no namespace) unless you give them one, and `use` the framework classes they extend:
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Model;

class Book extends Model
{
    public $id;
    public $title;
}
```
Two classes of `application/` cannot have the same fully qualified name: name them distinctly (`Book`, `ListBooks`, `BookFormController`) or give them a namespace.
## <a name="fundamentals"></a>Fundamentals

The Bookshelf (books, authors, tags, loans) is the example of this wiki.

+ **Capabilities**: one feature of the application (list the books, add a book) written once as a class: it declares its inputs with [validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation), the scope and permission level it needs, does the work and returns data. Learn more [here](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service).
+ **Routes**: the lines of `application/config/routing/web.php` that connect an address to what answers it. `Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']])` shows a page with the result of a capability; `Route::form('/books', 'create_book')` takes a form; `Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books')` is a REST address. Learn more in [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing) and [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes).
+ **Experiences**: web pages, Vue apps and single page applications on any device, REST clients and AI agents (MCP) all call the same capabilities, each shaped for its audience.
+ **Identity**: people sign in (`Route::auth`, passkeys); programs and AI agents use personal access tokens with scopes, which can expire and be revoked. Every change and every refusal goes to the audit log.
+ **Models**: one class per table, with one public property per column. The [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) of a model (`Book::where(...)`, `Book::insert(...)`) reads the table named after the class (`Book` -> `books`) unless the model declares `protected static $tableName`. Learn more in [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models).
+ **Queries**: lists, filters, paging and related rows with every value bound: `Database::table('books')`, `Book::where('author_id', 3)->with('author')->paginate(20, $page)`.
+ **Relationships**: a book's author, an author's books, a book's tags through a pivot table: a capability loads them with `with()` (`Book::with('author')`), which reads them from the names of the tables and columns, with no code in the model. Learn more in [Relationships](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/5.-Relationships).
+ **Naming conventions**:
    1. Every table's primary key is `id`.
    2. A foreign key is `<model name in lower case>_id` (`author_id` for the model `Author`), of the same type as the `id` it references (`INT UNSIGNED` for an `INT UNSIGNED` id), and every foreign key constraint has a name unique in the database (`fk_books_author_id`: `fk_<table>_<column>`).
    3. A many-to-many pivot table is `<table1>_<table2>` (`books_tags`, with `book_id` and `tag_id`), written in `create_db.sql` like any table; `with(['tags' => ['pivot' => true]])` on `books` reads `books_tags`, or `tags_books` when only that one exists.
+ **Tables**: a new table is a `create_db.sql` next to its model (`php caligrafer.php sql ...`); a change to a table that holds data is a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations).
+ **Views**: Pug pages rendered on the server ([Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)), or Vue apps in `public/` that call the capabilities through the JavaScript client.
+ **Validation**: the rules of [GUMP](https://github.com/Wixel/GUMP), in each capability's `$rules`.
## <a name="filestructure"></a>File structure

| Folder | What goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `application/` | your application: `services/` (capabilities), `models/`, `views/`, `controllers/`, `config/` (`routing/web.php`, `config.php`, and `schedule.php` or `container.php` when you add them), and `migrations/` once you write one. Each class is loaded the first time it is used, from a class map Caligrafy keeps up to date: no `require` |
| `framework/` | the framework. `core/` holds the framework classes (`Service`, `Capability`, `Context`, `Route`, `Model`...), `interfaces/` the REST, MCP and JavaScript client channels, `settings/` the templates `initialize` copies. Change it only to change the framework |
| `public/` | what the browser loads: scripts, stylesheets, images, client apps, and `public/uploads/` for uploaded files |
| `tests/` | your app's tests, run with `php caligrafer.php test` ([Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App)). Never loaded by a page; the production image leaves it out |
| `vendor/` | the libraries Composer installs |
## Related pages

+ [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer)
+ [How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works)
+ [Security and upgrading](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading)
