# Routing

A route connects an address (`GET /books/3`) to what answers it. Every route of a Caligrafy project is one line of
`application/config/routing/web.php`. A route names a capability (a feature written once, in `application/services/`)
and says how the web reaches it: a page that shows its data (`Route::page`), a form that calls it (`Route::form`), a file
to download (`Route::download`), a JSON API (`Route::capability`), or anything else a browser asks (`Route::action`).
Since 2.21.0 every request can be declared this way, so a new application has no controller. This page covers how routes
match, pages, redirects and capability routes. Forms, sign-in, webhooks, downloads and `Route::action` have their own
page: [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes).

## With Claude

Ask for the feature, not the route: the `caligrafy-quill` plugin writes the capability and the routes together.

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book title:string published_year:int author:fk
```

or, for one feature:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability get_book books:read read-only
"Show each book on its own page at /books/{id}, with a 'Book not found' page when the id does not exist."
```

What Claude writes: the capabilities in `application/services/<Folder>/`, the routes in
`application/config/routing/web.php` (`Route::page` for pages, `Route::form` for forms, `Route::capability` for the
REST API, inside the `try` block and before `Route::run();`) and the Pug views in `application/views/`.

**Check** before you say OK:

- [ ] Every new route is in the `try` block of `web.php`, before `Route::run();`.
- [ ] Pages are `Route::page`, forms are `Route::form`, a custom request is `Route::action`: no controller and no closure
      that reads or writes data.
- [ ] A fixed address such as `/books/new` comes before `/books/{id}` (the first route that matches wins).
- [ ] Each page's `data` names a read-only capability (`readOnly: true`).
- [ ] `curl -i` of each new address answers the status you expect (200, 302, 404).

## <a name='definingroutes'></a>By hand

You need a project from the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) with its
database. The commands below run in the project folder; with the Docker dev server, run them as
`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`. The addresses use `http://localhost:8080`, the Docker dev server.

1. **Create the Bookshelf tables.** Write `application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql` (it can run more than once: it
   never drops anything):

   ```sql
   /* Bookshelf: the first version of its tables, and sample books.
    * Run it with: docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql
    * Safe to run again: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips a table that exists, INSERT IGNORE a row whose id exists.
    */

   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authors (
       id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
       name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
       bio TEXT NULL,
       created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       PRIMARY KEY (id)
   ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (
       id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
       title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
       published_year SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
       summary TEXT NULL,
       author_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
       created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       PRIMARY KEY (id),
       KEY idx_books_author_id (author_id),
       CONSTRAINT fk_books_author_id FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES authors (id)
           ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
   ) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

   -- Sample data, with fixed ids so that book 3 is Kindred everywhere
   INSERT IGNORE INTO authors (id, name, bio) VALUES
       (1, 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 'American author of science fiction and fantasy, known for the Earthsea books.'),
       (2, 'Octavia E. Butler', 'American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.'),
       (3, 'Italo Calvino', 'Italian writer of playful, inventive novels and short stories.');

   INSERT IGNORE INTO books (id, title, published_year, summary, author_id) VALUES
       (1, 'A Wizard of Earthsea', 1968, 'A gifted boy learns magic and must face the shadow he set loose.', 1),
       (2, 'The Left Hand of Darkness', 1969, 'An envoy visits a planet whose people have no fixed sex.', 1),
       (3, 'Kindred', 1979, 'A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.', 2),
       (4, 'Parable of the Sower', 1993, 'In a collapsing California, a teenager starts a new belief system.', 2),
       (5, 'Invisible Cities', 1972, 'Marco Polo describes imaginary cities to the emperor Kublai Khan.', 3);
   ```

   Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql`. It prints
   ` application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql run on caligrafy`. A later change to these tables, once they hold
   data, is a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations).

2. **Describe an author and a book.** Write `application/models/Bookshelf/Author.php`:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Model;

   // One Author = one row of the authors table (Author::query() reads authors: the class name in lower case, plus s)
   class Author extends Model {

       // one public property per column of the table
       public $id;
       public $name;
       public $bio;
       public $created_at;
       public $modified_at;
   }
   ```

   and `application/models/Bookshelf/Book.php`:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Model;

   // One Book = one row of the books table. Book::with('author') adds the row of authors whose id is author_id
   class Book extends Model {

       // one public property per column of the table
       public $id;
       public $title;
       public $published_year;
       public $summary;
       public $author_id;
       public $created_at;
       public $modified_at;
   }
   ```

3. **Write the two capabilities the pages read.** Run:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListBooks --scope books:read --read-only
   docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/GetBook --scope books:read --read-only
   ```

   Each prints ` Created application/services/Bookshelf/<Name>.php: capability '<name>' (scope books:read)`. Replace
   the content of `application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php` with:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Service;

   // list_books: the catalog, sorted by title, 20 books per page, each with its author. Anyone may read it
   #[Capability(
       name: 'list_books',
       description: 'Lists the books of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page, each with its author (id, name, bio). Give author_id to list only the books of one author, and page for the next pages. Returns data (the books), total, page, per_page and pages.',
       scope: 'books:read',
       readOnly: true,
       public: true
   )]
   class ListBooks extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer', 'page' => 'integer');
       public $descriptions = array(
           'author_id' => 'Optional: only the books of this author',
           'page' => 'Optional: the page, 1 by default (20 books per page)'
       );

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           // two queries for the page (the count, then the books) and one for all their authors
           $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
           if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
               $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);   // the value is bound, never pasted into the SQL
           }
           return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
       }
   }
   ```

   and the content of `application/services/Bookshelf/GetBook.php` with:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Service;
   use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

   // get_book: one book with its author, or "not found"
   #[Capability(
       name: 'get_book',
       description: 'Returns one book of the catalog with its author (id, name, bio), by the id of the book.',
       scope: 'books:read',
       readOnly: true,
       public: true
   )]
   class GetBook extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');
       public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book');

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           $book = Book::with('author')->find($input['id']);
           if (!$book) {
               throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no book #{$input['id']}");
           }
           return $book;
       }
   }
   ```

   Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities`: the list shows `get_book` and `list_books`, both
   `public` and `read`.

4. **Declare the routes.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, inside the `try` block, after
   `Route::page('/', 'default/index');` and before `Route::run();`, write:

   ```php
       // the Bookshelf pages: their data comes from read-only capabilities
       Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
       Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book'], 'notFound' => 'Bookshelf/notfound']);
       Route::redirect('/catalog', '/books');
   ```

5. **Write the views.** `application/views/Bookshelf/books.pug` (the [Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)
   page adds the form that creates a book):

   ```pug
   extends ../default/master/site

   block title
     | Bookshelf

   block content
     section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
       h1.cq-display Books

     section.cq-band.cq-band--tight
       .cq-inner.cq-inner--narrow
         if $books['total'] == 0
           p.cq-empty-state No books yet.
         else
           ul.cq-rows
             each $b in $books['data']
               li.cq-row
                 .cq-row-main
                   p.cq-row-title
                     a(href=$home . 'books/' . $b['id'])= $b['title']
                   p.cq-row-meta= $b['author']['name'] . ', ' . $b['published_year']
   ```

   `application/views/Bookshelf/book.pug`:

   ```pug
   extends ../default/master/site

   block title
     = $book['title'] . ' · Bookshelf'

   block content
     section.cq-hero.cq-hero--page
       h1.cq-display= $book['title']
       p.cq-lead= 'by ' . $book['author']['name'] . ', ' . $book['published_year']
   ```

   `application/views/Bookshelf/notfound.pug`:

   ```pug
   extends ../default/master/site

   block title
     | Not found · Bookshelf

   block content
     section.cq-hero
       h1.cq-display Not found
       p.cq-lead= $message
       .cq-cta
         a.btn.btn-primary(href=$home . 'books') All books
   ```

6. **Try every route.** Run:

   ```bash
   curl -s http://localhost:8080/helloworld
   ```

   It prints `Hello World` (the template's own closure route). Open `http://localhost:8080/books`: the five books,
   *A Wizard of Earthsea* first, each with its author and year. Open `http://localhost:8080/books/3`: the title
   "Kindred" and "by Octavia E. Butler, 1979". Then:

   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/books/999
   curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/catalog | grep -i "^location"
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/nothing
   ```

   They print `404` (the "Not found" page with "There is no book #999"), `Location: http://localhost:8080/books`
   and `404`.

**Check**

- [ ] `/books` lists the books and `/books/3` shows one.
- [ ] `/books/999` and `/books/abc` show "Not found" with a 404 status.
- [ ] `/catalog` answers `302` with `Location: .../books`.
- [ ] An address no route declares answers `404`.

## <a name='basicroute'></a>How a request finds its route

`Route::run()`, the last line of the `try` block, compares the request with the routes in the order they are declared:

1. The HTTP method must be the same. `HEAD` is answered as `GET`. A form sends `PUT` or `DELETE` with a hidden
   `_method` field ([HTML form methods](#htmlformmethods)).
2. The path must have the same number of segments, and each fixed segment must be identical. A `{name}` segment
   matches any one segment. Leading and trailing slashes do not count, nor does the query string.
3. The **first** route that matches wins: declare `/books/new` before `/books/{id}`, or `/books/{id}` answers
   `/books/new` with the id `new`.
4. Nothing matches: `404` (`[ERROR 1005] Page Not Found`, or `{"error":{"code":1005,"message":"Page Not Found"}}` to a
   JSON request). The address exists with other methods: `405` with an `Allow` header
   (`Invalid Http Request Method: this address answers GET`).

A `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` that is not JSON is checked for its CSRF token before any route runs: without it the answer
is `403` `[ERROR 3000] Security Error - Cross Site Forgery`, whatever the address. `Route::webhook` addresses (checked by
their signature) and `Route::mcp` addresses (2.19.1: a post without a personal access token answers `401` with
`WWW-Authenticate`) skip it.

## <a name='parameterroute'></a>Route variables

`{name}` in a route captures one segment of the address:

```php
Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']]);
```

+ In a `Route::page`, the variables become the inputs of the `data` capabilities (`get_book` gets `id`) and variables
  of the view (`$id`).
+ In `Route::form`, `Route::download`, `Route::capability` and `Route::redirect`, they become inputs or fill the
  `{name}` of the target, the same way.
+ In `Route::action`, they become inputs too. Everywhere the route variable wins over a query string value of the same
  name: `/books/3?id=9` gives `id = 3` (2.21.2; in 2.21.0 and 2.21.1, `Route::action` and `Route::capability` gave `9`).
+ In a controller you keep, read them with `$this->request->fetch('id')`
  ([Request](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/3.-Request)). Since 2.21.7, on a `GET`, a query string value of
  the same name never replaces it.

A variable is always a string, and the route does not check it: `/books/abc` reaches `get_book`, whose `integer` rule
refuses it.

## <a name='pageroutes'></a>Page routes: `Route::page`

`Route::page($route, $view, $options)` answers a `GET` with a Pug view, through the framework's page controller.

```php
Route::page('/', 'default/index');
Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book'], 'notFound' => 'Bookshelf/notfound']);
Route::page('/books/new', 'Bookshelf/new', ['signedIn' => true, 'comeBack' => true]);
Route::page('/admin/books', 'Bookshelf/admin', ['level' => 1, 'data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
Route::page('/about', 'default/about', ['with' => ['title' => 'About the Bookshelf']]);
Route::page('/join', 'Bookshelf/join', ['visitorsOnly' => '/books']);
Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books'], 'query' => ['sort' => 'title']]);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | none | `name => 'capability'`: calls each capability as the person who opens the page and gives the result to the view as `$name`. Its inputs are the query string and the route variables; the route variables win (`/books/3?id=9` gives `id = 3`). `name => ['capability', ['author_id' => 2]]` gives fixed inputs instead. Only read-only capabilities: a capability that changes data, or does not exist, stops the page with an error that names it |
| `signedIn` | `false` | `true`: visitors are sent to `/login` |
| `comeBack` | `false` | `true`, with `signedIn` or `level`, or when a `data` capability needs someone: visitors go to `/login?return=<this page, with its query string>`, and `Route::auth` brings them back after signing in (2.20.0) |
| `visitorsOnly` | none | a path: people already signed in are sent there (a sign-up or landing page) (2.20.0) |
| `query` | none | what the view gets of the query string: `'query' => ['show']` gives `$show`, a string, `''` when absent (2.20.0); `'query' => ['app' => 'index']` gives `$app`, `'index'` when absent; the two can be mixed (2.21.0). A route variable of the same name wins |
| `level` | `0` | people whose level (the `permissions` column of `users`) is lower are sent to `/notAuthorized`, visitors to `/login` |
| `with` | none | fixed values for the view: `['with' => ['title' => 'Books']]` |
| `notFound` | none | a view shown with a `404` when a `data` capability refuses (not found, or inputs it refuses). It gets the route variables, the `with` values, `$message`, `$authorized` and `$user` |

`signedIn`, `level` and `visitorsOnly` need `Auth::authentication('User', 'users');` in `web.php`; without it, opening
the page stops with an error that says so.

**What the view receives**: the route variables, the names listed in `query`, the `with` values, the `data` results
(plain arrays: `$book['title']`), `$authorized` (true when someone is signed in) and `$user` (`id`, `username`,
`permissions`, or `null`). The rest of the query string stays out of the view: a `data` capability gets it as inputs.
`authorized` and `user` are reserved names: a `data`, `with` or `query` entry with one of them is an error.

**When a capability refuses the page's data**:

| The capability | The answer |
| --- | --- |
| needs someone signed in, nobody is | a redirect to `/login` (`comeBack`: with `?return=`), with the authentication module; else `403` |
| refuses the person (`forbidden`) | `403` `[ERROR 1006] Forbidden` |
| finds nothing, or refuses the inputs | the `notFound` view with `404`, else `404` `[ERROR 1005] Page Not Found` |

A request with `Accept: application/json` gets the view's data as JSON instead of the page.

## <a name='declarativeroutes'></a>Forms, sign-in, webhooks, downloads, redirects and everything else

One line each, calling a capability:

```php
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}', 'flash' => 'Book added']);   // a form's POST
Route::auth(['home' => '/books']);                                                          // /login, /logout, /register
Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_payment', ['verify' => 'stripe']);                  // events another service posts
Route::download('/books.csv', 'list_books', ['filename' => 'books.csv']);                   // a read-only capability as a file
Route::download('/photos.zip', 'list_photo_files', ['as' => 'zip', 'root' => 'public/uploads/photos']);   // its files as one ZIP (2.22.0)
Route::redirect('/old/books/{id}', '/books/{id}', 301);                                     // an address that moved
Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books');                           // what a page or a form cannot say
```

Every option, with a complete example of each:
[Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes).

## <a name='capabilityroutes'></a>Capability routes: REST, the JS client and agents

```php
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');          // one route, one capability, JSON
Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');       // {id} becomes the input "id"
Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book');
Route::capabilities('/capabilities');                          // GET lists, POST /capabilities/{name} calls: the JS client of the Vue apps
Route::mcp('/mcp');                                            // AI agents: the capabilities their token allows, as MCP tools
```

They check who calls (a personal access token, or the signed-in person with the `X-CSRF-Token` header for writes),
validate the inputs and answer JSON: `{"data": ...}` with `200` (`201` for a `POST` that changes data), or
`{"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}` with `401`, `403`, `404`, `409` or `422`.

```bash
curl -s -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/books/2
```

prints `{"data":{"id":2,"title":"The Left Hand of Darkness","published_year":1969,"summary":"...","author_id":1,"created_at":"...","modified_at":"...","author":{"id":1,"name":"Ursula K. Le Guin",...}}}`
(with `Route::capability('GET', '/api/books/{id}', 'get_book');` in `web.php`).
More: [REST](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#rest)
and [REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.-Helpers-,-Forms-&-REST-API#restapi).

## Reference

All are static methods of `Caligrafy\Route` (`use Caligrafy\Route;` at the top of `web.php`).

| Method | Answers | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page($route, $view, $options = [])` | GET | a Pug view with data from read-only capabilities ([above](#pageroutes)) |
| `form($route, $capability, $options = [])` | POST (or PUT, DELETE) | a form's post calls a capability, then redirects |
| `auth($options = [])` | several | `/login`, `/logout`, `/register`, `/notAuthorized` (needs `Auth::authentication(...)` before it) |
| `webhook($route, $capability, $options)` | POST | events another service posts, signature checked, no CSRF token |
| `download($route, $capability, $options = [])` | GET | a read-only capability's result as a CSV or JSON file |
| `redirect($from, $to, $status = 302, $options = [])` | GET | sends the visitor to `$to` (`301`, `302`, `303`, `307` or `308`); `['keepQuery' => true]` takes the query string along |
| `action($route, $capability, $options = [])` | GET, or `method` | a web-only capability answers: a view, a redirect, JSON or text ([Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action)) |
| `capability($method, $route, $name)` | the method given | one capability as JSON (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE`) |
| `capabilities($prefix = '/capabilities')` | GET, POST | the listing and `POST {prefix}/{name}` for the JS client |
| `mcp($route = '/mcp')` | POST (GET, DELETE: 405) | the MCP endpoint for AI agents |
| `notifications()` | GET, POST | the confirm and unsubscribe pages of notification emails |
| `bots()` | POST, DELETE | the data routes of the Watson bot apps (`/__bots__/...`) |
| `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete($route, $method)` | that method | a closure, `'Controller'` or `'Controller@action'`, for what existing projects declare that way ([Other ways](#controllerroute)) |
| `run()` | | matches the request and runs its route: the last line of the `try` block |
| `routes()` | | the routes declared so far: `[['method' => 'GET', 'route' => 'books/{id}'], ...]` (tests) |
| `handler($method, $route)` | | the closure or `'Controller@action'` of a declared route (tests) |
| `reset()` | | forgets every route (tests) |
| `Route::$currentRoute`, `Route::$currentBind` | | the matched pattern (`books/{id}`) and its variables (`currentRoute()`, `currentBind()`) |

Errors of the router (each one also answers JSON to a JSON request):

| Status | Error | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `404` | `1005` Page Not Found | no route matches, or a page's data is not found |
| `405` | `1000` Invalid Http Request Method | the address exists with other methods (`Allow` header) |
| `403` | `3000` Cross Site Forgery | a form post without the session's `_token` |
| `403` | `1006` Forbidden | a page's capability refuses the person |
| `404` | `1001` Invalid Controller or Action | a `'Controller@action'` route whose class or method does not exist |
| `401` | `1004` Access Denied | a JSON request to `Route::action` or a controller route without `X-CSRF-Token` or a token that grants `*` |

## <a name='controllerroute'></a>Other ways: closures and controller routes

`Route::get`, `post`, `put` and `delete` take a closure or a controller. A new request does not need them: the routes
above cover every case, with `Route::action` for what is neither a page nor a form. They stay for existing projects and
for the routes a new project's `web.php` ships: see
[Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers#when).

```php
Route::get('/helloworld', function () { echo 'Hello World'; });          // a closure
Route::get('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'BookController@byAuthor');      // a controller and its action
Route::get('/reports/{id}', 'Shop\ReportController@show');                // a namespaced controller
Route::get('/books', 'BookController');                                   // no action: index()
```

+ `'Name@action'` finds a declared class `Name` first (global or fully qualified, a leading `\` is accepted), then
  the example controllers of `Caligrafy\Controllers` (`'ClientController'`); a class or action that does not exist
  answers `404` `[ERROR 1001]`. More: [Namespaced controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers#namespacedcontrollers).
+ A **controller route** refuses a JSON request (`Accept: application/json`) unless it comes from a page of the app
  (the session cookie and the `X-CSRF-Token` header) or, with `Auth::activateAPI();` in `web.php`, from a program
  with a personal access token that grants `*` (`401` `[ERROR 1004] Access Denied: <why>` otherwise).
+ A **closure route** has no such check, and a JSON request skips the form's CSRF check. Never read or write data in
  a closure: use `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::action` or a capability route.

## <a name='htmlformmethods'></a>HTML form methods

HTML forms only send `GET` and `POST`. A `POST` with a hidden `_method` field set to `PUT` or `DELETE` is routed as
that method (method spoofing). In a Pug form, `=methodField('PUT')` writes the field:

```pug
form(method='POST', action=$home . 'books/' . $book['id'])
  =csrf()
  =methodField('PUT')
  button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Save
```

It reaches `Route::put('/books/{id}', ...)` or `Route::form('/books/{id}', 'update_book', ['method' => 'PUT'])`.
`_method` is read from the form fields or the query string, never from a JSON body: a script that sends JSON uses the
real method (`fetch(url, {method: 'PUT', ...})`).

## Common mistakes

+ **A route after `Route::run();`** is never declared. Every route goes before it, in the `try` block.
+ **`/books/{id}` before `/books/new`**: `/books/new` shows the book `new` (a 404). Declare fixed addresses first.
+ **A page whose data capability writes**: `Route::page` refuses it (opening a page must not change data). Use
  `Route::form` for writes, or `Route::action` when opening an address really has to change something.
+ **Data work in a closure route**: it has no permission rules and no CSRF check for JSON calls. Write a capability.
+ **`redirect()` in a closure without `return`**: `redirect()` only sends a `Location` header; code after it still
  runs. `Route::redirect` has no such problem.
+ **Before 2.16.0** an unknown address ran the first route of the file instead of answering 404.

## Related pages

+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes): forms, sign-in, webhooks, downloads, redirects, `Route::action`
+ [Request](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/3.-Request): what a web-only capability or a controller reads from the request
+ [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers): existing ones, and how to move one
+ [Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views): Pug pages and `errors()`, `old()`, `flash()`
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)
+ [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries): the query builder the capabilities use

# Request

`Caligrafy\Request` holds what a request brings: its method, its address, its route variables, its fields or JSON body,
its files and its headers. You rarely read it yourself: a capability receives its inputs already collected and checked
by its route (`Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::action`, `Route::capability`...), and a `Context` that says who is
calling. You read the request in a web-only capability, when the answer depends on something that is not an input (a
header, how the call was made), and in the controllers you keep.

## With Claude

Describe the behavior; the `caligrafy` skill knows the request API and reads it only where the inputs are not enough.

```text
"Add GET /authors/{author_id}/books: when the author has one book, go straight to its page; otherwise list them."
```

Claude declares `author_id` in `$rules`, so the capability gets it as an input, and adds one `Route::action` line to
`application/config/routing/web.php`.

**Check**

- [ ] What can be an input is declared in `$rules`: nothing reads `$_GET`, `$_POST` or `$_FILES` for it.
- [ ] Only a capability with `webOnly: true` calls `request()`: a plain capability is also reached by REST, MCP, the command
      line and jobs, which have no such request.

## By hand

1. **Write a capability that shows what it reads.** Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Demo/ShowRequest`, and replace the content of
   `application/services/Demo/ShowRequest.php` with:

   ```php
   <?php

   use Caligrafy\Capability;
   use Caligrafy\Context;
   use Caligrafy\Service;
   use Caligrafy\Web;

   // show_request: the inputs a capability gets, and what it can read of the request
   #[Capability(name: 'show_request', description: 'Shows what the request carries.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
   class ShowRequest extends Service
   {
       public $rules = array('id' => '', 'title' => '', 'sort' => '');

       public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
       {
           $request = request();
           return Web::json(array(
               'input' => $input,
               'method' => $request->method,
               'uri' => $request->uri,
               'parameters' => $request->parameters(),
               'wantsJson' => $request->wantsJson(),
           ));
       }
   }
   ```

2. **Route it.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, before `Route::run();`:

   ```php
       Route::action('/echo/{id}', 'show_request', ['method' => ['GET', 'PUT']]);
   ```

3. **Call it.** Run:

   ```bash
   curl -s "http://localhost:8080/echo/3?sort=title"
   ```

   It prints:

   ```json
   {"input":{"sort":"title","id":"3"},"method":"GET","uri":"echo/3","parameters":{"sort":"title","uri":"echo/3"},"wantsJson":false}
   ```

   `uri` is in the parameters of a `GET` because the server's rewrite rule passes the path as `?uri=` (`.htaccess`). The
   capability's inputs do not have it: only what `$rules` declares reaches `handle()`.

4. **Send a JSON body.** A JSON call to `Route::action` needs a personal access token that grants everything
   (`php caligrafer.php token create "echo test" --scopes "*"` prints it once) or, from a page, the `X-CSRF-Token` header:

   ```bash
   curl -s -X PUT -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_..." \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://localhost:8080/echo/3 -d '{"title":"Dune"}'
   ```

   It prints:

   ```json
   {"input":{"title":"Dune","id":"3"},"method":"PUT","uri":"echo/3","parameters":{"title":"Dune"},"wantsJson":true}
   ```

   Without the token it answers `401` with `{"error":{"code":1004,"message":"Access Denied: send the page's CSRF token in
   an X-CSRF-Token header (pages, with the session cookie) or Authorization: Bearer <personal access token> (programs
   and agents)"}}`.

**Check**

- [ ] `input` has the query string or the body and the route variable, as strings (`"3"`).
- [ ] A form post's parameters include `_token` and `_method`; a JSON body's parameters are the decoded body.

## <a name="accessrequest"></a>Getting the request

+ In a web-only capability (`#[Capability(..., webOnly: true)]`, served by
  [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webonly)), a closure route or a helper: `request()`, which builds a
  new `Request` each time.
+ In a controller you keep: `$this->request`, built once when the controller is created.
+ In any other capability: never. Its inputs come from the route (the fields, the query string and the route variables),
  and `$context` says who calls (`$context->user`, `$context->userId()`). The route variables win over the query string on
  every declared route: `/echo/3?id=9` gives `id = 3` (`Route::action` and `Route::capability` since 2.21.2). Still check a
  route variable that decides what is reached against the person.

## <a name="requestproperties"></a>Properties

| Property | What it holds | Example for `PUT /echo/3` with `{"title":"Dune"}` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$method` | the HTTP method in upper case, after `_method` (a `POST` with `_method=PUT` is `PUT`) | `PUT` |
| `$uri` | the path without its leading and trailing slashes, `/` for the home page | `echo/3` |
| `$fullUri` | the path, `?`, and the parameters as a query string | `echo/3?title=Dune` |
| `$uriComponents` | the segments of the path | `['echo', '3']` |
| `$parsedURI` | the same segments, from `parsePath()` | `['echo', '3']` |
| `$uriParameters` | `GET`: the query string (`$_GET`); `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`: the form fields, else the decoded JSON body | `['title' => 'Dune']` |
| `$parameters` | `$uriParameters`, or the route variables when there are none | `['title' => 'Dune']` |
| `$currentRoute` | the pattern of the matched route | `echo/{id}` |
| `$currentBind` | the route variables, plus the query string for a `GET` route; a route variable is never replaced (2.21.7) | `['id' => '3']` |
| `$fetch` | `$currentBind` as an object: `$this->request->fetch->id` | `{id: "3"}` |
| `$host` | the `Host` header | `localhost:8080` |
| `$authorization` | the `Authorization` header | `Bearer cq_...` |
| `$accept` | the `Accept` header | `application/json` |
| `$acceptEncoding`, `$acceptLanguage`, `$cache`, `$cookie`, `$userAgent` | those headers | |
| `$token` | the personal access token row, once `authorizeApiRequest()` checked it (`null` before) | |

## <a name="requestmethods"></a>Methods

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch($name)` | a route variable (or, for a `GET` route, a query string value) by name; by position when `$name` is an integer (`fetch(1)` is the first); `''` when there is none |
| `parameters()` | the request's parameters again (as `$uriParameters`) |
| `files($field)` | the `$_FILES` entry of a file input (`name`, `type`, `tmp_name`, `error`, `size`), `[]` when there is none |
| `wantsJson()` | `true` when `Accept` contains `application/json` and not `text/html` (an API call) |
| `bearer()` | the value after `Bearer ` in `Authorization`, else `null` |
| `authorizeSessionRequest()` | `true` when the `X-CSRF-Token` header (or a `_token` field) equals the session's CSRF token: a page of this app |
| `authorizeApiRequest($scope = '*')` | `true` for a personal access token that grants `$scope`, or the legacy API key while `LEGACY_API_KEY` is not `false` |
| `apiRefusal()` | why a JSON call to `Route::action` or a controller route was refused (the text after `Access Denied:`) |
| `isLegacyApiKey($key)`, `Request::legacyKeysDisabled()` | whether a value is this app's legacy API key; whether `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` turned those keys off |
| `forClient()` | what a client app's page may see of the request (2.19.1): `method`, `host`, `uri`, `fullUri`, `uriComponents`, `uriParameters` (the query string, without `_token`), `parameters`, `parsedURI`, `currentRoute`, `fetch` and `acceptLanguage`. Never the `Cookie` (the session id), the `Authorization` header or a `POST` body. The `Client/app` view gives it to the app's script as `env.request` |

**The CSRF check.** Building a `Request` for a `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` checks the CSRF token, and stops with `403`
`[ERROR 3000] Security Error - Cross Site Forgery` when the `_token` field is missing or wrong. It is skipped when the
request carries a bearer token, sends the session's token in `X-CSRF-Token`, asks for JSON (`wantsJson()`), posts to a
`Route::webhook` address, a `Route::mcp` address (2.19.1: without a personal access token it answers `401` JSON-RPC
with `WWW-Authenticate`, never as the session's user) or the notifications unsubscribe page, or comes from a `User-Agent` listed in
`APPROVED_AGENTS`. The token is read from the form fields only, never from a JSON body.

## Common mistakes

+ **`fetch('id')` is a string.** Compare with `==` or cast it: `(int) $this->request->fetch('id')`. Give it to a
  capability with an `integer` rule rather than checking it yourself.
+ **`fetch('id')` on a `GET` with `?id=9`** gives the route variable: since 2.21.7 the query string never replaces it. Read the
  query string value under another name.
+ **`fetch()` of a query string value on a `POST` route** returns `''`: the query string is only merged for `GET`
  routes. Read the body with `parameters()`.
+ **A JSON body without `Accept: application/json`** fails the CSRF check (`[ERROR 3000]`): the token is only read
  from form fields. Send `Accept: application/json` and `X-CSRF-Token` (pages) or a bearer token (programs).
+ **`fetch()` from the browser sends `Accept: */*`**, which is not JSON: set `Accept: application/json` yourself.
  `axios` sends `application/json, text/plain, */*`, which is.
+ **Reading the request in a plain capability**: it works for the web only. REST, MCP, the command line and jobs have no
  such request; declare the input in `$rules` instead, or give it from the route with the `inputs` option of `Route::form`.
  A capability that truly needs the request is `webOnly: true`.

## Related pages

+ [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing): how a request finds its route
+ [Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action): `Route::action` and web-only capabilities
+ [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers): `$this->request` in the controllers you keep
+ [Helpers, forms and REST API](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.-Helpers-,-Forms-&-REST-API): `request()`, `csrf()`, `methodField()`

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7-Understanding-the-flow-of-information -->

A **Vue app** is one more experience of your application, next to its Pug pages, its REST API and its AI agents. Caligrafy keeps the data and the rules on the server, in capabilities; the Vue app draws the screens in the browser and calls those capabilities through a JavaScript client that Caligrafy generates. This page follows one click from a Vue app to the database and back, and compares the two kinds of Vue app Caligrafy makes.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app app bookshelf
```
Claude scaffolds `public/bookshelf/`, generates the JS client into `public/js/capabilities.js`, wires the page route in `application/config/routing/web.php` and writes the screens with the page components. `/caligrafy-quill:new-app create bookshelf` makes a Vite single page app instead. Write the capabilities first, or in the same request (`/caligrafy-quill:new-capability`).

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The app's page opens and its browser console has no error.
+ Data comes from the generated client (`listBooks()`, `createBook()`), never from a hand-built request with an API key.
+ A refused input shows the field's message from the server.
## By hand

You follow one call of the Bookshelf app, with `curl` standing in for the browser. You need the Bookshelf tables, sample data and capabilities of [Views, steps 1 to 3](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#viewsstartup), and `Route::capabilities('/capabilities');` in `application/config/routing/web.php` (the Quickstart adds it).

**1. What the client sees.** Run:
```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/capabilities
```
Expected: `{"data":[{"name":"create_book","description":"Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. ...","scope":"books:write",...,"input":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string","maxLength":200,...},...},"required":["title","published_year","author_id"]}},...],"csrf":"<64 characters>"}`: the capabilities this caller may use, with their inputs, and the session's CSRF token. The generated client reads this token once, then sends it with every write.

**2. A call.** Run:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id": 3}' http://localhost:8080/capabilities/get_book
```
Expected: `{"data":{"id":3,"title":"Kindred","published_year":1979,"summary":"A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.","isbn":null,"author_id":2,...,"author":{"id":2,"name":"Octavia E. Butler",...}}}`: the book, with its author nested. In the Vue app this is one line, `await getBook({ id: 3 })`, which returns what is inside `data`.

**3. A refusal.** Run:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Lilith"}' http://localhost:8080/capabilities/create_book
```
Expected: status `422` and `{"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"published_year":"The Published Year field is required","author_id":"The Author Id field is required"}}}`. In the Vue app, `createBook()` throws a `CapabilityError` whose `fields` is that object: one message per field, ready for the form.

**Check**
+ The same answers come from the Pug page, from REST and from an AI agent: one set of rules.
+ No API key appears anywhere: a page uses the visitor's session cookie and the CSRF token; programs and agents use a personal access token.
## Reference

### The flow

```text
Vue app (browser)                     Caligrafy (server)
-----------------                     ------------------
createBook({ title, ... })
  -> POST /capabilities/create_book   Route::capabilities('/capabilities')
     session cookie + X-CSRF-Token      -> who is calling: the signed-in user, or a visitor
                                        -> may they use it: public, scope, level
                                        -> $rules check the inputs
                                        -> handle(): the query builder reads and writes the database
  <- {"data": {...}}            201     <- the answer, the same for every channel
  <- {"error": {code, fields}}  422     <- or a refusal: invalid, unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict
```

### The two kinds of Vue app

| | Vue as a library | Vite single page app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Created by | `php caligrafer.php app <name>` | `php caligrafer.php create <name>` |
| Lives in | `public/<name>/index.php` and `public/<name>/scripts/main.js` | `public/<name>/src/` (`.vue` files), built to `public/<name>/dist/` |
| Needs Node.js | no | yes (20.19+ or 22.12+), on your computer |
| Served by | Caligrafy: a page route renders it (view `Client/app`) and gives it `env` | `npm run dev` while you work; `dist/` once built |
| Its JS client | `public/js/capabilities.js` | `public/<name>/src/capabilities.js` |
| Good for | one screen or a few, next to Pug pages | a larger app with its own routes, components and store |
| Pages | [setting up](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library), [structure](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.1-Understanding-the-structure), [routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.2-Routes), [requests](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests), [forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms), [validations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.5-Validations), [components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.6-Components) | [setting up](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application), [routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications), [single file components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.3-Single-File-Components), [state](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.4-State-Management) |

### Who does what

| Caligrafy (PHP, `application/`) | Vue (JavaScript, `public/<app>/`) |
| --- | --- |
| tables, models, capabilities and their rules | screens, components, what the person types |
| who may do what: sessions, tokens, scopes, levels | showing what the server answered, and its errors |
| the page route that serves the app | the routes between the screens of a single page app |

Both kinds of app build their screens with Caligrafy's [page components](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#pagecomponents) (`layout.css`, `look.css`), so they look like the Pug pages.
## Other ways

A Vue app can call a [`Route::action`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#action) or a controller route that answers JSON, with `fetch` or axios and the headers of `apiHeaders()`: see [Requests, other ways](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests). Capabilities replace them: the same rules then serve the pages, REST and AI agents.
## Related pages

+ [How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works)
+ [Build once: services, capabilities and MCP](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP)
+ [Vue.js](https://vuejs.org/)

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.2-Routes -->

A Vue app as a library needs two kinds of routes on the server, both in `application/config/routing/web.php`: a **page route**, which serves the app's markup with its `env`, and the **capability routes**, which the app calls for its data. Routing between screens inside the browser is the job of a single page app ([Routing for single page apps](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.2-Routing-for-Single-Page-Applications)).
## With Claude

`/caligrafy-quill:new-app app <name>` adds the page route; `/caligrafy-quill:new-capability` adds capabilities and keeps `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` in place. To change a route, ask: "serve the bookshelf app at /shelf, for signed-in people only".

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The page route is a `Route::page(..., 'Client/app', ...)` above `Route::run();`, with `appName` the folder in `public/`.
+ `Route::capabilities('/capabilities');` is in `web.php` once.
+ Opening the address while signed out does what was asked (the app, or the sign-in page).
## By hand

You serve the Bookshelf app of [Setting up Vue as a library](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.0-Setting-up-Vue.js-as-a-library) three ways and give it its first books from the server.

**1. The ready-made address.** The template's `web.php` serves every client app at `/apps/<name>`. Its line names the example controller; write the same address declared, and open it:
```php
    Route::page('/apps/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']]);
```
Replace the `Route::get('/apps/{appName}', ...)` line with it. Open `http://localhost:8080/apps/bookshelf`: the app opens with no route of its own. It serves any folder of `public/` whose name is made of letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

**2. Your own address.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, above `Route::run();`, write:
```php
    // BOOKSHELF: the Vue app (public/bookshelf/index.php)
    Route::page('/bookshelf', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index']]);
```
Open `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`: the same app, and in the console `env.authorized` and `env.user` say who is signed in.

**3. The first books from the server.** Change the route to:
```php
    Route::page('/bookshelf', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index'], 'data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);
```
Reload, and type `env.books` in the console: `{data: Array(...), total: ..., page: 1, per_page: 20, pages: ...}`, the answer of `list_books`, in the page itself. The script can show it at once (`this.books = env.books.data`) and call the client for the next pages.

**4. The data routes.** Check that `web.php` has, once:
```php
    Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // the capabilities for the JS client of the Vue apps
```
Run `curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/capabilities`: `{"data":[...],"csrf":"..."}`.

**Check**
+ `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf` and `http://localhost:8080/apps/bookshelf` open the same app.
+ `http://localhost:8080/apps/nothere` answers `This client app does not exist...`.
## Reference

### Page routes

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Route::page('/bookshelf', 'Client/app', ['with' => ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index']])` | serves `public/bookshelf/index.php`. Takes every option of [`Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#parameterview): `data` (read-only capabilities, their answers in `env`), `signedIn` (visitors go to `/login`), `level`, `notFound`; `env` gets `authorized` and `user` |
| `Route::page('/apps/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']])` | serves `public/<appName>/index.php`, or `public/<appName>/<file>.php` with `?app=<file>`. `query` lists what `env` gets of the query string |
| `Route::page('/bot/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index', 'botSkillId']])` | a bot app: `?botSkillId=` is its assistant |
| `Route::page('/ml/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']])` | a machine learning app |
| `Route::get('/apps/{appName}', 'Caligrafy\\Controllers\\ClientController')`, and the same for `/bot/`, `/ml/` | what the template's `web.php` ships: the same result, and `env` gets the whole query string |

`appName` and `app` must be made of letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and only files directly inside `public/<appName>/` are served; anything else shows `This client app does not exist`.

### Data routes

| Route | What it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')` | `GET /capabilities`: the capabilities the caller may use and the CSRF token; `POST /capabilities/<name>`: calls one. The generated JS client uses it |
| `Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books')` | one capability at a REST address, for other programs ([Build once: REST](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#rest)) |
## Under the hood

+ **`ClientController`** (`application/controllers/core/AI/ClientController.php`) takes the last part of the path as `appName` and `?app=` as the markup file (default `index`), then returns `view('Client/app', ...)` with the query string. A page that first chooses what to show is a web-only capability: `return Web::view('Client/app', ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index', 'shelf' => $shelf]);`.
+ **A closure** `Route::get('/bookshelf', function () { return view('Client/app', ['appName' => 'bookshelf', 'app' => 'index']); });` works too, without `authorized` and `user`. `Route::page` replaces both.
+ **Controller data routes** (`Route::get('/api/shelf', 'BookController@index')` returning `api([...])`) still answer JSON, in code that has them: see [Requests, other ways](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.3-Requests). Capabilities replace them.
## Common mistakes

+ **`appName` that is not the folder name**: `This client app does not exist`.
+ **A `data` capability that writes**: `Route::page` accepts only read-only capabilities (`500` on every visit).
+ **Expecting the query string in `env` with `Route::page`**: only the names listed in its `query` option reach it.
+ **Two `Route::capabilities` lines**: keep one.
## Related pages

+ [Routing](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/2.-Routing)
+ [Views: `Route::page`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#parameterview)
+ [Understanding the structure](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.1-Understanding-the-structure)

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.5-Validations -->

**Validation** decides whether what a person typed is acceptable. In Caligrafy it happens once, on the server, in the capability's `$rules`: the same rules answer the Vue app, the Pug pages, REST and AI agents, and the messages come back one per field. A Vue app shows those messages; it can also check the obvious cases before sending, from the same rules, so the person waits less.
## With Claude

Ask for the rule, not for the screen: "a book's title needs at least 2 characters". Claude changes `$rules` in the capability (`/caligrafy-quill:new-capability` knows the [rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)), runs `php caligrafer.php client` again, and the forms show the new message with no change.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ The rule is in the capability's `$rules`, not only in the Vue script.
+ `php caligrafer.php call create_book title=D author_id=2 published_year=1987` answers `invalid` with the message.
+ The Vue form shows that message under the field.
## By hand

You add a rule to `create_book` and show it in the Bookshelf app of [Forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms), then add a check before sending. Commands run in the project folder with the Docker server.

**1. The rule.** In `application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php`, change the title's rule in `$rules` to:
```php
        'title' => 'required|min_len,2|max_len,200',
```

**2. Try it from the command line.** Run:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call create_book title=D author_id=2 published_year=1987
```
Expected:
```json
{
    "error": {
        "code": "invalid",
        "message": "Some of the inputs are invalid",
        "fields": {
            "title": "The Title field needs to be at least 2 characters"
        }
    }
}
```

**3. Update the client.** Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client public/js/capabilities.js`. The rules are on the server, so the functions do not change, but `GET /capabilities` now describes `title` with `"minLength": 2` (and `published_year` with `"minimum": 1450` and `"maximum"`: this year).

**4. See it in the app.** Open `http://localhost:8080/bookshelf`, type `D`, choose an author, type `1987`, press **Add book**: `The Title field needs to be at least 2 characters` appears under the title. The `addBook()` of [Forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms) already puts `e.fields` in `errors`.

**5. Check before sending.** In `public/bookshelf/scripts/main.js`, add this function above `const app = Vue.createApp({`:
```js
// The obvious cases, from the capability's own description: the server still decides
function check (schema, input) {
    const errors = {}
    for (const [field, rule] of Object.entries(schema.properties)) {
        const value = input[field] === null || input[field] === undefined ? '' : String(input[field])
        if ((schema.required || []).includes(field) && value === '') errors[field] = 'Required'
        else if (rule.minLength && value.length < rule.minLength) errors[field] = 'At least ' + rule.minLength + ' characters'
        else if (rule.maxLength && value.length > rule.maxLength) errors[field] = 'At most ' + rule.maxLength + ' characters'
        else if (rule.minimum !== undefined && value !== '' && Number(value) < rule.minimum) errors[field] = 'At least ' + rule.minimum
        else if (rule.maximum !== undefined && value !== '' && Number(value) > rule.maximum) errors[field] = 'At most ' + rule.maximum
    }
    return errors
}
```
At the end of `mounted()`, after `await this.load(1)`, add:
```js
        this.schema = (await this.api.capabilities()).find(c => c.name === 'create_book').input
```
At the start of `addBook()`, before `this.errors = {}`, add:
```js
            const found = this.schema ? check(this.schema, this.book) : {}
            if (Object.keys(found).length) { this.errors = found; return }
```
Reload, type `D`, choose an author, type `1987`, press **Add book**: `At least 2 characters` appears at once, without a call (the network panel shows no `POST /capabilities/create_book`). A year of `987` shows `At least 1450`.

**Check**
+ Removing the check of step 5 still refuses the book, with the server's message: the server is the rule.
+ The Pug page `/books` and `curl -X POST ... /capabilities/create_book` refuse the title `D` with the same message.
## Reference

### Where each part lives

| Part | Where | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$rules` | the capability | GUMP rules per input: `required`, `max_len,255`, `min_len,2`, `integer`, `valid_email`, `exists,authors.id`, `unique,books.isbn`... ([all rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)). Only these inputs reach `handle()` |
| `$filters` | the capability | applied before the rules: `trim`, `sanitize_string`... |
| `$descriptions` | the capability | what each input is, in the schema clients and agents read |
| `ServiceError::invalid(['author_id' => 'There is no such author'])` | `handle()` | a refusal decided by code, with the same shape |
| `e.fields` | the Vue app | `{field: message}` of a `CapabilityError` whose `code` is `invalid` |
| `capabilities()` | the Vue app | each capability's `input`: a JSON schema with `required`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `format` (email, uri), `enum`, `type` |

### Messages

Each field gets one message, the first rule it breaks, in GUMP's words with the field's name: `The Published Year field is required`, `The Title field needs to be at least 2 characters`, `The Published Year field needs to be a numeric value, equal to, or higher than 1450`. The whole refusal is `422` with `{"error": {"code": "invalid", "message": "Some of the inputs are invalid", "fields": {...}}}`.
## Other ways: a controller that validates

A controller in older code validates with `$this->check()` and answers with `api()`:
```php
$errors = $this->check($this->request->parameters(), array('title' => 'required|max_len,200', 'author_id' => 'required|integer'));
if ($errors !== true) {
    http_response_code(422);
    return api(array('error' => true, 'message' => 'Some of the inputs are invalid', 'errors' => $errors));
}
```
`fetch` then gets `response.status === 422` and the payload from `await response.json()`; axios rejects and puts it in `error.response.data`. The rules then live in that controller only: a capability gives them to every channel.
## Common mistakes

+ **The rule only in JavaScript**: REST, agents and anyone with `curl` skip it. Put it in `$rules`.
+ **A client check stricter than the server**: people are refused for no reason. Build it from `capabilities()`, as in step 5.
+ **An input sent but missing from `$rules`**: it is dropped before `handle()`. Add it with `''` (no rule) if it needs none.
## Related pages

+ [Validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation)
+ [Forms](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.7.4-Forms)
+ [Vue form bindings](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/forms.html)
